title: Malik Muhammad Offers Refreshingly Honest Answer on Jaylon Johnson's Struggles With Bears
full_text:
Anyone who has watched Chicago Bears games in 2026 knows full well just how bad things have been for Jaylon Johnson in 2026.
Johnson's coverage stats are abysmal. He's giving up a completion rate of 73.7% and a passer rating of 124.3.
But Johnson's struggles extend beyond just coverage. He has also been terrible at tackling and his 21.9% missed tackle rate is the second-highest of his career, per Pro Football Focus .
On Thursday, FOX Chicago Bears reporter Devan Kaney asked cornerback Malik Muhammad about his teammate's issues this season and the rookie gave a refreshingly honest answer.
"People don't know the cornerback position is super hard," Muhammad said. "It's one of the hardest positions, and I'm not giving (Johnson) an out or anything. Obviously, he knows he's gotta play better, we all know he's gotta play better, but the position is hard."
The surprising part of Muhammad's answer is his admission that Johnson does need to play better.
Sure, we all know that's the case, but for a player to admit that about his teammate is both rare and refreshing, and that's especially true for a rookie.
And we know the cornerback position is difficult to play, and might be one of the most difficult to play. But we also know that Johnson has played at a much higher level in the past, which is why his drop-off is particularly jarring.
Johnson's decline started last season , but that was chalked up to him not being healthy. The veteran doesn't have that excuse this season, which makes his struggles even more perplexing.
The Bears have a clear out in Johnson's contract in 2027, and at this rate they are likely to take that off ramp.
Johnson even admitted before the season started that he was basically in a contract year .
"This is definitely a contract year. We all know with the cap hit and all that stuff. It's definitely a contract year for me so at the end of the day, whether that's here or somewhere else, I gotta put it on tape that I am still a top guy," Johnson said.
Fortunately for the Bears, it doesn't look like they'll have to start with a totally blank slate at boundary cornerback next year if they do cut Johnson thanks to Muhammad's ascension to the team's top player at the position through eight weeks.
But there's still a long way to go between now and then and the rookie has to fully cement himself the rest of this season.
With Johnson struggling and Tyrique Stevenson unable to offer a reliable replacement, the Bears are reportedly in the market for a cornerback, according to ESPN's Dan Graziano .
"The Bears made their big move for (Jeffery) Simmons, but they're still poking around on potentially available cornerbacks, as are the Lions," Graziano wrote.
We've been high on the idea of the Bears trading for Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen. A lesser move that makes sense for Chicago is acquiring New York Jets cornerback Nahshon Wright, who is, of course, a former Bear.
Whether it's Woolen, Wright or another cornerback, the Bears need to make a move at the position before the deadline since neither Johnson nor Stevenson can be trusted.

title: Bengals Trade Idea Would Add Experienced Veteran to Cincinnati's Defense
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals are one of the better teams in the AFC, but they need to make a few big moves if they want to separate themselves as serious contenders in the NFL.
They could use some supporting help on offense. They have one of the best offenses in the league, but it's because of Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins. They could use an additional wide receiver or some help at running back. They could also use some support on defense, especially in the secondary. Their cornerback room is decent, but it might not be good enough to win the Super Bowl. Adding some support at the trade deadline would help quite a bit.
The Athletic and their writers, including Daniel Popper, recently put together a mock NFL trade deadline scenario in which the Bengals swung a trade for Los Angeles Chargers cornerback Donte Jackson in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick.
"Jackson is on an expiring deal with the Chargers, who have the worst record in the league at 0-7," Popper wrote . "His 23 career interceptions rank fifth among active players. Jackson has missed four games with a hamstring injury but was back in practice all three days last week in a limited capacity. The Bengals offered a 2027 sixth-round pick. The Lions offered a 2027 seventh-round pick. The Chargers accepted the Bengals’ offer."
Jackson is the perfect combination of impactful and affordable. The Bengals don't need a superstar on defense, as they already made their big trade to acquire Dexter Lawrence a few months ago. But their cornerback room needs some support, and Jackson has enough gas left in the tank to help them make a run for the Super Bowl.
Jackson being on an expiring deal would be a benefit for the Bengals, as they wouldn't be tied to him beyond just this season. Adding him in exchange for a late-round draft pick, while paying him pennies on the dollar compared with other starting cornerbacks, would be a move too good for Cincinnati to pass up.
The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET. Cincinnati has made an in-season trade in each of the past two seasons. They're guaranteed to be at least 5-3 at the deadline and could improve to 6-2 with a win over the Falcons in Madrid. title: Three Edge Rushers the Bengals Could Target Before the NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals escaped Sunday with a win, but their depth at defensive end took a hit. Cashius Howell suffered a right wrist injury that will require surgery during a 46-36 overtime victory over Tennessee, while Cedric Johnson exited with a left ankle injury.
Cincinnati improved to 5-2, and Boye Mafe increased his team-leading sack total to 5.5. Adding another veteran could help protect the pass rush from further injuries and give defensive coordinator Al Golden more options down the stretch.
The NFL trade deadline is Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET, giving the Bengals time to evaluate their needs and explore the market. Here are three edge rushers to consider as potential targets.
Mack would give Cincinnati an experienced option for its playoff push, but it won't come without competition to acquire him. The Chargers are 0-7, and Mack is on an expiring contract. The Chicago Bears are believed to be interested in acquiring him.
The 35-year-old is on a one-year, $18 million contract, which would make him a rental unless the Bengals negotiate an extension. That structure could appeal to a team seeking immediate help while continuing to develop its younger defensive ends.
Mack would work opposite Mafe, giving Golden another option in obvious passing situations. The Bengals would need to weigh the draft compensation against the remaining salary.
For the Bengals, Sweat would be a bigger investment with potential value beyond this season. The 29-year-old recorded a career-high 12 sacks in 2025 and is under contract through 2028.
The asking price could be the obstacle. PHNX’s Johnny Venerable reported that Arizona is seeking a high Day 2 pick for Sweat, who reportedly requested a trade after Jonathan Gannon’s dismissal.
For Cincinnati, the appeal would be adding another proven pass rusher alongside Mafe, with Dexter Lawrence creating problems inside. Sweat would make the most sense if the Bengals view him as part of their plans beyond 2026, since that reported price would be difficult to justify as injury insurance alone.
Uche would be a more affordable option for the Bengals. His one-year contract is worth roughly $1.4 million, and PFF included him among its potential trade candidates in October.
He has two sacks this season, including one against New England on Sunday. Cincinnati also saw him during its Week 5 win over Miami.
If Howell and Johnson avoid extended absences, Uche could still strengthen the rotation at a manageable salary, provided Miami’s asking price reflects that supporting role.

title: 'Going To Put On A Show' - Joe Burrow Hammers Home Love For International Games Ahead of Falcons Madrid Battle
full_text:
Joe Burrow seems really excited to represent the NFL on its international stage Sunday morning. He spoke to all the gathered media at the podium on Friday.
Cincinnati's most important player has been dreaming of playing an international NFL game for years.
"It means a lot to me that we're here. I think this is Year 7 for me, and I haven't been overseas yet. And we keep adding more and more games to try to build the NFL globally," Burrow noted. "I think it's worked over the last five years, and I'm hoping to add more and continue to build, and I love being part of that, and I want to help grow the game, and so I love being here.
"I love being the only game on TV on Sunday morning when people back home wake up, and I love showcasing our talents abroad and trying to bring attention to what we do, as far as what our offense brings. I think we're explosive, we're dynamic, we're fun to watch, and I think we're going to put on a show on Sunday."
Cincinnati has a couple more days to explore the Spanish capital as Burrow faces the harrowing trials of packing up all his clothes on Saturday night.
He told the media he does not like packing at all and that his mom put his things together for this trip. A little home feeling to carry him across this journey. All in all, Burrow's stayed largely anonymous in Spain; he likes not getting recognized as much in a new country.
"I was really excited about it. I hadn't been here yet, so that was exciting for me," burrow said about visiting Spain. "This is somewhere that I've always wanted to go, and so to be able to do it while doing what I love, playing football, is really a dream come true for me. I talked about last week how one of my favorite times of my life is playing AAU basketball and traveling around with my friends and staying in the hotels, and that's really what this is, just in the NFL, which makes it that much more special. As far as my recognizability abroad, sometimes, sometimes not.
"I ran into some students studying abroad from the United States the other day when I was walking around, and that was certainly surprising. It's often a little more than I expect when I'm in a different country; I usually expect to go pretty incognito and not have anybody recognize me. It's a little more than that, but I love being out here because I can feel like a normal person for a little bit."
Excited and feeling normal.
Just what Bengals fans want to hear from their star at roughly the midway point of the 2026 regular season.

title: 'Everything Is Always Blown Out Of Proportion' - Ja'Marr Chase Sets Record Straight Following Titans Outburst
full_text:
There are zero hard feelings between Ja'Marr Chase and Zac Taylor in Spain. Chase spoke to the media on Friday and detailed why he got so upset on the sideline late in last week's 43-36 win over the Titans.
The Bengals star wasn't happy with how the offense executed, and he talked to Taylor after the game about the situation.
"I'm a leader," Chase said in Spain. "I want the best for everyone around me, especially when the offense isn't clicking. They let me speak my mind and opinion at the end of the day as long as I do it with respect. And I believe Zac can vouch for me. He and I already talked. Everything is always blown out of proportion with whatever I do."
Chase had his best game of the season, posting 10 catches for 141 yards and a score. He clearly wasn't upset about his individual play; Chase has never fit the diva stereotype like that.
All in all, it's just a captain wanting to make sure his unit executes at the highest level.
"A lot of different things. It was an emotional game; I didn't hit him on the deep one, and we turned it over too many times. He wants to win and wants to execute on every snap, as do I. That's how it goes," Joe Burrow said about the emotion following Sunday's game.
Chase and Higgins have been the best wide receiver duo in the NFL this season. The latter is establishing himself as not just the best WR2 in the NFL, but Higgins is arguably a Top-10 receiver in the league alongside Chase.
The latest AFC Offensive Player of the Week one-upped Chase with 10 catches for 155 yards and two scores on the other side of the formation.
"Honestly, he's a whole different receiver this year than last year — run after the catch, more on back shoulder throws with Joe (Burrow). It's hard to cover that when you're constantly switching it up every game. I love what they're doing and can only be better from here," Chase said about Higgins.
Both are trying to keep that production going for the Bengals this week against Atlanta's 11th-ranked NFL defense by EPA/dropback allowed.

title: Bengals' Pursuit of Jonathan Taylor May Be More Fantasy Than Reality
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals have been named as a potential trade suitor for Indianapolis Colts superstar running back Jonathan Taylor, even though a deal isn't very likely to come to fruition.
There are a few teams reportedly in the mix. The Bengals' biggest issue with a potential deal is the fact that the return for him in a trade would need to be massive to get him out of Indianapolis. The Bengals would need to cut ties with multiple valuable draft picks to land Taylor.
The Athletic and writer Daniel Popper recently put together a mock NFL trade deadline scenario in which Taylor wasn't traded, even though the representative for the Bengals made a run at him.
"The Colts received offers on Taylor from three teams," Popper wrote. "The Vikings offered a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fourth-round pick. The Bengals offered a 2027 third-round pick.
"The Giants made the most aggressive offer: a 2027 second-round pick, a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fourth-round pick. This package aligns pretty closely with what the 49ers gave up for Christian McCaffrey ahead of the 2022 deadline. The Colts rejected the Vikings’ and Bengals’ offers. Those teams did not want to counter and dropped out of the race. That left the Giants’ offer."
It would be shocking to see the Bengals give up enough draft capital to bring in Taylor. The Colts are likely asking for a package similar to the blockbuster deal that sent Christian McCaffrey to the San Francisco 49ers a few years ago.
The Bengals would instantly jump a few slots in the power rankings if they added Taylor. Their offense would no longer be one-dimensional like it has been this season.
Still, it's difficult to imagine them giving up a second-round pick and then some in order to land Taylor.
The asking price is a lot, and the Bengals might not be willing to pay it.

title: 3 Wide Receivers That Bengals Could Trade for to Bolster Their Offense
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals could've pursued receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. before the Arizona Cardinals traded him to the Houston Texans. Harrison would have come to Cincinnati and slotted in as a much-needed wide receiver No. 3.
The Bengals need to add another playmaker on offense. Coming into Week 8, the Bengals had seen little production from their wide receiver room aside from Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.
If they opt for a trade, who could the Bengals target?
The Indianapolis Colts will almost certainly sell at the trade deadline, and they could look to move on from wide receiver Josh Downs.
Downs is a very talented option, but he needs a better offense with a more consistent quarterback. The Bengals would give him that with an offense centered around Chase, Higgins, and Joe Burrow. Downs would be a massive upgrade over what the Bengals have on their roster right now. This season, Downs has caught 26 passes for 307 yards coming into Week 8.
Another wide receiver who could be on the move is Jacksonville Jaguars pass catcher Brian Thomas Jr. Thomas has been moved down on the depth chart in Jacksonville and could desperately use a change of scenery.
Adding him to the Bengals' offense, which is high-powered and relies on throwing the ball, could be exactly what he needs. He hasn't done much this season, though he's tallied a few touchdowns.
The Bengals could also make a move for wide receiver Jauan Jennings, who hasn't made much of an impact in Minnesota this season.
Still, he has some potential left to provide to a high-powered offense. Jennings would be very affordable to acquire in a deal, and he would give the Bengals a veteran to add to their depleted wide receiver room. At the very least, he would be a solid veteran in a room with multiple young wide receivers.

title: Zac Taylor Drops Friday Injury Status Update For DJ Turner, Cedric Johnson Ahead of Falcons Spain Game
full_text:
The Bengals look likely to field Cedric Johnson (ankle) and DJ Turner (heel) to defend against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, barring any big setbacks. Alas, Zac Taylor spoke to the media on Friday before the team's final practice in Madrid, Spain, and noted the two are continuing with "day-to-day" status.
UPDATE: Turner is healthy and not on the report, while Johnson is questionable.
Injury report for #CINatATL 🔗: https://t.co/V922dusUlv pic.twitter.com/IQyHaklUnM
Turner practiced fully on Thursday, while Johnson went limited, so it would be pretty shocking if they didn't play. Jordan Battle (hamstring) was limited as well, and Kyle Dugger (quad) looks like he'll miss another game after not practicing again on Thursday.
"Everyone is progressing ahead. We'll take it day-to-day for both DJ and Ced," Taylor said before touching on the team's acclimation to the new country/setting. "We feel acclimated. We had a great day of practice yesterday. Field held up really well. Our guys have handled the week really well."
Cincinnati has a couple more days in Spain before battling the Falcons at 9:30 a.m. ET on Sunday and returning to Cincinnati ahead of the most important game of the season so far: A home AFC North battle against Pittsburgh for control of the division on Sunday Night Football.
They need to take out another NFC opponent first.
"I think this is the best compromise we found to make sure that we can get acclimated by Friday, get a really good practice where we feel better, and then play our best on Sunday," Taylor said on Thursday about the travel plans. "So we've all embraced that mindset, and I think it's working well for us so far."
All in all, Cincinnati is in a new country, but on a normal practice schedule.
"Normal Thursday for us," Taylor said. "We did our Wednesday practice on Tuesday before we left town. So now we're back on schedule. Our meetings were the same as they've always been on Thursday. So today is more of a third-down emphasis with some normal downs, and then tomorrow will be red zone-based."
The Bengals can enjoy the city even more on Saturday before Sunday showtime.

title: Colts' Jonathan Taylor Timeline Could Impact Bengals' Trade Deadline Plans
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals have been connected to a trade for Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor ahead of the NFL trade deadline. The Colts are listening to offers for Taylor and the Bengals are one of the teams reportedly interested in the star running back .
The deadline is Tuesday, Nov. 10 and the Bengals need to make their run at Taylor if they're going to land him.
NFL insider Jordan Schultz recently provided an update on the Colts' trade timeline, reporting that Indianapolis won't look to make a deal until after Week 9's games unless they're blown away by a trade offer.
"The Colts have received plenty of calls on several players, including Jonathan Taylor, Josh Downs, Grover Stewart and others," Schultz wrote on X. "But the belief around the league is that, barring an offer that blows them away, Indianapolis plans to wait until after Sunday’s game vs the Cowboys before revisiting the offers on the table and making the trades that make sense on Monday and Tuesday ahead of the deadline."
The Bengals have been connected to Taylor and Downs over the last few weeks. Having an additional week to separate themselves from the rest of the AFC is a good thing. If the Bengals win this week, it's another reason why they should go all in this season. They're not just a contender, but they're one of the best teams in the league. The difference between getting bounced in the AFC Championship and bringing home the Super Bowl might be having Taylor in the backfield next to Joe Burrow. If the Bengals have another big win this week while the running game struggles, it would reinforce the idea that Taylor would help them tremendously.
Downs would be a good target, too. The Bengals need a No. 3 wide receiver, and he has what it takes to help them out. The dream scenario would see the Bengals package draft picks to send to Indianapolis in exchange for Taylor and Downs.
The Bengals could land a playmaker on offense or some help on defense ahead of Tuesday's deadline. In the meantime, they're in Spain getting ready to play the Falcons on Sunday. Kickoff is at 9:30 am ET.

title: Referee for Bengals-Falcons Game Leads League in Defensive Pass Interference Flags
full_text:
CINCINNATI – The referee who worked the game with one of the worst calls of the Zac Taylor era will be on the call Sunday when the Cincinnati Bengals face the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid.
In a 2021 road game against the New York Jets , what looked like a routine tackle by Mike Hilton on a third-and-11checkdown should have result in the Bengals getting the ball back down three points with two minutes to go.
It looked as though Jets running back Michael Carter initiated the helmet-to-helmet contact as Hilton was going for his legs, but Hilton drew the flag, and the Jets killed the clock to win 34-31 as 11-point underdogs
It wasn’t Wrolstad who threw that flag. It was line judge Tripp Sutter, who has had multiple run-ins with the Bengals coaching staff.
Sutter won’t be working Sunday’s Bengals game as he is on fellow Cincinnati villain Ron Torbert’s crew this season.
The Bengals are 6-5 with Wrolstad as the head referee. The last Cincinnati game he worked was last year’s Thanksgiving night win in Baltimore.
Wrolstad and his crew rank third this year with an average of 17.14 accepted penalties per game.
Last year they were 12th (11.61), but in 2024 they were second (14.82).
In 2023, Wrolstad was 13th (9.88), and in 2022 he was 16th (9.35).
Wrolstad’s crew has called 17 defensive pass interference penalties this year, most in the league. No other crew has more than 13.
Ironically, the crew ranks last in defensive holding flags with just one all season.
The group also has five roughing-the-passer penalties, which are one shy of the league lead this year. And their 26 offensive holding penalties rank fifth.
Wrolstad has been a head official since 2014 and has earned playoff assignments in each of the four three seasons after being left off the postseason schedule in five of his first seven seasons.

title: Bengals Injury Report: Cincinnati's Injured Defenders Working Back to Action in Spain
full_text:
The Bengals hit the practice field in Spain for the first time this week as multiple defenders try to work back onto the field from injuries. DJ Turner II (heel), Cedric Johnson (ankle), and Kyle Dugger (quad) are fighting through issues this week, as is Jordan Battle (hamstring).

"We've got a team of people that logistically have handled this stuff for us that have been just top-notch," Taylor said. title: Browns Just Made A Batch of Roster Moves and One Position Group Deserves More Attention
full_text:
As the Cleveland Browns (5-3) gear up for a Week 9 road trip to face the New Orleans Saints (2-5) on Sunday, the team completed a number of roster moves over the past few days.
Among these transactions, one specific position group stands out.
During the week, the Browns signed guard Austin Blaske and tackle Xavier Truss to the practice squad , while also releasing tackle Andrew Coker and guard Vershon Lee from said practice squad.
While these moves don’t affect the active roster, they do come at a point where Cleveland leads the league in sacks allowed by a large margin. The Browns, coming off their second eight-sack game of the season, have now reached 33 allowed sacks for the campaign, with seven other teams tied for second place at a very distant 23 sacks allowed.
And Cleveland hasn't been able to establish the running game , either.
Most probably, that the team isn’t quite comfortable with the low end of the depth chart, either.
As the team is still waiting to see its starting five gel into a cohesive and well-oiled unit, Cleveland is shuffling some of the players on the practice squad just in case. And even if that doesn’t mean that Blaske or Truss will get some playing time soon, it could point to some changes on the horizon for the unit as a whole.
As things stand now, right tackle Tytus Howard and left guard Zion Johnson have been frequently singled out as the weakest link on a line that includes two rookies. Veteran Teven Jenkins, projected as a starter before the season began, hasn’t played a snap all season long and is currently on IR. Backups Dawand Jones at tackle, KT Leveston at guard and/or rookie Parker Brailsford at center could be close to getting a shot in the lineup.
If so, the depth behind any promotion to the first-team unit could get a makeover as well, and that’s where Blaske and Truss could find a way toward the 53-man roster.
Trading Howard or Johnson away after just half a season on the team doesn’t make much sense because of the heavy dead cap hits the Browns would incur for next year. But giving guys like Jones or Leveston a chance to see if they can gel with the rest of the unit does.
And taking a good look at other options for depth purposes, with an eye on the future, makes sense, because there’s no way Cleveland will want to keep playing behind the offensive line as it’s currently built in 2027 and beyond.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: What Browns Head Coach Todd Monken Had To Say About Shedeur Sanders Starting
full_text:
It's not every day that a second-year signal-caller is thrust into a starting role in Week 9 of the NFL season.
Let alone when that opportunity comes after the starting quarterback is placed in concussion protocol midweek, despite clearing it in each of the two previous days.
But that's the situation Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders finds himself in.
On Friday, Nov. 6, the Browns officially confirmed that Sanders would start this weekend in an outing against the New Orleans Saints. Heading into the contest, the Browns are 5-3, with a spot atop the AFC North still in reach.
With Deshaun Watson leading the team in all of the eight previous weeks, Sanders jumping headfirst into the fire this weekend has drawn an awful lot of attention.
Fortunately, he has all the support of head coach Todd Monken.
When asked about his thoughts on Sanders getting his first start of the season, he didn't hold back, expressing his excitement to the highest degree.
“Oh yeah, I’m fired up," he said. "I’m fired up to see him play. I mean, who wouldn’t be?... This is what he’s wanted, right? He wants to be a starting quarterback in the NFL. Let’s go. Let’s let it rip. Let’s see what we got. We’re not holding anything back."
#Browns HC Todd Monken said he's "fired up" to see Shedeur Sanders play on Sunday. “Oh yeah, I’m fired up. I’m fired up to see him play. I mean, who wouldn’t be?... This is what he’s wanted, right? He wants to be a starting quarterback in the NFL. Let’s go. Let’s let it rip.… pic.twitter.com/6NWSa8AfnJ
Sanders comes into Sunday's game with 1,402 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions across 10 games on his resume. He has also flashed a bit of versatility in his game, rushing 21 times for 169 yards and one touchdown.
He isn't a stranger to regular season NFL action, but he hasn't had a legitimate taste of it since January 4th of last season.
This time around, Watson's not in a bad situation, though.
The Browns are playing competitive football, Monken has helped round out the team on both sides of the ball to a respectable spot and there are new weapons for Sanders to be surrounded by.
And with improvements made across the board this past offseason on the fundamental and technical sides of his game, the 25-year-old has every avenue to succeed on the road from Caesars Superdome.
“He’s improved is his footwork, his drops, his mechanics, understanding where to go with the ball, sense of urgency in terms of working through his progressions, protections," Monken said. "There were so many things he needed to work on, and he’s done that like any young player. Any young player has a lot to work on, especially at the quarterback position. And you could see that from the moment we got here.
"And that’s why we opened up the competition and we split the reps, was because of his ascent. That’s what we did. And again, this is just another piece of that. Just like this weekend will be another piece of that.”
#Browns HC Todd Monken on where Shedeur Sanders has improved most in his game: “Where he’s improved is his footwork, his drops, his mechanics, understanding where to go with the ball, sense of urgency in terms of working through his progressions, protections. There were so many… pic.twitter.com/OhwAUkfupV
Sanders may not have this starting spot for longer than a single weekend, which is why leaving everything out on the gridiron is so important.
But who knows, if he goes out there and dominates , maybe the Browns will give him another opportunity to show what he has in the tank.
The Browns and Saints will collide at 1:00 p.m. EST on Sunday, Nov. 8.

title: Todd Monken Makes His Call: What's Ahead for Browns Second-Year QB Shedeur Sanders?
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have a new starting quarterback for the Week 9 matchup against the New Orleans Saints.
Deshaun Watson returned on a limited basis for the final practice ahead of the Saints matchup, but remained in concussion protocol.
#Browns QB Deshaun Watson (concussion protocol) returned to practice today. pic.twitter.com/LHaXZFaXl3
Despite this, Browns head coach Todd Monken announced that Shedeur Sanders would be the starter against the Saints. Monken even went as far as to say, "I'm fired up to see him play. I mean, who wouldn't be?" The question now is whether Sanders will rise to the occasion.
Sanders showed confidence early in the week ahead of the matchup with the Saints. Speaking during the media slot typically reserved for starting quarterback Deshaun Watson, he was asked what he saw on film from the Saints' defense. The Browns' new starter said, “Yeah, I’ve seen a lot. When I smile, just know that means something. I’m maturing. I’m maturing.”
#Browns QB Shedeur Sanders on the Saints defense: "Yeah, I've seen a lot. When I smile, just know that means something. (laughs) I'm maturing, you know what I'm saying? I'm maturing. Like, I could have gave that a decent answer, but now I'm just going to smile." pic.twitter.com/z9yKqtluRH
Some took it as confidence; others saw it as a way to give the media a non-answer and move on. After all, it isn’t like the starting quarterback is going to give away the team's game plan to the media. Regardless, Sanders has always been confident in himself, and with a full week of practice under his belt as the starter, he now has a chance to turn that confidence into results on Sunday.
Shedeur Sanders will be making his first start of the season against the Saints. Sanders started seven games for the Browns last season, passing for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns, and 10 interceptions.
Sanders’ record as the starter for the Browns was 3-4, and while he showed flashes of what made many think of him as a first-round talent, it was clear the young QB needed more development.
After an offseason of development , a preseason quarterback competition, and eight games spent learning behind Watson , Sanders now has a chance to show his progress. Monken said during OTAs on June 3, ‘I just tell you, we got two starting-level quarterbacks. We really do.” Sunday will test that assessment.
some of Shedeur Sanders best throws vs. the Titans from the All-22 tape. #Browns The first ball to Fannin with a DE barreling down in his face is just silly... pic.twitter.com/zsZSNHxgbT
Will his performance be reminiscent of the 2025 matchup against the Titans, where he threw for 364 yards and three touchdowns? Or will Sanders fall back into bad habits and have an outing like the 2025 Bears matchup, where he threw three interceptions?
Only time will tell. But one thing is for sure: Shedeur is confident in his ability to perform in year two.
Noah Olson is a Northeast Ohio native and lifelong Cleveland sports fan. He graduated from The College of Wooster with a major in Communications and has been sports writing since 2024. As a writer for BIGPLAY On SI, Noah brings a blend of local pride and an insider’s perspective, focusing on thoughtful analysis and storytelling rooted in Cleveland sports culture.

title: Rumors Swirling About Browns Trade Deadline Plans: Are New Additions on the Horizon?
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns haven't been rumored to do too much at the upcoming 2026 NFL Trade Deadline.
But reports from Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer show the front office could at least explore the market.
On Friday, Nov. 6, Breer released an updated look at the league at large, exploring different agendas teams will be heading into the deadline with. For the Browns, they are reportedly expected to look around for an additional rotational edge rusher and a blocking tight end.
"The Browns are actually positioned now as buyers , which is pretty fascinating," Breer wrote. "Cleveland has looked around at adding a rotational edge rusher and perhaps a blocking tight end, which would free them up to move Harold Fannin Jr. around even more."
Trade deadline updates, per @AlbertBreer : • Giants, Jaguars, Vikings looking for help at DT • Texans checked in on available RBs and safeties • Browns looked at adding rotational edge rusher and perhaps a blocking TE • Steelers monitoring WR market and could deal LB Cole…
While Breer didn't list any players specifically, there are a few notable names the front office could be taking a look at.
If the Browns are looking to add another body opposite or behind Jared Verse, there are a few options the front office could consider.
Just a week ago, the Tennessee Titans made a major trade, sending away defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons to the Chicago Bears. In return, they landed a handful of valuable picks to re-up the squad in the coming NFL Draft.
But they may not be done making trades just yet.
. @JFowlerESPN lists the Browns as a fit to trade for: - EDGE Khalil Mack - EDGE Jermaine Johnson - EDGE YaYa Diaby pic.twitter.com/Eau26cu7Ew
Rumors have swirled that the Titans could consider sending 27-year-old Jermaine Johnson on his way. Sitting on a $13 million deal, the interest around the league will be high for an edge rusher like him who is in the heart of his prime.
Over the last two years, he has totaled six sacks and consistently ranked in the top half of PFF ratings at his position.
If the Browns can move around the cap space needed to land him, they have the draft capital to bolster the line even more.
Outside of Johnson, the New York Giants' Kayvon Thibodeaux has been rumored to be on the trade block , alongside Los Angeles Chargers veteran Kahlil Mack. Both would likely be one-year rentals, but could end up securing an extension by the end of the season.
Even if the team goes a different route, adding a lesser-known name to bolster the depth, such a move would be smart given how lackluster Verse's play has been this season.
There really aren't a lot of tight ends that have ended up in trade conversations this season.
But that doesn't mean the Browns are flying in the dark.
A lot of the NFL's best teams are not going to part ways with their blocking tight ends, most notably the San Francisco 49ers, who have George Kittle, and even the Minnesota Vikings, who have Josh Oliver.
However, one addition that could make sense, while also being realistic, is John Bates from the Washington Commanders. With the Commanders performing so poorly this season, sitting at a record of 2-4-1 and third in the NFC East, moving on from Bates could land them important draft capital as they look to retool this offseason.
The 29-year-old isn't a headline-grabbing tight end, but he does provide unmatched consistency. Across the last six seasons, he has hauled in 77 passes for 722 yards and three touchdowns , all while being a top blocker in both the rushing attack and pass protection.
In his 2021 rookie season, he earned the highest PFF run-blocking grade ever recorded by a first-year tight end, before finishing first in run-blocking that season.
Currently signed to a three-year deal, the Browns would be able to keep Bates around for a good amount of time, making him less of an immediate fix but a long-term solution to the tight end room.
Such a trade would also create more opportunities for Harold Fannin Jr. and give him that receiving-first role full-time.
The Browns are certainly going to take a look at the trade block with the deadline approaching, especially if they can take down the New Orleans Saints this coming weekend and maintain a top spot in the division.
The only question is if the front office will be willing to pull the trigger on any deals.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Cleveland Native and Former NFL Player Calls Out Jared Verse's Recent Comments
full_text:
When Jared Verse joined the Cleveland Browns this past offseason, he quickly emerged as a leader both on the field and off.
He was seen numerous times helping the younger members of the team, including recently drafted offensive tackle Spencer Fano, while also maintaining a consistent presence in the media spotlight as he hyped up the Browns' potential for the 2026 season.
But as the year has ticked along, Verse has put himself in some uncomfortable situations.
That mouth that led to him being beloved his first few months now has him in hot water, especially following a loss to the rival Pittsburgh Steelers this past weekend , 27-6. All week leading up to the game, Verse bantered with the Steelers' Cam Heyward and called out numerous aspects of their game.
Obviously, as the scoreline shows, he wasn't able to back it up.
Cleveland native and former NFL offensive lineman LeCharles Bentley recently spoke out and criticized how loud Verse has been off the field and how quiet he has been on the field.
"I had a friend growing up… he always wanted to start fights with folks… it was cool for a while, until I realized, he just talked too much," a post on X from Bentley wrote. We stopped being friends when he got beat up for talking and I didn’t help. But he learned a lesson… stop talkin."
I had a friend growing up… he always wanted to start fights with folks… it was cool for a while, until I realized, he just talked too much. We stopped being friends when he got beat up for talking and I didn’t help. But he learned a lesson… stop talkin. #LessonLearned https://t.co/P1OTOtPI8S
Verse has seemingly been all bark, no bite, to begin the season, as through eight games he has a whopping 18 combined tackles, 10 solo, and four tackles for a loss . He has yet to record a sack, but has gotten into the backfield to at least produce six quarterback hits.
Either way, that productivity off the edge ranks him towards the bottom of the league in multiple areas.
To add insult to injury, Verse tried to blame the situations the defense has been put in for his inability to affect the game.
“I think attention has been focused on me not doing enough on this aspect, that aspect, I don’t think we’ve been getting enough 3rd and longs to put myself in the position to get the stats,” Verse said recently.
“I think attention has been focused on me not doing enough on this aspect, that aspect, I don’t think think we’ve been getting enough 3rd and longs to put myself in the position to get the stats,” Jared Verse on his lack of production this season. pic.twitter.com/0T8eD5RAOb
Bentley's comments echo the sentiment that a lot of people around the league seem to be feeling right now about Verse. For how vocal he has been, he just simply hasn't backed up the talk with productivity on the gridiron.
There is still plenty of season left to play, giving the freshly 26-year-old time to rebound and prove the doubters wrong, but he may want to lay low and pull himself out of the spotlight.
The Browns return to the field on Sunday, Nov. 8, for a road matchup with the New Orleans Saints . The two sides will go toe-to-toe at 1:00 p.m. EST from Caesars Superdome.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: What Shedeur Sanders Needs to do to Win First 2026 Start
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are preparing to head into their Week 9 matchup without their starting quarterback, Deshaun Watson .
The good news for Cleveland is that Shedeur Sanders is the backup. Don't forget Sanders and Watson battled it out in training camp, with many fans believing Shedeur should have been selected as the guy.
Now that he will be starting on the road against the New Orleans Saints , here are some things Sanders needs to do to get a win in his first start of 2026.
Currently, the Browns have allowed the most sacks in the entire NFL this season, with 33.
While a lot of fault goes to the offensive line, a handful of sacks and really lots of plays that didn't work successfully come from Deshaun Watson holding onto the football for far too long.
Especially with Sanders, if he sits in the pocket too long, he will most likely turn the ball over. Last season, we saw this on display as he finished his rookie season with 10 interceptions thrown.
If Shedeur can find targets quickly, Cleveland has some great playmakers that can take the majority of the workload. That leads me into my next key to starting Sanders
KC Concepcion is already one of the SHIFTIEST slot WR’s in the entire NFL. Through 7 GP, Concepcion has recorded 30 receptions and 383 total yards. The Browns rookie WR is IMPOSSIBLE to stop in open space 😳🕹️ https://t.co/AzawKHVuhW pic.twitter.com/d1OnKCQkgE
While Sanders does have some nice athletic talent and playmaking ability, it is still pretty raw as the quarterback is only in his second season.
With that being said, head coach Todd Monken needs to treat this start for Sanders like the week two matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
In that game, Deshaun Watson was able to bounce back from a really poor week one performance in Jacksonville. Not only did he look great, he built confidence that carried into the next games that followed.
For Monken and Sanders, they must take the same approach. Keep the game plan simple, and when Sanders needs to pass have him get the ball out quickly to the numorous young playmkaers this team has to offer.
Finally, the Browns were able to get their run game going against the Tennessee Titans. However, Pittsburgh did a great job once again at stopping Cleveland from gaining yards on the ground.
Looking at the Saints, in over 200 rushing attempts from opponents, they have allowed about 4.8 yards per carry.
This is great news for Cleveland. If Quinshon Judkins can move the ball down the field and capitalize on red zone drives, maybe the Browns can take a page out of the Buccaneers' playbook and not have to rely on the quarterback as much.
While it will be nice to see how much improvement Shedeur Sanders has made since last season, this game is a must win for the Browns.
Last season, there wasn't much on the line when Sanders stepped in. Now, Cleveland not only has a chance for their first playoff appearance since 2023, but their first AFC North title ever.

title: Sunday's Outcome Will Be Determined By One Thing The Browns And Saints Have In Common
full_text:
A movable object will meet a stopping force in New Orleans as the Cleveland Browns head south to take on the Saints. The Browns are coming off a thrashing by the Pittsburgh Steelers, and the Saints will be rested after their bye week.
They need to keep pace in a very competitive AFC North as they sit in third place with a 5-3 record.
The Browns are finishing a three-game road trip, in which they are 1-1. In their win, they were able to run the ball, and it was their best rushing game of the season. The contrary happened in their loss, as the ground game was nonexistent. The rushing offense has been lackluster all season; however, the Saints’ biggest issue is stopping the run.
The Saints are 29th in the league in stopping the run, giving up an average of 139.4 yards per game. However, the Browns are 24th, averaging 92.6 rushing yards per game. Quinshon Judkins has only 342 yards so far this season , and Deshaun Watson’s 217 yards help the offense’s rushing average.
Running the ball will be imperative to a Browns’ victory, as it is likely that Shedeur Sanders will start , as Deshaun Watson is in concussion protocol. Sanders can be successful if the offense can run, as it will allow fewer defenders in the secondary to mix up coverages and try to confuse the second-year quarterback. The Browns could also be missing Watson’s rushing ability to extend plays and get first downs.
#Browns Deshaun Watson (concussion) didn’t practice again today on Thursday of #Saints week. Shedeur Sanders very likely to start.
If Watson does start, then the Browns have to be able to run the ball to get it out of his hands. He took eight sacks last week and had more hits on top of that. He could use a game where he is on his feet more than his back, with the bye week looming.
On the other hand, the Browns have played five road games so far this season and have struggled to stop the run. They have given up over 100 rushing yards in each road game, averaging 147 yards per game. They just allowed the Steelers to rush for 200 yards, and the defense has looked tired.
Mason Graham, Michael Hall Jr., Carson Schwesinger, and Quincy Williams are banged up, and the defense relies on them to stop the run. Their defense is 24th in the NFL against the run. The line needs to be better disciplined and maintain containment of the line of scrimmage.
It is not all doom and gloom for the Browns' defense trying to stop the run. The Saints rank 28th in running the ball, averaging 86 yards per game. Their leading rusher is Kendre Miller with 159 yards. Travis Etienne has been out with an injury, but he may be available to return after their bye week . Alvin Kamara has shown his age this season by only amassing 125 yards.
If the trends continue and both offenses cannot run the ball, then the game will be in the Saints’ favor. They are 14th in passing with 229 yards per game, which is eight spots better than the Browns. If Sanders plays, then it will be his first start of the season. His best ability is throwing an accurate deep pass, but if they cannot run the ball, then the Saints' secondary will be ready.
Sunday’s game in the Superdome presents an interesting storyline, as both teams have a hard time running the ball and stopping the run. Something will have to give, and the Browns need to figure out a way to end the road trip with a win by controlling the run game on both sides of the ball.

title: 2 Browns Players Who Could Be on the Trade Block Before the NFL Deadline
full_text:
With the trade deadline quickly approaching on November 10th, we have already seen some massive trades around the league like Jefferey Simmons going to Chicago and Quenton Nelson shipped to Seattle.
In Cleveland, the Browns are in a tough spot of whether the team is buyers or sellers at the deadline as they sit at 5-3 and right outside of a playoff spot in the AFC. The idea of trading for a talented quarterback, who might command at minimum two first-round picks , has come into conversation along with trading for offensive line help.
There are some players however, who are also in the conversation of discarding before the deadline.
Anyone heard this one before? But seriously, Jeudy is the most expendable player on the Browns right now, and it’s not completely his fault. Except it mostly is; his inconsistency last season on a team that lacked offensive weapons was a huge signal for Browns GM Andrew Berry to go out and get young receiver talent immediately.
And that receiver talent has been on full display through eight games this season; both Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion have doubled Jeudy’s output of just 171 yards this season. Jeudy is still under contract next season for a cap hit of a little over $13 million; Cleveland would love to pawn that off to another franchise, but will definitely have to pitch in a draft pick for a team to take that on.
Harden continues to be the Browns starting slot corner despite below-average play, and that has been prevalent this season. Quarterbacks have a passer rating of 108.7 when targeting Harden, for reference, that’s higher than the passer rating of Caleb Williams, Josh Allen, and Drake Maye this year.
Playing slot is a very tough position to play with all of the great slot receivers in the game right now like Jaxon Smith-Njiba, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Puka Nacua, and Cedee Lamb. The problem is that Cleveland hasn’t played any of those guys this season, and while players like Zay Flowers and Parker Washington are close to that level, they weren’t exactly locked down against the Browns.
The good thing about Harden is that he’s cheap, he’s making just over a million dollars this season and next. You can’t rationalize keeping him as a starter just because he doesn’t cost a lot of money when he has allowed the 8th-most receiving yards by a defensive back this season, though.
Hi, I’m Paul, I’m from Northeast Ohio, and a recent graduate of Kent State University. As an Ohio native, I’m a huge fan of the Browns, Guardians, and Cavaliers. Just don’t ask me about my favorite college team, though.

title: Why Shedeur Sanders' Expected Start Comes at the Perfect Time
full_text:
Two years ago, Shedeur Sanders expanded his skill set beyond the football field and released a song called “Perfect Timing.”
Now, as Deshaun Watson is in concussion protocol, the second-year quarterback is gearing up to make his first start of the 2026 season, and the timing couldn’t be more in his – and in the Browns’ – favor.
Here’s three reasons why Sanders getting the Week 9 nod comes at a pretty much the perfect time :
During his media availability on Wednesday afternoon , Sanders was asked what he’s seen from the Saints' defense.
“Um, yeah, I've seen a lot," he answered. "When I smile, just know that means… something. I'm maturing, you know what I'm saying? I'm maturing.”
It seems Sanders doesn’t see Saints' defensive coordinator, Brandon Staley’s, unit as much of a threat.
And, the numbers don’t disagree with the quarterback’s (lack of) thoughts.
The Saints’ total defense ranks 28th overall in the league, giving up 372.7 yards per game and allowing 22 touchdowns so far this year. Its passing defense ranks 23rd overall, allowing 233.3 yards per game, and it doesn’t bring a lot of pressure up front.
New Orleans has also been pretty easy to score on this season. According to Pro Football Reference, 46.8% of the Saints’ defensive drives have ended in an offensive score, the second-highest among all 32 teams.
While the Saints aren’t the worst defense in the league, they’re far from the best – something that could make Sanders’ job a little easier on Sunday.
While it’s been reported that the Browns have no interest in trading Sanders by the November 10 deadline, it’s no secret there’s a lot of uncertainty in the future of Cleveland’s quarterback room.
When Watson was named the starter this offseason, it sent a clear message: Sanders is not the answer to the Browns’ struggles. At least not yet.
While Watson is doing just enough to keep the Browns a competitive team, he isn’t a top quarterback. During his time in Cleveland, he has yet to prove he’s the long-term solution. So who is?
Sanders has yet to prove it, either, despite flashes of his abilities when he took over under center last season.
Todd Monken, though, is excited to see what his young quarterback does with this week’s opportunity.
“He’s done his work,” Monken said. “All he’s done is be diligent and ask great questions. In every meeting, he’s dialed in.”
When it comes to the trade deadline, the Browns have some decisions to make.
This weekend could help solidify Sanders’ spot in the quarterback room, especially with Dillon Gabriel no longer on injured reserve.
After beating Pittsburgh in primetime the first time around, the Steelers got revenge on their home field to claim the top spot in the AFC North.
It was a tough outing for Watson, who was sacked eight times. He’s the most-sacked quarterback in the league so far this year.
The Browns need a morale boost, and it potentially coming from a different quarterback could be beneficial.
Cleveland has a stretch of winnable games ahead. After the Saints, the team hosts the 2-5 Texans, then the 4-4 Raiders after a bye week.
If Sanders wants to prove himself to his team and to Cleveland fans, starting with a win against New Orleans might just be the way to do that. Getting the Browns back on track after losing to their rival is the perfect opportunity to show he still has something to offer to the team that drafted him.
A Northeast Ohio native, Rachel grew up following all things Cleveland sports. She has experience in broadcast and digital media and graduated from West Virginia University with a degree in sports media.

title: Browns Have 4 Young Players Who Deserve More Playing Time as Season Hits Halfway Point
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns season hits the half way point and they sit as the eighth seed in the AFC at 5-3. They only play three more games against teams over .500 and have a chance to make a push for the playoffs. The team has arrived sooner than anyone thought because their roster is filled with rookies and second-year players.
Almost 30 percent of the game-day roster is composed of players from the last two draft classes. Eight such players are starters that have heavily contributed to winning. Carson Schwesinger was Defensive Rookie of the Year last season and KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston are competing for Offensive Rookie of the Year this season.
The young players have stepped up on both sides of the ball, but these non-starters need to get more playing time in the second half of the season to make the playoffs.
Sampson started the season as the backup running back to Quinshon Judkins, but got hurt in the first game. He returned in Week 7 against the Tennessee Titans and showed off his speed by averaging 7.5 yards per rush and 10.7 yards per reception in the win. Sampson only got one carry for seven yards in last week’s blow-out loss against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
The offense has struggled to run the ball all season and Sampson should be given more opportunities to find a spark. He can run on the outside and catch screen passes to keep the defense on its toes. The offense is night and day when he touches the ball.
The second-year receiver only has five catches this season for 86 yards. He got most of his playing time at the beginning of the season when Jerry Jeudy struggled and KC Concepcion left a game with a concussion. Jeudy improved and Concepcion did not miss any other time, so Bond got pushed to the sideline.
The speedster can take the top off of the defense and open up the middle of the field for Concepcion and Boston. He had a couple of bad drops in their loss against the New York Jets, but the weather conditions made things difficult. If Shedeur Sanders starts for the Browns , then Bond should get more playing time as they had chemistry last season and Sanders throws a better deep ball than Watson.
Huntington has gotten plenty of playing time and has played really well by stacking up 3.5 sacks. He anchored the middle of the defensive line when Mason Graham and Michael Hall Jr. were out with injury. Both players returned to the lineup and Huntington’s snaps will decrease.
Both Graham and Hall Jr. still look like they are playing injured and Huntington should start over Hall Jr. He has been providing pressure over the center and has gotten in the backfield to help stop the run. The defensive line needs him to help them slow down the rushing attack, which they have struggled to do this season.
The strong safety out of the University of Toledo was considered a “steal” in the second round of the NFL draft. His playing time has steadily been increasing and he has shown why. McNeil-Warren has laid some big hits on running backs and helped them stop the Titans at the goal line. He is behind Grand Delpit on the depth chart.
Ronnie Hickman has started at free safety and there have been a couple of communication breakdowns in the secondary. McNeil-Warren’s college film suggests he can play in the middle of the field and read the offense. He should get more opportunities to be a ball hawk in the secondary.
The young players are contributing up and down the roster and if the Browns wish to play their way into the playoffs, then these four players should be utilized more in the second half.

title: NFL Insider Identifies Dallas Cowboys' Most Logical NFL Trade Deadline Approach
full_text:
We are just days away from finding out if the Dallas Cowboys are going to add to their defense ahead of the trade deadline.
As we sit here on Saturday, the deadline is rapidly approaching on Tuesday, Nov. 10. The Cowboys certainly need help on defense , but Jerry Jones also has to weigh if its worth it to make a trade given how hopeless Dallas' unit looks this season.
When it comes to what the Cowboys might do at the deadline , The Athletic's Jonathan Jones believes a player-for-player swap is the only kind of trade that makes sense for Dallas.
"The only sort of trade that makes sense for Dallas would be a player-for-player deal involving someone on defense," he said.
The Cowboys have depleted their draft pick stockpile in recent years with some big trades, including the ones for Rashan Gary, Quinnen Williams and Joey Porter Jr., among others.
As a result of those deals, the Cowboys have just four picks in next year's draft, including one in the first, second, fourth and seventh rounds.
Then, in 2028, the Cowboys don't have their second- and seventh-round picks, although they do have two in the sixth.
Outside of being able to make a huge blockbuster trade that will add a premier edge rusher, which is the only kind of move that has any hope of saving Dallas' awful defense, it just does not make much sense to sacrifice more draft capital.
As we said, the Cowboys need a massive upgrade at edge rusher to even have a chance to turn their defense around.
Getting that kind of player is difficult in and of itself, but trying to land a top-notch edge rusher in a player-for-player trade will be impossible.
The only player who could come close to garnering that type of  return that the Cowboys could afford to trade is wide receiver George Pickens, and even then he probably won't be enough alone and draft capital would still be required.
We also know that the Cowboys are unlikely to have any interest in trading Pickens, even though it makes sense to do so given the fact he probably doesn't have a future in Dallas.
"As of right now there's nothing there (with a Pickens trade)," NFL Network's Ian Rapoport said on The Pat McAfee Show .
Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram is saying the same.
"“The fifth-year pass-catcher and second-year Cowboy is playing this season on the franchise tag after the team elected not to discuss a long-term contract with him in the offseason," said Harris.
"Despite trade rhetoric around the time of that decision being announced, the Cowboys never engaged in trying to send him away. Seven months later, that strategy remains the same ahead of the deadline, according to multiple sources."
We would not rule out Jerry saying "F them picks" even more and going out and making a significant trade, but it just doesn't seem like the most likely scenario at this point given everything we know.

title: Cowboys' Jonathan Mingo Trade Lands Among NFL's Worst Deadline Mistakes
full_text:
As the 2026 NFL trade deadline approaches , fans are anxiously awaiting the news that their favorite team made a huge move to improve their chances of making a postseason run. While some of the moves made at the deadline do allow a team to take a huge step forward, there are also plenty of trades that don't work out.
That was the case for the Dallas Cowboys in 2024 when they sent a fourth-round pick to the Carolina Panthers for wide receiver Jonathan Mingo and a seventh-round pick. At the time, Jerry Jones praised himself for the move, saying they had their eyes on Mingo in the draft the previous year, and he felt they landed someone who could develop into a potential starter opposite CeeDee Lamb.
That hasn't happened as Mingo has just nine receptions for 101 yards in 22 games for the Cowboys. His lack of production , as well as the fact that there were better options available, led Brent Sobleski of Bleacher Report to name the Mingo trade among the worst 10 deadline trades over the past decade .
"The amazing part of the Dallas Cowboys' acquisition of Jonathan Mingo is how little they've received in return even though he's still on the team. To make matters worse, the Kansas City Chiefs flipped a lower draft pick to acquire DeAndre Hopkins prior to the same trade deadline," Sobleski wrote.
It's shocking to realize that Mingo is still on the Cowboys' roster. As Sobleski stated, he hasn't been a "friendly" target for Dak Prescott. Mingo has caught just 31 percent of the passes thrown his way, and while he has had some great moments in the preseason and training camp, he hasn't found success on the field.
Dallas has tried multiple ways to get Mingo involved, even using him as a return man this season. With KaVontae Turpin banged up, Mingo has seen time as a punt returner as well as on kickoffs. He has 47 yards on seven punt returns and 69 yards on three kick returns.
Even with that usage, it's hard to justify his spot on the roster. It's even more difficult to defend the trade. And while hindsight is 20/20, this is a move that was ridiculed from the moment it was announced. Perhaps that's why Jerry Jones won't move on, since he may be desperate to prove his investment was worth it.

title: Jerry Jones Reaches New Level of Absurdity Defending Cowboys Coaching Salary Stance
full_text:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones is known for giving some of the wildest answers when asked about his franchise. One of the hottest topics as of late is his stance on coaching salaries .
Jones is facing criticism for hiring Brian Schottenheimer in 2025, a coach who was on no one's radar during the hiring cycle. The belief is that Jones wanted Schottenheimer since he wasn't an expensive coach, and Jones was being criticized for refusing to pay top dollar for a legitimate head coach.
In response, Jones went off the rails and went on a nonsensical rant about how there's no correlation between paying coaches and winning. It was a ridiculous, and factually inaccurate statement, but Jones might have made it even weirder somehow with his latest comments.
While appearing on 105.3 The Fan, Jones was asked about the criticism he's been facing for his refusal to pay coaches a top salary. Instead of addressing that, he decided to remind everyone just how rich he is.
“I drill wells. I have five wells going right now that cost more than any coach,” Jones said via Jon Machota of The Athletic.
It's really hard to think of a response to that. It's even more difficult to try and figure out how in the world Jones thought that was an adequete responese. Jones has been known to get defensive in the past, and that appears to be the case here. Instead of realizing that he is being asked why he doesn't believe coaching matters as much as every other franchise believes, Jones seemed to take this as an attack on his filthty richness.
What's even more ironic about his response is the fact that he made himself look even worse. Jones made sure to let the world know that money is no object for him, but that makes his refusal to pay for a championship-caliber coach even worse.
There is no salary cap when it comes to coaching staffs, meaning that Jones could decide to pay a coach whatever he wanted. By reminding the world that he makes billions outside of football, he's also proving his critics right. Jones has the means to pay any salary and it wouldn't make a dent in his pocketbook. Instead, he continues to pay his players while going cheap on the coaching staff.
Perhaps it's because he's still sour over Jimmy Johnson getting more credit than him in the 1990s or if he devalues coaches, which is what Colin Cowherd recently accused him of . Either way, Jones continues to be his own worst enemy as he pursues his first title run in over 30 years and his latest defense proves that he still doesn't understand how much of a problem he truly is.

title: Steelers Trade Rumor Gives Cowboys Potential Target for Addition on Defense
full_text:
If the Dallas Cowboys are looking to make an addition at the linebacker spot before the NFL trade deadline hits on Nov. 10, they might want to give the Pittsburgh Steelers a call.
According to Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer , the Steelers could sell at least one player at the deadline next week.
And that player, Breer says, is linebacker Cole Holcomb.
"Then there’s the Steelers, who, again, are sniffing around at receiver, and could deal veteran LB Cole Holcomb," he said.
Of course, the Cowboys and Steelers are no strangers to making trades with one another, as Dallas has acquired George Pickens , Broderick Jones and Joey Porter Jr. from Pittsburgh since 2025.
The Steelers don't profile as sellers with a 6-2 record, but based on what Breer is saying, it appears they could at least move Holcomb.
The veteran has no role on defense, as evidenced by his playing on just 4.3% of snaps this season, which could make him expendable for the right price.
On paper, the Cowboys are in good shape at the linebacker spot with DeMarvion Overshown, Dee Winters, Jaishawn Barham and Shemar James.
However, Overshown is once again proving to be unreliable after having injury issues this season. He has already missed a handful of games in 2026, and now he's back on the injury report in Week 9 with a hamstring issue.
As a result, the Cowboys might consider making a small move at linebacker, and trading for Holcomb would qualify as that kind of move.
Linebacker certainly isn't the Cowboys' biggest need, so they are not going to want to spend much if they do decide to add there, and that's especially true with Dallas not having many draft selections over the next few years.
Holcomb would be cheap and can likely be had for a late Day 3 pick, which wouldn't put much of a dent in Dallas' dwindling stockpile of picks .
Not only would Holcomb provide depth on defense, he can also make a big impact on special teams, where he thrives the most.
While that's all well and good, we'd like it's more likely Dallas won't be making a move at linebacker and will instead focus all of their attention on their biggest need, which is edge rusher.
Truth be told, the Cowboys should probably stand pat all together, as chances are there isn't a player out there who can save them.

title: Stephen A. Smith Slams Dak Prescott, Dallas Cowboys for Culture Issue
full_text:
Stephen A. Smith is calling out quarterback Dak Prescott and the Dallas Cowboys for a culture problem.
During the latest episode of "First Take" on ESPN on Friday, Smith went in on Prescott and the Cowboys for being too "comfortable," which he says makes them more OK with losing than the team should be.
More specifically with Prescott, Smith wants to see the Cowboys quarterback do a better job holding teammates accountable publicly.
"I just want to say this about Dak Prescott," Smith said. "Here's what really, realy bothers me about him: he's a damn great player, he can ball, he's not a scrub, but the priority is always in saying the right things and coming across polished. Sometimes I'd like to see him ticked off. Sometimes I'd like to see him annoyed at his damn teammates. Sometimes I'd like to see this cat that's getting paid $60 million a year, that's gotten $337 million over the last seven years, that has one playoff win to show for it in that span, come across as a little pissed off."
"They living the life in Dallas. That's why they're trash. Because they're so damn comfortable that losing doesn't hurt enough," Stephen A. added.
"I wanna see him ticked. I wanna see him calling out teammates. I wanna see him doing whatever it takes to ruffle feather and to get cats uncomfortable with mediocrity. I don't see that with Dak Prescott.
Of course, it's hard to know just how much Prescott holds players accountable behind the scenes, but we know he takes the diplomatic approach publicly.
For a team struggling as badly as the Cowboys are, it certainly wouldn't hurt to see team leaders getting more fired up about Dallas' situation, and Prescott is included in that.
Smith isn't the only one who has questioned the Cowboys' culture.
First, former Cowboys quarterback Ben DiNucci called Dallas' offense out for a lack of effort.
"You can’t turn on the Cowboys tape from last night and tell me guys on that offense are giving 100%," DiNucci said . "Lazy, no attention to details, no creativity with play calls."
Then, Cowboys legend DeMarcus Ware called the Cowboys' defense out for its effort.
“When I played and there were problems, the first thing we did was how do we control the trenches?" Ware said . "That’s something that’s free. It’s the effort and attitude of the team. That’s something that can be changed, that’s not a quantitative thing. It’s a heart thing, a pride thing, an ego thing these guys have to sort of turn up. Yes, a lot of people are saying their season is over, but in the locker room there has to be a mentality shift to say we still got it.”
Culture issues are certainly on the players, but the biggest culprits are the coaches because everything starts with them.
Defensive coordinator Christian Parker gets a finger pointed at him, but head coach Brian Schottenheimer deserves the most blame, and that's yet another stain on his wildly unsuccessful tenure as the Cowboys' head coach.
Before even addressing these culture issues, the Cowboys have a lot of problems to fix. But when you include the culture problems, also, that makes it even less likely Dallas will right the ship.

title: Dallas Cowboys' NFL Trade Deadline Plans Become Clearer After Jerry Jones Comments
full_text:
You never know what Dallas Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones is going to do. In recent years, we have watched him play several contract situations with high-profile players slowly , while also making big trades to bring in strong reinforcements like Quinnen Williams, George Pickens, and Joey Porter Jr.
So, as the NFL trade deadline approaches this season with the team in a major funk, there is no telling what direction the Cowboys could go. That leaves everyone asking: will Jerry Jones be a buyer or seller when Tuesday evening's deadline rolls around?
Because the Cowboys have lost three of their last four games, it appears that the team could either be dormant or look to trade away a major player like George Pickens , but neither of those appears to be in the cards.
Instead, Jones reignited speculation that the Cowboys could look to make another trade deadline splash in a few days, regardless of the result of Week 9's game against the Indianapolis Colts .
During his appearance on 105.3 The Fan, Jones revealed it is more likely that the Cowboys are " much more likely to add than subtract at the deadline ."
How much more likely the team is to add remains to be seen, but it also leaves the door open for Dallas to stay put and suffer through the second half of the season if they fall to the Colts on Sunday afternoon.
Even with a win, the Cowboys are a long shot to make a deep run in the postseason, but there is a sliver of hope thanks to the wide-open nature of the NFC East. Even though the Cowboys have been horrendous, they are still within striking distance of the New York Giants and sit just 1.5-games back of the division lead.
If the Cowboys win on Sunday and get a positive result in the Eagles-Giants game, Dallas and New York are neck-and-neck for the division, which should and could give Jones the motivation to add talent to the defense before the clock strikes 4:00 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November.
You just have to wonder how big of a piece the Cowboys could add that would make a difference, and how much it would cost for a team that is already depleted much of its draft arsenal. We will get our answer in a couple of days.

title: Latest Jerry Jones Word Salad on Paying Coaches Shows Cowboys Winning Isn't Top Priority
full_text:
Every time Jerry Jones speaks, he puts his foot in his mouth. That was the case again on Friday during an appearance on 105.3 The Fan. Jones was attempting to clarify previous comments he made about paying up for a top-tier head coach .
Jones said there was "no correlation" between highly paid coaches and NFL success , which was proven false, and now he's taking a different route.
Instead of owning up to the fact that looking for a bargain on the sideline to lead your team isn't going to pay off, Jones is simply saying he could pay for a coach if he really wanted to, because he isn't afraid to pay up for his oil wells.
Seriously, that's the direction Jones thought he should take his comments as Cowboys Nation is ailing and in desperate search of any optimism or hope.
“I drill wells," Jones said in an effort to ease Cowboys Nation's pain. "I have five wells going right now that cost more than any coach .”
Well, that's great Jerry, but did you just openly admit that you care more about drilling wells than the Cowboys' success? Because that is what it seems like and that's the interpretation fans are having.
" Wells don't win you a championship Jerr ," one fan wrote on X. Another added, "So you can do it but you choose not to because you’re stupid . Got it."
To make matters worse, he once again doubled down on the idea that he could pay a coach if he really wanted to. "Not one time in my life, if I wanted to do it, I let money stand in the way of doing it . That’s stood true since the day I walked into the Dallas Cowboys."
Someone take his microphone away. If you don't want to win, fine, but hire a general manager who wants to. Fans have been waiting for 30 years for the Cowboys to win another Super Bowl, but as long as Jerry Jones is in charge, it's becoming clearer that the team will have no shot.
And, to make matters worse, he doesn't even seem to care. So spare us the "all in" comments each and every offseason, and go out and hire a real general manager if you want to. Otherwise, fans will completely stop supporting the team.

title: Joe Milton Has Opportunity to Help Cowboys Despite Playing for Eagles
full_text:
Former Dallas Cowboys quarterback Joe Milton is now playing for the enemy, the Philadelphia Eagles, but he can still help out his former team this week.
Milton was signed by the Eagles off the Cowboys' practice squad last month amid the team having an injury concern with starter Jalen Hurts, who is now out for the rest of the season.
The Tennessee product started out as the team's backup to Tanner McKee, but that has now changed and it will be Milton starting for the Eagles in Week 9 , the team announced.
A former sixth-round pick in 2024, Milton has never started a regular season game in his young career, so this is a massive opportunity for him.
Not only is Milton making his first start, he's doing so against the New York Giants, the Eagles' Week 9 opponent.
The Giants are sitting in first place in the NFC East with a 4-2-1 record and the Cowboys arebehind them in second place at 3-5.
Dallas lost ground on the Giants last week after their abysmal loss to the Arizona Cardinals while New York was on a bye. Making the gap between New York and Dallas even bigger is the fact that the Cowboys lost to the Giants back in Week 1.
So, the Cowboys are going to be rooting for their ex- teammate, and not just because they want to see him do well. Milton can help the Cowboys gain ground on the Giants if he can lead the Eagles to a win and Dallas can take care of business against the lowly Indianapolis Colts, a team the Cowboys should beat.
That said, the Eagles are about as lowly as the Colts are right now, and they are banged-up.
Wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks haven't practiced over the first two days of this week and that puts the duo on track to sit out. If they don't play, Milton's job becomes much more difficult.
Along with tight end Dallas Goedert, Milton would be forced to rely on lackluster wideouts like Hollywood Brown, Darius Cooper and rookie Makai Lemon, which doesn't inspire much confidence for his chances of beating the Giants.
The Cowboys also have to hold up their end of the bargain and we know they are anything but certain to do that after already losing games to teams they were expected to beat, like the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Cardinals, for example.
We expect the Cowboys to beat the Colts this week, but we cannot say the same for the Eagles with the Giants.
