title: George Pickens Injury Update Is Optimistic For Final Game Before NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys will be wrapping up preparations for Week 9 against the Indianapolis Colts on Friday, and they are hoping for good news related to some of their top stars who have been limited in practice all week.
Among those players is star wide receiver George Pickens, who has been battling a sore hamstring. He has received the limited designation all week , but head coach Brian Schottenheimer showed some optimism on Friday morning during an appearance on 105.3 The Fan .
According to Schottenheimer, the team is "hopeful" that Pickens will be able to play on Sunday against the Colts, but he is expected to be a little bit limited once again. Pickens has been battling injuries all season, according to Schottenheimer, which is part of why there has been a drop- off in production.
Pickens taking the field comes at a crucial time, with the NFL trade deadline just days away . If the team decides to change course and trade away Pickens, a big game would help the team land a larger return when the deadline rolls around on Tuesday evening.
Along with the hamstring issue that popped up this week, Pickens has also been dealing with a shoulder issue throughout the year . This comes at a time when PIckens' involvement in the Cowboys offense has been questioned.
Schottenheimer, however, has remained adamant that the team is dedicated to making Pickens a part of the future, but his injuries have forced him off the field in some key situations. Because of the shoulder injury, Pickens becomes more of a liability in the run game because of his inability to block as effectively.
"Brian Schottenheimer told me that George Pickens snaps have been limited by his injuries," Clarence Hill of DLLS Cowboys said. "He has been taken off the field because blocking in the run game."
Pickens has some support from his teammates, including star quarterback Dak Prescott , so it doesn't appear to be a locker room issue like some would like to expect.
This season, Pickens has hauled in 39 catches for 533 yards and two touchdowns. He has not cracked the top 15 in the league in any of the main receiving categories, after ranking near the top in every one a year ago.

title: Why Broncos Could Target Eagles OG Landon Dickerson in Trade
full_text:
Jonathan Taylor is the biggest name the Denver Broncos realistically could target on the trade market ahead of Tuesday's NFL deadline.
But he might not be the only one.
ESPN recently named Philadelphia Eagles offensive guard Landon Dickerson as the player the Broncos should pursue , "rolling the dice" on a three-time former Pro Bowler who's already missed five games this season -- but also a veteran who'd arguably upgrade the starting lineup.
"One of the reasons quarterback Bo Nix had early career success was that he played behind one of the best offensive lines," national NFL analyst Seth Walder wrote on Nov. 4. "This season, that hasn't been the case with the Broncos ranking 20th in pass block win rate. Dickerson is not a guarantee after his performance fell off last season and a knee injury cost him a slew of games this season. But he doesn't have guaranteed money after 2026. The Broncos can be the team that rolls the dice on him returning to form."
The 37th overall pick of the 2021 draft, Dickerson has started 80 career games (predominatly at left guard) for the Eagles, winning a Super Bowl and along the way establishing himself among the sport's premier multi-faceted linemen. In college, the Alabama alum was named the nation's best center and a unanimous All-American, as well as taking home a slew of other blocking awards.
That ability carried over -- and blossomed -- in the pros. While he's suffered through an injury-ruined 2026 campaign, Dickerson graded out as the 27th- and 8th-best qualified guard in the league, respectively, across his last two seasons with the Eagles, according to Pro Football Focus' rankings.
For context, starting Broncos left guard Ben Powers, whose spot presumably would be given to Dickerson, finished 33rd and 38th over that same period, per PFF. Powers currently ranks 51st among  75 qualifiers.
That also, presumably, is why ESPN suggested Dickerson rather than Taylor or another offensive or defensive talent. Another positive is that Dickerson doesn't turn 29 years old until next September, and his position typically has a better long-term shelflife.
Although his best spot is guard, Dickerson is fully capable of holding his own at center, which would also provide some experienced depth behind incumbent starting pivot Luke Wattenberg.
While there's much to like about the prospect of adding Dickerson, any smoke that's billowed from Broncos Park has signaled an offensive acquisiton -- be it a running back, wide receiver, or tight end. There haven't been indications that they're looking to make a splash along the front-five, however.
The front office could sell it easier if Powers were injured or playing at an unprecendently poor level. Neither is the case as of this writing. He certainly isn't performing like an All-Pro -- there's an argument he's the weakest OL link -- but not alarming enough to lose his job. Yet.
With Denver sitting at 6-2 ( very likely 7-2 after facing the Carolina Panthers on Sunday), holding a first-place lead in the AFC West, and with a bye week next up, there's also an argument to avoid fixing what isn't ( that ) broken, uprooting the protection of franchise quarterback Bo Nix.
The only caveat: there's one more game to be played until the deadline, and the bye would be the perfect time to execute any unsuspecting changes. Everything is always possible.
Just don't hold your breath.

title: Broncos' Week 9 Injury Report: Final Decisions on Jones, Uwazurike
full_text:
The Denver Broncos released their final Week 9 injury report on Friday -- and in doing so, ruled out a trio of defensive players, including two starters.
Among those inactive against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday will be safety Brandon Jones, defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike, and cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine, all of whom suffered injuries during the team's Week 8 win over Kansas City.
Neither of the players got in so much as a limited practice this week -- three consecutive DNPs -- so the writing was on the wall for defensive coordinator Vance Joseph's esteemed unit.
Also on that side of the ball, the Broncos listed safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) and outside linebacker Dondrea Tillman (hip) as questionable to play at Carolina. Hufanga has missed the last three games due to his injury, while Tillman popped up on the injury report Friday despite a full practice.
Per The Denver Gazette's Chris Tomasson , "it's very uncertain" as to whether Tillman, who's classified as "week to week," will see the field at Bank of America Stadium. Perhaps he's given some time off ahead of next week's bye.
Elsewhere, wide receiver Pat Bryant is questionable for a Week 9 return following a four-game absence with his own ankle issue. Denver designated Bryant to return from injured reserve and he's expected to be activated to the 53-man roster.
Defensive end Zach Allen, receiver Courtland Sutton, and receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) were given no designation and are good to go versus Carolina .
The Panthers, meanwhile, ruled out four starters including cornerback Will Lee, linebacker Bobby Okereke, outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips, and left guard Damien Lewis.
The good news as it relates to Jones' absence is that it appears to be aligning with the return of Hufanga, and Denver demonstrated that on Friday by releasing fill-in starting S Taylor Rapp, presumably signaling that Hufanga will play in Week 9. Look for Devon Key and/or JL Skinner to also see an uptick in snaps.
Second-year corner will take Abrams-Draine's reps as the No. 4 CB behind Pat Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Ja'Quan McMillian. It's possible the Broncos promote one of their three defensive backs, Sean Fresch Jr., Brent Austin, or Ugo Amadi to help provide some depth.
With Uwazurike sidelined, the onus will fall more on DE Sai'vion Jones opposite Zach Allen, though it's also likely that third-round rookie Tyler Onyedim, a weekly healthy scratch, finally makes his NFL debut.
If Tillman can't go, Que Robinson could assume the lion's share of reps as the No. 3 OLB behind Nik Bonitto and Jonathon Cooper.

title: Mile High Roundtable Drops its Predictions & Picks for Broncos-Panthers

After defeating the Kansas City Chiefs last week, the Broncos now lead in the AFC West . If the Broncos want to retain their position atop the divisional mountain, they must take care of business and beat the teams they're supposed to.
The 3-4 Carolina Panthers may seem like just another sub-.500 opponent, but they can be dangerous. The Broncos must guard against the "trap-game" nature of this matchup and handle the Panthers on the road.
It's an East Coast road game with an early start, which has traditionally been an obstacle for the Broncos, but not since Sean Payton became the head coach in 2023. The Broncos have turned that particular ship around.
The Panthers have some young playmakers on offense and a defense that's better than some people realize. But if the Broncos play up to their potential, it's hard to see the Panthers keeping up with them.
That's a big if , though, as the Broncos have been frustratingly inconsistent on both sides of the ball, despite their winning streak.
How will this shake out? Let's go around the table to see how the Denver Broncos On SI Mile High Huddle staff see this one unfolding on Sunday.
Keith Cummings ( @KeithC_NFL ) 6-2 : East Coast road swings are never easy. Thankfully, the Broncos are a team that knows how to win late. Against the Panthers, the Broncos get an early lead and use Jonah Coleman to the maximum in a lopsided win.

Chad Jensen ( @ChadNJensen ) 6-2 : Thanks to all his years in New Orleans, Payton has a special place in his heart for NFC South opponents; he's undefeated against them as Broncos head coach. Outdueling Bryce Young won't be quite so easy this time around, though, as the Panthers' young quarterback has improved dramatically since then, but Nix's confidence has come flooding back over the past two weeks, and that leads to a romping day for the Broncos' offense on the road. Nix has his best statistical game of the year, with 280 passing yards and three touchdown passes.

They could make us sweat, as they like to do. But they’ll ultimately get the job done.

Carolina is playing football, but boy, they aren't good on the lines of scrimmage. Can they win up front as thoroughly as Denver has this year? Another win. Although this game does have “trap game” all over it, Denver has enough veterans not to falter.

The Panthers are similar to the Cardinals, in that they can challenge the better teams. But with the way the Broncos have executed, for the most part, in recent weeks, I believe they will have a similar performance as they did in Arizona, with a close, low-scoring first half, but they pull away in the second for a double-digit win.

title: Broncos' Stance on Jonathan Taylor Trade Has Shifted, Insider Claims
full_text:
Time is running out on the Jonathan Taylor sweepstakes.
The Indianapolis Colts have upped the ante, reportedly asking for a first-round value in exchange for the three-time Pro Bowl running back ahead of this coming Tuesday's NFL trade deadline. If the Colts can't get a first-round value for Taylor, they're looking for a Christian McCaffrey-type haul, which would be something like a second-, third-, fourth-, and fifth-round draft pick, according to Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer.
The Broncos have called the Colts; GM George Paton and head coach Sean Payton have discussed Taylor, but per Breer, Indy's steep asking price for the soon-to-be 28-year-old running back has cooled Denver's heels.
"The Giants, Broncos and Vikings have inquired, and discussed it, and it appears Denver and Minnesota might be a little less inclined to trade for Taylor now," Breer wrote on Friday .
The Giants are serious suitors for Taylor, and if the Broncos and the Vikings are bowing out, Taylor's market could dry up quickly. The Colts claim they want to keep Taylor as the cornerstone of their coming rebuild, and if they were to trade him, it would be at a premium.
Time will tell on that front.
If the Broncos make a move ahead of the November 10 trade deadline, they're expected to be buyers, not sellers. Even Payton said as much at the podium this week.
At 6-2, the Broncos are poised to make a run as their schedule opens up, but they're in dire need of a reliable run game, as that will separate the men from the boys down the stretch and into the playoffs.
Jonah Coleman has offered the Broncos they're only glimpse of rushing hope thus far. He's only touched the ball in three games this season — spending four weeks on injured reserve with an ankle sprain — but he's averaging 4.5 yards per carry and has been instrumental in the Broncos' last two wins, as well as Week 2's home victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars.
J.K. Dobbins, however, has been a near-bust this season. He's appeared in all eight games with seven starts, but he's averaging a career-low 3.3 yards per carry, and has seen his RB1 role erode in the wake of Coleman's rise.
Coleman had 41 snaps to Dobbins's 13 last week, and out-earned him in touches by far. Dobbins doesn't appear to be happy with how things are shaking out in Denver, which makes it no surprise that Breer has heard his name floated in trade talks.
"J.K. Dobbins’s name was raised in some trade talks, as Broncos rookie RB Jonah Coleman broke out, but it’s less likely now that RJ Harvey is hurt," Breer wrote on Friday.
That's the rub: Harvey's injury. The second-year back suffered a knee injury during practice last week and was placed on IR. That puts him out of commission until Week 13, at the soonest — assuming his knee is healthy.
For this reason and more, the Broncos are looking to add to their running back stable ahead of the deadline, but because of Dobbins's veteran presence, they won't overpay. And unless Dobbins was included in a trade for, say, Taylor or another back, like Tennessee's Tony Pollard or Baltimore's Derrick Henry, he'll serve as the fail-safe behind Coleman.
Complicating matters is Tyler Badie's thumb injury. He's got two more games to go on IR himself, which is why the Broncos elevated Cody Schrader from the practice squad last week against the Kansas City Chiefs.
There's one more game to go before Tuesday's deadline. Barring a massive maneuver, the Broncos are likely going to see how Sunday's road game against the Carolina Panthers shakes out before deciding on a path forward.
If the Broncos are able to run the ball well with Coleman and Dobbins, perhaps the Broncos stand pat and bide their time for Harvey's return. If it's another inconsistent struggle session, even if Coleman flashes a few big plays, it might be enough to spur the Broncos to action before 4 p.m. EST on Tuesday.
I can't see the Broncos giving up a first-round pick for a running back so quickly nearing the 2,000-carry milestone, but if Sunday is another rough rushing outing, perhaps Paton and Payton come around to the idea of giving up a few early- and mid-round picks in a facsimile of the McCaffrey trade.

title: 3 Keys to a Broncos Victory Over Panthers: Avoiding the Trap
full_text:
The Denver Broncos hold first place in the AFC West and are now entering the less daunting part of their schedule — at least, on paper. The Broncos have faced five playoff contenders in their first eight games, and while it hasn't been perfect, they can feel good about being 6-2.
The Carolina Panthers might not be as formidable as some of the other teams the Broncos have faced thus far, but they can't be taken lightly. The Panthers already hold a win over the Detroit Lions and have shown they can do good things on offense.
The Broncos will also have to travel, and both of their losses have come on the road. The Broncos also have just one double-digit win this season and need to show they can get those victories against the opponents that might not rank among the top in the NFL.
The Broncos have to respect their opponent this week and treat this game no differently than they would a top team. The Broncos' fourth-quarter comebacks may be fun to watch, but that's not something you want to do when the matchup favors you on paper, especially on the East Coast with an early start.
Let's break down three things the Broncos must do to come away with another road win before they go into their bye week — and to show they must be taken seriously as a playoff threat.
It's easy to look at the Panthers' starting quarterback and assume he's no threat. In Young's first two seasons, he had just 26 touchdown passes, though he did better in his third season with 23 passing scores. But one could still point to his 17-34 record as a starter and assume too much.
However, Young has made steady progress as a passer and is on pace to surpass 30 passing touchdowns this season. He could stand to improve his completion percentage, which stands at 58.7%, but he has improved his yards per attempt to 7.1 and his adjusted yards per attempt to 7.3, per Pro Football Reference .
Young also has the ability to extend plays if he gets out of the pocket, and he can be a threat to run with the ball if he escapes pressure, as evidenced by the 752 yards rushing and nine touchdowns he's totaled thus far in his career.
The main thing is for the Broncos' defense to keep Young in the pocket, where he becomes more vulnerable. Though he isn't taking sacks at the pace he did as a rookie — he took a whopping 62 sacks — he still has a tendency to take too many. He's been sacked 23 times in seven games, already nearing the 27 he took last year in 16 games.
With the Panthers dealing with injuries on the offensive line, this could be a game in which the Broncos pass rush could have a big day. But to do that, the Broncos can't underestimate Young, who can do plenty of damage if you aren't disciplined on defense.
Along with giving Young his respect, the Broncos have to be aware of two key playmakers on the Panthers' offense. You may not hear their names called among the top offensive playmakers in the NFL, but they are players capable of a big game at any time.
Hubbard already has a pair of 100-yard rushing games to his credit, with 120 yards against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6 and 122 yards against the Lions in Week 4. He's averaged 4.6 yards per carry, scored five rushing touchdowns, and has caught 22 passes for 150 yards and two scores.
More importantly, Hubbard does a good job of taking care of the football. His career high is four fumbles in 2024, but he's never had more than two otherwise. This season, he has yet to lose the football.
Meanwhile, McMillan has proven to be a good find for the Panthers, who took him in the second round of the 2025 NFL Draft. He surpassed 1,000 yards receiving as a rookie, with 70 receptions on 122 targets and seven touchdowns.
This season, McMillan remains Young's favored target, with 42 receptions on 65 targets for 569 yards and two touchdowns. McMillan had a strong outing against the Lions, with 192 yards on 14 receptions, scoring both of his touchdowns this season.
While McMillan's scoring has been limited, he's still a threat, and it's not a given that Patrick Surtain II will match up with him on every play . One should expect McMillan to test everyone in the Broncos' secondary.
As with Young, the Broncos must respect these playmakers. If the Broncos can contain both Hubbard and McMillan, it will go a long way toward securing a win.
There's a lot of excitement surrounding Jonah Coleman and no small amount of skepticism surrounding J.K. Dobbins , but this could be the game that allows both — perhaps —  to stand out.
Through seven games, the Panthers have given up 4.8 yards per carry to opposing running backs and 12 rushing touchdowns. The Chicago Bears, Lions, and Eagles all had at least 100 rushing yards against the Panthers.
The Panthers aren't exactly a standout at defending the pass, though they have been better in that respect, giving up 5.8 yards per reception and holding their last two opponents —  Tampa Bay and Green Bay — to under 200 receiving yards.
So if the Broncos are going to get that running game going, this may be the week to do it. This could be especially true for Coleman, who has averaged 4.5 yards per carry and might be in position to have a big game.
As for Dobbins, he's had his moments, but not enough of them. But if there's a game that he has a chance to make an impact, this is it.
If Coleman and Dobbins play well, it will take some pressure off Bo Nix to carry the load. It should also help Nix build on the good things he's done the past couple of weeks and allow him to make the most of the opportunities he gets against the Panthers.
This may not be a "get-right" game for the Broncos' offense, but it could be the game that shows they can be productive at running the football — and that they can do better than the 3.8 yards per carry average they have in the first seven games.
The Panthers aren't as strong as the Kansas City Chiefs, Seattle Seahawks, and Los Angeles Rams — all teams the Broncos have found a way to beat — but Carolina isn't a team to take lightly. The Panthers have been able to do well against playoff contenders, as evidenced by their win over the Lions.
While the Panthers aren't loaded with playmakers, they do have capable players who shouldn't be overlooked. On defense, they aren't a top team but that doesn't mean the Broncos can get away with a bad performance.
The Broncos need to build on what they've done well in recent weeks and continue to improve in areas that may need attention. They're at the midway point of the season and need to show they should be taken seriously as a team poised to make a deep playoff run.
A blowout win isn't what's needed here, but the Broncos must look to build an early lead as they did against the Arizona Cardinals, then make sure they don't let the Panthers back into the game.
While the Broncos have shown they can work that fourth-quarter magic, they don't want this game to come to that. Better to show that they can build a comfortable lead going into the fourth quarter, then put it away, to show they can be a serious playoff threat.

title: Broncos' Week 9 Injury Report: Concerning Brandon Jones Update
full_text:
Denver Broncos starting safety Brandon Jones was among three players who missed practice for a second consecutive day and now appear highly questionable to play in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers.
Jones suffered a hamstring injury in last week's victory over the Chiefs and has yet to resume practicing. Ditto for defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike, whose shoulder issue has held him out. Ditto for cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine, who's dealing with an ankle affliction.
Each player will need to get in at least a limited session Friday to have any chance of suiting up at Carolina.
In more fortunate news, Denver's other starting safety, Talanoa Hufanga, was upgraded from DNP (Did Not Practice) to a limited participant on Thursday, giving him a shot at returning after being sidelined for the last three games with his own ankle malady.
Wide receiver Courtland Sutton and defensive end Zach Allen were also upgraded to full following a veteran rest day on Wednesday. Both will be active in Week 9.
WRs Jaylen Waddle (chest) and Pat Bryant (ankle) were full participants, as well. Bryant will return from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury.
On Carolina's side, five players did not practice: OLBs Jaelan Phillips and Trevis Gipson, CB Will Lee, OG Damien Lewis, and LB Bobby Okereke. Quarterback Bryce Young (ankle) was a full participant and will play against the Broncos.
“You’ve definitely seen his ascension, and he’s very comfortable with what they’re doing," Broncos head coach Sean Payton said of Young on Wednesday. "It’s an explosive team. I think they’re seventh or eighth in explosives. They do a great job mixing the play action, the ‘RPO’ (Run-Pass Option) game. They’ve drafted well. So all those numbers are different today than they were two years ago.”
Assuming Jones is ruled out, Taylor Rapp would likely fill in as a starting safety at Carolina. If Hufanga can't go, Devon Key or JL Skinner would slot in next to Rapp. Skinner, in particular, had a standout game in last week's comeback victory over the Chiefs .
Assuming Uwazurike is scratched, Sai'vion Jones would likely be penciled in as a starting DE opposite Allen, with third-round rookie DL Tyler Onyedim a possibility to make his NFL debut.
Assuming Abrams-Draine is out of commission, second-year CB Jahdae Barron could see an uptick in snaps behind CBs Patrick Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Ja'Quan McMillian.

title: Broncos ILB Alex Singleton Captures Esteemed NFL Award
full_text:
One year after being diagnosed with testicular cancer , Denver Broncos inside linebacker Alex Singleton was awarded one of the high honors of the NFL regular season.
The league announced Thursday that Singleton has been named AFC Defensive Player of the Month for October.
In the midst of a fantastic fifth year in Denver, Singleton is indeed deserving of the award for his work from Weeks 4-8, when he notched 68 total tackles, five tackles for loss, five quarterback hits, and two sacks. He won Defensive Player of the Week for his 19-tackle effort against the Cardinals.
“It was sick," he said of taking home DPOW. "It is one of those really cool things that when my kids don’t believe me one day that this is what I did that I can be able to show them.”
Singleton, a longtime defensive captain, currently leads the league in tackles (101) — 19 more than the second-leading tackler, Titans LB Anthony Hill Jr. He's also grading out as the sport's 10th-best LB among 76 qualifiers, according to Pro Football Focus .
“He’s very important. He’s the green dot," Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph said of Singleton on Oct. 29. "He’s been with us four years now, and there are certain things that he can fix during the week that I don’t have to fix any longer. It’s meetings on Fridays where it’s him and his teammates. That’s the way it has to be with a veteran like Alex. His tackling has been always very good. So it’s fun to see him get recognized for being a big-time player because to me, he’s been a special player for four years now. He’s had 171 tackles, 156 tackles. I think what, 137 last year and he missed two games. So he’s been special in my mind for four seasons.”
Singleton is on pace for roughly 215 tackles this season, which would break the NFL single-season record (214) set by Hardy Nickerson in 1993. He'd also become the first Broncos player with 200-plus tackles in a single year since Randy Gradishar accomplished that feat in 1983.
The veteran 'backer will have a chance to add to his growing total in Week 9 , facing a Carolina Panthers offense that ranks 22nd in rushing offense, with RB Chuba Hubbard accounting for about 70 percent of Carolina's total carries per game.

title: Jonathan Taylor's New Price Tag Just Changed Things for Broncos
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are still being linked to the running back trade market ahead of November 10's NFL deadline.
The Broncos became the favorites to land Jonathan Taylor after Sunday's 28-24 win over the Kansas City Chiefs, but a significant obstacle could be in the way. According to ESPN 's Adam Schefter, the Indianapolis Colts have received at least one offer of a second-round pick plus additional compensation for Taylor, but they've yet to pull the trigger on a trade.
The Colts are holding out for a better offer — and they could be looking for a first-round pick. The Colts are now trying to send the signal that they want to hold onto Taylor as the cornerstone of their rebuild, but in an appearance on the Pat McAfee Show on Tuesday, NFL insider Ian Rapoport implied that Indy is looking for a first-round offer to part with their Pro Bowl back.
Would Taylor be worth a first-round pick to a team like the Broncos? That's the question.
As the Colts try to raise Taylor's value ahead of the deadline, the Broncos have to resist the temptation to overpay. As reliable and consistent as the veteran back is, he'll turn 28 in January, and he's rapidly approaching the dreaded 2,000-carry milestone.
Taylor just signed a two-year, $44 million extension this summer, but his 2027 and 2028 salaries are $15 million and $9.46 million, respectively. His contract isn't prohibitive, especially for the caliber of back he is, but it's the cost to acquire him that could be the hitch in the Broncos' giddyup.
The Broncos have only made two first-round picks in the past five years, due to costly trades involving Russell Wilson, Sean Payton, and Jaylen Waddle. Nobody is questioning the compensation Denver gave to New Orleans to acquire Payton's rights — he's been worth every penny, so to speak — but the Wilson trade blew up in the Broncos' face, and the jury is still out on Waddle.
As the Broncos begin to age into one of the NFL's older rosters, keeping the draft pipeline flowing could become increasingly important. That's especially true as it pertains to a future Bo Nix contract, as that'll limit the number of salary-cap dollars available to pay veterans.
Giving up a second-round pick for Taylor, plus perhaps a couple of mid-round selections, would already be pushing the envelope for Denver. But if the Broncos believed he would be the missing piece to get them over the Super Bowl hump, it would quickly become a case of ' F(orget) them picks ' — a phrase the Los Angeles Rams have made famous.
I'm not convinced Taylor is worth a second-round pick, let alone a first-rounder, especially given the emergence of Jonah Coleman. Plus, the Broncos expect to get RJ Harvey back from injured reserve in a few weeks, and they still have J.K. Dobbins, whom Payton vociferously claimed on Wednesday is still a "huge part of what we're doing."
If the Broncos were to acquire Taylor, he'd be the de facto No. 1 running back, pushing everyone else, including Coleman, down the depth chart. Again, that's a collateral effect the Broncos could live with, if Taylor was the answer to unlocking this offense.
And he very well could be. The Broncos are the NFL's worst third-down offense halfway through the season, mainly because of their inefficiency on first and second down. Taylor could ostensibly help fix that in a hurry, moving the chains and giving Bo Nix much more favorable third-down situations.
I could see Taylor being an immediate difference-maker, but the idea that Denver would have to go another year without making a first-round selection... it would put a lot of pressure on Payton to win a Super Bowl this year.
Another option could be to trade for a guy who could simply fit into the Broncos' running back committee. Payton often laments the difficulty of feeding more than two running backs on game day, though a third back often gets some usage in the offense, like Harvey on third down and in the passing game.
This is much more of an issue for Denver now, only because Harvey is out of reach for the next three games. The Broncos' next three games are at the Carolina Panthers, home against the Las Vegas Raiders, and on the road against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
If the Broncos believe they can weather that three-game storm without Harvey, with Coleman and Dobbins, they probably don't make a trade for a running back. But if they're worried about it, maybe they don't swing for the fences with Taylor and instead look at a more affordable option like Tennessee's Tony Pollard , who already has 595 rushing yards and six touchdowns in a terrible Titans offense.
It's a pickle. Since the Broncos have become competitive, we know GM George Paton has considered making trades ahead of the deadline as recently as last year (Waddle). But Paton has never actually pulled the in-season trigger.
At the same time, Paton never got close to a Lombardi Trophy until last year, and that, ladies and gentlemen, is why all bets are off. If the Colts stick to their guns, looking for a first-round value in exchange for Taylor, the Broncos may look elsewhere for help. They'll still be looking, though.
But if it's just a negotiating tactic, Taylor could end up going for much less, just as we saw when the Colts dealt away All-Pro left guard Quenton Nelson (for a third- and a fifth-rounder) and veteran defensive lineman DeForest Buckner (a fourth-rounder). The Colts gave up both trenchmen for much less than was expected.

title: Broncos HC Sean Payton Addresses Trade Chatter
full_text:
Sean Payton wouldn't outright dismiss the idea of the 6-2, first-place Denver Broncos being "buyers" — acquiring star-level talent at a likely costly price — ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, as many within the fan base are hoping for.
But the veteran head coach did shoot down any speculation about the club being "sellers" — shipping off key pieces amid a potential championship run .
“Well, we’re a team that’s playing better, so we’re not looking to sell," Payton told reporters following Wednesday's practice.
The Broncos don't have a trade chip like the Colts do with running back Jonathan Taylor, whom Denver is the current betting favorite to land. Their highest-value commodities are players on expiring contracts.
That group includes wide receiver Marvin Mims, cornerbacks Riley Moss and Ja'Quan McMillian, safety Brandon Jones, offensive guard Ben Powers, tight end Evan Engram, and backup quarterback Jarrett Stidham.
A group that Payton isn't rushing to break up, realizing the landscape of today's NFL.
“I always think there’s buyers and sellers, right?" Payton said Wednesday. "It’s probably more noticeable in the last five years than maybe in our… Or at least I notice it more. Teams that are playing well are the potential buyers. The teams maybe that aren’t are the potential sellers.”
Taking Payton at his word, the Broncos rightfully have no business doing other teams any favors by giving away crucial pieces of their roster. Not when they're competing in a wide-open AFC. Not with their Super Bowl window wide open. Not here, not now.
Perhaps if Denver was 2-6, the "sellers" argument would be justified. But as of now, they hold the No. 2 seed in the conference, seemingly on track to capture the AFC West for the second consecutive year.
Trading Moss, a starting corner, for a hypothetical fourth-round pick isn't more valuable than simply retaining him for the remainder of the 2026 campaign. Ditto for Jones. Ditto for McMillian. Ditto for Mims. Each player is a significant contributor, if not a full-blown starter. Why fix what isn't broken?
Some fans don't want to hear this, but it'd actually be better if the Broncos maintained the status quo — did nothing — than suddenly face-lifted the lineups before Tuesday's deadline.
The options are on the table for Payton and his right-hand man, general manager George Paton, as the decision-making process remains fluid.
“We would meet and meet in the evening. The early part of it, all the GMs, they all talk with each other, but he and I’ll visit daily," Payton said. "So it’s not like it’s consuming two hours. His group is spending a lot of time separate from the time that I’m involved with our group. In other words, they’re doing their evaluation, we’re doing football, but he and I daily will visit about a bunch of things.”

title: Broncos Get Good News on Pat Bryant, Concerning Update on Talanoa Hufanga
full_text:
After missing the last four games with an ankle injury, the Denver Broncos designated wide receiver Pat Bryant to return from injured reserve, opening his window to be activated to the 53-man roster.
That will likely happen sooner rather than later as Bryant was marked as a full practice participant on the team's first Week 9 injury report ahead of Sunday's road game at Carolina .
Bryant was carted off the field amid Denver's Week 4 loss against the 49ers with what appeared to be a significant injury, though the second-year wideout avoided being placed on short-term injured reserve.
Also listed as a full participant was Bryant's fellow pass-catcher, WR Jaylen Waddle, who's still nursing a minor chest issue. Waddle looked no worse for wear in last week's comeback victory over Kansas City , snagging three passes for 39 yards and a touchdown.
WR Courtland Sutton, meanwhile, was considered limited as he enjoyed a veteran rest day. Ditto for defensive end Zach Allen. Both will play against the Panthers.
What's less certain is the Week 9 status of four key defensive players in safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), safety Brandon Jones (hamstring), defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike (shoulder), and cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine (ankle) — all of whom did not practice on Wednesday.
Jones, Abrams-Draine, and Uwazurike were injured in Week 8 and their status for Sunday's contest is to be determined. They'd need to get in at least a few limited practices on Thursday and Friday to increase their chances of suiting up.
Hufanga has been sidelined since Oct. 11 — he was initially expected to miss 2-3 games — and could be held out once more with Denver's Week 10 bye looming.
Finally, the Broncos — if they choose to activate him this week — could be back at full strength in their receiving corps, with Waddle, Sutton, Bryant, Marvin Mims, and Troy Franklin all sharing the same field together.
Bryant totaled nine receptions for 133 yards and a touchdown prior to going down, with his lone score coming in Denver's Week 3 upset of the Los Angeles Rams. He also snagged a two-point conversion earlier in the season.
With sure hands and a wide catch radius, Bryant will again provide quarterback Bo Nix a security blanket over the middle of the field and in the red zone, helping to boost a passing offense that currently ranks 25th in the NFL, averaging 180.4 yards per game through the air.

title: Everything Lions Fans Need to Know From a Dolphins Insider
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have a showdown Sunday with the Miami Dolphins. After back-to-back emotional wins over NFC North opponents, the Lions must now avoid an emotional let-down and handle business against a Dolphins team that continues to improve.
Alain Poupart covers the Dolphins as the publisher of Dolphins OnSI . He recently spoke with Lions OnSI and answered five questions to preview the matchup.
Poupart : "This might be a tricky question because the Dolphins are in the early stages of a rebuild and it’s a very, very young team that lacks talent and depth. What they have shown is they will play hard and not give up, which admittedly should be the bare minimum for any team. Stylistically, the Dolphins look like they want to be a running team and defensively they play mostly zone."
Poupart : "I think the physical attributes are pretty obvious, and have been obvious since the start of camp, but he’s still a very inexperienced QB despite having been in the league for five years. He’s also operating with a less-than-ideal supporting cast and a lot of youth, which leads to rookie mistakes like receivers running the wrong routes. His play has been a bit uneven in terms of decision-making, but he’s actually made improvement in that regard in recent games. I still think more data needs to be collected, but I would say right now there’s not a screaming need for the Dolphins to absolutely draft a quarterback near the top of the 2027 draft."
Poupart : "I’m going to guess Lions fans probably don’t know a lot of Dolphins players because Miami is a pretty nondescript team, so I’ll go with one of the good-looking rookies, third-round pick Caleb Douglas. He’s a wide receiver from Texas Tech who’s long and also runs very good routes. He looks like an absolute keeper for Miami."
Poupart : "The Dolphins are not like other teams with bad records because this season never was about wins and losses but rather player development and evaluation. Because of that, nobody should assume they’ll be in selling mode because hanging on to players who could help in 2027 and beyond will be more valuable than marginal draft picks. The Dolphins already have done their salary cap dumps, they don’t need to do any more. So they’ll trade only if the offer because too good to pass up; for example, a second-round pick for Brooks would be hard to turn down, but I don’t see anybody offering that. Brents is a really promising-looking corner who’s had injury issues, but again the Dolphins aren’t simply going to give him away. And, yes, both players would be good additions for the Lions."
Poupart : "The Dolphins are last in the NFL in pass defense and allow 76.9 completion percentage with little pass rush. I just don’t see how they stop the Lions offense. title: Detroit Lions 2026 Trade Deadline Tracker: News, Rumors, Updates
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is quickly approaching.
For teams like the Detroit Lions , this weekend's slate of games is the final opportunity to get eyes on potential targets before the pressure to make a deal reaches a fever pitch. The deadline is set for 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, Nov. 10.
The Lions are 5-2 entering Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins and are right in the mix for the NFC North crown. However, every team in the division is currently above .500, and just earning a playoff spot in a crowded NFC will be a challenge.
Because of this, the Lions are facing pressure to make a trade to bolster their roster ahead of the deadline. General manager Brad Holmes has made deadline deals in the past, but has prioritized supplemental additions rather than making a big splash throughout his tenure.
The NFC North has been busy leading up to the deadline, with the Chicago Bears making the headlining move up to this point in their blockbuster to acquire former Tennessee Titans standout defensive lineman Jeffrey Simmons.
With other teams around the NFC also being active, the Lions need to make a deal to keep up in what is sure to be a competitive stretch run amongst teams looking to make the postseason.
This year, the Lions' consensus biggest need is at the cornerback position. Though the team has gotten improved performances from D.J. Reed and Roger McCreary in recent weeks, the depth is limited and the secondary remains one of the worst in the league against the pass.
Leading up to the deadline, players potentially linked to the Lions include Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen, Los Angeles Chargers cornerback Donte Jackson and Kansas City Chiefs cornerback Kristian Fulton.
With the recent injuries to Jack Campbell and Jimmy Rolder, the Lions' linebacker depth has also taken a hit and they could be in the market for a player at that position as well.
Last year, the Lions did not make an addition at the trade deadline. The year prior, they made a deal to acquire veteran defensive end Za'Darius Smith from the Cleveland Browns after losing Aidan Hutchinson to a season-ending leg injury. Smith notched four sacks in eight games for the Lions in 2024.
Holmes also made a deal at the 2023 deadline, acquiring wide receiver Donovan Peoples-Jones from the Browns. That deal didn't pay off, as Peoples-Jones played a very limited role before not making the team the following year.
In 2022, the Lions were sellers as Holmes traded tight end T.J. Hockenson to the Minnesota Vikings at the deadline. However, the Lions rebounded in the second half of that season to finish with a winning record at 9-8 and missed the postseason by just one game.
Follow along leading up to Tuesday's deadline for all the latest news and rumors surrounding the Lions.
November 7th, 10:30 a.m. -- Interest is high from contending teams to add a tight end at the deadline. Multiple teams have expressed interest in tight end Sam LaPorta and have contacted Lions.
November 7th, 9:35 a.m. -- The Athletic expresses a team the Lions and Bears could call for a cornerback is the Denver Broncos, due to their depth at the position.

title: Five Detroit Lions Ruled Out, Star WR Questionable Against Dolphins
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have released their official 2026 Week 9 Friday injury designation report, ahead of the teams road contest against the Miami Dolphins.
According to the team, five starting players have been officially ruled out, including Kerby Joseph, Jack Campbell, D.J. Wonnum, D.J. Reed and Cade Mays.
Three players were ruled questionable, including wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown, running back Sione Vaki and running back Jacob Saylors.
Joseph has taken scout team reps at practice and has steadily improved with each day.
Safeties coach Jim O'Neil expressed Joseph has looked better than expected and the coaching staff has seen the work put in to try and get back to playing.
“It’s been great. Two weeks ago, it was classroom work, where we were really locked in. Then it was walkthrough and individual. Yesterday was his first team practice, and he looked a lot better than what I anticipated him looking like. So, it was very encouraging," O'Neil said. "So now he’s gotta stack multiple days. He’s got to stack them, so today will be a big day for him , but he looked awesome yesterday at practice."
Joseph will not likely play against the Patriots next week, but could see action on Thanksgiving.
“He’s worked his ass off. He has. He’s gone through a mental battle, he’s gone through a physical battle, and he’s in a great place right now. And I’m excited for him, and I know how hard he’s working," said O'Neil. "I know how hard it must be to be at the top of your game and then have it taken away from you. He’s grinded to get back to the level that he’s used to playing at and at his standard.”
Safety Brian Branch left the game against the Vikings with a head injury, but appears ready to play against the Dolphins.
With players returning, the coaching staff can do even more things with the former Alabama Crimson Tide defensive back.
“As we get guys back, guys like with Kerby’s skillset or (Thomas) Harper’s skillset, that just opens up the door to do more stuff with Branch. He can go down, he can do dime roles , he can play nickel roles," said O'Neil. "You can use him more of a chess piece as we get some guys back in the defense and in that secondary.”

title: Detroit Lions Will Likely Be Without Key Defenders Against Dolphins
full_text:
The Detroit Lions will likely be without two key defenders and center Cade Mays against the Miami Dolphins.
Prior to practice, head coach Dan Campbell indicated it was very unlikely Mays, cornerback D.J. Reed and defensive end D.J. Wonnum would suit up against the Dolphins in a Week 9 road contest.
Reed has missed practice this week dealing with a hip injury, while Wonnum is in concussion protocol after taking a shot in the helmet from teammate Brian Branch against the Minnesota Vikings.
Unfortunately for Sheppard's defense, Reed was playing at a high level the past two weeks. The former NFL linebacker could turn to Roger McCreary, Keith Abney or Ennis Rakestraw to fill in for the veteran defender.
When asked if Ahmed Hassanein had an opportunity to be active this week, the former NFL tight end indicated rookie defender Anthony Lucas could be a player from the practice squad to be elevated this week.

"Again, what have I said about my man E? It's always been about availability and how many reps did he get that week," said Sheppard. "He's a little nicked up and banged up. And then guys, I just outright trust (Lions passing game coordinator/defensive backs coach) Deshea Townsend. When it come to DB play, that's what you have got to know. I never played DB. title: Devastating Jack Campbell Injury May Force Lions LB to Make Tough Decision
full_text:
This week, members of the Detroit Lions roster, including the linebackers unit, have been reflecting on the impact of seeing one of their leaders and teammates being carted off the field against the Minnesota Vikings.
Cognitively, players understand the inherent risk of playing a violent sport. Still, nothing can prepare an individual when a player is lying face down and motionless on the field.
Many expressed that while the group must quickly turn the page, they are still keeping Jack Campbell at the forefront of their thoughts.
Derrick Barnes expressed to local reporters this week the jarring scene at Ford Field has forced him to contemplate if he wants his young son to even play the game of football.
Barnes expressed, via the Detroit Free Press , “I don’t think you’re playing football. Right after I said that, he’s like, ‘Daddy, I play football. Daddy, I play football.' So, I’m like, ‘We’re going to have a long conversation. I want to tell you the great things about it and the bad things about it and you make that decision if you really want to.’ But no, I told him, I said, ‘Man, don’t worry about it. We’re going to get you into some baseball, man. Some golf.’ Things I wish I’d have done. Especially golf. Things I wish I would have got to as a young kid.”
The team is preparing this week with a fighters mentality, knowing that Campbell would not want the group sulking or feeling down for him, given what he is going to be facing over the next several weeks and months.
"Jack’s a fighter, we all know Jack and knowing Jack, he wants us to keep going throughout our day. That’s why we all love Jack, humble guy, so to hear the news from Coach this morning was awesome. It was a sigh of relief," linebacker Malcolm Rodriguez said. "Obviously he’s progressing better. It’s one of those things where he’s going to keep fighting. I know he wants to come back and play already. It’s just how Jack is and that’s why all the guys in here love him."

title: Odds Detroit Lions Beat Miami Dolphins in Week 9
full_text:
The Detroit Lions will head down South to take on the 1-6 Miami Dolphins this Sunday.
Led by first-year head coach Jeff Hafley, the Dolphins have struggled to do much right in 2026. Through seven games, they've scored the second-fewest points (16.7/contest), plus they've allowed the ninth-most points (25.9/game).
Additionally, Miami did not notch its first win of the season until Week 7, defeating Aaron Glenn and the N.Y. Jets, 28-25.
Undeniably, it's been a rough season for Hafley & Co., which find themselves in possession of the third-worst record in the NFL. The only teams which have been worse are the Tennessee Titans (1-7) and the L.A. Chargers (0-7).
The Lions, under Dan Campbell, were once in the same unenviable shoes as the Dolphins. When Campbell first took over in the Motor City in 2021, Detroit was far from one of the most formidable teams in the NFL. Instead, just like the Dolphins currently, Campbell & Co. experienced their fair share of struggles and lost plenty of games on their way to establishing their tough, gritty identity. In fact, Detroit started the aforementioned campaign 0-10-1 before winning its first game in Week 13 against the Minnesota Vikings.
In that sense, Campbell sees plenty of parallels between those Lions and this current iteration of Miami.
“Coach Hafley’s done a good job in his first year,” the sixth-year Lions head man expressed to reporters this week. “A lot of similarities — it reminds me of what we were when we came in. They’re young, they’re hungry, they’re active, they run, they hit, they hustle, they finish, try to play disciplined ball. And they’re playing that way.”
As much as Campbell's squad is undoubtedly the better team, you can't take anyone lightly in the NFL. And for as bad as the Dolphins have been, it's important to note they have not lost a game by more than seven points since Week 4. Their last double-digit loss came in Week 3 against the Kansas City Chiefs (24-10).
And on top of all that, the Lions are severely banged up entering this Week 9 matchup , after suffering a plethora of injuries a week ago against Minnesota.
They lost five total defensive players in the divisional tilt, including defensive captain Jack Campbell, the two best members of their secondary (Brian Branch and D.J. Reed) and EDGE DJ Wonnum. And they all are in danger of missing Detroit’s interconference contest in Miami.
As a result, Miami – led under center by fifth-year passer Malik Willis – might have a chance to do some damage against Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's unit .
Yet, the Lions are seven-point favorites, per multiple sportsbooks, for a reason, and should emerge victorious in the road affair.
At this present juncture, I'll give Detroit a 72 percent chance to secure the Week 9 victory .

title: Exploring If Dolphins LB Jordyn Brooks Fits Detroit Lions Defense
full_text:
The Detroit Lions could get a look at multiple potential trade targets when they travel to Miami to take on the Dolphins on Sunday.
Miami enters the matchup with a 1-6 record under first-year head coach Jeff Hafley. Because of the state of their organization, the Dolphins could be looking to offload some of their assets ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
One potential player they could be willing to deal is linebacker Jordyn Brooks. He's an interesting option for Detroit, as he just signed a three-year contract extension in July that will keep him under team control through the 2029 season.
While this would be a hefty financial ask for the Lions to take on the remainder of Brooks' contract that comes with $35 million guaranteed and $51.3 in total new money, the possibility of the Lions making that move was brought up by Sports Illustrated NFL insider Albert Breer .
Breer noted that the injury to Jack Campbell, a defensive captain and All-Pro contributor for the Lions, leaves a big void in the middle of Detroit's defense. In Brooks, they would be getting a reliable veteran that could help stabilize the group for a lengthy period of time.
"There is the fact that that leaves a significant hole for the Lions at the linebacker position," Breer said. "And so, would you make a call on somebody like Jordyn Brooks in Miami? I don't think Miami wants to let go of its veteran leaders, but they're another team that needs players. I look at Jordyn Brooks as somebody that you could potentially make a move for if you're willing to put something valuable in front of the Dolphins.
"I think it's somebody that could be around for an extended period. A lot of that is going to depend on Jack Campbell's status," Breer continued. "I don't want to talk too much about this in football terms because I think we're more worried about him as a human being right now, but again there are football implications to that."
Jordyn Brooks @PoupartNFL Let’s save the Dolphins and raid their team pic.twitter.com/prs49CPMV0
Brooks would be a player that would absolutely fit Detroit's defense . As an inside linebacker in Miami's defense, he has had a phenomenal season. Per Pro Football Reference, Brooks has recorded 63 tackles without missing any which is the most without a missed tackle by any player this season.
The veteran is also the eighth-fastest player to reach 900 career tackles since 1994, doing so in 104 games. He's a steady tackler and a phenomenal producer from the second level of the Dolphins' defense.
However, the Dolphins likely wouldn't be inclined to move him for a minimal price. This would be a big ask for Detroit, given the level of team control the Dolphins have and how they could utilize not only his on-field abilities but also his leadership to rebuild under Hafley.
In general manager Brad Holmes' tenure, the Lions have not been apt to make big moves at the deadline and instead have made marginal moves to supplement the roster they've already built.
Because of this, adding Brooks would be unlikely despite of how well he would fit Detroit's defense moving forward.

title: Calvin Johnson Shares Important Sentiment About Team Spending
full_text:
Pro Football Hall of Fame wide receiver Calvin Johnson raised eyebrows during his recent appearance on the "Chasing No. 1" podcast that features Bengals wideout Ja'Marr Chase.
Nearing the NFL trade deadline, many supporters of the Detroit Lions are again clamoring for the team to be willing to add high-end talent.
Johnson referenced his team in Motown and how the organization was not willing to make an all-in move when Matthew Stafford was under center.
"The biggest thing for me is that, I used to always say, we tell everybody we got the team here in Detroit," said Johnson. "We had the dudes, but you can't win a Super Bowl on a budget, man. You got to go all in. You got to go all in. That's what you see teams do. They go all-in and get that one piece or two pieces that they're missing, to get them all the way there over the last couple seasons."
Additional Detroit Lions NFL Insider Analysis: Week 9 Officiating Crew For Dolphins Game Are Favorable
“You can’t win a Super Bowl on a budget” pic.twitter.com/1YYn6olWgm
The Rams were willing to make a blockbuster trade in 2020, shipping the Lions two first-round draft picks in order to land the former No. 1 overall pick.
In his first season away from Detroit, Stafford was able to hoist the Lombardi Trophy for the first time.
Johnson expressed he believed the Lions could have had more success, had the organization been more willing to go all-in.
"We had most of the pieces there in Detroit," Johnson noted. "And so for me, when he won Super Bowl, literally the first year after he left Detroit, I'm out there like, 'I mean, I told y'all what we had.'"
A recent ESPN report indicated general manager Brad Holmes has been inquiring about available cornerbacks in the trade market.
Unfortunately, the Lions may also be competing with the Chicago Bears for the same quality defenders.
“The Bears made their big move for Jeffery Simmons, but they’re still poking around on potentially available cornerbacks, as are the Lions,” Graziano wrote earlier this week. “Detroit might also be in the market for help at linebacker, particularly in the wake of the terrible injury to mainstay Jack Campbell.”

title: Lions Second Year Defensive End Could Prove Himself Against Dolphins
full_text:
With injuries on defense, the Detroit Lions could give a second-year defensive end his first opportunity in the NFL.
An injury cut Ahmed Hassanein's rookie season short, as he was waived with an injury diagnosis last season and returned on the practice squad once the injury settlement expired. However, he was never elevated to the active roster and as a result never made his official debut.
Hassanein had a strong training camp this year and made the team, but has been a healthy scratch for every game up to this point. As a result, he's still awaiting his NFL debut midway through his second season as a professional.
Things could change for Hassanein on Sunday against the Miami Dolphins, as veteran DJ Wonnum is currently in the NFL's concussion protocol after a collision with safety Brian Branch against the Minnesota Vikings.
In fact, Lions star defensive end Aidan Hutchinson went as far as to say he believes Hassanein will get an opportunity Sunday against the Dolphins in an interview with 97.1 The Ticket .
"If I was a betting man I'd say Ahmed's probably getting his opportunity this weekend. Derrick Moore is gonna be out there for sure, both those guys," Hutchinson said. "D-Mo's shown a ton of progression these first few weeks, and I know Ahmed's just itching to get out there, man. He can't wait. I think it's going to be a good opportunity for those guys, and couldn't be happier for them."
A bigger update regarding Wonnum's status could be forthcoming this week at practice, and this will likely be telling as to whether or not the veteran could suit up for Detroit on Sunday. If he can't, it would potentially pave the way for Hassanein to be active for the first time in his career.
If Hassanein is active for the first time, it will be an intriguing look at the 2025 sixth-round pick out of Boise State. His journey to the NFL has been well-known, as he took an unlikely path after being born in Egypt and worked his way to an opportunity with Boise State.
After being drafted by the Lions, Hassanein has traveled a long journey toward what could be his first chance with the team. He underwent a position change this offseason, moving from a rush end to a big end with more responsibilities in the run game as well as more versatility as far as where he lines up.
Still, he found his way into the backfield on multiple occasions throughout the preseason including a sack of Cincinnati Bengals starting quarterback Joe Burrow in the opener this year.
Now, with injuries creating an opportunity for him, Hassanein has a chance to prove himself on the biggest stage Sunday against the Dolphins.

title: Seven Former Top Draft Prospects Who Should Interest Packers at Trade Deadline
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Green Bay Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst might have one eye on the game and one eye on his phone when his team plays at the New England Patriots on Sunday.
The NFL trade deadline looms on Tuesday, and Gutekunst should break from tradition and strongly consider having his team add a key contributor.
As Gutekunst has said frequently over the years, the team’s scouting reports from before the draft matter when it comes to adding veterans. So, from that perspective, here are seven former top-50 draft picks who could fill needs for the Packers.
Jackson Powers-Johnson was the 44th pick of the 2024 draft. This wouldn’t be a deal so much to help this year’s team but a forward-thinking move on a young player with position flexibility who will be under contract in 2027.
Powers-Johnson started 14 games as a rookie, when he was guilty of a whopping 14 penalties, but has gotten the nod in only four of his seven appearances this season. His 1,566 career snaps are split fairly evenly among the three interior positions.
Would any team value that sentence more than the Packers?
Christian Barmore was the 38th pick of the 2021 draft. He had a breakout third season with 8.5 sacks and 13 tackles for losses but missed most of the 2024 due to blood clots.
Packers assistant coach DeMarcus Covington was Barmore’s position coach in New England.
“When he walks through the door, you’re going to know who he is. Just how big he is, how long he is, how tall he is,” Covington said when Barmore was a rookie. “Now, for us, as we get him into our program, it’s all about teaching him the way we do our fundamentals and technique, and the way how we do things around here. You still get a young kid that doesn’t have much experience playing football, and, so, the sky’s the limit for him. He’s going to do well for us.”
Barmore had only two sacks and four tackles for losses in 2025 but 3.5 sacks and three TFLs in seven games (two starts) this year. He could provide some pass-rushing juice to help lessen the load on Devonte Wyatt and Karl Brooks.
He is playing under a four-year, $84 million extension that runs through the 2028 season. The acquiring team in a trade would take on cap hits of about $6 million for the rest of this season, $20 million for 2027 and $21 million for 2028, but there’s no guaranteed money to be concerned about.
Rashod Bateman was the 27th pick of the 2021 draft. He never quite became the player the Ravens envisioned. He had a bit of a breakout with 45 catches for 756 yards and nine touchdowns in 2024 but caught only 19 passes in 13 games in 2025 and has 20 catches in nine games in 2026.
He’s got 4.39 speed in the 40, which would fit Green Bay’s vertical passing attack.
He’s under contract through the 2029 season. If traded, he’d have cap charges of $8.25 million in 2027, $10.25 million in 2027 and $12.25 million in 2029, but there’s no guaranteed money.
Cesar Ruiz was the 24th pick of the 2020 draft. He has played mostly right guard during his career but also has some center in his background.
The Packers are in an interesting spot at guard, where they like Laken Tomlinson so much that they started him at right guard last week. It’s a position he hadn’t played in a decade and didn’t get to practice on a short week. So, would the Packers bother adding any interior blocker?
Ruiz has not allowed a sack this season. He’s a good-but-not-great run blocker.
Next year is the final season of a four-year, $44 million contract extension. The cap hit for the rest of this season is negligible, and he is due a base salary of $9.5 million with no guaranteed money in 2027.
Brian Thomas was the 23rd pick of the 2024 draft. At 6-foot-3 and with 4.33 speed in the 40, he looked like the next great receiver as a rookie, when he caught 87 passes for 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns. However, he caught only 48 passes in 2025 and has just 10 in eight games in 2026.
The Packers have only two proven playmakers at receiver with Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Thomas could improve the depth this year – his size and speed would fit the offense – and work his way into a bigger role next year, when he plays the final season of his rookie contract with a cap charge of just $2.79 million.
Zaven Collins was the 16th pick of the 2021 draft. Once Zaire Franklin returns, the Packers will have depth at linebacker. Once Micah Parsons returns, the Packers will be back to full strength on the edge.
Collins has production in both roles. He had 100 tackles and 11 tackles for losses in 2022 and five sacks in 2024. This year, he has 23 tackles, including two sacks, in eight games (four starts).
Collins is playing the final season of his second contract. He’d cost the Packers about $2 million on the cap this year. He could be a versatile weapon for Jonathan Gannon and get the team a compensatory pick if he were to leave in free agency after the season.
The Packers have interest in Jonathan Taylor. Presumably, they’ll have interest in other backs, such as the Titans’ Tony Pollard.
Ashton Jeanty was the sixth pick of the 2025 draft. ESPN.com’s Bill Barnwell mentioned Jeanty as a “luxury target” for the Packers, who have a history of adding Raiders players with Josh Jacobs, Keisean Nixon and Nate Hobbs.
“Jeanty has struggled so far as a pro, but his pass-catching ability gives him a solid floor, and he would find it easier to access his explosiveness in a better offense,” Barnwell wrote.
Jeanty was billed as the next great running back after a dominant career at Boise State. However, after rushing for 975 yards and five touchdowns as a rookie, he’s rushed for only 337 yards with a 3.1-yard average and one touchdown this season. Would a back who hasn’t performed behind a bad offensive line change the trajectory of a running game with a bad offensive line?
Jeanty, however, is under contract for two more seasons, so this wouldn't be a one-year rental. Instead, he could replace Jacobs as RB1 next year with bargain cap charges of $4.10 million in 2027 and $5.73 million in 2028.

title: Seven Packers Trade Prospects at DT Include Two With Jonathan Gannon Ties
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers’ defensive tackles have done the dirty work to help power a defense that’s played like a top-10 unit for most of the season.
“They’re doing their job,” coach Matt LaFleur said on Friday, a couple days before a big showdown against the defending AFC champion New England Patriots. “There’s a lot of selfless play that goes into playing good team defense depending upon what the calls may be. Sometimes, they just have to eat up blockers and they’re doing their job.”
They’ve done their job, even while injuries have chipped away at the unit. Javon Hargrave is out for the season with a torn Achilles, and Warren Brinson and Jonathan Ford are on injured reserve, as well. The return of Jordon Riley has been important, but the Packers are short on depth at an important position group.
Could they find help at the NFL trade deadline? Here are seven candidates.
Moro Ojomo was a seventh-round steal by the Eagles in 2023 who is going to get paid when he hits free agency at the end of the season. The 25-year-old had six sacks last season. He doesn’t have any in eight games (three starts) this year but does have three tackles for losses.
Of 89 defensive tackles who have played at least 100 pass-rushing snaps, he is 33rd in pass-rush win rate, according to Pro Football Focus.
Whatever trade compensation the Packers would give up, they could recoup some of it via a compensatory draft pick if he’s not re-signed.
Christian Barmore was a second-round pick by the Patriots in 2021. The 27-year-old had a breakout third season with 8.5 sacks and 13 tackles for losses. However, he missed most of the 2024 season so has only 6.5 sacks and eight tackles for losses in 28 games the past three seasons.
He does have 3.5 sacks and three tackles for losses in seven games this year. Of 89 defensive tackles who have played at least 100 pass-rushing snaps, he is 10th in pass-rush win rate.
While the Patriots are contenders, SI.com’s Albert Breer said Barmore is available and might be had for a fourth-round pick. The Packers will get an up-close look on Sunday.
The finances could be tricky; Barmore has base salaries of $12 million in 2026 (the Packers would have to pay $6.6 million if it if the trade happened today), $18 million in 2027 and $19 million in 2028. There is no guaranteed money remaining, though, so the acquiring team could make Barmore a half-year rental, though that wouldn’t be ideal.
Zach Sieler had back-to-back seasons of 10 sacks in 2023 and 2024 and reached double-figures tackles for losses the last three seasons. This year, the 31-year-old has only two sacks – both against Minnesota in Week 4 – but he does have six TFLs.
He is 53rd in pass-rush win rate, according to PFF.
Sieler is playing under a three-year, $64 million contract extension. He’s got a minimum base salary for 2026, so would count for next to nothing on this year’s cap, but the salary soars to $12.655 million in 2027, $15.465 million in 2028 and $16.215 million in 2029. According to Spotrac, $10 million of his 2027 base salary is guaranteed if on the roster on the third day of the league-year.
The Dolphins have publicly said he’s not available – the finances would make it tough for them – but perhaps the relationship between Packers GM Brian Gutekunst and his counterpart, Jon-Eric Sullivan, would change that reality.
Grover Stewart was drafted by the Colts in the fourth round in 2017. He’s been an ironman Other than playing in only 11 games in 2023, he has missed only two games in his career. He’s not much of a pass rusher with 13.5 career sacks but he’s a volume tackler.
He had 74 tackles, including 10 for losses, in 2024. He’s on pace for a third consecutive season of 55-plus tackles. He is 82nd in pass-rush win rate, according to PFF, but that’s not what he’s paid to do.
Stewart, 33, is playing the final season of a three-year, $39 million contract. If the trade were to be made today, he’d count about $6.1 million on Green Bay’s cap for the remainder of the season.
A fourth-round pick by the Rams in 2021, Brown has only one sack and 12 tackles for losses in his career. The 330-pounder played in every game the past two seasons but has missed two this year, including Thursday’s game against the Packers.
Brown signed a three-year, $21 million contract in free agency in 2025. He would count about $3.0 million on this year’s cap. He has a base salary of $7.35 million for 2027 with a cap charge of $8.0 million.
Roy Lopez was drafted by Houston in 2021 but played the 2023 and 2024 seasons under Jonathan Gannon with the Cardinals. After playing for the Lions in 2025, he returned to Arizona in 2026. His head coach is Mike LaFleur. So, those would be two key references.
The 29-year-old started 16 games for the Cardinals in 2024 and has started every game for them in 2026. He is on pace to set career highs in tackles and tackles for losses. He ranks 73rd in pass-rush win rate, according to PFF, but he is an excellent run defender.
Lopez rejoined the Cardinals with a two-year, $10.5 million contract. The cap hit for this season would be negligible.
Father Time eventually tackles every player. Calais Campbell, who turned 40 just before the season, signed a one-year, $5.5 million contract with the Ravens in free agency. It’s been a long time since he turned in the last of his six Pro Bowl seasons. Plus, for the first time since his rookie season in 2008, he’s been mostly a backup. He has one sack and two tackles for losses, and ranks 46th in pass-rush win rate, according to PFF.
Still, after recording 5.5 sacks for the Ravens in 2022, 6.5 for the Falcons in 2023, five for the Dolphins in 2024 and 6.5 with Gannon and the Cardinals in 2025, there has to be some production left in the future Hall of Famer.
“Fantastic. Better than I ever could have thought honestly,” Gannon said late last season of coaching Campbell . “Obviously, played really well this year. Captain, leadership, pro’s-pro. Energy, juice all the time. I learned a lot from him. It's been awesome. …
“He’s been in a lot of places, he's had a lot of success. Everything from defensive line play to how we structure a team meeting to the schedule to everything. He's been around the block, and he's a really good resource because of how long he's been doing it.”
The cap hit for Green Bay if he joined the team today would be about $2.1 million.

title: Packers-Patriots Final Injury Report: Keisean Nixon Provides Fun Clue; Five Out
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Green Bay Packers cornerback Keisean Nixon is questionable for Sunday’s game against the New England Patriots.
Not all questionable designations are created equal, and Nixon’s jovial conversation with reporters after practice on Friday strongly suggests he will be on the field against the defending AFC champions.
“I don’t know, man,” Nixon said. “I hope I wake up Sunday and I feel good enough to play in the game. We’ll see. I hope so.”
Nixon did not practice on Thursday and was limited participation on Friday. Was he taking a rest day on Thursday?
“I just hope I’ll be ready to play on Sunday. We’ll see,” Nixon said. The tone of his voice, however, took all the mystery out of it.
Reporters on Fridays only to get to watch the players go through the opening warmups. Nixon was running around, making leaping catches on balls thrown by Xavier McKinney and typically running around like a fully healthy player.
“I was running? You saw that?” Nixon said.
“That was AI. It was AI. It was not me. I was AI, for sure. For sure, AI,” Nixon said.
What about the smile on the practice field?
“That was AI,” Nixon replied. “Whatever y’all are doing to edit them videos is crazy. Y’all are getting good at it. For sure.”
That Nixon is going to play is no surprise. He hasn’t missed a game since signing with the Packers in 2022.
“Yeah, we always talk about how your best ability is your availability and the fact that he’s been able to do that is pretty uncommon. So, he’s a ‘G,’” coach Matt LaFleur said.
Including playoffs, this would be Nixon’s 81st consecutive game in a Packers uniform.
“It’s not really a streak that means something to me. I just don’t want to not play,” Nixon said. “Technically, I don’t look at it as, ‘Oh, I never missed a game.’ I just want to play every week, so I get my body prepared for it to play. Me just not missing a game is just because I want to play.”
Five players are out for the Packers, including edge rusher Micah Parsons, who was designated for return this week following last year’s torn ACL. He was limited participation at all three practices this week, an obvious good sign as he anticipates progressing into team drills next week.
The four other players who are out are starting linebacker and defensive captain Zaire Franklin (shin), starting center Sean Rhyan (ankle), former starting right guard Travis Glover (knee) and tight end Josh Whyle (concussion). Those players missed all three practices this week.
Along with Nixon, running backs Chris Brooks (ankle) and MarShawn Lloyd (knee) are questionable. Brooks was designated for return after missing the last four games; he could be added to the roster on Saturday.
The Patriots will be without their top two receivers. Along with former Packers standout Romeo Doubs, who is on injured reserve, star receiver A.J. Brown (knee/ankle) is out.
“I know he’s working extremely hard to get back, and he’s staying engaged in meetings and everything else, and doing everything that we ask him to do,” Patirots coach Mike Vrabel told reporters on Friday. “I’m not going to speak on somebody else’s feelings. I can only comment on what I see and how he comes into the building; he’s engaged and certainly doing everything he can to get back.”
In a potential lift, star tight end Hunter Henry (foot) returned to practice on Friday and is part of a long list of players who are questionable. All of those players practiced on Friday, including starting safety Kevin Byard (chest) and starting cornerback Carlton Davis (neck).
Also, All-Pro punt returner Marcus Jones is off the injury report and will play. He did not practice on Thursday.

Questionable: RB Chris Brooks (ankle), RB MarShawn Lloyd (knee), CB Keisean Nixon (groin).
No injury designation: LG Aaron Banks (knee), S Javon Bullard (personal), WR Christian Watson (rib).
Out: WR A.J. Brown (ankle/knee), RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness).
Questionable: S Kevin Byard (chest), CB Carlton Davis (neck), TE Hunter Henry (foot), WR Mack Hollins (calf), RT Morgan Moses (foot), S Brenden Schooler (hamstring), G Greg Van Roten (hamstring).
No injury designation: DT Christian Barmore (illness), OLB Gabe Jacas (knee), LB Dre’Mont Jones (shoulder/knee), CB Marcus Jones (foot), QB Drake Maye (right shoulder).
