title: Packers Friday Update From Practice: Keisean Nixon’s Status Seems Obvious
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Green Bay Packers cornerback Keisean Nixon didn’t practice on Thursday due to a groin injury, but he seems well on his way to being in the starting lineup for Sunday’s game at the New England Patriots.
Reporters are only allowed to watch the pre-practice warmup routine on Fridays. Nixon was flying around, whether it was playing catch with Xavier McKinney or doing some straight-line sprinting.
That Nixon seems on track to play shouldn’t be a surprise. The Packers signed him in free agency in 2022 and he’s played in every game over the four-plus seasons.
“Well, we’ll see him out there today,” coach Matt LaFleur said before practice. “Obviously, it’s always concerning when a guy doesn’t practice on a Thursday but, if I know Kei like I think I do, I would expect him to put himself in a position to potentially go out there and play.”
There was a new name to the list of players not practicing. Standout nickel defender Javon Bullard was not on the field for the start of practice, but that was for personal reasons rather than an injury.
Otherwise, the list was the same as it’s been all week.
Starting center Sean Rhyan, who suffered a high-ankle sprain during the opening series at Detroit, will miss a second consecutive game. That means John Williams could make another start, this time against New England’s formidable front.
Starting linebacker and defensive captain Zaire Franklin, who suffered an injured shin at practice before the Detroit game, will miss a third consecutive game. That means another game of Isaiah McDuffie and Ty’Ron Hopper, who will have to deal with physical running back Rhamondre Stevenson.
Travis Glover, who had been the starting right guard, will miss a second consecutive game with a knee injury that he played through at Detroit.
Tight end Josh Whyle suffered a concussion early last week against Carolina.
Running back MarShawn Lloyd, who was added to the injury report on Thursday, practiced on Friday. Fellow running back Chris Brooks, who was designated for return from injured reserve this week following the ankle injury sustained at Tampa Bay, was limited participation on Wednesday and Thursday and was practicing again on Friday.
Talented running back TreVeyon Henderson, who missed last week’s game due to illness, released an important update on Friday.
“Recently, I experienced an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms that required hospitalization for several days. During that time, I underwent extensive medical testing and evaluation. While the results of my comprehensive medical testing have come back positive and reassuring, the cause of this remains unknown and unexplainable.”
Here’s his full statement.
🙏🏽 pic.twitter.com/l52XuixPOc
The Patriots have some key injury concerns with receiver A.J. Brown (ankle/knee), tight end Hunter Henry (foot) and All-Pro returner Marcus Jones (foot) not practicing on Thursday.
Patriots coach Mike Vrabel told reporters on Friday that Brown will be out and Henry and Jones will be questionable.
Packers cornerback Brandon Cisse was named the NFL’s Defensive Rookie of the Month on Thursday. Here’s our story about Cisse credited for his development.
“It’s pretty remarkable,” LaFleur said. “I think first off, I think the guy’s wired the right way. He loves football, he’s always studying, and I think our coaches have done a really nice job with him in regards to getting him up to speed, because it’s certainly a different game than it is at the college level. It’s a big-time credit to him to come in with the right mindset and the right work ethic and go out there and play really good football.”
The teams will release their final injury reports of the week after they get done practicing on Friday. For now, here are the reports from Thursday.

title: It’s Been Forever Since Packers Were Buyers at Trade Deadline; That Must Change
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – If this were Jeopardy , the answer would be Anthony Smith. The question would be who was the last player the Green Bay Packers acquired at the NFL trade deadline.
Even with one contending team after another, it’s been a long, long time since the Packers were buyers at the trade deadline. They’ve been sellers several times since 2010, when the injury-plagued Packers acquired Smith, who played in four games before joining the legion of players who watched the team win the Super Bowl while on injured reserve.
From one perspective, there’s no reason to believe the Packers will acquire a player before Tuesday’s trade deadline strikes. After all, it’s hard to ignore a decade-and-a-half of inactivity.
On the other hand, though, general manager Brian Gutekunst has been aggressive at times. He made big moves in free agency in 2019, 2024 and 2025. Last year, he made the blockbuster trade for Micah Parsons.
This year, he quickly turned the forever-young Packers into a middle-aged team with plenty of youth but also a lot of flecks of salt-and-pepper hair by adding the likes of Tyrod Taylor and Javon Hargrave in free agency, Jonnu Smith at the end of training camp, and Laken Tomlinson and Kevin Zeitler to address the five-alarm fire on the offensive line.
So, while it’s the same general manager calling the shots, it’s perhaps a different roster-building philosophy given the window of opportunity presented by Jordan Love’s excellent play and Micah Parsons’ upcoming return to the team.
The Packers, obviously, are a flawed team. The best teams win in the trenches. While Green Bay’s defensive line has been the unsung heroes for a quality defense, the offensive line has been the antiheroes for the worst-in-league-history rushing attack.
However, the NFC is filled with flawed teams. Just look at the NFC standings:
1. San Francisco 49ers: 6-1. The 49ers are old – 16 players are 30-plus – and counting on running back Christian McCaffrey to be the straw that stirs the offensive drinks. The top receivers are thirtysomethings Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel.
2. Minnesota Vikings: 6-1. The Vikings lead the NFC North. They have a Super Bowl-worthy defense and a No. 1 overall pick-worthy offense, with no ability to consistently get the ball to all-world Justin Jefferson.
3. New York Giants: 4-2-1. With Jaxson Dart on injured reserve, the Giants are counting on J.J. McCarthy at quarterback and Cam Skattebo at running back.
4. Carolina Panthers: 3-4. The Packers just beat up on the Panthers.
5. Chicago Bears: 6-2. The No. 1 wild card team might be the No. 1 threat to win the NFC because of Caleb Williams. They just made their Parsons-style trade by handing a flawed but productive defense All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. Love shedded their secondary at Lambeau.
6. Detroit Lions: 5-2. On both sides of the ball, the Lions are a Super Bowl-worthy team at Ford Field but not on the road.
8. Seattle Seahawks: 4-4. The defending champions are just 1-3 in conference play. They have a one-man offense due in large part to their inability to replace running back Kenneth Walker.
9. Los Angeles Rams: 4-4. The presumptive Super Bowl champions at the start of the season haven’t beaten a quality opponent all season due in part to aging Matthew Stafford’s mediocre performance. The upcoming return of Myles Garrett could change everything.
Looking at that group of teams, there’s no reason why the Packers can’t contend for a championship, though what happens on the trade market will play a key role in how everything shakes out.
The early moves by the NFC contenders have put the pressure on Gutekunst. Surely, he can’t look at his roster and believe it will be good enough to survive a gauntlet of playoff road games and compete for a championship – even if Parsons emerges as a big-time X-factor down the stretch.
The Packers can’t run the ball. At all. They haven’t rushed for more than 86 yards or better than 3.5 yards per carry in a game all season. They’ve signed veteran linemen. They’ve regained the services of Josh Jacobs. Nothing has helped.
Perhaps there’s a trade to be made on the offensive line – though just another decent lineman really wouldn’t do any good. The Seahawks acted boldly by acquiring All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson from the Colts for third- and fifth-round picks. That seems like a bargain for a future Hall of Famer.
Perhaps Gutekunst will feel compelled to acquire a running back, whether it’s as an insurance policy given the latest on Jacobs or to provide a better one-two tandem with Jacobs.
Maybe the Packers can overcome the lack of a running game if they are better in other areas. Green Bay’s defensive tackles have played well, regardless of what the stats would tell you, but injuries have worn down the depth. Adding a player, like the Bears did with Simmons and the 49ers did with DeForest Buckner, would make sense, regardless of whether he’s a run-stopping force or a pass-rushing presence.
Another weapon in the passing game wouldn’t hurt, with last week’s injury to Christian Watson providing a painful reminder of the lack of playmaking depth beyond Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft.
Either way, the NFC arms race kicked off with Nelson and Buckner and continued with Simmons. Those were big moves made by teams ahead of the Packers in the playoff standings. For as good as Love and the defense have played this season, you get the feeling that good won’t be good enough.
Especially with the death march that looms for a No. 7 seed.
The Packers are a good team chasing a bunch of other good teams. With the trade deadline now four days away, there is a massive opportunity for Gutekunst. With all of the compensatory picks from last year’s free-agent losses, he’s got the capital to get something done.
To do big things requires bold actions. The Packers’ championship drought is too long. Now is the time to stop “being in every conversation” and actually make the move to perhaps bring another title to Titletown.

title: Why Brandon Cisse’s Meteoric Rise as Packers Defensive Cornerstone Is Only Just Beginning
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Being a rookie cornerback in the NFL isn’t easy, even if Green Bay Packers second-round pick Brandon Cisse has made it look that way at times.
The NFL named Cisse its Defensive Rookie of the Month on Thursday. With the Packers going 4-1 in October, Cisse broke up seven passes – including back-to-back-to-back games with two – intercepted the first pass of his career and added two tackles for losses.
“I found out this morning from Coach LaFleur. Sent me a text, we talked about it,” Cisse said. “Super-excited to win an award like that. I thank my teammates, my coaches, so onto this month. What happened in the past don’t matter now, so we got to get ready for this weekend.”
The closing part of that statement encapsulates everything about Cisse. From the moment he set foot on the practice field, he’s never looked out of place. For the most part, he’s avoided the rookie rollercoaster. But he’s also never satisfied, never complacent, which means the rookie award is just part of his path and not the final destination.
There are reasons for that.
“I think first of all my family,” he said. “My parents, they did a great job at home with me of raising me the right way. I’d definitely say them. And my siblings, being super-competitive is probably where I get the competitive drive from.”
Cisse then mentioned Stephon Gilmore. Cisse finished his career at South Carolina, which is where Gilmore starred before embarking on a long NFL career that included being the 2019 NFL Defensive Player of the Year. Cisse reached out to Gilmore, and they hit it off.
“That’s my mentor and that’s somebody who’s helped me out tremendously,” Cisse said. “Anytime you have somebody who’s played at that kind of elite level help you out, it makes things a lot easier.”
Cisse said they talk every other day; he figured they’d connect via FaceTime on Thursday night.
“In my career, there’s a lot of different things, but I would say being consistent,” Cisse said. “It’s easy to be good one time. Making sure that you’re never too comfortable is what I would say that I learned from him. Never too comfortable. There’s always something you can grow at, and he pushes me in that aspect. I’m thankful to have somebody like that in my corner.”
Cisse was a second-round pick by Green Bay. The new cornerback joined the team’s new defensive coordinator, Jonathan Gannon, who cut his teeth by coaching defensive backs.
Gannon is a “tough critic” – which Cisse has embraced more than maybe some young players might. So, it’s not just that Gannon has been a key part of Cisse’s early success. It’s that he’ll be a big part in Cisse’s future success, whether that’s this year’s playoff push or becoming a true defensive stopper.
“I think it’s helped me tremendously,” Cisse said. “When I came in, he told me how it was going to be and what his expectation from me was, and he was going to be tough on me, no matter how good I become or how bad I play. Good or bad, it’s always going to be tough criticism.
“I appreciate that. I think it really changed my career having someone consistently on me every day about the little things, what to get better at. It just really made me never get comfortable. I appreciate that because, right now, I’m just looking forward to this week and trying to make sure I go out there and do my job to the best of my ability.”
What does tough coaching mean?
“There’s such a thing as chasing perfection, I would say, but every little detail matters,” Cisse explained. “Every time you have a coach that’s on you about every little detail – make sure you’re taking an extra step here, taking a better angle here, make sure you’re wrapping up or making sure you’re finishing off on the ball.
“There’s always going to be somewhere to grow, and I think anytime you have a coach that’s consistently on you about that, I think it’s tough coaching at times or being able to chew you out when you need to be chewed out.”
So, just because Cisse has allowed two or fewer catches in five games and less than 50 yards in six games, or that he leads all rookies with eight passes defensed, or that he’s in the top third in the league in catches allowed per coverage snap, or that he just became the first Rookie of the Month who played at South Carolina doesn’t mean that he’s playing as good as he could play.
Sometimes, talent can mask bad technique, for instance.
“There’s times when you can make plays but that’ll just get you away with in the moment,” Cisse said. “It won’t be something that’ll last forever. So, there’s sometimes you want to clean up technique because those things can last forever instead of just making a play in the moment.”
Cisse’s Rookie of the Month honors didn’t surprise safety Evan Williams, the NFC’s Defensive Player of the Month.
“I feel like he’s very mature in the way he shows up every day, the way he builds his habits,” Williams said. “You see a lot of guys come in just excited to play, excited to be out there, not really savoring the moment, but he’s somebody that is so intentional every time he’s on the practice field and just has a certain poise about him, which isn’t typical for a 21-year-old.
“When he’s on the field, he’s never rattled, never shaken, always knows exactly where he needs to be and obviously knows where to put himself to make some plays. So, yeah, not a surprise. I expect more of the same coming forward for that guy.”
Cisse was congratulated by his teammates for his accomplishment. Before he talked to reporters, he got a hug from right tackle Anthony Belton.
“I got a great group of teammates,” he said. “They’ve done a tremendous job. I can’t thank them enough, honestly. They’ve made my job coming here a lot easier than I expected it to be. Even coming here, just making it feel like home.
“I’ve been kind of in South Carolina my whole life and coming to Green Bay, I was a little worried. I’ve been in the Carolinas too long. How I was going to be able to adapt away from home? But those guys have made me a lot better and picked me up even when I’m down.”

title: Packers Placed Big Bet on Christian Watson, And Everyone Is Cashing In
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Green Bay Packers receiver Christian Watson has set career highs for receptions and receiving yards.
The Packers gave Watson a huge contract extension with a base value of $92 million in June. Their offseason decisions at the position and the contract were bets that a player who hadn’t quite reached his potential during his first four seasons would do it in Year 5 and beyond.
The Packers, obviously, won the bets, because it’s almost impossible to believed they’d be taking a 5-3 record into Sunday’s game at the New England Patriots without him having by far the best season of his career.
Watson entered the season with career highs of 41 catches (in 14 games as a rookie in 2022), 620 yards (in 15 games before a torn ACL in 2024) and seven touchdowns (as a rookie). This year, with the Packers hitching their wagon to Watson instead of Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks, he’s caught 42 passes for 708 yards and six touchdowns.
Watson ranks fourth in the league in receiving yards and seventh in receiving yards per game. Among receivers with at least 20 catches, he’s second with a 16.86-yard average – 0.02 yards behind Cincinnati’s Tee Higgins.
Watson’s 17-game pace is 89 receptions for 1,505 yards and 13 touchdowns. That’s noteworthy because of the escalators in his contract, which would increase his 2027 base salary.
If Watson finishes with 85-plus receptions, there is a $750,000 escalator. So, he’s on pace to hit that one. If he gets to 95 receptions, the escalator increases to $1.15 million.
If Watson finishes with 1,200-plus receiving yards, he’d also hit the $1.15 million escalator.
If Watson reaches a dozen touchdowns, there’s another $1.15 million escalator.
At his current pace, Watson would hit $3.05 million in escalators, with an opportunity to max it out at $3.45 million if he cranks up the catch production a bit. If Watson is selected to the Pro Bowl, that would be an additional $250,000.
Watson’s production has exploded because of the additional opportunities. His hard work to become much more than just a size-speed threat has come to the forefront.
“He just had some nagging injuries, stuff like that, so he never really got to have a training camp that first year,” passing-game coordinator Jason Vrable said this week. “I think that puts you behind the 8-ball a lot, and that kind of happened to Savion last year. And it’s not an excuse; it’s just a reality.
“To get better in this league, you have to grind out reps at a high level. You have to go against good corners – like some of the guys we have now – and you have to battle one-on-one. You have to callous yourself, or else you’re just going to do the same stuff you did in college. So, if you weren’t good at a slant route in college, and you’re not going to come into the pros and run it on air and be good. It’s a sport that demands you to go against a man across me who’s a good player and build yourself.”
Watson, of course, suffered a broken rib in last week’s win against Carolina. After a brief trip to the hospital, he was back on the field to finish the game .
If the injury didn’t keep him from returning to that game, he sure as heck will be on the field against the Patriots with a little additional padding.
“There’s only so much you can do,” he said after Wednesday’s practice. “It definitely still hurts. But I’ve been hurting out there plenty of times before, and I’m sure a lot of guys are dealing with other stuff. So, that’s just part of the game.”
Watson missed the end of the 2024 season and the first half of the 2025 season with a torn ACL. In the 18 games back in the lineup, Watson has 77 receptions for 1,319 yards and 12 touchdowns. He ranks 13th in yards and third in touchdowns over that span.
So, to be sidelined was difficult beyond the pain.
“I mean, just frustration, to be honest, because once I was able to catch my breath, obviously the pain and stuff was still there,” he said. “But if felt like that I could kind of just play through and still be out there. So, just frustrating that I had to go miss the game and potentially miss the rest of the game.
“I was definitely frustrated, but I understand that doctors have a job to keep us safe and, obviously, I knew that there could be a possibility for something more serious or whatnot. So, I was just trusting the doctors to do their job and keep me safe. I was frustrated, for sure, but understanding, as well.”
Watson is on a prolific pace that could have him challenging Davante Adams (1,553 yards in 2021) and Jordy Nelson (1,519 yards in 2014) as the most productive receiver in Packers history.
“He’s playing at a high level right now,” Vrable said. “I’m happy for him to finally get some respect that I do believe that he deserves.”

title: Packers-Patriots Thursday Injury Report: Injuries Impacting Specific Matchup
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers have an injury concern at quarterback. The New England Patriots have all sorts of problems at receiver.
Those injuries highlight Thursday’s injury report and could play a role in Sunday’s showdown between five-win teams.
Five players didn’t practice for the Packers. One of them was starting cornerback Keisean Nixon, who once again is dealing with a groin injury . He was limited participation at Wednesday’s practice.
Nixon missed the Wednesday practice before the Dallas game because of a groin injury but started and played every snap in a big-time performance against the high-flying Cowboys passing game.
Nixon signed with the Packers in free agency in 2022. He has played in every regular-season game during the past four-plus seasons and a total of 80 in a row with the team including playoffs.
As defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon said recently, Nixon is playing like a “starting-caliber” cornerback. Last year, Nixon allowed seven touchdowns and was penalized 12 times. This year, according to Pro Football Focus, he has allowed zero touchdowns and only been flagged three times.
“He’s competitive,” Gannon said. “He really is competitive and he plays the game with an edge. He doesn’t back down. I love that about him.”
Also not practicing for the Packers were starting linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), starting center Sean Rhyan (ankle), former starting guard Travis Glover (knee) and tight end Josh Whyle (concussion). Whyle’s status could get Jonnu Smith back on the field after he was inactive for the Carolina game.
Superstar edge rusher Micah Parsons practiced for the second consecutive day as he knocks off the rust following last year’s torn ACL. He’s only doing individual drills this week so was limited participation.
“Any time you get a player like that, it makes your job a lot easier,” cornerback Brandon Cisse said. “So, look forward to having him back soon, whenever that time is. He's an unbelievable player, unbelievable talent, so any time you get somebody like that rushing the passer, it makes your job a lot easier. So, yeah, I've been looking at him. Just excited to have him back.”
Also, running back MarShawn Lloyd, whose first two seasons were ruined by lower-body injuries, didn’t miss a practice during the offseason or training camp and hasn’t even been on the injury report this season.
Until now. Lloyd was limited participation with a knee injury.
Other than the addition of Lloyd and the status of Nixon, Green Bay’s injury report is unchanged from Wednesday.
The Patriots’ offense could be depleted.
Former Packers receiver Romeo Doubs is on injured reserve for at least a couple more weeks. Premier receiver A.J. Brown, who is battling ankle and knee injuries and has played in only three games this season, didn’t practice again. The knee is the big issue and “is threatening to hold him out this week,” according to ESPN.com’s Adam Schefter.
Making matters worse, tight end Hunter Henry, who leads the team in receptions, did not participate for a second consecutive day due to a foot injury.
DeMario Douglas, a sixth-round pick in 2023 who stands only 5-foot-8, has filled the void as much as possible. He’s second on the team with 26 receptions and leads the way with 332 yards and four touchdowns.
“I was telling somebody the other day, it’s hard not to love a teammate like Pop,” quarterback Drake Maye said. “He’s constantly the same. He’s always laughing and smiling. I love when he starts dancing in the end zone; we got him in the end zone a couple times this year.
“He can turn an easy catch and he’s hard to tackle. So, like I’ve always said, you can’t guard him in a phone booth, so he’s fun. We’ve got to get him the ball in space more and let him go do his thing because he’s fun to watch.”
New England’s premier punt returner, cornerback Marcus Jones, did not practice because of a foot injury. He had two punt-return touchdowns last season.
“He’s very, very dynamic. He can break the game open at any point,” Packers special teams coordinator Cam Achord said this week. “I’ve played a lot of good returners; he’s in that bunch – top three guys – in the National Football League.”

title: Packers Thursday Update From Practice: Two Key Updates on Defense
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Including playoffs, Keisean Nixon has played in all 80 games since joining the Green Bay Packers in 2022.
Is that streak in jeopardy?
There’s plenty of time before the Packers play at the New England Patriots on Sunday, but Nixon was one of five players who did not practice on Thursday. He was limited participation with a groin injury on Wednesday.
Nixon has a history of playing through pain, including this season.
Last week, he was limited participation all week with a shoulder injury but started and played all but one snap against Carolina. A couple weeks earlier, Nixon did not participate in the Wednesday practice due to a groin injury, was limited the next two days and played every snap in the win against Dallas.
“I take my body serious,” he said before the Dallas game. “It’s my resume, it’s my life. I take pride playing every Sunday. That’s just my goal, what I want to do.”
While it might not be showing up in the stats, Nixon is having an excellent season. He has one interception and six passes defensed – he ranked among the NFL leaders with 17 passes defensed last season – but has been sharp while playing a lot of man coverage.
He’s allowed a catch rate of 68.1 percent, compared to 61.0 percent last season, according to Pro Football Focus. However, he’s allowing only 9.0 yards per catch, he’s been guilty of just three penalties and hasn’t allowed a touchdown.
Along with Nixon, these four players did not practice: Linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), guard Travis Glover (knee), center Sean Rhyan (ankle) and tight end Josh Whyle (concussion).
Rhyan suffered an ankle injury early in the win against Detroit but the team opted to not place him on injured reserve, with coach Matt LaFleur saying before Thursday’s practice that it was only a short-term injury.
Micah Parsons made his practice debut on Wednesday. A big mile marker for a player returning from a major injury is his ability to stack practices. So, so far, so good for Parsons.
In the second big update on Thursday, one day after being limited participation in his debut, Parsons was back at it again.
Not babying Parsons back into it. Here he is playing the role of an o-lineman for big Chris McClellan. pic.twitter.com/jpcs1ABbDW
As was the case on Wednesday , perhaps the most noteworthy part of what Parsons did in front of reporters wasn’t his work as a defensive player. It’s that he stood in as an offensive lineman while getting knocked backward by big rookie defensive tackle Chris McClellan.
“It was good just to get him back out there,” LaFleur said.
The Packers' closer, Micah Parsons, delivered the perfect closing line at the end of his 14-minute conversation with reporters following his first practice today. ⬇️ https://t.co/PwSwqluMNq
The NFL on Thursday named safety Evan Williams its NFC Defensive Player of Month and cornerback Brandon Cisse its NFL Defensive Rookie of the Month.
“Yeah, it's in the rearview mirror,” Cisse said on Wednesday of the first half of his rookie season. “Yeah, just on it this week. How great can I be this week? How can I get better each day in practice? That's just kind of what my mindset is on that.
“I just try to make sure I come to work every day with something to get better at. I don't try to look back in the past or all the plays I made or all the plays I've been wrong, and because all that matters is what's here now and it's going about this weekend. So, I'm just preparing the right way.”
Cisse led all rookies with seven passes defensed in October.
Brandon Cisse is the NFL Defensive Rookie of the Month. Here are the notes from the league. pic.twitter.com/vmw4Cm6Lxx
Williams, according to the league, became the third safety since 2000 to record at least 40 tackles and three takeaways in a month, joining Rodney Harrison (October 2003 with New England) and George Wilson (October 2011 with Buffalo).
Evan Williams is the NFC Defensive Player of the Month. Here are the notes from the league. pic.twitter.com/DCeWQi9bWY
Among the players who did not practice for the Patriots on Wednesday was standout tight end Hunter Henry. He is leading the team with 29 receptions and is second with 326 yards but is dealing with an injured foot.
“I think he’s been someone for me that I can count on since my first snap in there my rookie year,” quarterback Drake Maye told reporters on Wednesday. “He’s been a security blanket and a great guy in the huddle, a great leader on this team.
“So, anytime you lose a guy like Hunter, a captain that does everything the right way, talks to the guys in the huddle, knows what I like, my body language, route running, does stuff in the run game. It’s tough. But I know he’ll do his best to get back out there as quick as he can.”
The teams will release their updated injury reports after Thursday’s practices. For now, here are the reports from Wednesday.

title: Two Trades That Could Save Packers’ Season (And Two Deals They Should Avoid)
full_text:
The trade deadline is looming, and while the Green Bay Packers are historically inactive on the day, they have changed their ways under general manager Brian Gutekunst. The Packers never signed big-money free agents, traded up in the draft or made aggressive moves for players like Micah Parsons until they did.
This year, the Packers reportedly have been making calls to gather some price points ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline.
Gutekunst has said before he wants to be in every conversation, even if he is unable to pull the trigger on every potential trade.
As a result, the Packers could acquire some help before the deadline strikes. They probably should. The NFC North is a blood war that just got tougher with Chicago’s addition of Jeffery Simmons last week. Simmons was incredibly impactful in his first game with the Bears. The Lions and Vikings have beaten the Packers this season.
Yes, Parsons will return to the lineup, which could be argued as just as good as making a deadline acquisition. He does not, however, solve the issues of Green Bay’s terrible run game or perilously thin defensive tackle group.
With that in mind, here are some moves the Packers should be looking at making, and others they should avoid.
Jonathan Taylor is awesome. There’s no denying that. He’s one of the top running backs in football but stuck on a terrible team. The Indianapolis Colts are mired in a rebuild and started selling off some pieces starting in late October when Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner were sent to two other NFC contenders, the Seahawks and 49ers, respectively.
Taylor would be the next logical piece to potentially get moved, and the Packers have a need in their run game .
So why should the Packers avoid acquiring the former Wisconsin Badgers legend?
Simply put, it would be a misuse of resources. The Colts are reportedly looking for either a first-round pick or something similar to the package of second- through fifth-round picks that the Carolina Panthers got when they traded Christian McCaffery to the San Francisco 49ers.
The Packers, of course, do not have a first-round pick thanks to last year’s deal for Micah Parsons.
As good as Taylor is, can he save the Packers’ putrid run game on his own? The answer is that it is unlikely.
While it should be noted that a team can only acquire what is on the market, if the Packers are willing to move significant draft capital, they should be looking for other spots on the roster.
According to ESPN, the Packers were interested in potentially acquiring Quenton Nelson before he was sent to Seattle.
ESPN has since connected the Packers to the market of Philadelphia Eagles star Landon Dickerson. Dickerson would give the offensive line some toughness and championship pedigree.
Dickerson has played mostly left guard with the Eagles, though he won the Rimington Award as the nation’s best center while at Alabama and started the 2024 NFC Championship Game against Washington with Cam Jurgens on the shelf for a back injury.
Dickerson and left tackle Jordan Mailata are the last men standing from the Eagles’ powerful 2024 offensive line that steamrolled its way to a title. Jurgens was traded to Baltimore and Lane Johnson retired with physical issues and a desire to focus on his mental health.
The issue with Dickerson are the injuries from his career are starting to pile up. He had two separate ACL injuries from college and struggled with a meniscus injury and bone bruise as recently as this year.
The Packers have enough issues with offensive linemen with uncertain injury histories. The other issue, which is a solvable problem of sorts, is where would he play?
Including playoffs, Dickerson has played 5,478 snaps at left guard, 81 snaps at center and 91 snaps at right guard, according to Pro Football Focus. The Packers have a need at center with Sean Rhyan sidelined with a high-ankle sprain. Left guard, however, belongs to Aaron Banks as evidenced by their actions.
Trading for Dickerson, only to ask him to play right guard, would be another misuse of resources and another case of playing musical chairs along the offensive line when it’s unnecessary.
With the asking price likely to be a mid-round pick, there could be better options that present themselves.
We just finished saying not to trade for Jonathan Taylor because of the price point. That is different than saying the Packers should not be in the market for a running back at all.
The Packers need help at running back, regardless of whether or not Josh Jacobs remains on the field. Jacobs’ backups have done little to inspire confidence in their ability to do much of anything in his absence or since his return to action.
Jacobs’ future is uncertain because of new information that emerged during the legal process of his situation.
Enter Tony Pollard. Pollard is stuck on a bad Tennessee team but is averaging 4.5 yards per carry and has forced 23 missed tackles, according to PFF. When Jacobs is at his best, he is good at breaking tackles, but the rest of the backfield depth chart appears to go down at first contact. Pollard could be a starter in Jacobs’ place or someone who could capably back him up.
Since he’s not nearly as accomplished as Taylor, Pollard will likely be much less expensive. That could put him in the price range the Packers should be shopping in.
Reports surfaced earlier this week that the Patriots were looking to move defensive lineman Christian Barmore.
“They have listened and talked to other teams about trading him. My understanding is the price would be about a fourth-round pick,” Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer told NBC Sports Boston . “This is a player that very clearly is available, and if somebody’s willing to swing the Patriots a fourth-round pick, I think something could happen.”
If that’s the case, the Packers should be all over a move like that one as they are slated to have a surplus of fourth-round picks. They own their own pick as well as Dallas’ fourth-round pick thanks to an offseason deal of Rashan Gary. Plus, the free-agent departure of Romeo Doubs could net a fourth-round compensatory pick.
That surplus could help the Packers add to a defensive tackle room that is one rolled ankle away from getting very thin.
They could also use some more impact in that room. Devonte Wyatt has not lived up to his billing following last year’s season-ending injury. Chris McClellan has had some nice moments but is a rookie. Karl Brooks has worn down each of the last two seasons and is better suited when he’s in a rotational role.
Javon Hargrave is out for the season, Warren Brinson is on injured reserve and Anthony Campbell is a former undrafted free agent.
Barmore has 3.5 sacks and 10 pressures this season. Last year, he had 50 pressures, according to PFF.
The Packers could use more disruption in the middle of their defensive line, and Barmore fits the bill.
The Patriots are unlikely to move Barmore to Green Bay when they are slated to play each other this weekend, but if the price is truly a fourth-round pick, that is a move the Packers should be all over as soon as Monday.

title: 3 Safeties Texans Could Target Ahead of NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
Just days ahead of the NFL trade deadline, the Houston Texans had been liked to some reported interest from SI 's Albert Breer surrounding two particular positions to potentially add to their roster: that was running back and safety.
And when breaking it down, you can understand why the Texans could be interested in adding another piece at either position at the deadline.
Both position groups have seen injury and underwhelming performance over the first eight weeks of the season, and the Texans could have a simple route to an upgrade at either spot by pulling the trigger on a trade at the deadline.
We've already broke down some of the top running backs that the Texans could consider a move for last week. But who are some of the safeties that Houston's front office could try and acquire before Tuesday's deadline?
Let's take a look at three safeties that could make sense for the Texans to call about:
Here's a low-cost depth addition that could make sense for both the Texans and the Jets' perspective.
Cisco is in the last year of his current contract, has seen a near career-low snap share of 35% this year in New York, and might be a candidate that their front office wants to move off of before he's let go this offseason.
Enter the Texans, who don't have to force Cisco into any big responsibilities on an already loaded defense, but add him in as someone who can provide depth at a position of need, and has over 50 games of starting experience through his six years in pro.
Another reason to consider Cisco: there's a chance the Texans could simply part ways with as low as a seventh-round pick to land him. That's a worthwhile investment to make if it helps move the needle forward for the production of this underwhelming secondary.
Here's a big fish that the Texans could consider, if they were willing to spend a bit more of a premium at the deadline.
Bates is a proven All-Pro talent at the safety position. He'd be a major statement addition to any secondary if traded at the deadline, but especially so for the Texans. And if the Falcons wind up dropping to 3-6 this weekend against Bates' former team in the Cincinnati Bengals, maybe a move is considered.
Bates is on the last year of his current contract, and would make for just over a $6 million cap hit for the rest of the season for any team acquiring him. The Texans could narrowly squeeze him on the books , but there's a good chance he ends up as a half-year rental.
But don't expect the Falcons to part ways with Bates for just anything. He's fresh off a Second-Team All-Pro appearance in 2025, and has had a strong start to 2026. He's had a nose for the ball by finding his way to four total turnovers in eight games, paired with 46 combined tackles.
I'd expect the Texans to give up at least a mid-round pick in exchange for Bates, and there's a chance a player could be sent out in a deal like this as well. Combining the cost with the implications that come his expiring contract, this could be wishful thinking to expect Houston to take the gamble here.
The Texans have already sparked a reunion with one of their former defensive standouts earlier this year by signing 2014 No. 1 pick Jadeveon Clowney . Why not add to that list with someone like Saints safety Justin Reid?
Reid has been a valuable starter for the Saints' back-end for the past season and a half, so there might not be a ton of interest from New Orleans to consider a trade.
But Reid is turning 30 years old in February, and could be on a 2-6 roster by the end of this weekend. Trading a productive veteran like him for future assets seems like a perfect way to get a head start on the offseason ahead.
And for the Texans, adding Reid offers an answer to their rumored safety concerns with a proven starter under contract for this season and next, and only hits the books for a $650K cap hit for the remainder of this season.
Reid might be the best candidate for the Texans to look towards on this list: someone who would command a solid investment of a mid-to-late round pick, but would offer a steady sense of security at the position that Houston seems to be looking for at the deadline.

title: Texans Final Injury Report for Week 9 vs. Chargers: Who's In, Who's Out
full_text:

OUT - S Reed Blankenship (hand/concussion) OUT - RB David Montgomery (groin)

There's optimism that Blankenship will be able to return next week. But until then, the Texans will be leaning on M.J. Stewart as their starting safety opposite Calen Bullock.
As for those who were previously on the Texans' injury report that are now officially ready to suit up, that includes Pro Bowl linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair and star defensive back Jalen Pitre , who each were able to log full practices over the past two days.

Joe Alt is back starting on the left side of the offensive line. Ladd McConkey is back to full health after getting banged up earlier in the year, and this could give Los Angeles a bit more optimism than normal for Week 9 at home against the Texans.

title: What Texans' Jadeveon Clowney Said About Swirling Trade Rumors
full_text:
The Houston Texans haven't found themselves involved with too many trade rumors in the days leading up to the NFL trade deadline.
However, one rumor that did begin floating around over the Texans' bye week is the report that teams were interested in defensive end Jadeveon Clowney , according to ESPN 's Adam Schefter.
Another pass rusher who has generated some interest ahead of next Tuesday’s trade deadline is Houston defensive end Jadeveon Clowney. https://t.co/haFgCAaWA8
Seeing Clowney involved in trade rumors did come as a bit of a surprise initially.
The Texans just signed Clowney right before the regular season as a depth piece in their already-stout edge rusher group headlined by Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter. And halfway through the season, he still fills a key role in this defense as Houston's primary EDGE3 on the depth chart.
So do the Texans actually have any intent on trading Clowney ? And what did Clowney himself have to say about the rumors involving his name just days ahead of the trade deadline?
In a recent live stream heading into Week 9's game vs. the LA Chargers, KPRC2 insider Aaron Wilson revealed that he had talked to Clowney on Thursday about the recent trade rumors he was linked to.
Overall, it still feels like Clowney wants to remain in Houston for the season, and the Texans want to keep him around past the deadline.
However, the whole situation does come a bit out of Clowney's control.
"They weren't shopping him," Wilson said of the Texans' Clowney rumors. "I actually talked to him about it today, and he's open to whatever. But he'd prefer to be here."
"He's not fighting it. He doesn't even have a no-trade clause. There's not much he can do without it."
Through the five games that Clowney has played on the season so far, he's been a bit less involved compared to some of the earlier stops in his career. But he's still remained a productive pass-rusher in the process.
Clowney has put together a total of nine tackles, two TFLs, and 1.5 sacks, all while playing in less than 40% of the Texans' defensive snaps.
Perhaps teams around the league in need of a pass-rusher could see the Texans' lack of usage for Clowney, paired with their lowly result to start the year with a 2-5 record, and see it as an opportunity to strike on a cheap veteran on a one-year deal for the second half of the season .
Yet, given the Texans have a clear role for Clowney on their defense and the team as a whole is eager to continue to try and climb out of their early-season role, Houston's front office would have to get a really intriguing asset offered their way to consider moving off of their nine-year NFL veteran.
So don't hold your breath on a Clowney trade happening barring any unforeseen changes. Maybe a loss against the Chargers this weekend changes the mindset in the building. But as of right now, Clowney himself is content with staying, while the Texans' front office isn't actively shopping him around.

title: Texans Have Reported Trade Interest at Two Positions of Need
full_text:
The Houston Texans are quickly closing in on the NFL trade deadline.
And to this point, the chatter surrounding what the Texans could do in the days ahead to shake up their roster has been relatively quiet.
Texans general manager Nick Caserio noted at the bye that Houston has talked to essentially every team around the league leading up to the deadline, but didn't hint that any move was imminent.
However, according to a new report from SI' s Albert Breer , there's a couple of positions of need that the Texans have been rumored to add at the trade deadline.
Per Breer's latest trade deadline notebook, he mentioned that the Texans have "checked in" on available running backs and safeties.
As to which specific players the Texans could be looking to target is still a bit of a mystery. However, you can understand why Houston's front office might have its eye on those two positions for a potential upgrade.
At running back, the Texans have been hit with some early-season injuries and haven't exactly produced as well as expected heading into the year.
Veteran running back David Montgomery has been sidelined since suffering a groin injury in Week 5 vs. the Tennessee Titans that has left him out for essentially four games. Jawhar Jordan has also been placed on injured reserve after a standout performance in Week 6.
That's led to Houston's depth chart at running back being led by Woody Marks, Dare Ogunbowale, and newly-signed Emari Demercado heading into Week 9 against the Los Angeles Chargers.
Therefore, if there's an upgrade for the backfield that the Texans could add for the right price at the deadline, bringing in an extra ball carrier to lean on for the second half of the season might not be the worst idea.
At the safety position, the Texans have also dealt with lingering injuries and overall poor performance.
Not only has offseason signing Reed Blankenship struggled in his first few games with Houston, he's also been out with a concussion/hand injury for both Weeks 7 and Week 9 after the bye. Jalen Pitre has also missed time with a shoulder injury, but is expected to return against the Chargers.
If there's any chance that Blankenship is expected to miss more time than initially expected, or if the Texans simply want to make an upgrade at the safety position that's been pretty underwhelming through the first half of the season, now at the trade deadline would be a perfect time to do so.
The Texans currently rank 29th in the NFL for passing yards allowed, and have logged a total of three interceptions through seven games. Adding another solid safety for depth in the back-end could be a route that Houston's front office takes as well.
Houston will have until 3 p.m. CT on Tuesday, November 10th, to finalize any moves on the trade market before the deadline hits. But at the very least, those two rumored positions of interest will give Texans fans more reason to keep an eye on this team in the days ahead.

title: Texans' 3 Biggest Keys to Victory vs. Chargers to Escape 2-5 Hole
full_text:
The 2-5 Houston Texans have a pivotal game on the horizon in Week 9, as they'll be taking a West Coast road trip to face the 0-7 Los Angeles Chargers.
Really, it's a pivotal game for both sides . A loss for Houston here would tank them to a 2-6 record on the year, a record that only three teams in NFL history have been able to come back from for a postseason appearance.
A loss for the Chargers means that they fall to a dreary 0-8 on the year. And with only a few days away from the trade deadline, there might be some big moves to consider for this roster in order to better prepare for a key offseason in 2027.
So how can the Texans bounce back from their latest loss to the New York Giants and keep hopes alive for a late push to the playoffs?
Let's take a look at three of the Texans' biggest keys to the game as they head on the road to face the Chargers:
The last time the Texans' offense took the field in Week 7 vs. the Giants, we saw Nico Collins held down to one of his worst performances in recent memory . His two receptions for six yards rank as the second-lowest receiving total of his career.
That result simply can't be the case again this week for Houston. The Texans' offensive staff needs to get Collins back to being deemed an alpha, WR1 on a weekly basis, and getting him a chance to execute on at least a half-dozen targets.
The Chargers have done a pretty good job of limiting Collins in their past matchups, considering he averages just five targets per game for over 73 yards. But Collins has also been able to log some explosive performances against this defense as well.
In Houston's Wild Card matchup back in 2025, Collins finished with seven receptions for 122 yards and a touchdown; his best playoff performance to date, and one of just seven times in his career where he's posted over 120 receiving yards and a touchdown in the same game.
If the Texans can find their way to a similar statline for Collins this weekend, it's hard to imagine this Chargers offense having the horses to keep up with that Houston scoring production.
Among the Chargers' weaknesses on the offensive side of the ball, one of their most dreadful has been just how reckless the unit has been when it comes to ball security and limiting turnovers.
It's often said that NFL games are defined by the turnover battle. And that's certainly been the case for the Chargers many times this season. Los Angeles has lost the turnover battle in five of their first seven games through the 2026 campaign.
So for a Texans defense that has the ball-hawking talent in the secondary and a pair of ferocious contributors off the edge , getting multiple takeaways can be an easy way to get a defining leg up on Los Angeles.
The Texans haven't been a defense that has racked up as many turnovers as they put together over the course of their 2025 season. They've accumulated just six total giveaways over the first seven weeks, a number that was sitting at 11 through the first seven weeks of last year.
But this game, on paper, seems like one where the Texans can take ahold of a "get right game," and hopefully provide some much-needed momentum within the takeaways category heading into the second half of the regular season.
Another area in which the Chargers' offense has struggled in their first seven games of the season: limiting sacks on Justin Herbert.
Herbert is currently tied with the second-most sacks in the NFL with 23 as part of the Chargers' winless start. He's been hit with at least three sacks in five of his first seven games.
Being without starting right tackle Rashawn Slater––and for a two-game stretch, starting left tackle Joe Alt––certainly hasn't helped their case, but it's clear that this offensive line has been underproducing through the first half of the regular season.
And this week, they'll be up against one of their toughest matchups of the season thus far, with Texans' star duo Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter off the edge . So it's hard to imagine things start to look a whole lot better for the Chargers and their pass protection in Week 9.
The one name I'll be keeping an eye on is none other than Will Anderson. After Anderson got off to a roaring start through the first five games by recording a league-leading 7.5 sacks on the year, he's been held to zero sacks over the past two weeks.
If Anderson can get back on track as the Defensive Player of the Year favorite, many were talking him up to be a couple of weeks ago. It’ll be a long day for the Chargers' offense, which has been the case already for multiple games throughout the season.

title: Texans Need to Trade for RB After David Montgomery Injury Update
full_text:
The Houston Texans will be without veteran running back David Montgomery for at least one more game –– per head coach DeMeco Ryans.
According to Ryans after the Texans' first practice of the week before facing the LA Chargers, Montgomery has already been ruled out for this weekend as he continues to rehab from his lingering groin injury he's been working back from since Week 5 .
DeMeco Ryans said RB David Montgomery has made some progress but added that he'll be out on Sunday vs. the Chargers.
Montgomery will continue to be listed as week-to-week, but there's still no exact date to circle just yet for when the Texans' lead running back will return to the lineup.
And with that mysterious timeline in mind, perhaps there's a case to be made for the Texans to go out and trade for another running back before the NFL trade deadline arrives early next week.
Now, it wasn't too long ago when the Texans made their initial trade to bring Montgomery into the building in the first place.
Houston sent multiple day three draft picks and Juice Scruggs to the Detroit Lions earlier this offseason to add Montgomery as a one-two punch for Woody Marks, and hope to elevate this lackluster rushing attack for their 2026 campaign.
But as we now arrive to the halfway point of the Texans' 2026 season, those improvements in the run game haven't quite come to fruition as expected.
While C.J. Stroud has helped lead the way in the passing game for positive strides, Houston ranks 29th in the NFL for total rushing yards (593) and yards per attempt (3.6) through their first seven games.
When Montgomery has been on the field for the Texans, he's been largely inefficient and ineffective . He's averaging just 2.7 yards per carry and less than 30 yards on the ground per game.
Marks has managed to be a bright spot in the Texans' ground game. But otherwise, the rushing production could certainly use a facelift heading into the second half of the season, as well as a healthy counterpart for Marks to lean on if Montgomery is sidelined longer than expected.
The Texans have a couple of different approaches to take here when it comes to improving their running back room at the deadline.
On one hand, Houston could take a massive swing at the position to push the chips in for this season. But that might not be a super realistic result to expect.
Jonathan Taylor might be too hard to pry away from the Texans' AFC South rivals, the Indianapolis Colts, and the Philadelphia Eagles have already made it clear to Saquon Barkley that he won't be traded at the deadline .
Or, the Texans can take a different approach: add a depth piece at a lower cost who can work alongside Marks, and Montgomery whenever he's back to 100%.
That route seems like a much more favorable bet to see the Texans consider. As to which running backs fall into that bucket? Guys like TreVeyon Henderson, Devin Singletary and Tony Pollard have all seen their names in some lingering trade rumors in the past several days, and could give Houston some targets to keep an eye on.
However, at the very least, running back should be a position of need on the Texans' radar from now up until next week's trade deadline.
This is one of the final moments of the season in which the front office can go out to add an immediate upgrade to their roster before taking on the second half of their schedule (and the postseason), and being without a stable ground game will only hurt the Texans' offense long-term.
Adding one more reliable ball carrier into the room could add some much-needed security and stability on the ground, while also providing a backup plan in case Montgomery is at all limited after recovering from his lengthy groin injury absence.

title: Why Texans' Week 9 Game vs. Chargers Matters More Than You Think
full_text:
The Houston Texans are just days away from their Week 9 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers –– a game that sets up as a pivotal one as this team sits at a 2-5 record through their first seven games.
But the Texans' game against the Chargers might be more than just pivotal.
A win, of course, would be a nice lift for Houston's chances at a late-season turnaround at a 3-5 record. And with a few more winnable matchups up ahead on their schedule, the tide can turn pretty quickly for this team as it did around this time last season.
However, a loss against the Chargers that puts the Texans to just 2-6 might hold even more gravity moving forward. Especially with the NFL trade deadline right around the corner , a loss here in Week 9 might be what pushes Houston over the edge to sell off some assets on a potentially lost season.
If the Texans were to drop to a 2-6 record on the year, they'd be up against a pretty uphill climb to make the postseason, especially when looking back at just how many times it's been done across NFL history.
Only three teams in the history of the league have climbed out of a 2-6 hole for a spot in the playoffs: the 1970 Cincinnati Bengals, the 2020 Washington Football Team, and the 2022 Jacksonville Jaguars.
Simply put, it's not easy for a team to pull off seven or more wins in the second half of the season after facing some immense struggles early in the year. The Texans did manage to do similar last year as they came back from 0-3, then 3-5, but a loss here against the Chargers would feel a little bit different.
The Chargers, at many times over the past several weeks, have looked like the worst team in football this season.
Los Angeles has had the lowest scoring offense in the NFL through eight weeks, is the 20th-best scoring defense, and has given up the most turnovers in the league.
If the Texans were to lose back-to-back games against the New York Giants , then the winless Chargers––especially knowing that Houston is coming fresh off a bye––it'd be pretty tough to have optimism that this team is capable of making the climb to the postseason, let alone make a deep run with multiple playoff wins.
So then, the Texans could turn their attention to some trade deadline moves; and moves with a mindset to sell off some of their talent on the roster, rather than be buyers.
Perhaps Jadeveon Clowney can get shipped off to a contender . Maybe a receiver gets dealt. Wyatt Teller and Braden Smith could be on their way out. And then, the tone of Houston's remaining season changes for the worst.
That's what makes this weekend's game so important against the Chargers. A win sets up for a much-needed bounce back after the bye, and puts Houston at the same record they sat at this time last year.
A loss, though, might just be the first domino to fall for what could inevitably be a lost season in Houston.

title: 3 Players Texans Should Call About Before the NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Houston Texans are less than a week away from the NFL trade deadline.
And when taking a step back to look at where this team stands heading into Week 9 with their 2-5 record, it's hard to tell whether or not the Texans will be true buyers or sellers over the course of the next few days.
However, the Texans and their front office are still bound to do their due diligence by calling around the league and asking about the availability of a select few players in a potential deal––if the price is right.
With that in mind, let's sort through three players who could be deemed trade candidates at the deadline that the Texans should call about in the days ahead:
The Texans' run game has been–– to put things bluntly–– lackluster through the first half of their 2026 campaign. And heading into Week 9 against the LA Chargers, Houston will be without their offseason trade addition David Montgomery for a third-straight game due to a lingering groin injury .
That's left this Texans' run game lacking in both production and overall depth. So there's a good case to be made that Houston could go out and add a low-cost veteran to their backfield at the deadline to iron out some of those concerns.
So why not try to spark a reunion with a former Texan in Devin Singletary? While he projects to have a bigger role in New York with Tyrone Tracy being placed on injured reserve, it wouldn't hurt for Houston to at least give the Giants a call on the eight-year veteran.
Singletary brings in another layer of depth in the backfield, has proven to be productive in multiple situations throughout his career, and even had one of his most impressive seasons back in 2023 with the Texans, logging over 1,000 scrimmage yards and four touchdowns.
For a day three pick (or a couple), maybe the Texans could strike a deal with the Giants in hopes that Singletary can complement this backfield led by Woody Marks, and hopefully Montgomery in the next couple of weeks.
This would certainly be the biggest swing the Texans could take on this list, but adding Eagles offensive lineman Landon Dickerson might not be out of the realm of imagination.
The Eagles are 2-6 and could be due to hit the trade market as sellers at the trade deadline. Someone like Dickerson could be a premier piece on their roster who can generate a good bit of value if the front office were to ship him out.
And the Texans could have a perfect spot for Dickerson up front as their starting left guard . Dickerson would allow Keylan Rutledge to slide over at center, paired with Ed Ingram at right guard, and forge together a really solid three-man unit on the interior.
Dickerson hasn't played extremely well this season. He's logged a 54.5 overall grade on the season via Pro Football Focus , and ranks in the bottom five of eligible guards for his pass-blocking grade (36.2).
However, that allows the Texans to potentially buy low on his value and hope that a new situation in Houston can spark production from earlier in his career. Maybe a fourth-round pick and another day-three pick could pique the Eagles' interest.
It also helps knowing that Dickerson has just one penalty called against him so far this season. Limiting those flags on the offensive line will be key for the Texans' offensive success moving into the second half of the season, and Dickerson could be an easy plug-and-play guard to do just that.
The Texans' secondary has really struggled this season compared to how elite they looked over the course of their 2026 campaign.
Houston currently ranks 28th in the NFL for total passing yards allowed (1,708), and 20th for net yards gained per pass (6.4) through their first eight games of the season.
And those struggles have really shown in games that Jalen Pitre has been on the sidelines, which has been the case for the Texans' last two games.
This week against the Chargers, Pitre is expected to make his return after he was able to practice on Wednesday. That's good news for the Texans and their hopes of turning things around in the secondary. But that shouldn't stop Houston from adding more depth at the nickel position if the price is right.
One name that could make sense for the Texans is Taron Johnson of the Las Vegas Raiders, who's in his age-30 season under contract for this year and next, and has been relatively productive between his time with both the Raiders and the Buffalo Bills.
Could the Texans part ways with a mid-round pick for Johnson? Maybe the Raiders want to hang onto their starting nickel, knowing that they could be within reach of a Wild Card spot this season.
But in the event Las Vegas wants to sell off an aging veteran for a Houston team that's desperate for a lift in their secondary, this is a move that could add up for both sides.

title: Texans' Latest David Montgomery Injury Update Should Raise Concerns
full_text:
The Houston Texans have been a bit depleted in their running back room because of their recent injury to veteran David Montgomery, who's been sidelined with a groin injury dating back to the first half of their Week 5 game against the Tennessee Titans .
Since Montgomery first went down, the Texans had labeled his status as "week-to-week," expecting to be an issue that could resolve itself after the bye, but wasn't anything that required the veteran running back to be placed on injured reserve.
However, now nearly a month removed from the injury to Montgomery, it seems like Houston still won't be getting him back in the lineup ahead of their Week 9 game vs. the LA Chargers .
According to Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans, the Texans will be without Montgomery for another week against the Chargers because of his lingering groin injury, but adds that the running back has made "some progress" in his recovery.
"David is still sidelined. He'll be out still," Ryans said on Wednesday. "We're trying to get him out on the field; trying to get him going. But right now, it's still week-to-week. But he has made some progress."
That's not exactly the most optimistically sounding update for the Texans' starting running back–– especially coming so early in the week.
Rather than the Texans attempting to give Montgomery a few attempts to go in practice over the course of this week before facing the Chargers, Houston has prematurely ruled him out multiple days before the weekend even arrives.
That means Montgomery will be missing over a month and at least three games while still recovering from said injury, and still might not be officially ready by the time the Texans are ready to take on the Cleveland Browns in Week 10.
In reality, Montgomery seems to have a real chance of missing four games on the Texans' schedule (on top of the extra time he was able to get during the bye last week). That's the stint of any player taken out of the lineup to then be placed on short-term injured reserve; an approach that Montgomery and Houston did not take.
So what's really going on with Montgomery here? In reality, we might not have a clear picture until arriving at next week's practice. If he's able to participate in any capacity then, that'll be a good sign for his in-game availability next weekend.
But until then, it'll be Woody Marks continuing to take the lead as the Texans' No. 1 running back against the Chargers, which is a role he's started to find his grove in quite well.
Over the course of the past three games, the Texans have given Marks at least 19 touches a game to average over 80 yards from scrimmage throughout those matchups.
Expect Houston to continue leaning on Marks in the backfield until further notice while still patiently waiting for his veteran counterpart to return from injury.
