Jared Koch is the Publisher of Houston Texans On SI. He has covered the NFL and NBA with On SI since 2023, and is a graduate of Western Kentucky University.

title: Week 8 Film Review: CJ Allen's First Start Provides Hope for Colts' Future
full_text:
It's fair to say that nearly halfway through his rookie season, CJ Allen's path to consistent playing time  has been arduous.
Lauded early on by recently fired general manager Chris Ballard as a "special dude" , Allen had to fight through injury and questionable personnel decisions to receive his first opportunity in the starting lineup.
"He stands for all the right stuff. He's an athletic, fast MIKE. He'll be a green-dot guy for us from the get-go. I mean, he's a face of the program type of guy. He's a really special dude now,' Ballard said about CJ Allen after drafting him 53rd overall in the 2026 NFL Draft.
Unfortunately for the Georgia product, his first shot at significant playing time ended in a monumental drubbing at the hands of the Jacksonville Jaguars .
However, as I will cover throughout the rest of this article, little of the blame should be attributed to Allen . Granted, anytime a defense gives up thirty-five points to an opposing offense, there will be some mistakes committed by its spine.
Nevertheless, for a rookie making his first start against Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars , I came away impressed with his play, especially against the run. In my opinion, there weren't many coverage reps that showcased specific proclivities in that department.
It'll likely require a much different game script than the one the Indianapolis Colts found themselves in last Sunday to see meaningful coverage reps for the young rookie.
pic.twitter.com/acV9dbeQRX
One of the more memorable plays from CJ Allen's first start was this sack coming off a play action drop back.
The reason Allen gets a free run at Trevor Lawrence is because of the stunt game up front executed by Adetomiwa Adebawore and Grover Stewart. Tomi starts from a 4i alignment on the right side of the formation and hesitates at the snap to allow Stewart to collision the right guard. This sets Adebawore free to loop back around and preoccupy the center and left guard. In some defenses this is simply called an "Indian" stunt.
Grover does a fantastic job occupying the "whole man" of the right guard and not allowing him to get hands on Allen, who has a chasm in the B-gap to run through.
One reason I wanted to highlight this play is because of the way CJ Allen finished the sack. Time and time again the Colts have failed to finish sacks on the rare occasion they've generated pressure.
Highest pressure rate this season, per @NextGenStats : 1. Vikings – 45.8% 2. Jets – 41.3% 3. Rams – 41.0% 4. Broncos – 40.3% 5. Packers – 40.2% Lowest pressure rate: 28. 49ers – 32.0% 29. Eagles – 31.5% 30. Cardinals – 31.5% 31. Saints – 31.4% 32. Colts – 26.5%
pic.twitter.com/3CHdHmcYdI
This play looks to be an outside zone run by the Jaguars that gets blown up by Grover Stewart getting his helmet on the outside shoulder of the left guard and not allowing the center or guard to climb to either linebacker. We also get a gap exchange between Akeem Davis-Gaither, who immediately scrapes to the playside C gap, and Laiatu Latu, who knifes inside the left tackle's base block, forcing Bhayshul Tuten to cut back into CJ Allen.
Allen does a great job recognizing fast flow away from him and beats the climbing backside guard to the spot. He's able to "get skinny" and dip his shoulder underneath the bigger offensive lineman to penetrate the cutback lane.
I'd like to see the rookie finish off Tuten in the hole, rather than allowing him to fall forward after an awkward tackle attempt. However everything else about this rep, from the play recognition to the block avoidance was stellar.
pic.twitter.com/D0ANl2JFwz
The Jaguars motion to an offset I set out of 13 personnel and end up running what I'm effectively calling "double iso". Since the Colts are in an under front, the center and playside guard double Grover Stewart at nose, leaving the offset tight end isolated on CJ Allen. Another tight end wraps into the C gap and is isolated on Cam Bynum.
CJ Allen knows he needs to "take grass" on the tight end, so he attacks downhill and collisions the lead blocker. He does so with his outside shoulder on the inside half of the blocker to "spill" the ball carrier to a teammate. The violence with which he attacks downhill ensures the lead blocker can't get vertical displacement, and allows Mooney Ward a nice clean picture to fit into when Tuten hits the hole.
pic.twitter.com/dBxf4VBabG
The Jaguars run outside zone towards CJ Allen this time. The right tackle completely washes Allen out of the run fit, and he fails to make the tackle from behind once the running back breaks into open space.
The issue here is allowing the offensive linemen to get frame to frame with him. Once Cole Van Lanen was able to square the rookie up and get his hands inside his chest, he was never going to be able to deconstruct the block.
This Bhayshul Tuten touchdown was the result of several catastrophic breakdowns in the Colts defense. That happened far too many times on Sunday, and wasn't always due to the failures of one player. That is yet another unfortunate trend that has permeated throughout the Colts' 2026 season.
pic.twitter.com/RH1ESLBvnX
The final play I chose to highlight was this lead toss play. I think Allen may be looking for play action or even be boot/counter/reverse responsible. Either way, after widening with the fast motion of the receiver, he's a tick late getting back over the top, and gets cut off by the right guard.
The second play I highlighted showed Allen getting skinny and giving the blocker less surface area to get hands on him. I'd like to see something similar in this instance. Instead he allows the blocker to completely drive him out of the play as he fights to get over the top.
Like with any player, there are certainly some reps that CJ Allen would have liked to have back. But on the whole, I thought he showed substantial promise in his first career start.
There will probably be times throughout his career where he has difficulty tracking the ball carrier through the hole due to his lack of elite size, but the speed in which he attacks open space and his tenacity coming downhill stood out on film. On several plays Allen's pre-snap communication revealed he had a good idea of what run play was coming at him, and the majority of his post-snap reactions were evidence that the rookie has played high level football for a long time.
Akeem Davis-Gaither, the Colts' primary starting linebacker thus far, was downgraded to out for Week 9, so CJ Allen is slated to assume green dot duties for the first time in his career.
Indianapolis' second-round pick provided another reason for fans to turn one eye towards the future last Sunday, even as Indy's season as a whole took another turn towards going completely down the drain.

title: Trade Talks Are Heating Up For Daniel Jones: Where Colts Currently Stand
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts have kicked off their rebuild with a fire sale of its current roster .
Owner/CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon turned to assistant manager Ed Dodds after firing longtime general manager Chris Ballard, and he's been tasked with the responsibility of netting draft capital for players who don't fit the Colts' plans.
Longtime franchise cornerstones in left guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner were the first to see the door, and running back Jonathan Taylor, wide receiver Josh Downs, and defensive tackle Grover Stewart have been the top remaining Colts candidates who are most likely to be traded ahead of the November 10th deadline.
However, there's one player who has surprisingly been named a potential trade candidate over the past week: quarterback Daniel Jones.
What first appeared as merely a rumor has evolved into legitimate smoke.
The Indianapolis Colts are reportedly receiving calls from multiple teams across the league regarding Daniel Jones's services, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .
Jones has done his best to right the sinking ship in Indianapolis, but unfortunately, it's not been enough. The Colts' starting quarterback, who is in his first season since tearing his Achilles tendon, has mightily struggled this season, but such regression is not all on him, and teams across the league have recognized that.
Instead of thinking Jones has reverted to his normal self, some teams think he can replicate his early-season success from 2025 with the ideal situation and supporting cast. As a result, teams have been calling Indianapolis to see what it'll take to add Jones to their late-season roster.
As we covered earlier this week , the Baltimore Ravens and the Minnesota Vikings have been floated around as the most likely suitors. The former has since traded for quarterback Jacoby Brissett, effectively taking them out of the Daniel Jones sweepstakes, though the latter remains a viable option.
As of now, the Vikings plan to move forward with Carson Wentz as Kyler Murray deals with a sore hamstring, but there's enough smoke surrounding the hypothetical that sends Jones to Minnesota that warrants a trade watch.
Jones and Vikings' head coach Kevin O'Connell spent the back half of the 2024 regular season together after the longtime Giants' quarterback was traded to Minnesota for a fresh start, and their familiarity and time well spent together suggest a reunion is on the table almost two years later.
Furthermore, The Ringer's Tom Pelissero reported that the Colts have told interested teams they aren’t trading Daniel Jones.
In my humble opinion, this feels like a ploy from the Colts' side to try to net more interest and subsequent compensation, because if it's not, Indianapolis would be giving us an all-time case of malpractice.
However, it's worth noting that Pelissero has a strong history of source-reporting from within the Colts' building. He typically has the best grasp on what's going on behind the scenes in Indianapolis among national reporters, so I'm hoping this is merely a negotiation tactic of sorts.
It would be irresponsible for the Colts not to take any draft capital-related return for Daniel Jones, full stop.
Even though Jones signed a two-year, $88 million deal earlier this offseason, his contract is tradeable.
Jones is on a base salary of $5.49 million, with $510K in per-game roster bonuses ($30K/game). Trading him would mean his $44 million signing bonus would be a sunk cost for the Colts.
Jones has a $10.51 million injury guarantee for the 2027 season that becomes fully guaranteed on March 15 should he remain on the Colts' roster. Indianapolis could elect to bench Jones down the stretch to avoid triggering said guarantee, but there's also another option.
According to Rapoport's sources, Jones could waive the injury guarantee in question if that's what ends up holding him back from being traded elsewhere.
The Colts were already likely to part ways with Jones in the upcoming offseason, but netting draft capital on top of getting him off the books sooner rather than later would be an unexpectedly fantastic next step in kicking off the rebuild.
Indianapolis Colts' head coach Shane Steichen has been steadfast in his belief in Jones, and he'll continue to start him, so long as he has the opportunity.
"Daniel (Jones) will be our starting quarterback," Steichen said about the Colts' starting quarterback role for Week 9 and beyond.
"Obviously, evaluating the tape, looking back at it, some things he could do better, some things that we need to help him with moving forward. But I do feel that Daniel gives the best chance to win right now.”
Jones's preparation and mindset have given him the edge in Indianapolis, and now teams across the league are intrigued to add him to their roster for a late-season push.
The Colts continuing to play their top trade candidates through the deadline doesn't seem like the best idea, but if Jones can do enough in what could be his last game with Indianapolis, they'll look like geniuses.
Regardless of what it took to get there, if the Indianapolis Colts can find a trade partner for Daniel Jones, even if the compensation is a lowly future seventh-round draft selection, this will officially be successful start to the rebuild.
Only time will tell, and we're running out of it as the NFL Trade Deadline on November 10th at 4 PM EST is within striking distance.
Noah Compton is the Publisher of Indianapolis Colts On SI. Noah is from the Indy area and has been covering the Colts since 2022, including stops at FanSided, The Blue Stable, and SBNation.

title: Colts-Cowboys Injury Report: CJ Allen Takes on Bigger Role, Cowboys Navigate Week 9 Injury Concerns
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts and Dallas Cowboys have released their final injury reports ahead of Sunday's Week 9 matchup, providing a clearer picture of what each team will be working with. Both sides have several notable developments to sort through, with potential implications for their respective lineups as they prepare for a cross-conference matchup.
Let’s take a look at both team’s final injury reports.
Akeem Davis-Gaither's absence will mark an important milestone in rookie CJ Allen's development, as the Colts will turn to the rookie to take over defensive playcalling duties. Davis-Gaither has served as Indianapolis' primary green-dot for much of the season, making Allen's transition an important step in his progression. After making his first career start against Jacksonville last week, Allen will now have the extra responsibility of communicating defensive play calls and helping lead the unit on the field. Sunday will provide a clearer idea of just how ready Allen is to take over as the defensive leader.
Walley, meanwhile, will miss his second consecutive game after suffering a knee injury against Minnesota in Week 7. His continued absence leaves an open void in the slot. Kenneth Harris and Kapena Gushiken both saw opportunities in that spot against Jacksonville, and with Cam Taylor-Britt still on injured reserve, Indianapolis will likely need to lean on both again against Dallas.
Strangely, AJ Haulcy popped up on the injury report Friday with an apparent ankle injury, which limited him in the final practice session. He’s now listed as questionable, meaning Indianapolis may give Hunter Wohler an increased snap share, even if Haulcy does suit up.
Anthony Gould does not have an injury designation, meaning he’s cleared concussion protocol and is all set to make his return, giving the Colts’ return game an extra boost.
A much busier report for the Cowboys, who will be without two players on Sunday. KaVontae Turpin's absence is particularly notable given his contributions as a return specialist and his ability to provide another weapon in the passing game. Malachi Lawrence, meanwhile, will miss another opportunity to add to Dallas' pass rush.
Dallas has some significant questions surrounding its passing game, with both George Pickens and Jake Ferguson listed as questionable. Pickens was limited throughout the week with a hamstring injury, while Ferguson missed the first two practices before returning in a limited capacity Friday. Ferguson's potential absence would leave the Cowboys thinner at tight end, while Pickens' availability could have a considerable impact on Dak Prescott's receiving options.
Defensively, the Cowboys received some encouraging news with Caleb Downs and PJ Locke, who both returned to full participation Friday and carry no game designation. Downs' availability is particularly noteworthy, as he'll have the opportunity to face his older brother, Colts wide receiver Josh Downs, for the first time in their NFL careers. The two could find themselves matched up frequently given Caleb's responsibilities in the nickel and Josh's role as Indianapolis' primary slot receiver.

title: Snapping the Skid: 3 Keys to Colts’ Ending Losing Streak vs. Cowboys
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts are looking to get back on track Sunday when they welcome the Dallas Cowboys to Lucas Oil Stadium. After a disappointing 42-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, Indianapolis faces another difficult challenge against a Dallas team with a potent offense. That said, their leaky defense provides a great opportunity for Indianapolis to regain its offensive footing.
The Colts have plenty of work to do on both sides of the football, but there are opportunities to exploit against a Cowboys team that has struggled. If Indianapolis hopes to get back into the win column, these are three things it must accomplish.
Let Jonathan Taylor Lead the Way
The Colts have a tremendous opportunity to get their ground game back on track against one of the NFL's worst run defenses. Dallas enters Sunday's matchup allowing a league-high 152.8 rushing yards per game and surrendering 5.0 yards per carry through its first eight contests.
That's an encouraging matchup for Jonathan Taylor. While he's been held in check the last few weeks, Taylor has otherwise remained one of the Colts' most important offensive pieces.
Indianapolis needs to make a concerted effort to get Taylor involved early and consistently, particularly against a Dallas defense that has something to prove in run defense. Establishing the ground game would also take some pressure off Daniel Jones, giving the quarterback more manageable passing situations and preventing the Cowboys from simply pinning their ears back and attacking him.
There's also the possibility that Sunday could mark Taylor's final game with the Colts.
With the NFL trade deadline approaching on Nov. 10 and several teams reportedly expressing interest in the three-time Pro Bowler, the Colts could have a significant decision to make in the coming days. If this is his final appearance, Taylor has an opportunity to give Indianapolis fans one last memorable performance.
Make Dak Work For Everything
Dallas presents a significant challenge for an Indianapolis defense that has struggled to consistently get stops this season. The Cowboys enter Sunday's matchup averaging 247.9 passing yards per game, ninth in the league.
Dak Prescott has plenty of weapons at his disposal, headlined by CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Both receivers present difficult matchups for a Colts secondary that has struggled to limit explosive passing plays. Indianapolis has already surrendered 23 completions of 20-plus yards through eight games, ranking 23rd in the league in that category.
The Colts need to find a way to disrupt Prescott's rhythm and make him uncomfortable in the pocket. That responsibility will fall heavily on Adetomiwa Adebawore, who has emerged as Indianapolis' most productive interior pass rusher with four sacks this season. Laiatu Latu and Jaylahn Tuimoloau must provide additional pressure off the edge. Tuimoloau showed some encouraging signs against Jacksonville, recording a sack and four quarterback pressures.
Colts' head coach Shane Steichen indicated that more opportunities could be coming for rookie Caden Curry, who played the best game of his young career against the Jaguars.
The Colts rank last in the NFL in pass rush win rate and have recorded just 16 sacks through eight games. Dallas has allowed only 11 sacks this season, making this a difficult matchup on paper. However, the Cowboys surrendered four sacks in last week's loss to Arizona, giving Indianapolis some reason for optimism.
If the Colts can replicate that kind of pressure while keeping Lamb and Pickens from making plays downfield, they'll have a much better chance of slowing down Dallas' offense.
Turnovers have been a major problem for Indianapolis throughout its recent slide, and the Colts cannot afford to keep giving opponents extra opportunities. The team enters Sunday's matchup with 15 giveaways through eight games, resulting in a league-worst -11 turnover differential.
Daniel Jones has shouldered much of that responsibility, throwing nine interceptions and losing four fumbles. With Indianapolis already facing an uphill battle, costly mistakes from its quarterback could make it difficult to keep pace with the Cowboys.
The Colts need to do a better job protecting the football, particularly when facing a Dallas offense capable of capitalizing on short fields. That means making smarter decisions in the passing game, avoiding unnecessary risks and taking care of the ball when plays break down.
Indianapolis has enough challenges to overcome in this matchup without giving Dallas free possessions. If the Colts want a legitimate chance to snap their four-game losing skid, they need to eliminate the mistakes that have repeatedly put them behind the eight ball.

title: Colts vs. Cowboys: Downs Brothers Headline 3 Key Matchups
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts are back home Sunday, and after last week's 42-7 embarrassment in Jacksonville, there isn't much room left for another lifeless performance.
Dallas comes to Lucas Oil Stadium at 3-5, but don't let that record fool you. This Cowboys roster has plenty of talent, and there are some fascinating individual battles that could decide this game.
Here are three matchups I'm watching closely.
Let's start with the one we have been waiting for since April.
Cowboys rookie defensive back Caleb Downs and Colts receiver Josh Downs have been eyeing this matchup since Dallas selected Caleb No. 11 overall, and there's a legitimate chance these brothers could line up directly across from each other Sunday.
First, Caleb has to get cleared. He remains in concussion protocol while also dealing with an ankle injury, although he returned to practice in a limited capacity Thursday.
Meanwhile, Josh has requested a trade, and with Tuesday's deadline approaching, there's no guarantee he'll be in Indianapolis much longer. Through eight games, he has 30 receptions for 330 yards and one touchdown.
Neither brother has had the last couple weeks go exactly how they wanted.
But if Caleb plays, forget everything else. Two incredibly talented brothers lining up against each other in an NFL game is just awesome, and somebody could leave Sunday with bragging rights that might last until their next matchup.
Quenton Nelson is in Seattle, and the Colts are now tasked with rebuilding an offensive line that just lost its All-Pro cornerstone.
Rookie Jalen Farmer has an opportunity to make this left guard position his own. In his first career start, Farmer allowed two pressures across 37 pass-blocking snaps, good for a 5.4% pressure rate, according to Next Gen Stats.
Unfortunately for Farmer, Quinnen Williams is waiting.
Williams has generated an 11.8% pressure rate this season and leads Dallas with five sacks. Since Week 6, he leads all defensive tackles with 15 pressures, nine quick pressures and four sacks.
The problems aren't limited to the interior, either.
Bernhard Raimann and Jalen Travis have combined to allow a 13.0% pressure rate, third-highest among NFL tackle duos. Dallas' edge rushers sit at 13.6%, while Rashan Gary has generated pressure on 18.8% of his rushes.
If this new Colts offensive line wants to establish an identity without Nelson, Sunday would be a pretty good place to start.
For all the criticism Sauce Gardner has received this season, the numbers still tell us he's one of the best coverage corners in football.
Gardner leads all qualified NFL cornerbacks with a 30% forced incompletion rate, per PFF. Surprisingly, Charvarius Ward isn't far behind at 21.4%, placing both Colts corners among the league's top five in that category.
They're going to need every bit of it Sunday.
CeeDee Lamb has 60 receptions for 709 yards and six touchdowns through eight games, while George Pickens has added 39 catches for 533 yards and two scores.
That's 99 receptions, 1,242 yards and eight touchdowns between two of the league's most dangerous weapons.
Gardner can't cover both of them, and Pickens' hamstring situation is worth monitoring. But if Ward and Gardner can hold their own on the outside, Indianapolis has a chance to make Dak Prescott work for everything.
After what happened in Jacksonville, that's exactly the type of response this Colts secondary has to have.
Michael Greene is a graduate of Indiana University and the Scouting Academy. He's in his first year covering the Indianapolis Colts and NFL, with a unique focus on fantasy football.

title: Colts Shoved Adonai Mitchell Out, and Now Are Paying the Price
full_text:
Last year, when the Indianapolis Colts appeared on a fast track to the Super Bowl, then-general manager Chris Ballard executed a blockbuster trade.
He sent Indy's 2026 and 2027 first-rounders to the New York Jets for All-Pro cornerback Sauce Gardner.
Sadly, Gardner hasn't played full capacity since the trade due to injuries, but even when his high-level talent is on the field, the Colts still can't win consistently. In short, the Jets have won this trade.
But everyone talks about the first-rounders Indianapolis surrendered; one part of that trade has been overlooked: Giving away the ultra-talented wide receiver, Adonai Mitchell.
Mitchell was drafted by the Colts with the 52nd-overall pick in Round 2 of the 2024 NFL Draft with expectations to blossom under future Hall-of-Famer and Indy wide receivers coach, Reggie Wayne.
2024 was a tough year for Mitchell, who caught only 23 passes for 312 receiving yards. The worst statistic was his catch percentage, which was an underwhelming 41.8.
Year two wasn't much better for the former Texas Longhorn, but he looked to be hitting a stride in Week 4 against the Los Angeles Rams - that was, until disaster struck in the third quarter.
Mitchell hauled in a beautiful deep pass from Daniel Jones, proceeded to spin out of the tackle after a highlight catch, and took the pill to the house for a touchdown.
However, Mitchell got caught up in the moment too soon and fumbled the ball before crossing the goal line, which negated the score and resulted in a touchback, giving possession to the Rams.
"UNBELIEVABLE!" Kevin Kugler on the Colts-Rams call as Adonai Mitchell has a play that starts out great and ends quite poorly. #NFL pic.twitter.com/jyTigKoqwJ
Along with a bad holding penalty later in the game that cost Jonathan Taylor a rushing score, this was a brutal game for Mitchell.
However, Mitchell was only 23 and still navigating the NFL way. Instead of letting him learn his lesson and continue building as a pro in Indy, the Colts opted to get rid of him.
Now in 2026, Indianapolis' wide receiver corps is a barren wasteland.
Alec Pierce was given a mountainous contract but is sidelined with a heel injury and has no timeline to return. This already put the Colts' wide receiver room in a bind.
Now, top pass-catcher Josh Downs is over the situation with the Colts, and has requested a trade in the process.
Josh Downs has requested a trade from the Colts, per @JFowlerESPN pic.twitter.com/0eMonnkhne
If we remove Downs from the equation and assume he's dealt before the November 10th deadline, below is what Indianapolis has in their razor-thin receiver room.
Indianapolis could desperately use Mitchell, but that ship has sailed.
Mitchell has only seen four games this year for the Jets after dealing with a finger injury that required surgery. However, he's looked great and appears to be finding his footing in the NFL.
Mitchell has been explosive, hauling in 16 catches for 265 receiving yards and a touchdown.
He's also riding serious momentum after a monstrous seven-catch, 142-yard, one-touchdown performance in Week 8 against the Las Vegas Raiders.
Geno drops it to AD for a TD! LVvsNYJ on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Cqbp8f0YsS
Ballard made some baffling decisions during his tenure in Indianapolis, but letting go of such a promising weapon after a few struggles early in his young career is inexcusable.
Mitchell looks like a future star, while Indianapolis is desperately trying to operate an offense with a mentally absent Downs and an over-the-hill Keenan Allen as the top wide receivers.
The past is the past, but with every play the ascending Mitchell makes for the Jets, it just pours salt in the wound of the rebuilding Colts, whose 2026 season is all but lost.
But at the end of the day, the NFL is all about making good decisions. Forcing Mitchell out of the organization and alienating him is on Indianapolis, and they have nobody to blame but themselves.
Adonai Mitchell says he went home to an empty house after his dropped Rams TD and had to keep himself alive "I recognize that the ball's coming to me before the ball snaps. So, I'm already on 10" "I got caught up in the emotion of it and the thrill of, you know, finally, like… pic.twitter.com/W6I1clbJSn

Drake Wally is a Senior Writer for the Indianapolis Colts On SI. His works have also appeared on Bleacher Report, MSN, Yahoo, and SBNation. He also co-hosts the Horseshoe Huddle Podcast.

title: Week 9 Injury Report: Colts Could Catch a Break Against Cowboys
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts and Dallas Cowboys released their latest injury reports Thursday ahead of Sunday's matchup in Indianapolis.
While the Colts received some encouraging news regarding several potential returnees, Dallas is dealing with significant questions at tight end and in the secondary.
Let’s take a look at both teams’ Thursday practice reports.
Did Not Participate - DT Grover Stewart (rest) - LB Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee) - CB Justin Walley (knee)
Limited Participants - TE Drew Ogletree (knee)
Full Participants - WR Keenan Allen (rest) - LB Bryce Boettcher (groin) - WR Anthony Gould (concussion) - RB Jonathan Taylor (rest) - OT Jalen Travis (thumb) - CB Charvarius Ward Sr. (rest)
The Colts received some encouraging injury news Thursday as several key players made progress ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Dallas Cowboys.
Jonathan Taylor, Keenan Allen, and Charvarius Ward all returned to full participation after sitting out Wednesday on rest days. None of the three absences appears particularly concerning, and all should be in a good position to play Sunday barring an unexpected setback.
It's worth noting that despite the Nov. 10 trade deadline quickly approaching, Taylor remains a regular piece of the Colts' plans despite being the most discussed name on the market.
Indianapolis could also receive reinforcements at a couple of positions. Linebacker Bryce Boettcher and wide receiver Anthony Gould have both logged consecutive full practices after missing the previous two games. Gould is still required to clear the NFL's concussion protocol before returning to game action, but his progress is an encouraging sign. Boettcher's potential return would be particularly helpful for a linebacker group dealing with some uncertainty.
Akeem Davis-Gaither and Justin Walley, meanwhile, have both missed the first two practices of the week. Davis-Gaither's continued absence leaves the Colts with questions about their linebacker depth, though Boettcher trending in the right direction could aid in that department. Still, being without their usual playcaller on defense could present several problems for the Colts. Walley's situation is worth monitoring in a secondary that could use the additional depth. Without participating at all this week, both Walley and Davis-Gaither are trending in the wrong direction heading into Friday.
Tight end Drew Ogletree also showed some progress, moving from a DNP designation Wednesday to limited participation Thursday. His availability remains unclear, but the progression is a positive development.
Defensive tackle Grover Stewart was the other notable absence Thursday, although his designation was rest-related. His absence shouldn't necessarily raise any concerns, particularly given the nature of the designation, but his status will be worth monitoring Friday.
Overall, the Colts appear to be trending in a positive direction with several potential contributors moving closer to returning. Boettcher and Gould could provide meaningful reinforcements as their respective positions are lacking solid depth, while the continued absences of Davis-Gaither and Walley call for close monitoring. Friday's final report will give a clearer picture of who will be active and who will be sidelined.
Did Not Participate - TE Jake Ferguson (ankle) - OLB Malachi Lawrence (ankle) - WR KaVontae Turpin (ribs)
Limited Participants - DB Caleb Downs (concussion/ankle) - S P.J. Locke III (concussion) - LB DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring/back) - WR George Pickens (hamstring) - CB Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) - TE Luke Schoonmaker (groin) - OG Tyler Smith (ankle)
Full Participants - DT Jonathan Bullard (calf) - DT Kenny Clark (back) - OT Broderick Jones (personal) - OLB Marist Liufau (forearm) - OLB Von Miller (rest) - OT Drew Shelton (hamstring) - LB Dee Winters (calf)
The Cowboys have several injury concerns heading into Sunday's matchup with the Colts, particularly in the secondary and at tight end. While there have been some encouraging developments, Dallas still has a laundry list of guys whose availability remains uncertain.
The Cowboys could receive some reinforcements at linebacker, with Dee Winters progressing from limited participation Wednesday to a full practice Thursday. Winters' potential return would be particularly helpful with DeMarvion Overshown being limited with hamstring and back issues. Meanwhile, Marist Liufau has also returned to full participation as he works through his 21-day return-to-practice window, potentially giving Dallas another option at linebacker.
The secondary is another area worth monitoring. Caleb Downs and P.J. Locke both progressed from not participating Wednesday to limited participation Thursday while dealing with concussions, an encouraging sign for Dallas. Both players must complete the NFL's concussion return-to-participation protocol. Their return to practice is encouraging, but neither is guaranteed to be available Sunday.
This matchup was circled on the calendar as soon as the Dallas Cowboys selected safety Caleb Downs with their first-round draft pick, given that his brother, wide receiver Josh Downs, is on the Indianapolis Colts.
With Josh Downs being a popular name in trade circles ahead of the deadline next Tuesday, it was starting to look like he may be shut down and/or traded before the Colts' Week 9 matchup against the Cowboys, but now it's looking like he will at least play in one more contest for the team that drafted him in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft.
First and foremost, we're hoping that Caleb Downs isn't seriously injured for the sake of his long-term health, but also because the thought of two brothers playing against each other at the next level is an exciting storyline.
Joey Porter Jr. also went from a full participant on Wednesday to limited on Thursday with an ankle injury. With multiple defensive backs dealing with injuries, Dallas could be facing some significant depth concerns against Indianapolis.
At tight end, Jake Ferguson has missed the first two practices of the week with an ankle injury, leaving his availability for Sunday in question. Luke Schoonmaker has been limited in consecutive practices while dealing with a groin injury, but his participation is an encouraging sign. Getting Schoonmaker back would be particularly important if Ferguson remains sidelined, as Dallas could otherwise be severely shorthanded.
The Cowboys also have some questions at wide receiver, where George Pickens has been limited for two consecutive days with a hamstring injury. His continued participation is encouraging, but his status will be worth monitoring ahead of Friday. KaVontae Turpin, meanwhile, has missed both practices with a rib injury. His potential absence would affect both the receiving corps and special teams, where he provides an explosive return option.
Defensively, Dallas could also be without rookie pass rusher Malachi Lawrence, who has missed the first two practices dealing with an ankle issue. Defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard has progressed to full participation as he works through his 21-day return-to-practice window, which could eventually provide some additional depth up front if he's activated off injured reserve ahead of Sunday.
Overall, Dallas has several more injury concerns than Indianapolis heading into Friday's final practice sessions. The potential absences of Ferguson, Downs and Locke are particularly noteworthy given the impact they could have on the Cowboys' offensive and defensive personnel. There is some positive news with Winters, Bullard and Liufau progressing, but Dallas still has plenty of questions to answer before Sunday's matchup.

title: Indianapolis Colts Fire Sale Tracker: Analysis, Trades, Rumors, and More
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts will be the center of the NFL world for the foreseeable future.
This is the second consecutive season that Indianapolis will be featured in trade talks at the midway point, but unlike last year, it's not because they're the number one seed in the AFC.
Instead of buying at the deadline, the Colts will be selling.
The 2026 NFL Trade Deadline (November 10th, 4 PM EST) is quickly approaching, and the Colts are amidst a complete teardown of their franchise.
The Colts fired longtime general manager Chris Ballard after they fell to 2-4 in a humiliating loss, and have been active in the trade market ever since as they look to recoup any valuable draft capital they can after Ballard traded away their 2027 first-round pick, as well as their 2026 first-rounder and WR Adonai Mitchell.
It was the beginning of a poetic end, as the last Ballard-led Colts game was a loss to the 0-5 Tennessee Titans, a team that many still consider the worst team in the NFL. Even then, this version of the Colts may very well be the league's worst.
On top of only one playoff win in three appearances, the Colts failed to win the lowly AFC South across 9.5 seasons (2017-2026) under Chris Ballard.
Despite ample evidence to suggest otherwise, Indianapolis Colts' Owner/CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon decided to bring back both Chris Ballard and head coach Shane Steichen for the 2026 season, referencing their hot start to the previous year as a reason to give them another chance.
The former had been given far too many chances to that point, but to be fair to Irsay-Gordon and her sisters, Co-Owners Kalen Jackson and Casey Foyt, this was the organization's first full offseason under new ownership.
Following the decision to give Ballard and Steichen one last shot in her postseason press conference, Irsay-Gordon said that the "sense of urgency has never been higher" for the GM/HC tandem.
Many didn't believe her, given that she was entering her first full offseason as an NFL Owner/CEO and appeared to be betting on an inevitable collapse, but Irsay-Gordon did what needed to be done, even if it came a bit too late.
In the past 14 days, the Indianapolis Colts have fired longtime general manager Chris Ballard, fallen to 2-6 on the season, and traded away two of their franchise cornerstones.
This article is meant to serve as a one-stop shop for all things Indianapolis Colts-related ahead of the NFL Trade Deadline. I will be updating this story as new information presents itself, so be sure to regularly check back in.
Navigate our trade central (finalized trades, rumors, etc.), future outlook, and more below.
Outside of players still on their rookie contract, as well as some exceptions such as cornerback Sauce Gardner, wide receiver Alec Pierce, left tackle Bernhard Raimann, and a few others, nobody on the Colts roster is safe.
Although the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline is on November 10th at 4 PM EST, the Colts have already gotten a head start on their fire sale.
In order, our trade central will featured finalized trades, a rumor mill, and will conclude with analysis on the team's overall outlook.
A current third-round pick and a future fifth-rounder may seem scoff-worthy at first glance, but when you break down the history of traded compensation for other guards across the league, Nelson's haul starts to make more sense.
Indianapolis' return of a 3rd and a 5th for Quenton Nelson is the most pure draft capital for a guard since at least 2011, per Spotrac. only 4 have netted a 4th: 2013: G. Carimi, 4th 2014: L. Mankins, 4th + player 2021: B. Bredeson + 5th + 7th, 4th 2025: J. Thuney, 4th
I think this is both the best example of why the return for Quenton Nelson isn’t as irresponsible as some are suggesting, and also why the Chris Ballard era needed to end: non-premium positions.
It stings to see any team trade their homegrown future Hall of Famer, but this is the bed the Colts made, and now they must sleep in it.
The Colts' 2026 fourth-round rookie guard Jalen Farmer is Nelson's immediate replacement.
Buckner's departure creates a similar challenge on the defensive line. More responsibility will fall on the remaining interior defenders, including Stewart and Adetomiwa Adebawore.
Not only is the opportunity there, but Adebawore has earned the increased role in question.
After seven weeks, Adebawore is undeniably the Colts' best pass rusher. He is currently tied for second with the most sacks among interior defensive linemen league-wide and leads the team in most major pass-rush statistics.
We've known that Adebawore has some nasty pass-rushing chops, but the biggest development has been his improvement in run defense.
Adebawore has blossomed into a legitimate starting defensive tackle, and it comes at no better time as the Colts have parted ways with their longtime pillar across the defensive line.
However, the Colts' newfound star is on an expiring deal. Adebawore is playing in the final year of his rookie contract, so a big payday is set to come his way.
Update (11/3) : The Indianapolis Colts have signed Adetomiwa Adebawore to a two-year, $35 million contract extension that includes a $13 million signing bonus and $22.5 in new money through 2027.
Update (11/5) : NFL Insider Jordan Schultz : "The belief around the league is that, barring an offer that blows them away, Indianapolis plans to wait until after Sunday’s game vs the Cowboys before revisiting the offers on the table and making the trades that make sense on Monday and Tuesday ahead of the deadline.
ESPN's NFL Insider Adam Schefter confirmed on Halloween that the Indianapolis Colts are officially open to trading Jonathan Taylor and have been active in talks.
Schefter added that the Colts have already received an offer of a 2027 second-round pick along with additional compensation for Taylor's services.
Colts Owner/CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon views Taylor as "a key part of the organization and a likely mainstay in their rebuild," according to Schefter and fellow ESPN Insider Ian Rapoport , the latter of whom added that Indianapolis could change its stance if the right offer comes along, leaving the door open without signaling that a deal is imminent.
Taylor's most comparable trade package is that of Christian McCaffrey's blockbuster haul from 2022.
In exchange for McCaffrey, the Panthers received a 2023 NFL Draft second-round pick, a 2023 third-rounder, a 2023 fourth-rounder, and a 2024 fifth-round pick.
The Colts are understandably trying to pry a first-round pick from an interested suitor's hands, but it doesn't feel like they'll be able to achieve that.
However, if teams get desperate enough, the Colts may end up pulling off a much-needed heist to kickoff their rebuild.
Of course, the highly unlikely yet somewhat feasible hypothetical first-round compensation would come via a contender, thus the projected draft pick would not be able to relieve the hurt that is the Colts' projected Top 5 pick that is sitting in New York, though it would help tremendously.
The good news for this pipe dream is that Taylor is garnering heavy interest across the league. According to Schefter, multiple teams have reached out to Indianapolis, and those talks are said to be active and ongoing.
"The list of teams that have expressed at least some level of interest in trading for Taylor is thought to include the Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings, and New York Giants," Schefter wrote.
NFL Insider Jordan Schultz added on Monday that the Cincinnati Bengals and Seattle Seahawks have entered the Jonathan Taylor sweepstakes.
"My understanding is that 5-6 teams have been aggressively pursuing him: Giants, Packers, Broncos, Seahawks, Bengals, Vikings," Schultz said on The Pivot .
"I think it'll take at least a second-round plus additional compensation to get it done, and I actually do expect that to happen."
The aforementioned Christian McCaffrey blockbuster haul remains the ideal return for the Indianapolis Colts.

title: Jonathan Taylor Sweepstakes Tracker: Colts Analysis, Trade Rumors, and More
full_text:
Unfortunately for Indianapolis Colts fans, Jonathan Taylor and trade request are two terms that have been used together in a sentence before.
Back in 2023, the Colts' prolific running back requested a trade from the Indianapolis Colts amid ongoing contract disputes. Taylor infamously showed up to practice in a black hoodie during his subsequent hold-in, signifying the trying times of a franchise that was entering its first season with then-rookie Anthony Richardson at quarterback.
Following the reporting of Taylor's trade request, former longtime Owner Jim Irsay made sure the league knew he was going to do whatever it takes to keep the star rusher around for the then-rebuild, which was really more of a slight re-tooling, a more conventional dart throw, but I digress.
“We’re not trading Jonathan [Taylor]... end of discussion,” Irsay said in a text to Sports Illustrated ’s Albert Breer . “Not now and not in October!”
And as fate would have it, the Colts would up re-signing Jonathan Taylor in October to a three-year $42 million contract extension, which included $26.5 million in guaranteed payments.
But just three years later, the star running back is back at the center of trade talks.
The 2026 NFL Trade Deadline at 4 PM EST on November 10th is quickly approaching, and it's become increasingly likely that Jonathan Taylor has played his last snap as a member of the Indianapolis Colts.
We're breaking down everything we know about the state of the sweepstakes in question, and will update this article as new information presents itself.
Without further ado, let's dive into how we got here, which teams are reportedly interested in Jonathan Taylor's services and what they're offering.
Despite loud rumors and an ongoing fire sale suggesting otherwise, Taylor has not requested a trade.
In all honesty, it feels and looks like Taylor is one of the few remaining longtime veterans on the Colts roster who genuinely still wants to be in Indianapolis.
Earlier in the offseason, Taylor signed a two-year extension to stay in Indianapolis through the 2028 season. Taylor said he wanted to remain a Colt for life before the extension, hinting toward the goal of a long-term deal, but he and the Colts found a solution that satisfied both parties.
Chris Ballard was already on the hottest seat in general manager history as he entered the final year of his deal, and the Colts didn't want to fully commit to another era under his rule.
And it was smart to think that way, considering we are wrapping up Week 8 and Ballard has been out of the building for two weeks now. Along with him went longtime franchise pillars Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, and all eyes have been on Jonathan Taylor ever since.
Mere months after committing to stay in Indianapolis for the next three seasons, Taylor appears to be on his way out.
In his first game without Quenton Nelson leading the way, Taylor rushed for just 23 yards on eight carries. The Colts failed to establish any sort of rushing attack against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8, and Taylor saw just five carries come his way in the first half.
After the game, Taylor appeared to be rather emotional and was giving multiple teammates and coaches hugs. Sure, it could've just been a lot to take in, or perhaps I am looking too far into it, but it truly felt like this was the last we've seen of Jonathan Taylor in Indianapolis.
Couple this with the fact that ESPN's NFL Insider Adam Schefter confirmed on Halloween, the day prior, that the Indianapolis Colts are officially open to trading Taylor and have been active in talks, and it seems like he's as good as gone.
Schefter also reported that the Colts have already received an offer of a 2027 second-round pick, along with additional compensation, for Taylor's services.
Colts Owner/CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon views Taylor as "a key part of the organization and a likely mainstay in their rebuild," according to Schefter and fellow ESPN Insider Ian Rapoport , the latter of whom added that Indianapolis could change its stance if the right offer comes along, leaving the door open without signaling that a deal is imminent.
Taylor's most comparable trade package, or at least the one Indianapolis is seeking, is that of Christian McCaffrey's blockbuster haul from 2022.
In exchange for McCaffrey, the Panthers received a 2023 NFL Draft second-round pick, a 2023 third-rounder, a 2023 fourth-rounder, and a 2024 fifth-round pick.
The Colts are understandably trying to pry a first-round pick from an interested suitor's hands, but it doesn't feel like they'll be able to achieve that.
However, if teams get desperate enough, the Colts may end up pulling off a much-needed heist to kickoff their rebuild.
Taylor doesn't quite warrant the first-round consideration as a pure rusher who is a subpar back in the passing game, though he does have an argument.
Regardless of his flaws as a third-down back, Taylor's ability as a true rusher is nearly unmatched. He remains at the top of his game at 27 years old, is durable, and carries a favorable contract for the next two seasons.
The Colts already paid Taylor his $15 million signing bonus before the season, so a potential suitor would only be on the hook for $15 milllion in 2027 and $9.46 million in 2028.
Of course, the highly unlikely yet somewhat feasible hypothetical first-round compensation would come via a contender, thus the projected draft pick would not be able to relieve the hurt that is the Colts' projected Top 5 pick that is sitting in New York, though it would help the next regime's outlook tremendously.
The good news for this pipe dream is that Taylor is garnering heavy interest across the league.
According to Schefter, the Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings, and New York Giants have reached out to Indianapolis, and those talks are said to be active and ongoing.
Per Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk, the New York Giants appear to be all-in on Taylor, but it must be at the right price.
"The Giants are one of those teams, and they are very interested. They view Jonathan Taylor as being on par with Derrick Henry in that second tier, just below the best running backs in the NFL. The general concern at this point, though, is that the Colts want too much," Florio said following Week 8's Sunday slate .
“One source with one of the teams currently in the mix with Taylor puts it at 50-50 as to whether it gets done before the trade deadline."
Furthermore, Denver Broncos beat reporter, The DNVR's Zac Stevens, said that he feels the Broncos are truly all-in on Taylor.
"I believe the Broncos are going to do everything in their power to trade for Jonathan Taylor...." Stevens said in a postgame reaction piece on the DNVR Broncos Podcast. "The Broncos are going to try to pull this trade off, from my understanding. They want Jonathan Taylor now."
That wraps up just about everything we're aware of as of Monday, November 2nd. Be sure to check back in for any updates regarding the Jonathan Taylor sweepstakes.
NFL Insider Jordan Schultz added on Monday that the Cincinnati Bengals and Seattle Seahawks have entered the Jonathan Taylor sweepstakes.

title: Colts-Cowboys History Suggests Sunday Could Get Weird
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colt s are 2-6, fresh off a 42-7 beatdown in Jacksonville, and five days away from the NFL trade deadline.
So, instead of thinking about the fire currently burning through this franchise , let's take our minds somewhere else for a minute.
The Dallas Cowboys are coming to Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday, and these two franchises have a history that stretches all the way back to 1960. It has included blowouts, Hall of Famers, overtime chaos, and somehow, one of the strangest Super Bowls ever played.
Dallas leads the all-time series 11-7, including an 11-6 advantage in the regular season. But the Colts own the only postseason meeting, and that one happens to be the biggest game these teams have ever played.
Super Bowl V was an absolute disaster. The Baltimore Colts and Cowboys combined for 11 turnovers; Baltimore committed seven of them, and Dallas was penalized 10 times for 133 yards.
Johnny Unitas left with an injury, Earl Morrall finished the game and Cowboys linebacker Chuck Howley became the only player from a losing team to win Super Bowl MVP.
Still, the Colts somehow survived.
Rookie kicker Jim O'Brien drilled a 32-yard field goal with five seconds remaining to give Baltimore a 16-13 win and the franchise its first Super Bowl championship.
That game probably sums this series up better than anything: weird, messy and unpredictable.
The first meeting was not nearly as dramatic.
Baltimore destroyed the expansion Cowboys 45-7 in 1960, setting the tone for what has become a series filled with lopsided results. Dallas eventually flipped the matchup, including a six-game winning streak over the Colts from 1972 through 1993.
Indianapolis finally snapped that run in 1996, when Jim Harbaugh led a second-half comeback in Dallas and the Colts escaped with a 25-24 win.
Since then, the absurdity has continued.
Peyton Manning threw four interceptions in a 38-35 overtime loss in 2010. Eight years later, Marlon Mack ran for 139 yards and two touchdowns as Indianapolis shut out Dallas 23-0, snapping the Cowboys' five-game winning streak.
Indianapolis trailed just 21-19 after three quarters before Dallas scored a franchise-record 33 points in the fourth, turning a competitive game into a 54-19 embarrassment. Former Colt Malik Hooker even added an interception and a fumble-return touchdown against his old team.
Probably nothing predictive. History from 1960 is not going to help Shane Steichen win a football game in 2026.
But one thing is certain: these matchups have rarely gone according to plan.
The Colts' last two meetings with Dallas ended 23-0 and 54-19. Before that came an overtime thriller, and buried deeper was a Super Bowl remembered as the "Blunder Bowl."
Now a 2-6 Colts team welcomes a 3-5 Cowboys team to Indianapolis with both seasons already hanging in the balance.
If history has taught us anything, it's that when these two teams meet, just about anything can happen.
Michael Greene is a graduate of Indiana University and the Scouting Academy. He's in his first year covering the Indianapolis Colts and NFL, with a unique focus on fantasy football.

title: 3 Jaguars Trade Deadline Predictions: From Brian Thomas Jr. to Defensive Help
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars could look a lot different come Tuesday afternoon. Or they might not. That middle line is what makes the chaos of the NFL Trade Deadline an annual event.
Nearly every team in the NFL faces questions around the NFL Trade Deadline , which falls on Tuesday at 4 p.m. this year. For some teams, it is about whether or not they are selling after disappointing starts to their seasons. For other teams, it is about becoming buyers when a window to win and, in the Jaguars' case, a window to compete for top playoff seeding is a reality.
With the Jaguars looking like perhaps the best team in the AFC , and even in the entire NFL, after a 6-2 start, there are plenty of reasons to think they could be active during this year's deadline. James Gladstone has swung all kinds of trades since being hired, including one at the deadline last year for Jakobi Meyers.
So, how do we think this year's trade deadline will play out for the Jaguars with just a few days left? We drop our final predictions below.
The biggest question swirling around the Jaguars and the trade deadline has nothing to do with whether they might have a big move up their sleeves to chase a Super Bowl window. Instead, it is about former first-round wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr., who was one of the most productive receivers in football as a rookie but who has been out-produced in the Jaguars' passing game by Tanner Koziol over the last month.
It all makes sense from each side. The Jaguars have a spread-it-around offense that frequently switches in-game from being a run-first, multiple-tight end offense and one that is also comfortable spreading it out and throwing it all over the field. Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers are the clear top two receivers in the pecking order, which means Thomas' only real snaps come when the Jaguars are in 11 personnel, which they are in at a lower rate this season.
Thomas entered 2026 with zero career games held without a catch. He now has three in the last four games, and he has just one catch since October 4 when he caught two passes for 17 yards and a touchdown in Week 4 against the Cincinnati Bengals. Since then, he had three targets and no catches in London against the Eagles, he was benched in the second-half of Week 6 against the Texans, he caught a touchdown against the Colts, and then h e didn't see a target on Thursday Night Football against the Baltimore Ravens
The idea that Thomas is going to suddenly turn on a switch and become a big factor in the Jaguars' passing game seems unlike. This is an offense that has been low-volume in the passing game and whose explosive plays come over the middle of the field far more than out the outside. Thomas is a great talent, but he is not a great fit for the Jaguars' scheme or Trevor Lawrence right now.
With that said, there are also several teams who make sense as potential suitors for Thomas' skill-set. It would make sense for a team to see him as lost in the shuffle in Jacksonville but still tremendously talented, because that is simply what seems closest to the truth. From the Jaguars' angle, though, it also doesn't make sense to give away a player who does still command double teams down field for nothing.
If the best the Jaguars are getting offered for Thomas is a Day 3 pick that won't make them any better now, it doesn't make much sense to make the deal. The Jaguars are one of the NFL's best offenses with Thomas playing his minimal role, so I think they would be OK if that continued to be the case. The Jaguars could then to look to deal Thomas in March and the 2027 offseason instead of in-season when they are actively pushing for an AFC South title and the No. 1 seed.
If a team offers something along the lines of a second-round pick or even a top defender for Thomas, that may be tough to turn down. But are teams going to offer that when Thomas is such a non-factor in the offense? That remains to be seen, but for now there is zero reason for the Jaguars to lower what is likely a high asking price for Thomas.
My prediction is that no team ups the ante enough to make it worth it for the Jaguars to move Thomas. They like him, he works hard, and has never been a problem. Unless a team makes a big deal, I think the Jaguars will feel more than fine with keeping him, and I do not see a team making that big deal right now.
The Jaguars have been hit hard at the safety position over the last few weeks. The room looked like the defense's potentially most deep position entering the season and it played well in the first few weeks, but Week 4 injuries to Eric Murray and Caleb Ransaw took things off-track from a healthy perspective. Ransaw has been on injured reserve since, while Murray missed a game, came back in Week 6, and then sustained a season-ending elbow injury in Week 8.
The Jaguars' current in-house options are Antonio Johnson, Rayuan Lane, Kaevon Merriweather, rookie Jalen Huskey, and practice squad safety Cam'Ron Silmon-Craig. Lane has made some big plays and was named AFC Defensive Player of the Week after a career game in Week 8, while the staff is clearly high on Merriweather.
But Huskey has not seen much time on defense and was arguably at fault for the long touchdown run the backups allowed the other night, leaving the Jaguars with a thin group of players they'd trust in a pinch in a defense that has long depended on multiple-safety packages. The safety depth has not been a big issue yet with the Jaguars playing two struggling passing games in back-to-back weeks, but the Chicago Bears and a rematch with the Houston Texans loom later in the year. So potentially does Josh Allen in the playoffs.
It would make sense for the Jaguars to add a veteran here who could step in and start across from Johnson right away, pushing Lane and/or Merriweather to the No. 3 and special teams spots There are some interesting safety option s that would check the boxes. Budda Baker would be a fan-favorite move. Jessie Bates might be the best fit for what the Jaguars actually need, and then there are a host of other high-floor options.
I can not put my finger on exactly which safety the Jaguars will add, but I do predict they add one. I think they recognize the need, and there is a market for the position entering the trade deadline weekend.
With Davon Hamilton out for the season , defensive tackle has been the most-talked-about potential target area for the Jaguars in most reports. This likely would have still been true had Hamilton not been injured since it has been reported that the Jaguars contacted the Tennessee Titans about Jeffery Simmons in a pipe dream. With Hamilton now out for the year though, the urgency should be there for the Jaguars to make a move.
The Jaguars' defense did well to slow down Derrick Henry and the Ravens' running game on Thursday Night Football in their first game without Hamilton anchoring their run defense, with backups Matt Dickerson and Albert Regis stepping up to fill the role. But the Jaguars will need the defensive line to set the tone for the run game for two more months, not just against a predictable Ravens front on a short week.
If the Jaguars do not add a nose tackle, they will have to rely on a platoon at the position through the rest of the season. The Jaguars showed they can get by with that against the Ravens, though the run defense was not as dominant down-to-down as it had been with Hamilton in the middle. The issue is, who would you add?
Vita Vea would be perfect, but the Buccaneers might not have reason to move him. Derrick Brown would be another seamless fit who could transform the front beyond 2026, but would the Panthers even trade him? Daron Payne would have been an easy connection, but his injury has nixed that. There are some cheap veterans who would improve the Jaguars' depth in a pinch, but those are not exactly big swings.
Instead, I think the Jaguars take a swing by sending a Day 3 pick to the New England Patriots for defensive…

title: 3 Things We Learned From Jaguars' Week 9 Dub: Nate Boerkircher's Impact
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars had a big night in Baltimore on Thursday.
It was the Jaguars' first time on the Thursday Night Football stage since 2023, and the Jaguars responded with a 23-point blowout of the Baltimore Ravens. The win showed grit on the road after a short week and some big hits in terms of injuries, and the Jaguars are in quite a good spot moving forward.
But did we actually learn anything new from the Jaguars in their latest blowout? We break it down below, starting with ...
While Nate Boerkircher should have tacked on another touchdown on a failed one-yard target that looked like a play just broken down at the last second, it was still an impressive day. The athletic traits and ball-tracking he has shown on explosive downfield throws in back-to-back weeks has begun to make it clear that the Jaguars knew what they were looking for when it came to Boerkircher. The Jaguars' rookie tight end is amongst the rookie leaders in most stats at the position, and he is doing it in a loaded offense.
Consider just how many big plays the Jaguars have made out of 12 and 13 personnel sets over the last few weeks, it is fair to say that the Boerkircher pick has, in part, helped the Jaguars become everything they wanted to be offensively. He has developed at quite a quick pace, and chances are he is due for a few more big plays down the stretch.
Yes, it was a third-string undrafted free agent quarterback. B ut the Jaguars' defense once again did its thing against both the run and the pass. Even with injuries at safety and no Davon Hamilton, the Jaguars only gave up one explosive gain all game and it was with the backups and rookies in the game. The Jaguars' defense forces quarterbacks to go to areas of the field with the football where the Jaguars think they can make plays, and this resulted in two different interceptions on Thursday,
Anthony Campanile's unit has been top-notch in every game but really one this season. Outside of the Houston Texans game, the defense has given the Jaguars the chance to build big leads and let the offense figure itself out each week. It didn't take the offense that long this time, though the Jaguars held the Ravens to just three points when it was still really a game. Anthony Campanile should not be long for coordinator life if owners know what they are doing.
While Trey Hendrickson is obviously dealing with an injury that hampered him, he is still Trey Hendrickson. Despite the Ravens lining up their No. 1 edge rusher against Walker Little for seemingly all game, Hendrickson didn't sniff a pressure of Trevor Lawrence. Little ended the game with zero pressures allowed, making it the second game in a row he has allowed zero pressures. In three starts, he has allowed just two pressures.
Basically, Little is allowing a pressure every 1.5 games. Losing Anton Harrison for the season was obviously a blow to the Jaguars' offensive line depth, but a three-game sample size suggests that Little has been the Jaguars' best left tackle this season. If Little can keep playing high-level football in terms of pass-protection, keeping him on the roster is going to look like one of the best decisions of the entire offseason.
Little has played strong stretches of football before, but he seems to really be hitting his stride in his latest stint as a starter. The Jaguars could have a lot of options at left tackle moving forward depending on what the rest of the season looks like for Little.

title: 5 Players the Jaguars Should Call About Before Trade Deadline
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- There might not be many more interesting teams than the Jacksonville Jaguars at the NFL Trade Deadline.
The Jaguars are clearly AFC contenders after a Thursday Night Football blowout of the Baltimore Ravens pushed them to 6-2. Their window is now, and they have a general manager who has had no issues with being aggressive before.
So with the Jaguars having some clear needs at spots such as defensive tackle, defensive end, and safety entering the final days of the trade market, which moves should the Jaguars explore right now before it is too late? We break it down below.
We have mentioned Budda Baker in the past , and it is not hard to see why. The Jaguars have some serious injury issues at safety with Eric Murray out for the year and with Caleb Ransaw on injured reserve for the last month. The issue hasn't popped up over the last two games with the Jaguars playing Daniel Jones and a third-string undrafted free agent in the last two weeks, but it could loom large in matchups later in the year with the Chicago Bears and Houston Texans.
One obvious name that could be explored at safety is Budda Baker. He has seemed over Arizona's losing for a bit now, and a Cardinals loss to the Seattle Seahawks in Week 9 could make it clear that it is time for them to start selling. The Jaguars' decision-makers have a lot of experience with Baker from their NFC West battles while with the Los Angeles Rams, and he could help fill voids for the Jaguars in terms of veteran experience after the loss of Murray.
Would the Cardinals be willing to part with a face of the franchise when they have been somewhat competitive at times in 2026? That remains to be seen. Everyone has a price, though, and the Jaguars should learn what this price is.
All signs point to the Jaguars looking for defensive tackle help , and Derrick Brown is probably the best overall player who could be moved for some reason or another. He is not on the Jeffery Simmons tier of defensive tackles, but he is a top-10 interior defensive lineman who would give the Jaguars a building block for years to come. He is hitting his peak as one of the best nose tackles in football, and he is one of the few nose tackles who could step in the shoes of Davin Hamilton without much of a dropoff.
The Panthers may not see reason to be sellers even if they lose in Week 9 due to the weakness of the NFC South. But if the Jaguars were to make the offer sweet enough, perhaps they could convince the Panthers to move their star defensive tackle as they look to remake a defense that has been one of the worst in the NFL for years.
While Christian Barmore could not be a direct replacement for Davon Hamilton , he does seem relatively available according to most reports. He is not one of the top-two defensive tackles for the New England Patriots in terms of snaps this year and they might be looking to dump his money, which could make for change of scenery desired for both sides. If Barmore can be had with a mid-Day 3 pick and goes on to be his best version for the rest of 2026, it could be the steal of a season.
Can Barmore be that player, though? He has been in the past, especially as a pass-rusher. He has not been that player this season, though, and the Jaguars would have to make sure that he is a fit for their scheme and their culture. He would not be a nose tackle, but he could help their third-down unit quite a bit if he is at his best.
I still can't stop coming to the conclusion that Khalil Mack makes a ton of sense for the Jaguars. He would likely love to go to a contender, they might be 0-8 after Sunday, he is cheap and on an expiring deal, and it likely would not take more than a fifth-round pick to trade for him. But for some odd reason, the Chargers have not really dealt with reality when it comes to moving their pieces.
Calling about teammate Dalvin Tomlinson as nose tackle depth makes sense too, but Mack would just be the perfect fit. If the Jaguars want to get better at rushing the passer on 3rd-and-longs, why not add an edge guy across from Josh Hines-Allen and moves Travon Walker inside? The Jaguars did this on Thursday with Dennis Gardeck and Bryan Thomas Jr. Imagine if they did it with Khalil Mack.
Most trade deadline rumors about Eagles defensive tackle Moro Ojomo connect him to the Jaguars in some form or fashion, which makes a lot of sense considering their need for more depth. Arik Armstead and Ruke Orhorhoro are playing well, but adding a talent like Ojomo could push them over the top in 2026 while being an option to build around in 2027 and beyond.
The Eagles are reportedly hesistant to trade Ojomo, who is in a contract year. If the Eagles do hold onto Ojomo, they could try to re-sign him or see him walk for a compensatory pick in 2028. It would likely cost quite the deal to make the Eagles move Ojomo, but he is a young and ascending talent who could prove to be worth it.

title: What the Latest Reports Tell Us About the Jaguars Ahead of the NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are in quite the position entering the final weekend before the trade deadline.
After a 33-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens that proved to be mostly effortless on both sides of the ball, the Jaguars are 6-2 and have a ton of options in front of them before Tuesday's trade deadline hits.
We have seen the Jaguars take big swings before, and the team has continued to be tied to a number of potential moves ahead of next week. With the AFC this wide open, there stands to be good reason why the Jaguars might want to be aggressive.
So, what do the latest rumors and reports about the trade deadline suggest for the Jaguars? We break it down below.
Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer has the latest for the Jaguars, with moves at the defensive tackle spot still taking the most priority. It was expected for the Jaguars to have some real interest in the defensive tackle market even before Davon Hamilton was lost with a season-ending injury, and Breer notes that the Jaguars are one of several teams looking to add at the position by Tuesday.
"The defensive tackle market has been hot, with big names DeForest Buckner and Jeffery Simmons already moved—to the 49ers and Bears, respectively—and teams like the Giants, Jaguars and Vikings still turning over rocks looking for help," Breer said.
The issue for the Jaguars if they want to land a true difference-maker is that there is not another obvious move like Jeffery Simmons, DeForest Buckner, or Dexter Lawrence from the offseason. There are some talented and useful players, but there is not another Simmons that the Jaguars can find. With that said, the Jaguars should have a host of options overall if they deem the defensive tackle position as a must-add.
"Grover Stewart’s an option, with the Saints’ Davon Godchaux and Nathan Shepherd, Patriots’ Christian Barmore and Panthers’ Bobby Brown III others who’ve come up in trade talks," Breer said. "To this point, the Eagles have said no to teams on Moro Ojomo (more on him in a bit), and the Dolphins have done the same with Zach Sieler. The pie-in-the-sky swing for someone to take, in the Simmons aftermath, might be for Panthers star Derrick Brown. That would be very expensive, though, with Carolina not actively looking to move him."
In terms of pure needle-moving, the addition of Brown is what would serve as the ultimate game-changer for the Jaguars. Ojomo is up there, too, though the Eagles are appearing to be stubborn on whether or not he is actually going to be on the market.
Thursday night was not exactly a productive outing for Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr., who did not see a target. Thomas has one catch since Week 4 and he has three different zero-catch games in the last month after having zero such games in the first two years of his career. He is just another piece of the offense, but that might not exactly mean the Jaguars are in any rush to move him, either.
Breer notes that the Kansas City Chiefs had eyes on Thomas, though he indicates that interest has since expired. Thomas may not be very productive for the Jaguars, but it has also been true the entire time the Thomas saga has dragged on that the Jaguars will not just deal him for anything. The Jaguars would likely require a top pick, and it doesn't seem like anyone has played ball, yet.
"Kansas City had interest in Jacksonville’s Brian Thomas Jr., but the Jaguars have been less inclined to sell on the former first-rounder," Breer said.
"While he hasn’t been statistically productive, and isn’t the best fit for Liam Coen’s scheme, Thomas brings a downfield element that’s really important in keeping defenses honest against the run, and opening things up underneath for Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington. So now Downs, who’d probably cost a fourth-round pick, would loom as a possibility for the Chiefs."
It almost feels now as if a Thomas move would be a surprise. He won't put up big numbers the rest of the season, though, so look for trade talks to heat back up next March if he does not get moved by Tuesday.
