title: Chiefs’ Need for a Wide Receiver Becomes Even More Glaring After Second Straight Loss
full_text:
After falling 28-24 to the Broncos yesterday, the Kansas City Chiefs suffered their second consecutive defeat and effectively lost their hold on the AFC West. Denver scored 15 unanswered points in the final quarter as the Chiefs' offense completely stalled out.
While the defense was largely responsible for the fourth-quarter collapse and Patrick Mahomes had one of his best statistical performances of the year, the issues with KC's offense became even more glaring . Andy Reid's squad had three opportunities to put points on the board in the final quarter and came up empty every time, including a two-minute drill where one more touchdown could have won the game.
Aside from Rashee Rice, who made his return from a hamstring injury, no Chiefs wideout surpassed 20 yards on the day. It was painfully evident down the stretch that Mahomes and his unit had no reliable options open downfield. This inevitably brought back doubts about the state of the wide receiving corps. During Monday morning's segment of Get Up on ESPN, NFL insider Adam Schefter resurfaced the idea that Kansas City has been actively searching for targets for Mahomes to throw to. He suggested it would be a surprise if a new face does not join the pass-catching group by next week's trade deadline.
"I think they are looking around for a wide receiver," Schefter said. "I think it would be a surprise if they didn't make some type of deal for some receiver before next Tuesday's trade deadline at 4 p.m. Eastern. They're going to look for a wide receiver, but that doesn't change that idea that this team needs better help up front and better play from its offensive tackle position."
“I think it would be a surprise if [the Chiefs] didn’t make some type of deal for some receiver before next Tuesday's trade deadline.” — @AdamSchefter on what he believes the Kansas City Chiefs will do heading into the trade deadline. pic.twitter.com/MopDZBiFru
Whether a move for a receiver comes later today or an hour before the deadline, general manager Brett Veach knows this is a primary point of concern for the Chiefs. It's only a matter of time before he pulls the trigger on a deal.
Even in a contest where the offense looked effective across three quarters, Kansas City's need for a receiver has become even more apparent. We've already explored a number of players they could look to acquire before the deadline, though the caliber of receiver they get depends on the draft capital they are willing to give up and the salary they are willing to take on.
Since losing Tyquan Thornton earlier this season to a dislocated ankle, the Chiefs' passing attack has often looked anemic. Thornton had unexpectedly emerged as perhaps Mahomes' favorite deep target, and his absence has been a significant blow. No matter how much we try to defend Xavier Worthy on a weekly basis, the reality is that he hasn't been living up to his billing as a WR2 . His route running has been anything but crisp, he struggles to make defenders miss in the open field, and his lack of size makes him a liability when he cannot utilize his speed in a straight line.
Internal options Cyrus Allen and Jalen Royals have flashed their talent at times, but it doesn't feel like they are ready to take on a prominent role just yet at this point in their careers. The outrage from Chiefs Kingdom if KC simply turned to its in-house prospects would be immense.
Going into this season, there were already lingering questions about the receiver group and how it would fare. Losing Thornton early in the year and seeing how the offense looked without Rice only magnified those concerns.
Schefter and many other reporters have confirmed the notion that Kansas City has been exploring the trade market. If the front office is truly committed to maximizing the championship window and giving Mahomes the weapons he needs, a trade needs to be made as soon as possible.

title: One Move the Chargers Can’t Afford to Get Wrong at the NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
How does one handle a 0-7 start? The Los Angeles Chargers have not opened a season like this since 2000, when the franchise was located in San Diego and the team dropped its first 11 games on the way to a 1-15 season.
This is a club that during its first two seasons under head coach Jim Harbaugh finished 11-6 and reached the playoffs. There were ugly playoff losses at Houston and at New England, but there were high expectations entering 2026.
Who could have foreseen that the Bolts would drop their first two home games to a pair of teams that finished with identical 3-14 records in 2025. Even odder was that Harbaugh’s club would fall to both the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders by 26-14 scores.
70 seconds of horrific Justin Herbert interceptions pic.twitter.com/JxamkAbtZv
It was spiraled out of control ever since. The 0-7 Chargers are the lone winless team in the league. They are averaging an NFL-low 14.1 points per game. Mike McDaniel’s first season as the team’s offensive coordinator has seen his unit produce just nine touchdowns—zero in the past two games. The club has committed a league-high 17 turnovers—12 of those by two-time Pro Bowl quarterback Justin Herbert.
The defense has held its own for the most part, but they are in the bottom half of the league (23rd) against the run, allowing 124.6 yards per game on the ground. Last season, they ranked eighth in the NFL (105.4) in this area.
#Chargers OC Mike McDaniel says he’s making a change this week, moving from the sideline to the booth to call plays: “I think we’re going to try that this week. Seems like a good action to take based on how things have gone this year.” pic.twitter.com/zWVj8Jx6PN
With the Chargers on the ropes, there’s been plenty of “fire sale” discussions regarding the organization. From Herbert to wide receiver Quentin Johnston to edge rushers Khalil Mack and Tuli Tuipulotu. Interesting enough, the departure that has been the most discussed is dismissing McDaniel, who is making a change for this week's clash with the Houston Texans.
Back to the players. It’s hard to imagine the Bolts parting ways with Herbert, but a wide receiver starved team may be interested at Johnston at the right price. That leaves Mack and Tuipulotu, both who can hit the free-agent market in 2027.
The fifth overall pick the 2014 draft by the then-Oakland Raiders has put together quite the 13-year résumé in the National Football League. And it may surprise some to know that despite stints with the Silver and Black and the Chicago Bears, Mack has played more seasons and more games for the Chargers than either of those other two franchises. By all indications, the nine-time Pro Bowler would prefer to stay with the Bolts.
As for Tuipulotu, it’s still somewhat inexplicable that despite plenty of cap room, the Chargers and general manager Joe Hortiz didn’t manage to get a contract extension done with the improving sack artist.
So back to the original premise of the piece. So what is the one move that this franchise can’t botch before Tuesday’s trade deadline? At this time, that is apparently is a moot point. Because unless something dramatic happens over the next few days, the disappointing Chargers are reportedly content with doing nothing personnel wise in terms of dealing player.
@minakimes says she's been told the #Chargers aren't trading anyone. That would just be absolute malpractice by Joe Hortiz and the front office. pic.twitter.com/j838JXQ1HE
Yes, never say never in today’s NFL. However, the less-than-aggressive approach by the franchise this offseason appears to be their business model these days, regardless of what is currently happening on the field.
The clocking has been ticking for two months when it comes to the Chargers winning their first game of the season. And now the NFL trade deadline is basically three days away as in Tuesday, November 10, at 4:00 pm ET.

title: Chargers’ Most Likely Trade Deadline Move is More Self-Inflicted Wounds
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers just can’t get out of their own way.
That’s not going to naturally stop at the NFL trade deadline. Every Chargers trade deadline rumor says the same thing: No point in calling Joe Hortiz out in Los Angeles.
Justin Herbert trade rumors aren’t really a thing. But every other player, including Khalil Mack, should be up for grabs.
Just don’t tell the Chargers, who seem adamant that nothing major should change despite the risk of hitting 0-8 at the deadline.
The Chargers should do right by Mack and trade him away. He’s appealing to other teams as a future Hall of Famer on an expiring contract who, through the mess that is the Chargers this year, still sits on three sacks and five tackles for loss while playing in a rotation.
Mack, though, doesn’t sound like he wants to leave the Chargers.
"Yeah, they know how I feel, man," Mack said this week, according to The Athletic's Noah Furtado . "It's just tough with all the outside noise. And so, ultimately, I want to be here, and I want to help them win. Even though it's tough right now, you always see the light at the end of the tunnel."
Not to beat the horse (or Bronco), but not trading Mack would just be another obvious mistake by the Chargers.
Obvious, like bringing on Mike McDaniel but not spending to give him the speed and stuff he needs to run his system well. Obvious, like once again not properly addressing the interior of the offensive line. Obvious, like not sitting on $20-plus million in free cap space in November while winless. Or keeping around struggling “bargains” like Quentin Johnston. Or not playing a first-round pick like Omarion Hampton enough…after taking a running back in the first round.
It goes on and on and on with the Chargers and has led to perhaps the worst outright roster in football and a hold on the No. 1 pick in next year’s draft.
Hanging onto Mack would be another misstep, even if the trade return wouldn’t be that high.
Trade offers and Mack himself.
From an outsider’s view, it really doesn’t sound like Mack wants to leave, despite it all. There were rumblings in the past of his not wanting to be dealt from other teams, either.
Maybe Mack changes his apparent stance over the next week and something happens. We won’t crush the Chargers too much for honoring the wishes of any player, let alone Mack.
That said, if the Chargers hit 0-8, they need to at least pick up the phone. And if a contender like the Chicago Bears gets antsy and ups the offer enough, to say a fourth-round pick or a little higher, the Chargers would be foolish not to hit on the best of both worlds by picking up a nice asset while sending Mack off to get a chance at a Lombardi Trophy.

title: Omarion Hampton Week 9 Outlook Is Brighter Than Ever Thanks to New Mike McDaniel Quote
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers still have not won a single game to start the 2026 NFL season, with a major part of that being because of this team's offense under what was once the best hire of the offseason, Mike McDaniel.
This offense is currently the worst in the league by points scored , with specifically the rushing offense being ranked 18th in rushing yards per game. While 18th would be okay if your team were a pass-heavy unit, this team was supposed to be built on the run to support the pass. The passing offense ranks T-26 in passing yards per game.
With such an awful offensive unit, you would think that the team's first-round second-year running back has been hurt or benched. You would be more correct to call what has gone on as a benching. This is now expected to change.
Omarion Hampton , the Bolt's 2025 first-round pick, had an injury-plagued rookie season, but had enough flashes during the year to show why the team selected him with the pick they did. Going into year two, this season, Hampton was praised to be a possible league-leading rusher under McDaniel.
Like everything else, nothing but disappointment has occurred, as Hampton started off the season rushing the ball well, with two games with a touchdown, one of those having over 100 scrimmage yards. Unfortunately, in those games, he fumbled the football, yielding a massive decline in playing time since. He went from around 60% of the offensive snaps to around 35%. It is safe to say it was a soft benching for the former first-round pick.
This year, he has a 3.5 yards-per-carry average, not inspiring much confidence for his future. While his vision has declined in this wide-zone offense, he has been getting next to no blocking and movement in the run game, not helping his case and the entire offense's case in general.
Now that the team continues to lose, it seems that McDaniel has finally given up on the running back by committee idea, hopefully giving the lion's share of the workload to Hampton for the foreseeable future.
McDaniel said in today's presser: "We've had some strong consideration on adjusting the exact flow...I'm excited about someone dictating the rotation...O's had a really great week of prep"
Chargers OC Mike McDaniel on HC Jim Harbaugh indicating Omarion Hampton will get more touches: "We've had some strong consideration on adjusting the exact flow" "I'm excited about someone dictating the rotation" "O's had a really great week of prep"
So, if you are a fantasy owner of Hampton , it may be time to finally consider taking him off your bench and starting him once again. If you are not, it could be worth trading for him while he's a buy-low candidate.
Outside of fantasy, hopefully this workload increase will allow Hampton to find his rhythm and confidence in this offense, giving more excitement for this year while having something to build on for next.

title: Chargers and Mike McDaniel Finally Make a Change Against the Houston Texans
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-7, have been battered by injuries and have looked lost on offense. The Chargers' season is lost but right now, they are trying to find any glimmer of hope in the darkness that has been the 2026 season.
2026 is the first year with new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. The NFL at large was excited and congratulatory to the Chargers when they hired the biggest name on the coaching market in Mike McDaniel to take over the Chargers offense from recently fired Greg Roman. The projections and expectations for the Chargers were sky-high but with franchise quarterback Justin Herbert paired with McDaniel, the belief was sky-high as well.
To say the train fell off the tracks would be an understatement for the Chargers offense. They are dead last is most offensive categories and put up their worst offensive performance based on epa per drive coming out of their bye week and after getting some reinforcements in their wide receiver room.
Los Angeles' offensive production has been so bad that it appeared heading into the bye week that Mike McDaniel may not survive as the offensive coordinator. However, the Chargers have no one on staff that could in theory take over. Passing game assistant Adam Gase was floated as an option in the media but he does not have direct experience in McDaniel's system and had been out of the NFL for years. The best shot the Chargers had to turn the offense around was to get healthy and for McDaniel to get the players on the same page.
Getting the offense and specifically Justin Herbert, back on track still seems to be the goal. Justin Herbert played six NFL seasons before the current 2026 season and had one of the lowest career interception rates in the history of the NFL entering the 2026 season. That rate has skyrocketed with Mike McDaniel.
From the 1970 merger through the end of last season, 120 QBs attempted at least 2500 passes. Here were the career leaders in interception rate: 1. Aaron Rodgers (1.4%) 2. JUSTIN HERBERT (1.7%) 3. Tom Brady (1.8%) 4. Joe Burrow (1.8%) 5. Patrick Mahomes (1.8%)
After opting not make any changes to the coaching staff during the bye week, the Chargers and McDaniel are still searching for answers. McDaniel announced at a press conference on Thursday that he would be attempting to change his persepctive and move to the booth to call plays against the Texans this week.
McDaniel cited his time working with 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan who called plays from the booth during their time with the Atlanta Falcons. The view from the booth gives a more complete picture of the offense and defense for McDaniel to make in-game adjustments.
McDaniel moving to the booth is not the only changes on the horizon. Head coach Jim Harbaugh hinted that Omarion Hampton may see his share of carries increase or at the very least, a more consistent rotation as opposed to a consistent change of back based on play call or formation. It did appear that defenses have been able to pick up on significant tendencies based on which back was on the field.
Los Angeles has also opened the practice windows for tight end David Njoku, linebacker Denzel Perryman. If the Chargers activate them for the game against the Texans, the Chargers will have a few more reinforcements hitting the field.
#Chargers HC Jim Harbaugh said the team will open the 21-day practice window for David Njoku and Denzel Perryman today.
The Chargers will face their nemesis, the Houston Texans in week nine and will finally be trying a few changes on offense. It may also indicate some changes coming to the offensive line as well with guard Kayode Awosika returning to practice in a limited fashion.

title: Fantasy Football Start or Sit: Herbert, McConkey Could Put Up Big Numbers Against Texans
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers have an important matchup ahead as they prepare to face the Houston Texans this weekend.
With fantasy football seasons reaching an important point , making the right lineup decisions can have a major impact on the standings. Not every player on the Bolts offense deserves a spot in fantasy lineups, however. Here are two players worth starting and three who could be better left on the bench.
Justin Herbert is the first Chargers player fantasy managers should consider starting this weekend.
His ability to make plays both inside and outside the pocket gives the offense an advantage, even against a defense capable of putting pressure on opposing quarterbacks.
The Texans will likely make things difficult throughout the afternoon, but Herbert has the arm strength and playmaking ability to take advantage of opportunities downfield. His connection with the Chargers receiving group also gives him multiple ways to move the football.
There are certainly easier matchups available, but Herbert has the talent to produce a strong fantasy performance. Fantasy managers should feel comfortable keeping him in their starting lineups.
Ladd McConkey is another Chargers player who deserves consideration this weekend. His ability to create separation and find openings in opposing defenses makes him an important part of the passing game.
His versatility allows him to contribute in different areas of the field rather than relying entirely on deep receptions. Honestly, he has been one of the only bright spots for the offense.
McConkey has the skill set to make an impact regardless of the opponent. His involvement in the passing attack makes him one of the more appealing fantasy options on the Chargers roster.
Quentin Johnston is a player fantasy managers may want to reconsider starting this weekend. While his size and athletic ability give him the potential to make explosive plays, his production can be difficult to predict.
The biggest concern is consistency.
Johnston needs opportunities to establish himself in the passing game, and there is no guarantee those opportunities will translate into a productive fantasy afternoon.
Kimani Vidal is another player who presents some uncertainty heading into this matchup. Running back production often depends on receiving a consistent number of touches, and that is something fantasy managers need to consider before putting Vidal into their lineups.
The Chargers’ offensive approach and distribution of opportunities could limit his overall involvement. Even if he finds opportunities to contribute, there is no guarantee he receives enough work to produce meaningful fantasy numbers. Houston is not an opponent managers should overlook, making Vidal a difficult player to trust this weekend. There are likely more dependable options available at running back.
Oronde Gadsden II rounds out this week’s sit recommendations. The young tight end has the athletic ability to create problems for opposing defenses, but fantasy managers should be careful about expecting consistent production every week.
Tight ends can be particularly difficult to evaluate because their involvement often depends on the overall offensive game plan. If the Chargers prioritize their outside receivers or running game, Gadsden could see fewer opportunities to make an impact.

title: 1 X-Factor Explains Why Chargers Won’t Find Quentin Johnston Trade Partner
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers should be hosts of the NFL’s biggest fire sale at the trade deadline .
Khalil Mack should go . So should plenty of others. Tuli Tuipulotu should not. Neither should Justin Herbert, obviously.
One of those plenty of others , though, is wide receiver Quentin Johnston.
After all, Johnston is the embattled former first-round pick who has struggled with drops since entering the NFL. There was a brief thought that the arrival of offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel would mean the Chargers replace him with more speed and reliability.
The Chargers instead responded by picking up Johnston’s fifth-year option.
Calling it a mistake would be an understatement.
When the Chargers picked up Johnston’s fifth-year option, it was pretty obvious general manager Joe Hortiz was on the hunt for a “deal.” So it goes for an organization that still has nearly $30 million in free cap space right now and had nearly $100 million before free agency. They’re 0-7 for a reason, folks.
Herbert’s turning in the worst year of his career and Johnston still looks like Johnston, having caught just 12 of his 25 targets for 202 yards and no scores.
On paper, a former first-round pick who is still just 25 years old should have some appeal to other teams at the deadline. But there’s the matter of that pesky contract.
The Athletic’s Noah Furtado put it best: “Is there a team willing to eat $18 million in 2027 for an X wideout known for shaky production who comes down with fewer jump balls than he should and has unreliable hands to boot? Any deal that gets the Chargers a draft pick makes sense … for the Chargers."
That $18 million is fully guaranteed. Another team could go get a veteran or make a trade at a fraction of that cap hit right now.
Barring a shocker, this is another delayed decision by the Chargers to move on later than they should. Guys hanging on for a few more years than necessary, like Bradley Bozeman, continue to cripple the team’s chances.
Now, since they’ve dragged feet on moving on from Johnston, it’s hard to say if Mike McDaniel will be around next offseason. Which makes it hard to say if Johnston will even fit the next coordinator’s scheme.
No matter what happens there, the Chargers are stuck because they wanted a bargain. No team is going to swoop in and pay up a draft pick for him at the deadline while absorbing that contract for fun, too.

title: NFL Trade Deadline Rumors: Justin Herbert's Reality Amidst the Noise
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-7 and the trade deadline is rapidly approaching. The Chargers have confounded the rest of the NFL as they have yet to engage in trade discussions on any of their players but that has not stopped the calls and the speculation.
The Chargers appeared to be attempting to stand pat through their week seven bye and emerge from the bye with answers and limited reinforcements returning to the field in an attempt to keep the ship from sinking. It is believed around the NFL that after their loss to the Rams, dropping them to 0-7, the Chargers will finally be ready to take calls and listen regarding some of their players.
Rumors surrounding franchise quarterback Justin Herbert have been swirling with his play this season being far below his career averages and seemingly lost in Mike McDaniel's complex timing based offense. On one hand, Herbert is one of the most polarizing quarterbacks in the NFL. There seems to be little grey area of opinion on him and this season is something completely different. On another, Herbert has a track record of six years of excellent play and this season is a clear outlier with the enitre offense falling off the tracks.
Herbert's track record of elite play would generate a massive trade market if he were available, even despite the terrible season he is having in 2026. For this reason and his position as a polarizing quarterback, the media has been all over trade speculation as the November 10th trade deadline rapidly approaches.
The lack of success this year for the Chargers and Justin Herbert has been frustrating and confusing. The Chargers made the splash of the offseason with the hiring of offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel and it has been an unforeseen disaster. McDaniel tried to have Justin Herbert adjust the way he plays to fit the Shanahan system as opposed to adjusting the system to fit the skill of the quarterback.
Herbert has a long throwing motion, which widely accounts for why a 6'6 quarterback gets passes batted down at the frequency in which he does. Most quarterbacks who succeed in Shanahan systems have a short and quick throwing motion. It would have made more sense to try to design and incorporate segments of the system that fit Herbert as opposed to asking him to play more like Tua Tagovailoa, McDaniel's quarterback in Miami.
The changes have resulted in significant regression for Herbert and the offense. The lack of changes to the system to fit the players, wide receivers included, has resulted in the Chargers being winless heading into week nine and McDaniel on the hot seat. McDaniel being on the hot seat makes trading Justin Herbert a near non-starter simply because the results with McDaniel have lowered Herbert's overall value to it's lowest point.
Justin Herbert's contract provides the real reality of his trade market. Media headlines can speculate all they want, Herbert has a full no-trade clause. He's not going anywhere unless he wants out.
Herbert's contract is also structured in a way that trading him would hit the Chargers with over $80 million in dead cap between this season and next with the bulk hitting in 2027. Trading Herbert would be a signal for a full tear down and rebuild for the Chargers. Unless Herbert signals to ownership that he is 100 oercent done, there is no way the Chargers move on from him.

title: The Chargers Refuse to Budge as Trade Deadline Approaches
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are approaching an important point in their 2026 season.
Despite a difficult start and growing questions , the Chargers have reportedly shown little interest in entertaining offers for their veteran players.
Sports Illustrated Senior NFL writer Albert Breer noted “Los Angeles has gotten calls on edge guys Khalil Mack and Tuli Tuipulotu, but hasn’t budged on either.” The Bolts seem to be getting calls for several players, but are simply not interested.
The Chargers entered the season with expectations of being competitive in the AFC West. After consecutive 11-6 finishes under head coach Jim Harbaugh, there was reason to believe the organization could continue building on its recent progress. Instead, the 2026 campaign has taken a dramatically different direction.
With the trade deadline approaching, the Chargers have an opportunity to reconsider their approach and potentially acquire additional draft capital for the future.  Does it make sense though?
If they truly think this team could do a whole 360 next year, then keeping most players isn't a terrible idea in the long run.
Several veterans have emerged as potential names to watch as the deadline gets closer. Khalil Mack is among the most recognizable, while players such as Bud Dupree, Denzel Perryman, Dalvin Tomlinson, Quentin Johnston and Donte Jackson have also been mentioned in discussions surrounding possible trade candidates. For a team struggling to find wins, the possibility of moving veteran contracts could become an important part of its long-term planning. However, there is a difference between recognizing the need for change and completely dismantling a roster.
Hortiz must also consider what those decisions could mean for the younger players already in the building. Maintaining some veteran leadership could have value, particularly for a team that would need to establish a stronger foundation moving forward. That creates a complicated situation for the them. Holding onto experienced players could provide some stability, but passing on opportunities to acquire future draft selections could limit the organization’s options during the offseason.
The decision is not necessarily about trading every available veteran. Instead, it comes down to determining which players remain part of the organization’s long-term plans and which ones could provide greater value elsewhere.
The Bolts appear determined not to make a rushed decision simply because the season has not gone according to plan, but that approach could change as the deadline gets closer.

title: 3 NFL Trade Deadline Deals the Chargers Should Explore Right Now
full_text:

title: Chargers' Criminally Overlooked Trade Candidate's Departure Would Fix Some Issues
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers have an interesting big board of trade targets at the deadline , considering they’re the worst team in the NFL, clutch the No. 1 pick in the draft order and need to think beyond this season.
That also means the Chargers are positioned as big sellers at the trade deadline. Khalil Mack is the obvious name to go first , if Jim Harbaugh and the club actually change their stance on trading away players.
But there are some overlooked Chargers players who could be on the move, too. Think, veteran cornerback Donte Jackson, should a contending team get really desperate at the premium position.
But there’s another sleeper name worth considering: Kimani Vidal.
Sure, running back isn’t a premium spot anymore. But its importance has been upped in recent years again, hence the Chargers going after Omarion Hampton in the first round at all.
Speaking of the Chargers and Hampton, Vidal is a pretty sneaky trade candidate because we can’t help but mention that offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is effectively ruining him.
No exaggeration: Hampton has effectively managed to regress from his oft-injured rookie season. He’s carried the ball just 89 times for 309 yards and three scores on a 3.5 average. McDaniel has often preferred to yank him from the lineup in favor of Keaton Mitchell (39 carries, 15 catches) and Vidal (29 carries, nine catches).
Hampton is supposed to be the workhorse first-round product. The other guys are role players. That’s why Harbaugh is getting questions about, well, not splitting up the touches in the backfield so much.
“Yeah, maybe,” Harbaugh told The Athletic’s Noah Furtado . “I think that’s something that we’re looking at, and I think we’ll try that, yeah. … I’ve been in that position before (with a three-back rotation), and it’s worked. I also think there’s a place to getting the backs in rhythm.”
Vidal, a sixth-rounder in 2024, has been a really fun success story through the way he has played well when given a chance amid injuries on the depth chart. He’s a solid way for other contenders to beef up their rotations before the playoffs.
Granted, a Vidal trade wouldn’t get much back in return. But for the Chargers, removing one overthinking roadblock for McDaniel and getting Hampton back on track might just be worth more than any late-round pick they get for Vidal’s departure.

title: Rams Injury Report: Trent McDuffie's Status Adds to Secondary Concerns Despite Key Returns
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams could be without their two starting cornerbacks on Sunday against the Washington Commanders. Earlier this week, the Rams announced that Jaylen Watson’s season was over with a shoulder injury . After missing all week of practice with a back injury, the Rams could also be without Trent McDuffie as he is officially listed as questionable.
"He's really done a great job in practice," said McVay on Friday about Garrett. "He has progressed really well, made a tremendous impact in practice on Wednesday and Thursday, feels really comfortable with the game plan. It's been great having him out there."
If the Rams are without McDuffie and Watson, they will be relying on Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes as their top two cornerbacks. While Wallace has filled in for McDuffie and Watson throughout the season, Forbes has remained in a rotational role. Without both McDuffie and Watson, Forbes would be thrown into a full-time role for the first time this season against his former team.
While the big news for the Rams on Friday was the team announcing that Myles Garrett would make his return against the Commanders, he won’t be the only player returning from injury.
The Rams were initially set to get tight end Terrance Ferguson back, he injured his hamstring during Friday's practice. Ferguson had been out since Week 3 with a medial ankle spring and would have been a welcomed addition back to the offense. Ferguson was expected back as the Rams activated his practice window this week. However, the team sent out an updated injury report on Friday with Ferguson's status updated to out on Sunday against the Commanders
With Ferguson out, the Rams could be shorthanded at tight end for a second straight week. Colby Parkinson was listed as questionable, but was a limited participant on Friday. If the Rams are without both, they would likely need to lean on rookie Max Klare.
The Rams are also likely to be without long snapper Joe Cardona as he manages an ankle injury, leaving Jake McQuaide in that spot. Wide receiver Jordan Whittington (back), linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), and safety Kam Curl (foot) were all listed as questionable as well. Curl was upgraded to a limited participant on Friday, but his status is still up in the air. However, Curl will have motivation to play against his former team if he is able.
While Steve Avila and Matthew Stafford were listed on the injury report earlier this week, neither was given an injury designation on Friday. Stafford was a full participant all week with an elbow injury while Avila was a full participant the last two days as he manages a hamstring. Both should be good to go.
On the Commanders’ side, they will be without wide receivers Treylon Burks and Dyami Brown. Defensive tackle Jer'Zhan Newton was listed as questionable.
If the Rams are without Watson and McDuffie on Sunday, it will be a significant blow to the secondary, especially if Curl is also unable to play. The return of Garrett should help take some pressure off the defensive backs, but the Rams will be relying heavily on their depth to get through Sunday against the Commanders.

title: Myles Garrett Set to Make Return vs. Commanders, But What Should Rams Expect?
full_text:
Ever since he was placed on injured reserve after Week 1, the Los Angeles Rams have been awaiting the return of edge rusher Myles Garrett. What was initially given a six-week timeline turned into seven. When the Rams a ctivated Garrett’s practice window this week , there was some positive momentum that he could be ready for Sunday’s game against the Washington Commanders. On Friday, head coach Sean McVay confirmed that Garrett will play.
Rams DE Myles Garrett is expected to play vs. Commanders, Sean McVay says
The Rams traded for Garrett in what was their biggest acquisition of the offseason . However, shortly into training camp, Garrett began missing practices with what was described as knee soreness and then was placed on injured reserve that week as he underwent arthroscopic surgery.
"There were just things I was dealing with mechanically that only continued to worsen as I played more throughout that game," said Garrett on Friday. "It was rough and I was trying to avoid it, but you learn and you grow. Now it's just a lesson that I had to learn from and I took the necessary steps to come back.”
With Jaylen Watson heading on injured reserve earlier this week, the Rams won’t get a look at what their defense could have been with Garrett, Watson, Trent McDuffie, and Aaron Donald. However, the Rams will get a look at what their defense can do with Donald and Garrett on the field together for the first time.
Trading for Garrett played a large role in Donald coming out of retirement. The Rams’ season certainly hasn’t gone as Donald may have expected, but nine weeks into the season, he’ll finally get to play alongside one of the biggest reasons he came back.
“It's good to have the pieces back to the puzzle. It was good to see him out there yesterday and today. He’s looking good, looking fast,” said Donald on Thursday. “Getting to work with him in full pads and playing off each other. It looked pretty good today, so I'm excited about having him here, having him back, and seeing what we do Sunday.”
As Garrett gets set to make his return , the question now becomes how much he’ll play on Sunday against the Commanders. The Rams have played it safe with Garrett since the summer and paid the consequences for not doing that in Week 1. While the Rams opened Garrett’s practice window and will activate him for Sunday’s game, it remains unlikely that he’ll play 100 percent of the defensive snaps.
The Rams have a strong rotation with Josaiah Stewart and Wesley Bailey, who have both filled in nicely while Garrett has been out. Additionally, Garrett coming back remains a step-by-step process. The Rams activated his practice window, slowly got him back into rhythm by having him take half the practice reps, and will now see how he reacts to a game.
“As far as what that snap count looks like if he is able to play, it's really truly like, 'Let's just see how today goes, and then let's see how tomorrow goes and [then] the following day,’” McVay said.
Back in Week 2 against the New York Giants when Donald played his first game of the season after slowly ramping up, he played 56.9 percent of the defensive snaps. In Week 1, Garrett played 61.5 percent of the defensive snaps while not being 100 percent.
It seems likely for Garrett's snap count to end up somewhere in that same range. He may play half or slightly more than half of the defensive snaps against the Commanders. The Rams will slowly ramp him up over the next few weeks, depending on how his body reacts. Overall, the goal will be to get Garrett to 100 percent for the second half of the season after the bye week.

title: Rams’ Most Likely Trade Deadline Move at Wide Receiver Is Far From Guaranteed
full_text:
Things remain quiet on the trade deadline front for the Los Angeles Rams. While they may inquire about players to see if there is a deal worth making, a trade remains unlikely right now given how competitive the wide receiver and defensive line markets have been.
With that said, if the Rams were to make a move, wide receiver seems to be the most likely position they would target. While the need for better wide receiver depth has been emphasized with Davante Adams being out, it's still something the Rams could use when he returns. The Rams simply don’t have a wide receiver they can trust behind Adams and Puka Nacua.
Konata Mumpfield has a 38.1 percent targeted success rate and has averaged -0.32 EPA per target. Despite running a route at the 25th-highest rate in the NFL, his 0.13 targets per route run ranks 86th out of 103 qualifying wide receivers.
Over the past few weeks, the Rams have been adamant that they trust their wide receiver depth. “I do think there are some guys on the roster that are capable of being able to step up if their number is called,” said McVay before referring to Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell.
“We definitely feel good about those guys being able to catch the football, but with a 60, 70-play game, there's going to be a lot that we require them to do,” added offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase on Thursday. “We feel like those guys can step up and do all those things.”
The Rams have consistently said that they trust their wide receiver depth, but their actions suggest otherwise. Mumpfield and Atwell have combined for just three receptions over the last two weeks without Adams. Comparatively, Nacua has 19.
Wide receiver is the most pressing need on the roster, and it’s an obvious one. Things will certainly improve to an extent when Adams gets back and Terrance Ferguson returns to action. However, at some point, the Rams will have to be able to throw the ball with three wide receivers on the field.
Last season, with the game on the line in the NFC Championship Game, the Rams had to rely on Mumpfield and Ferguson, who were both rookies. The Rams need a player they can trust in crucial situations to get open outside of Nacua.
The Rams don’t necessarily have the draft capital to compete with other teams in the wide receiver market. Josh Downs remains a top option for the Rams, but he also has other suitors such as the Kansas City Chiefs and Pittsburgh Steelers. According to Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer, Downs would probably cost a fourth-round pick.
Brian Thomas Jr. has been mentioned as a potential Rams target, but Breer reported that the Jaguars have been less inclined to trade him. Said Breer, “Thomas brings a downfield element that’s really important in keeping defenses honest against the run, and opening things up underneath for Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington.”
That leaves the Rams looking at secondary options, and at that point, is it worth making a move simply for the sake of it?
Treylon Burks and Calvin Ridley could be among the options. However, Burks has never had more than 450 yards in a season and hasn’t proven to be reliable. Breer reported that Ridley may only cost a sixth-round pick. While Ridley would only cost around $2.8 million this season, his cap hit jumps to $29 million next season, with $7.5 million in dead money if he's cut.
Which receivers are winning most of their routes? Data: @FantasyPtsData , min. 120 routes (% of routes with a positive separation score) pic.twitter.com/IMy3n6ZNOP
For as much as the Rams need a wide receiver, they may be waiting for an opportunity during the season if a veteran player is cut, similar to Odell Beckham Jr. in 2021. Brandon Aiyuk could be among those options .
The Rams certainly have a need at wide receiver. It’s been a need since the spring and the Rams have ignored it at every turn. Given their lack of draft capital and a hot wide receiver market, it seems unlikely the Rams will make a move at this point.
This is a team in a championship window, and for as much as the coaching staff has said they trust their wide receiver depth, that very clearly has not been the case. If the Rams make a trade, the most likely move at the trade deadline would be for a wide receiver.

title: Rams Midweek Report: A Concerning Trend on Offense, Matthew Stafford's Elbow, and Trade Buzz
full_text:
Through the first eight weeks of the NFL season, the Los Angeles Rams’ offense has been productive but inconsistent, to say the least. The Rams rank fourth in yards per game and third in offensive success rate. However, after failing to score 20 points against the Arizona Cardinals before scoring 35 against the Las Vegas Raiders, the Rams went three-and-out on their first five possessions last week against the Los Angeles Chargers. That was something that a Rams offense hadn’t done this century.
The Rams’ offense has had its games in which it has looked like a top-5 unit. However, they have struggled to find consistency. For an offense that made things look easy at times in 2025, the Rams have looked condensed and lacked the same level of explosiveness.
There is certainly some context to that as Davante Adams and Puka Nacua have each missed games. Terrance Ferguson has also been out since Week 3. At the same time, the Rams haven’t pushed the ball down the field very often.
Through eight weeks this season, the Rams’ passing game has an explosive play rate of just 4.1 percent. At this point last year, the passing game had an explosive play rate of 17.5 percent and it was 18.2 percent for the season.
The passing game is less than one-fourth as explosive as it was last year. That lack of explosiveness certainly helps explain some of the Rams’ troubles scoring consistently. Picking up yards hasn’t been an issue. The Rams also rank sixth in touchdown rate once they get into the red zone.
However, the Rams rank just 16th in points per play and have the seventh most plays per drive. The Rams are having to work extremely hard for their points because they have struggled to generate explosive plays.
Since Davante Adams went down with an injury, the Rams have just one passing play over 20 yards, and it was the 40-yard pass to Tutu Atwell last week. They have an overall explosive play rate of 5.8 percent, which ranks 27th.
The Rams have found success out of 13 personnel, but at some point the Rams need to be able to throw the ball. It’s easy to run against inferior teams when the game script is in your favor. However, when that goes south against a true contender, they need to be able to have confidence in their passing game. The eventual return of Ferguson and Adams will help, but is it enough?
Two of Matthew Stafford’s 10 lowest single-game averages in intended air yards per attempt have come this season. He has had four straight games averaging under six intended air yards per pass attempt. Over the last four weeks, Stafford has an average depth of target of 5.5 yards, ranking 25 out of 27 quarterbacks.
That’s simply not a world the Rams can live in consistently. When the quarterback isn’t pushing the ball down the field, there’s more pressure on the skill players to create after the catch.. Outside of Puka Nacua, there isn’t anybody the Rams trust to do that.
The Rams may be able to manage the situation until their bye week. However, it’s also a reason why adding a third wide receiver is so imperative to their success over the second half of the year.
One of the big stories coming out of Sunday’s game was Matthew Stafford being seen leaving the locker room with a bag of ice around his arm. Coincidentally, after not showing up on the injury report all season, Stafford was listed with a right elbow injury this week.
Despite Stafford saying he’s fine, this isn’t something to completely sweep under the rug either. It’s well known that Stafford is one of the toughest quarterbacks in the NFL. It will take more than an elbow injury to keep him out.
“Listen, I'm 38 years old trying to keep up with these young bucks,” said Stafford on Wednesday. “A little bit of soreness and stuff that is not uncommon this time of year. Again, I haven’t missed a rep at practice. I haven’t missed a rep in a game and I feel good. I'm not too worried about it.”
That’s what anybody would expect Stafford to say. He’s not going to let on that he’s in more pain than he’s actually in or dealing with something that would be considered concerning. Here’s what I will say, and it has since been confirmed to me by multiple sources.
According to Doug McCain of 97.1 The Fan LA, who is highly connected in LA Sports, Stafford suffered an elbow injury against the Denver Broncos, specifically when trying to tackle Talanoa Hufanga on the pick-6. It reportedly got to a point where the team was considering surgery. However, Stafford has opted to play through it and try to get right.
The Rams have a history of downplaying injuries. Look no further than this season with Myles Garrett. You can also point to Stafford’s back injury prior to last season and his elbow injury in 2022. Again, Stafford is going to try and play through it, which he has done successfully up to this point. At the same time, it is a situation worth monitoring.
This week, the Rams opened up Myles Garrett’s practice window . The Rams will now have 21 days to opt to take Garrett off of injured reserve and put him on the active roster. It’s important to clarify that just because the Rams activated Garrett’s practice window, it does not mean he will play on Sunday. His return could still happen after the bye week, as that would be when his 21-day practice window expires.
With that said, NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport reported earlier this week that when Garrett gets on the field for practice, it should all happen quickly. The expectation is for Garrett to play this week, but the Rams have prioritized a return to performance, not just a return to play.
“It's about that return to performance and a lot of it's going to be predicated on his communication and feedback to us,” McVay said. “Ultimately, being able to see that hopefully the expectation is he's ready to rock this week.”
Garrett practicing this week is certainly a positive. If he does play, it seems unlikely that he would play every snap on defense. The Rams have a strong rotation with Josaiah Stewart and Wesley Bailey. They will likely lean on that. The important thing is for Garrett to get on the field and feel like himself.
Things have remained quiet on the trade front for the Rams . However, that doesn’t mean they haven’t made calls or been monitoring certain situations. The Rams may not be players at the deadline, but they have at least done their due diligence.
What I will say is that they have called on wide receivers, specifically Josh Downs and Brian Thomas Jr. However, if a move does get done, it won’t happen until next week. According to NFL Insider Jordan Schultz , the Colts are trying to maximize draft capital out of their roster and believe teams could up their offers after Sunday as the trade deadline gets closer.
Schultz named Downs as one of the players to monitor who could be on the move. However, after willingly giving up Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner last week, the Colts are holding out on players like Downs and Jonathan Taylor. Right now, it appears the Pittsburgh Steelers and Kansas City Chiefs are the main players on Downs, but the Rams have called.
Earlier this week, the Rams cut wide receiver and returner Alex Bachman before re-signing him to their practice squad. As of now, it appears the Rams may be handing return duties over to Kyren Williams or Tutu Atwell. With that said, Williams is unlikely to offer more as a returner than Bachman and risks getting hurt. Atwell hasn’t returned punts since his rookie season, when he got hurt doing so.
Brennan Presley earned Second-Team All-Big 12 honors as a returner in 2022. He’s performed well in his preseason opportunities. Presley is exactly the type of player who should be a primary special teams contributor. It seems worth at least bringing him up to see what he can do.

title: Rams' Trade Deadline Priorities Shouldn't Change Despite Jaylen Watson Injury
full_text:
With less than a week to go before the NFL trade deadline, it remains unclear whether the Los Angeles Rams will be active. On Wednesday, the Rams announced that cornerback Jaylen Watson would undergo shoulder surgery and be done for the season. With needs at wide receiver and defensive line, it’s fair to wonder if cornerback is now added to the list as well.
Over the last two weeks, head coach Sean McVay has talked a lot about opportunity cost and how the price of acquiring a player could prevent the Rams from making a move.
“I would never rule out opportunities to get better, but at what opportunity cost?” McVay said on Monday. “You have to be able to figure out what does that look like for the long and the short.”
As it stands, it seems unlikely that the Rams will be active at the trade deadline, but the injury to Watson certainly adds a wrinkle. While the Rams may have a need at cornerback with Watson out, the needs at wide receiver and even defensive line remain far greater.
For the most part, the Rams should be able to manage at cornerback without Watson . Defensive backs coach Jimmy Lake has done a great job with the depth of that group, specifically with Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes.
According to Pro Football Focus, Wallace and Forbes both rank among the top 12 cornerbacks in the NFL. Forbes has a coverage grade of 79.9, which ranks seventh, and Wallace ranks 12 with a coverage grade of 76.4.
Additionally, Wallace ranks sixth in yards per coverage snap in 2026, and Forbes’ 0.49 yards per coverage snap ranks seventh. Forbes has been in more of a rotational role, but through eight weeks Wallace has the second-most snaps at cornerback on the roster behind Jaylen Watson.
“Josh has played a lot of snaps,” said McVay. “They both have played a bunch of meaningful snaps and they've earned the confidence of their teammates, their coaches, and I'm excited for them.”
Without Watson in Week 4 and McDuffie in Weeks 6 and 7, Wallace has played a large role on defense and stepped in nicely. It’s certainly different having to do that over the course of a season rather than filling in for a week or two here and there. At the same time, Wallace has done well in those opportunities. Wallace doesn’t give the Rams the same length as they would have with Watson, but he still brings decent size and has tackled well.
Despite the opening at cornerback, the Rams' priorities at the trade deadline should remain adding a wide receiver and a defensive lineman. The Rams aren’t going to be able to replace Davante Adams, but adding a third wide receiver who can play alongside him and Puka Nacua would make sense.
This season, Konata Mumpfield has remained extremely inefficient. Mumpfield has caught just 9-of-21 targets and has a -0.32 EPA per target. Tutu Atwell remains a limited receiver and Jordan Whittington is simply a special teams player.
It’s true that the Rams operate a lot of their offense out of 13 personnel, but that only works in a neutral-to-positive game script. In situations when the Rams have to throw the ball or are trailing, they have to be able to have three wide receivers on the field. Right now, even when Adams comes back, it’s hard to feel confident in them doing that. The Rams rank tied for 15th in EPA per pass out of 11 personnel.
At some point, it’s fair to say that the Rams will miss Poona Ford’s presence in the middle of the defensive line. The Las Vegas Raiders don’t have a strong rushing attack, and the same can be said about the Los Angeles Chargers. Ford played a big role in the Rams’ defense performing well against the run last season. Without Ford, the Rams are asking a lot of Ty Davis and Ty Hamilton to fill that void.
The Rams aren’t going to be able to address every need at the trade deadline if they opt to make a move. They will have to prioritize which positions make the most sense to address and whether adding a player at those positions would help close the gap as they push for a playoff spot in the second half of the season. While the Rams have a need at cornerback with Watson’s season coming to an end, the needs at wide receiver and defensive line remain much greater.

title: Rams vs. Commanders Prediction: Preview, Key Matchups, and What to Watch
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams finally won back-to-back games for the first time this season last week, beating the Los Angeles Chargers. Now, the Rams will head on the road to take on the Washington Commanders as they look to carry that momentum.
Through the first eight weeks of the season, the Rams have been inconsistent, but over the last two weeks, they’ve seemingly found their identity . The Rams have leaned into 13 personnel and the run game, making things easier on offense. They arguably had their best offensive performance two weeks ago against the Las Vegas Raiders and then were able to turn things around in the second half last week with a similar approach.
This season, the Commanders have been up-and-down as well, as they’ve managed an elbow injury to Jayden Daniels. However, despite being 2-4-1, they’ve played the NFC West tough. The Commanders beat the Seattle Seahawks back in Week 3 and then lost to the San Francisco 49ers by six.
After having a pass rate over expected of +4.9 in the first six weeks of the season, that has dropped to +0.6 over the last two games. The Rams have been much more balanced on offense and will look to continue that against the Commanders. This season, the Commanders rank 30th in EPA per rush allowed and 31st in defensive rushing success rate.
One of the best rookies this season has been linebacker Sonny Styles. It wouldn’t be surprising to see Sean McVay test Styles’ eye discipline, but his athleticism has been special to watch. Styles has had a Fred Warner-esque effect on the Commanders defense in coverage because of his range. The Rams have relied on their running backs in the passing game more often, and Styles will match up against them well. Styles also ran through Saquon Barkley in Week 1 on a blitz. The Rams’ running backs are going to have their hands full with Styles.
"That's not normal." DQ on Sonny Styles in coverage. #Commanders HC Dan Quinn and @LoganPaulsenNFL went to the 49ers tape for three Sonny plays: a square tackle in space, a third-down breakup on Mike Evans that had DQ comparing his range to Fred Warner's, and Sonny dropping into… pic.twitter.com/M6Td3iVtwc
This could be the first game back for Rams edge rusher Myles Garrett. That will certainly provide a boost for the Rams’ pass rush. Through Week 8, quarterback Jayden Daniels has yet to throw an interception, but with a new offensive coordinator, Daniels ranks 14th in EPA per play, and when he’s forced to throw, he ranks 19th. The Rams have struggled at times with running quarterbacks, notably Josh Allen in Week 5. Meanwhile, the Commanders have a scramble rate of 9.5 percent, which is the fourth-highest in the NFL. Having Garrett back could help with that, but the Rams’ linebackers will need to be on their game.
The Commanders have been steady at right tackle with Josh Conerly Jr. However, Brandon Coleman is susceptible to allowing pressure on the left side. Coleman has allowed 23 pressures this season, which is the seventh-most in the NFL. His 60.5 pass-blocking grade via PFF also ranks 49th out of 60 qualifying tackles. That should provide an opportunity for Josaiah Stewart to generate pressure and for Garrett to make an impact if he does play.
For a second time this season, the Rams will be playing an early game on the east coast. The last time was back in Week 4, when it took a 10-point fourth-quarter comeback for the Rams to win. If the Rams lean on 13 personnel and the run game, they should win this game. The Commanders don’t have Terry McLaurin and could struggle on offense. The Rams can’t get pass-happy in this game and risk falling behind. They need Kyren Williams and Blake Corum to combine for 25-30 carries, and that will put the offense in a good spot. Prediction: Rams 27, Commanders 23

title: Rams Injury Report: Myles Garrett Returns, But Bad News Continues to Pile Up
full_text:
While the Los Angeles Rams got some good injury news on Wednesday, the injuries also continue to pile up. Both Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson opened their practice windows as they work to return from injured reserve. However, cornerback Jaylen Watson’s season is over with a shoulder injury and cornerback Trent McDuffie was a non-participant with a back injury.
The biggest knock for the Rams is Watson being placed on injured reserve and being out for the season. Watson was the team’s top free agent signing as the Rams looked to rebuild their cornerback room this offseason. After missing Week 4 with a dislocated shoulder, Watson reaggravated the injury in the third quarter of the team’s win against the Chargers.
“The likelihood of it coming out and doing further damage to it is a very high probability. You could strap it, but it would restrict his movement,” said head coach Sean McVay. “Just some of the different things that we've received from our doctors, it's the right thing to do by him, even though it sucks because he's been such a bright spot for us.”
McDuffie was also a non-participant in practice with a back injury that he suffered at the end of Sunday’s game against the Chargers. He’ll be a player to monitor throughout the week. Long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle), tight end Colby Parkinson (ribs), and safety Kam Curl (foot) also didn’t participate in practice. Parkinson missed last week’s game and he’ll be one to watch as well.
While the Rams got bad news with Watson, Wednesday marked the first time since Week 1 that Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald were on the practice field together . Garrett opened his 21-day practice window on Wednesday, leaving open the possibility that he could play against the Commanders.
“It's exciting. It's great to be able to get him back out there,” said McVay. “He'll probably take half the reps today. If you have 30 reps, he'll take 15 and then we'll see how he feels coming out of that. Hopefully, it's just a little bit of an increase incrementally at a time.”
The Rams are taking it day-by-day with Garrett. McVay made comparisons to the 2022 season with the number of injuries that the Rams have dealt with. They have erred on the side of caution with Garrett since training camp and that will likely continue.
In addition to Garrett being back, Ferguson and running back Ronnie Rivers returned to practice as well. Ferguson should provide some insurance if Parkinson can’t play for a second straight week, while Rivers could be helpful on special teams.  Also limited were linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), left guard Steve Avila (hamstring), and wide receiver Jordan Whittington (back).
Coming out of the Chargers game, one of the big stories was Matthew Stafford being seen walking out of the locker room with ice around his right arm . Stafford showed up as a full participant on Wednesday’s injury report with a right elbow injury.
“It feels good. Full practice as I have been all year and hope to continue to be that way,” said Stafford. “Listen, I'm 38 years old trying to keep up with these young bucks. A little bit of soreness and stuff that is not uncommon this time of year. Again, I haven’t missed a rep at practice. I haven’t missed a rep in a game and I feel good. I'm not too worried about it.”
On the Washington Commanders’ side, quarterback Jayden Daniels was listed as a full participant with a left elbow injury that he’s managed most of the season. Wide receiver Treylon Burks and Stefon Diggs didn’t practice. However, Diggs missed practice for rest purposes.
For every step forward that the Rams seem to take on the injury front, they continue to take another step back. Garrett and Ferguson returning to practice are certainly encouraging developments, but losing Watson for the season is a significant blow. With McDuffie now dealing with a back injury, the Rams will need to hope that their improving health along the defensive front can help offset some of the concerns in the secondary.

title: Why the Rams' 2026 Bye Week Is Causing Controversy
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are quickly approaching their bye week, which is set to take place in Week 11. However, it won’t be a typical bye week that most teams get. While most teams get a full week off, making it 14 days between games, the Rams are only getting 10 days . Essentially, the Rams’ bye week has been negated with a mini-bye.
On Tuesday, Kelly Stafford posted a story on Instagram, criticizing the NFL for its scheduling choice.
Kelly Stafford, wife of #Rams QB Matthew Stafford, calls out the NFL for the team's bye being only 10 days. Because the Rams host the Packers on Wednesday night (Thanksgiving Eve), their Week 11 bye is only 10 days between games instead of the usual 14. pic.twitter.com/jdrdjispll
“Just curious to hear the thought process behind making the Rams the only team in the NFL without a true bye week,” wrote Stafford. “Because damn, after 18 years around this league, even I need a week off during the season and I have never played a single snap. I’m tired just watching from the stands. Can’t imagine how the guys feel.”
Instead of a typical bye week, the Rams will have a shortened break because of their upcoming Wednesday matchup against the Green Bay Packers. Stafford mentioned that the Rams are the only team to have a shortened bye week, but it’s worth mentioning that the Packers will be in the same situation.
The NFL did the right thing by putting the Rams and Packers in the same situation with both teams playing on a Wednesday. At the same time, the Rams were just one of three teams with a negated bye week in 2026.
With that said, the Rams got more rest after Week 1 coming back from Australia. They’ll get 10 days off for their actual bye and then eight days off before playing the Kansas City Chiefs. The Rams will then get a third-mini-bye before they play the San Francisco 49ers in Week 14.
When the NFL released its schedule, the Rams were a team with a significant rest disadvantage. The Rams were set to play five games with less rest than their opponen t. According to Warren Sharp ’s schedule analysis, the Rams were tied for 24th in net rest in 2026.
There is certainly reason for criticism for how the NFL came up with the Rams’ schedule. The lack of a true bye week is one of them.With that said, the Packers will be in the same situation.
That doesn’t mean that the NFL shouldn’t be criticized. Just because another team is in the same situation doesn’t make it right. Teams are given one bye week per season and the NFL has taken that away from two teams. With the NFL scheduling games on Thanksgiving Eve , it wouldn’t be surprising if two more teams faced the same situation next year.
Given that Kelly Stafford spoke out about the Rams’ lack of a true bye week, it’s fair to wonder if the players, especially Matthew Stafford, feel the same way. With the number of injuries that the Rams have had to manage this season, the extra four days would likely have been beneficial.

title: Rams May Be Better Equipped to Overcome Jaylen Watson Injury Than Expected
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams got more bad injury news on Wednesday when it was reported that cornerback Jaylen Watson would undergo shoulder surgery , ending his 2026 season. It has been a consistent theme for the Rams in 2026, and just as they were set to get Myles Garrett back, Watson is now out for the year.
There’s no doubt that losing Watson will be a huge blow to the secondary. The Rams made Watson their top free agent target in the spring after trading for his teammate Trent McDuffie. After giving up 346 yards passing and three touchdowns to Sam Darnold and the Seattle Seahawks in the NFC Championship Game, the Rams made it a point to rebuild their cornerback room and Watson was a big part of that.
Among qualifying cornerbacks, Watson’s 0.71 yards per coverage snap ranked 10th in the NFL. His 4.87 yards per target ranked sixth. The Rams signed Watson to give them a lengthy, physical outside cornerback to play on the boundary and he’s been able to provide that. Watson has nine pass breakups, which ranks fifth this season.
With Watson out, the Rams will be relying on Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes in his spot. While there is certainly a difference in being a rotational player and playing full time, the Rams have gotten good production out of Wallace and Forbes this season.
“I think those guys have done really well," said head coach Sean McVay. "Jimmy Lake has done such a great job really with those corners as a whole group. Josh has played a lot of snaps. I thought 'E-Forbes' really played well last week. Both of those guys have been tapped in. They've been ready to step up and it seems like there have been a lot of games that we've had our top corners get banged up and they've played a lot more."
Wallace ranks sixth in yards per coverage snap in 2026 and he’s played often. When Watson was hurt in Week 4, Wallace played 100 percent of the defensive snaps. He also played all of the defensive snaps in Weeks 6 and 7 with McDuffie out due to injury. Wallace may be a rotational player, but he’s played just five snaps fewer than Watson this season on defense and more snaps than McDuffie.
Additionally, Emmanuel Forbes has played well in 2026. Using Forbes less in a smaller, rotational role has benefited both the team and the player. The Rams have been able to be more selective about the situations he plays in.
Forbes’ 0.49 yards per coverage snap ranks seventh in the NFL and his 3.13 yards per target ranks fourth. Despite playing just 25 percent of the defensive snaps this season, Forbes has been credited with seven impact plays via Sumer Sports.
According to Pro Football Focus, Wallace and Forbes both rank among the top 12 cornerbacks in coverage grade. Forbes has a coverage grade of 79.9, which ranks seventh, and Wallace ranks 12 with a coverage grade of 76.4.
While it may have been disappointing when the Rams lost Aubrey Pleasant in the offseason, the impact that defensive backs coach Jimmy Lake has had on the cornerback room can’t go unnoticed. Under Lake, Wallace and Forbes have developed into reliable depth cornerbacks who have held their own when called upon. The Rams also signed Cam Lampkin to the active roster on Tuesday, who was a preseason and training camp standout.
Given that Wallace has played in a full-time role for much of the season, the moment shouldn’t be too big for him. Wallace has gotten grabby at times as he’s been called for three defensive pass interference penalties. However, for the most part, he’s exceeded expectations.
Again, losing Watson for the season is a significant blow to the defense. However, Wallace has stepped in well when his number has been called and Forbes has also played well. The Rams have spent much of the season overcoming injuries, and Watson's absence presents another challenge. With Watson out, the Rams’ depth will certainly be tested, but based on what Wallace and Forbes have shown, there’s reason for optimism.

title: Rams Suffer Another Major Injury Blow as Jaylen Watson Ruled Out for Season
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams will be without cornerback Jaylen Watson for the rest of the season . After re-injuring his shoulder, Watson will undergo surgery, ending his 2026.
Rams CB Jaylen Watson is getting shoulder surgery and is out for the season.
Watson left in the third quarter of Sunday’s game against the Los Angeles Chargers after aggravating a shoulder injury. He had previously dislocated his shoulder in Week 3 and was forced to miss one game. Watson had played the next two games without issues, but re-injured his shoulder on Sunday.
Head coach Sean McVay discussed Watson’s shoulder injury during his media availability on Monday and expressed optimism about his status. However, after further evaluation, it was decided that surgery was the best option.
“We'll see what his status looks like as the week progresses,” McVay said on Monday. “Came in, had some good strength, feeling good and optimistic. We'll take his status a day at a time and see where he's at by the time the game rolls around.”
Watson now heads on injured reserve and is set to miss the rest of the year. In Watson’s place, the Rams will likely rely on Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes. Wallace has filled in for both Trent McDuffie and Watson this season. He has quietly developed into a reliable depth cornerback. Wallace has allowed 0.71 yards per coverage snap in 2026, ranking 20th in the NFL among qualifying cornerbacks. Forbes has also played well in a smaller role and will be relied on going forward as well.
Coming into the season, Watson was one of the Rams’ big offseason additions. After allowing Sam Darnold to throw for 346 yards and three touchdowns in the NFC Championship Game, the Rams made it a point to rebuild their cornerback room.Watson was the team’s big free-agent signing following its trade for McDuffie.
The Rams simply can’t seem to shake the injury bug this season. It has been one injury after another all year. Two weeks ago, the Rams had to place Poona Ford, Kobie Turner, and Davante Adams on injured reserve. Just when it seemed like they were going to get healthy and get Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson back , the Rams had to place Watson on injured reserve.
Losing Watson is another blow to the defense that the Rams will have to manage over the second half of the season. Wallace and Forbes have shown that they can step up when needed, but Watson being out for the year is still a significant loss for a secondary that had finally started to find its footing.
