title: Miami Dolphins Week 8 Instant Takeaways: Second-Half Collapse Costs Potential Signature Win
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins really had a shot at getting their first signature win of the Jeff Hafley era, they really did.
But if it hadn't already been established, the game served as a reminder this is a team that's operating with a very small margin for error, and there were a few too many of those in the second half, along with a controversial officiating reversal that changed the momentum.
Truth to be told, this was an encouraging performance by the Dolphins in the big picture, even if they did let one slip away after leading 13-3 at halftime after completely shutting down an injury-riddled New England offense.
The Dolphins are making progress, that's what's important here. And, yes, they did make progress and still look much improved from the team they were in the early weeks of the regular season.
Dolphins fans no doubt will lament the replay official overturning the Dolphins' fourth-down stop when they were leading 13-10 in the third quarter, instead giving New England a first down that kept alive what became the touchdown drive that gave them the lead for good.
But it wasn't the only play that swung the tide.
Ollie Gordon II got flagged for an unnecessary and, frankly, stupid unsportsmanlike conduct for yapping at an opponent to turn a third-and-5 into a third-and-20 in that forgettable third quarter. Then Zane Gonzalez, elevated from the practice squad for a second consecutive week, badly missed a 43-yard field goal attempt to basically put the Dolphins in a position where there only shot was to recover an onside kick, which basically never happens in the NFL anymore.
Beyond that, New England simply was the better team in the second half when they outscored the Dolphins 21-6, though the Dolphins again were plucky and fought to the end, as we figure they'll do all season even if the wins aren't that frequent.
-- It figured that Gordon would have a tougher time against the Patriots, particularly with Kadyn Proctor missing the game with his concussion, and that's how it played out. And we wouldn't fret over his ability to have other big games.
-- While we don't necessarily complain about play-calling, there was a pretty obvious lack of urgency in the fourth quarter when the Dolphins were down two scores and still running the ball, and often letting the play clock run down.
-- This isn't their identity, but this was a game where the Dolphins needed to air it out in the fourth quarter, not be calling running plays on second-and-12.
-- Malik Willis was fine, even though his performance wasn't as good as it was against the New York Jets. He certainly wasn't the reason the Dolphins lost.
-- Guard Jonah Savaiinaea has no doubt made significant improvement in his second season, but there's still some lapses that show up in his game.
-- Jarrett Kingston did a respectable job in place of rookie Kadyn Proctor, though he had to overcome a shaky start.
-- On the flip side, Austin Jackson had one of his best performances of the season.
-- The defense hardly could have played better in the first half and it seemed as though everybody chipped in.
-- What hurt more than anything in the second half were the two big plays, the two long touchdown passes that accounted for almost half of Drake Maye's passing yardage.
-- Props to Jacob Rodriguez for creating a turnover with a perfect Peanut punch, though he overall had a pretty quiet game.
-- The pass defense continues to get shredded, with Maye completing 80 percent of his passes. The coverage on DeMario Douglas' 43-yard touchdown was particularly depressing as he caught a pass wide open between defenders and had so much space that he could zigzag the rest of the way to the end zone.
-- Chris Johnson is normally a very good tackler, which is why it was so baffling to see whatever that was that he attempted against Maye when he came in free from behind for what should have been a sack. He should have had redemption later on that drive with a fourth-down stop, but of course there came the overrule from the replay assistant when television replays didn't suggest anything obvious enough to overturn the original ruling.
-- That play was just yet another example why instant replay stinks.
-- Yes, Willie Gay Jr. looked kind of bad on Maye's rushing touchdown off an option play, but the reality is he was one defender against two offensive players. There didn't appear to be anybody outside to handle the pitch had he zeroed in on Maye, so he was kind of in an impossible position there.
-- The special teams again had a rough outing, but missed field goals will happen and long punt returns allowed unfortunately have become commonplace. What's unforgivable is Jaylen Wright fielding a kickoff near the sideline instead of putting himself out of bounds before touching the ball, which would have created a penalty on the Patriots and given Miami the ball at its 40. Those are fundamentals the Dolphins simply have to recognize.
-- Guess we could blame it, like everything else, on Miami being a young team. But those are the kind of mistakes we want to see disappear sooner rather than later.
-- In the final analysis, though, this was a frustrating loss because the Dolphins put themselves in position for the big upset and weren't able to deliver. The first part alone, though, was a sign of progress.

title: Examining the Outside Factors That Could Impact the Dolphins' Week 8 Game Against New England
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins' Week 8 matchup against the New England Patriots won't be lacking for storylines, including Miami's quest for a second consecutive victory, but there are some that go beyond X's and O's.
The Dolphins will go into the game following their breakthrough 28-25 victory against the New York Jets to face the defending AFC champion Patriots, who have a 4-3 record following a Thursday night loss against the Chicago Bears in Week 7.
The Patriots will go into the game missing star wide receiver A.J. Brown and backup running back TreVeyon Henderson, while the Dolphins will be without rookie first-round pick Kadyn Proctor with star running back De'Von Achane on injured reserve.
New England will enter the game as a 7.5-point favorite, according to the FanDuel Sportsbook, but if you believe in the idea that weather can be an equalizing factor, then the weather in Miami Gardens on Sunday should be considered.
It was raining in Miami Gardens on Sunday night, but the forecast called for the weather to actually get worse — if not much worse — throughout the afternoon and into the night.
The outlook as of 10 a.m., according to Weather.com, read as follows: "Storms likely for the next several hours. Potential for heavy rainfall."
There also is a flood watch in several areas of the northern parts of Dade County, where Miami Gardens is located.
With the expectations of thunderstorms, we also can't help but look back to the Dolphins' 2018 season opener against the Tennessee Titans when two lightning delays lasting more than an hour each made the game last more than seven hours.
And obviously the field conditions could become a factor at some point with the ball getting slippery and footing also potentially becoming an issue.
The other outside factor in the Dolphins-Patriots game that needs to be watched, even though it hopefully won't affect the outcome one way or the other, was the officiating crew switch late in the week.
The officiating around the NFL has come under a lot of scrutiny this season, but it may have reached a high point (or low point maybe?) in the Green Bay Packers game against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field last week, leading to Packers safety Xavier McKinney lashing out publicly after the game.
McKinney drew a fine from the NFL for using the term for bovine excrement in talking about the officiating, but he wasn't the only one complaining.
Ton Brady openly criticized at least one call for roughing the passer during the game, but the most egregious call came for an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty when Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown got up after catching a pass, a Packers defender tackled him thinking the play wasn't over but knocked down an official in the process, with the official responding by throwing a flag while on his back.
Likely as the result of not wanting the spotlight on the officiating crew of Alex Moore, the NFL took them off their scheduled assignment for the Sunday night game between Philadelphia and Washington and moved them to the Dolphins-Patriots game, which will be shown to a ridiculously small portion of the country as the "other" 4:25 p.m. on CBS opposite Kansas City at Denver.
Moore's crew, for the record, officiated the Dolphins' home opener against the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 3, calling eight penalties on each team. Moore also worked the Dolphins-Patriots game at Hard Rock Stadium in Week 2 of 2025.

title: Every Option the Vikings Should Explore as Kyler Murray Injury News Worsens
full_text:
What started out as a sore hamstring after the Lions game has now been revealed to be a Grade 2 strain for Kyler Murray, according to Tom Pelissero.
Vikings QB Kyler Murray is rehabbing a Grade 2 hamstring strain that will keep him out of Monday night’s game against Buffalo – and potentially beyond. More in The Sweep: https://t.co/2WjDotsn76 pic.twitter.com/FSPegIsdWo
The Vikings had already planned on keeping Murray out for Monday night's contest against the Bills, but it now seems that he'll miss more time as well. Carson Wentz will get the nod at quarterback, but with the trade deadline looming on Tuesday, there's plenty of routes the Vikings can examine for the remainder of 2026.
Here's every possible avenue the Vikings could explore at quarterback, and why they can (or can't) work.
Wentz has already played this for Minnesota season, rallying a Week 1 comeback against the Packers, and keeping things steady in a monsoon at Chicago. There's plenty of folks who think Wentz has actually been the better option all along, and that the Vikings offense will see a boost with him under center.
Wentz is a very different quarterback than Murray, but does different mean better in this case? It's possible. Unlike Murray, Wentz will throw across the middle, find Justin Jefferson, and work on-schedule.
He also plays with his feet in cement, though, and the Vikings interior hasn't exactly been cooking up pancakes up front. The Vikings offense should find some better rhythm under Wentz, but his first test's difficulty will be set to HARD.
With the trade deadline quickly approaching, Wentz will only get one game to audition for the job. The high-powered Bills are sure to put up points, even against Brian Flores, and Wentz will have the task of keeping pace. If the offense stumbles, general manager Nolan Teasley could start working the phones.
If Wentz doesn't show up on Monday, the Vikings may turn their attention outside of the building to fix their offensive woes. The options are plentiful, but really there's only two that make any sense whatsoever.
If Las Vegas falls this weekend to San Fransisco to drop to 4-5, there's a slight chance they may be willing to part with Cousins. A win, however, all but ensures the 38-year-old sticks in silver and black.
Cousins is putting up MVP-type numbers this year, with 19 touchdowns to just five interceptions, making this trade potentially difficult. Still, outside of Wentz and maybe Max Brosmer, Cousins probably knows this offense better than anyone else, and the Vikings should look to add him--maybe even if Wentz looks serviceable.
The Raiders will have little motivation to deal the respected veteran Cousins, even in a loss, and the Vikings would surely have to overpay to get the guy they could've just signed this March anyway. Sunk-costs aside, Cousins is probably the best quarterback for the 2026 version of the Minnesota Vikings.
Herbert is one of the worst quarterbacks in football this season with a league-leading 10 interceptions, but his track record up to this point shows a top-10 guy who just hasn't meshed with his new coordinator.
The Chargers have swiftly declined any and all inquiries up to this point, but at 0-7 with little direction going forward, they'd be foolish to hang up the phone if Teasley starts dangling multiple-first rounders in front of them.
The Vikings obviously have quarterback needs in 2026, but the only quarterback under contract for 2027 is Brosmer , and Herbert would certainly solve that issue. Clearly this season hasn't gone to plan for him, and Kevin O'Connell and the Vikings would need to be certain that this year is simply a speed bump, and not a cliff.
Herbert is a needle mover, and the same just can't be said for Daniel Jones or Geno Smith despite their potential fits and cheaper price tag.
There's always the possibility that Minnesota still believes this thing can get figured out with Murray as QB1 despite his underwhelming start. With Murray now expected to miss at least two weeks, the Vikings could try and keep this thing afloat until his return.
Murray has avoided the big mistakes this year, which obviously helps, but he's also avoided the big plays too. His uber-conservative play has kept games close, but he hasn't elevated the offense in any meaningful way either. Jefferson isn't involved, and the explosive plays just haven't been there.
The good news, though, is that those problems mostly aren't due to lack of ability, and if Murray can settle into the playbook a bit more, maybe those plays start to trickle in.
Many are already out on Murray, believing that a full summer and six games is already enough time to be comfortable with the offense--which he's obviously not. For the few that still think a couple more weeks is all he needs to see things click, it wouldn't be too surprising to see Murray as the signal-caller to start the playoffs.

title: The Best, Worst and Most Likely Vikings Outcomes vs. the Bills in Week 9
full_text:
The 6-1 Vikings are turning to Carson Wentz at quarterback for Monday night's game against Buffalo as Kyler Murray tends to a hamstring injury. It's possible that the move sparks a change in the offense, and Minnesota finally gets some rhythm and life on that side of the ball. Equally possible, though, is that the Vikings are no closer to figuring out their offensive woes as the Bills roll.
Either way, Monday night's outcome will have significant ramifications for how the rest of the season goes in more ways than one. That said, here are the best, worst, and likeliest scenarios for Week 9.
The Vikings are turning to Wentz for the third time in the last two seasons, and maybe this start will somehow be better than his first two stints as starter. Truthfully, Wentz hasn't been terrible during his appearances, throwing for 213 yards per game and a solid 9:5 TD/INT ratio over his seven contests. But he'll need to bring his best to keep pace with the NFL's No. 1 scoring offense.
If the defense does its thing and limits the damage done by Josh Allen and company, and Wentz looks much sharper than Kyler Murray, the Vikings may finally have direction after floating in uncertainty for much of the last few weeks.
It's clear that the offense has not only been lackluster, but is now actively holding the team back from its true potential. A strong statement from Wentz may give the Vikings all they need to push their chips into the center for the remainder of 2026.
The Bills' defense has yielded a 300-yard passer in three games this season, so the opportunity for Wentz and the Vikings' offense to succeed is certainly there.
Offense looks ok? Defense is fine? Surely this can't be the worst-case scenario! While this scenario may not be the worst individual game result, it would make the Vikings' course of action for the remainder of the year dreadfully nebulous.
If the Vikings stumble in a close game, they'll fall to 6-2 with the trade deadline up next, followed by dates with the Packers and 49ers. Another underwhelming performance paired with a strong record sends some mixed signals , but the pressure for the Vikings to still be buyers at the deadline would be immense.
Still, with a tough schedule and no obvious direction after a theoretical defeat to Buffalo, would general manager Nolan Teasley feel comfortable enough to go all-in on the 2026 edition of the Vikings? It's hard to say, and that call would be made infinitely easier by a win or a blowout loss.
That's not to say a big loss is especially helpful, but it may protect the Vikings from suffering the same fate as the now-tanking Indianapolis Colts just a year after their big swing at a title.
Brian Flores and his defense do all they can, but like in Detroit, the levee is going to burst at some point.
Allen is a bit scary, but so is the Minnesota defense. The Vikings have already proven they can handle almost anything, but it's hard to stay on the field for over 35 minutes without some fatigue showing. The defense has allowed just 10 total points in the fourth quarter all season, and seven of those came last week against the Lions. But if Wentz and the offense don't offer any help on Monday, there's only so long Flores can keep Allen and the Bills at bay.
Ultimately, the Vikings probably keep things close for a while thanks to their elite defense and ability to take care of the ball on offense. Wentz will push the ball downfield more than Murray ever did, and there's a good chance the offense looks much healthier. But much like what happened with the Lions, the defense, believe it or not, has a limit. If Kevin O'Connell can't engineer long drives that end in points, the Bills will probably pull away late, which will culminate in a consecutive loss for the Vikings.

title: 3 Most Important Things to Watch for as Vikings Host Bills in Week 9
full_text:
Through nine weeks, the 2026 Vikings’ season has been quite the rollercoaster. A 6-1 start hasn't been enough to silence growing concerns about a struggling offense and the need to find a long-term answer at quarterback .
Now, the Vikings and their top-tier defense prepare to host the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football, hoping a QB change provides the spark their offense needs.
Let’s break down what’s on the line under the Monday night lights.
Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell ended any speculation about the team’s Week 9 QB on Thursday, announcing that Carson Wentz would start , as Kyler Murray recovers from a hamstring injury. Time will tell if this is the boost Minnesota’s problematic passing game needs, but Wentz seems to know his top task: get the ball to Justin Jefferson .
#Vikings QB Carson Wentz says he understands why Justin Jefferson is frustrated about not getting the ball as much as he wants: “Just get him the rock. He's as good as I've been around. ... I want to get him the rock as much as anybody.” pic.twitter.com/TAEk1MgSi8
Jefferson has thrived with Wentz compared to the other QBs he’s played with over the past two seasons, averaging close to 40 more receiving yards with Wentz than with Murray. If the Vikings want to win on Monday, Jefferson will need to be the star we all know him to be, and Wentz will need to take advantage of a defense that allows the third-most passing yards per game in the NFL.
Brian Flores and the Vikings defense facing off against Josh Allen is the reason this game was tailor-made for a primetime slot. Allen needs no introduction, as he’s been one of the league’s top QB’s for close to nine seasons now. The combination of Allen and running back James Cook (brother of former Viking Dalvin Cook) has helped the Bills post the second-most yards per game in the NFL this season.
The Vikings’ defense faced a similar challenge against Jared Goff and Jahmyr Gibbs last week in Detroit and held their own for the first half. Minnesota sacked Goff four times and held Detroit to only six first-half points.
Eventually, Gibbs took over, but the first-half formula could translate to this week, especially if the offense actually helps out this time. The Vikings' defense has proven it can hang with the best, and shutting down Allen and Cook would be another statement for Flores.
Of all the games left on Minnesota’s November slate, their one matchup against a non-conference opponent is admittedly the least consequential from a standings perspective, but it still carries major implications. With the NFL trade deadline approaching on Tuesday, Minnesota’s performance against one of the league’s top teams could give general manager Nolan Teasley confidence in which direction this team is heading.
The Vikings are going to start Carson Wentz Monday night against the Bills. Kyler Murray is dealing with a hamstring injury and is week to week. Could Minnesota look to add a QB before the deadline? My report on our @NFLonPrime postgame show. pic.twitter.com/gQMQBvvWW7
While numerous reports have emerged in recent weeks surrounding potential trade targets for the Vikings, steam has picked up over the last 24 hours around a potential QB acquisition. Two NFL insiders, James Palmer of NFL on Prime and Adam Schefter of ESPN , have hinted strongly that the Vikings may be looking for an upgrade. Schefter stated Friday on his podcast that he’s “watching the Vikings’ quarterback position.” (h/t: VikingzFanPage)
If the Vikings see another strong defensive effort wasted by a poor passing game, Teasley may have no choice but to find a fix to save the season.

title: 3 Vikings Coaching Decisions I'd Make If I Were Kevin O'Connell Ahead of the Bills Game in Week 9
full_text:
The loss at Detroit served as a wake-up call for a Minnesota team that had enjoyed beating up on some listless teams over the past few weeks. Now with Buffalo up next, things won't be any easier in Week 9, and the Vikings will be forced to make some adjustments after last week's defeat.
With Carson Wentz getting the nod at quarterback and the NFL's top offense coming into town, here's everything I would do if I were in head coach Kevin O'Connell's shoes.
The Vikings are rushing the ball at a slightly higher clip than passing it in 2026, with a 199-193 split. Sacks, playing with leads and other factors are certainly at play here, but with Wentz under center this Monday, the Vikings should let it fly.
To keep pace with the No. 1 scoring offense in the NFL, Kevin O'Connell will need to find ways to put points on the board. Surely that means opening up the passing game and getting Justin Jefferson the ball—something that has proven to be a challenge for the Minnesota offense halfway through the season.
The last Vikings passer to throw for over 250 yards was Wentz, way back in Week 7 of 2025. The anemic passing attack has got to get going against Buffalo, and O'Connell should have few concerns about taking the ball out of the hands of Jordan Mason and Aaron Jones.
Safety Theo Jackson was a DNP at Thursday's practice with a quad injury and seems to be in danger of missing Monday's contest. In that case, Harrison Smith and Joshua Metellus would get an increased workload, but UDFA rookie Jacob Thomas should get some significant action too.
Jackson has played 60% of the defensive snaps this year, but hasn't made a tremendous impact. He's allowed two touchdowns and a perfect quarterback rating when targeted, and while Jackson's been solid against the run, he remains untrustworthy deep in coverage.
Enter Thomas who despite an impressive preseason hasn't gotten much run during the season so far, playing just 7% of the defensive snaps. If Jackson does have to miss the game, it'll give the coaching staff a built-in excuse to give their undrafted rookie a long look. There's a decent chance they don't regret it.
The Vikings have already attempted to trade Jauan Jennings once, and now he popped up on Thursday's injury report, leaving the door open for a possible OBJ practice squad elevation.
The Vikings have already done it once this season (he didn't play), and another elevation means Beckham has just one left before he either needs to be signed to the 53-man roster or be set free. His role on the field since signing with the Vikings has been essentially non-existent, and it's clear that he's far from making an impact between the lines.
Beckham is a nice veteran to have, however, and one who also happens to be great friends with a certain Justin Jefferson. Why force a decision on his status with the team sooner than they need to? Let's treat Beckham for what he is at this point in his career, and let him ride out his days teaching and cheering from the sideline.

title: 3 Bold Vikings Predictions Heading Into Monday Night’s Matchup With Bills in Week 9
full_text:
It may be hard to believe, but we’re already in Week 9 of the NFL season, as your 6-1 Vikings prepare for a matchup every fan had circled on their schedule.
The Vikings will host the 6-1 Bills in a Monday night matchup four years in the making. The teams last faced off in an all-time classic in Buffalo in 2022, with Minnesota winning 33-30 in overtime. Expecting the same level of cinematic excitement on Monday night may lead to disappointment, but there’s reason to think this game could still be great, especially if the Vikings’ offense improves .
Let’s dive into my boldest predictions for Monday night.
Accountability time: I was wildly off the mark with my prediction for Justin Jefferson’s yardage total against the Lions last week . To be fair, even the most pessimistic of skeptics didn’t expect the passing game to be that shaky. Luckily for Jefferson, Carson Wentz may be on his way to save him.
Kyler Murray is battling through a hamstring injury and was officially ruled out for Week 9 on Thursday. Head coach Kevin O'Connell revealed that Wentz will start against the Bills on Monday, while Murray remains "week-to-week," according to ESPN 's Kevin Seifert.
Kyler Murray (hamstring strain) is OUT for Monday's game, per Kevin O'Connell. Carson Wentz will start vs. Bills. O'Connell says Murray is week to week.
If there’s one thing Wentz does well, it’s getting Jefferson involved early and often. Jefferson averages 9.3 targets and 89.1 receiving yards per game with Wentz under center through seven games. Compare that to 7.6 targets and 52 yards per game in three full games with Murray.
Wentz will need to feed his star wideout if the Vikings want to end the night with a statement win.
This one is a swing, but I’m betting on the Vikings defense to defend their home turf against one of the best offensive units in the NFL.
Josh Allen and the Bills are averaging 393.1 total yards per game, trailing only the Lions. The Vikings defense, meanwhile, allows the second-fewest yards per game at only 271.6. Getting to Allen early while preventing him from taking off will be the key. This will be one of their hardest challenges of the year, but I'm certain defensive coordinator Brian Flores and his unit are preparing hard for this one.
Minnesota’s defense put up a strong effort in Detroit last week, but a total lack of help from the offense eventually opened the door for Jahmyr Gibbs to ice the game. A better offensive performance and home-field advantage should keep the unit energized. The Vikings will need it against a loaded offense led by Allen and James Cook.
The ingredients for a Wentz legacy performance are starting to add up. The Vikings’ passing game needs a serious boost;o Jefferson and Jordan Addison need targets, and head coach Kevin O’Connell almost certainly wants to silence the doubts around his offensive scheme. Time to let it rip.
The Carson Wentz career arc is like no other. pic.twitter.com/wFV21ULa0W
The Bills’ 254.7 passing yards allowed per game are the third-highest total in the NFL this season, an average higher than any passing performance we’ve seen this year from a Vikings passer. Murray’s 247 yards against the Dolphins is currently the season high, but I think that changes Monday.
Mark me down for Wentz over 250 through the air.

title: Vikings Need to Think About 2027 QB Plans ASAP After Another Kyler Murray Injury
full_text:
Just like that, the Kyler Murray era may have ended before it really began.
Head coach Kevin O’Connell announced Thursday that Carson Wentz will start against the Bills on Monday as Murray is “week to week” with a hamstring injury. O’Connell was noncommittal about which quarterback would start the remainder of the season when asked by Dane Mizutani of The Pioneer Press.
Kevin O’Connell says his focus is on this week’s game when asked if Carson Wentz could be the starter going forward if he plays well on Monday Night. pic.twitter.com/ghKhxis1QJ
While Murray may still see the field for the Vikings this season, the outlook for an extension has taken a significant hit. Not only has Murray already missed two games this season with a concussion, but his on-field performance has been mediocre at its best.
With no QB under contract after this season, it’s time for general manager Nolan Teasley to find an answer at the most important position in sports.
There are currently three members of the Vikings QB room, and none of them seem to be the answer going forward. Murray and Wentz are both on one-year deals signed this past offseason, while Max Brosmer is in the final year of a two-year deal he signed as an undrafted free agent.
So far, none of them have performed well enough to secure a long-term extension, but with Minnesota’s history of backup QBs and playoff runs, there may still be hope for Wentz.
Former GM Kwesi Adofo-Mensah was fired largely due to his handling of the QB situation last season, and his replacement’s first major move was trading the QB he selected tenth overall in 2024 to the Giants for a fifth-round pick. With no answer, and the only QB locked in beyond this year shipped off, Teasley must get this right.
There are two main approaches he can take.
Next year’s QB class was highly touted before this season, but serious concerns about the group’s readiness have emerged as the college season has progressed. The Vikings also likely won't have a premium first-round selection.
The last thing they want is to repeat the mistakes they made with McCarthy and Christian Ponder by drafting a QB they aren’t fully sold on simply because they needed to.
ARCH MANNING THROWS A COSTLY INTERCEPTION WITH 20 SECONDS LEFT!! pic.twitter.com/Hq9o38IUzf
I’d say the odds of the Vikings finding their immediate franchise QB in April’s class seem low, but a poor end to the season or draft-slot maneuvering could put them in striking range of the right guy. But failing to win a playoff game this season could cost O’Connell the time needed to develop a young signal-caller.
This is the likeliest path the Vikings will take, but even this is incredibly complicated. Minnesota is projected to have limited cap space next offseason and is set to lose multiple key starters on both sides of the ball. Would spending big on a QB be the right move if the rest of the roster takes a hit?
Some projected free-agent QBs include Deshaun Watson, Kirk Cousins, Jacoby Brissett, Anthony Richardson and Mac Jones. Jones is likely the best mix of fit and long-term upside, but he could be the priciest QB of the bunch. A reunion with Cousins seems possible, but he’s set to enter the 2027 season at the fresh age of 39.
Kirk Cousins to Brock Bowers in the end zone for the @Raiders TD! 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/7no1cq9Huf
With neither path looking especially promising, the best option may be to sign a trustworthy vet and swing for a high-upside prospect in the draft. If that seems too risky, it may be time for Teasley to work the phones for an aggressive QB trade.
Has anyone checked on Justin Herbert lately?

title: Kyler Murray Ruled Out: How Carson Wentz Can Beat the Bills
full_text:
Kyler Murray or Carson Wentz? The Vikings' quarterback debate reached its pinnacle last Sunday after a troubling defeat to the Detroit Lions, leaving many to wonder whether Kevin O'Connell would consider making a switch after another lackluster performance from Murray.
That question has been answered, although not in a traditional sense. Murray was dealing with a sore hamstring after the loss, and O'Connell has now said it'll keep the quarterback sidelined at least this week, per ESPN's Kevin Seifert. Wentz will get the start against the Bills.
Kyler Murray (hamstring strain) is OUT for Monday's game, per Kevin O'Connell. Carson Wentz will start vs. Bills. O'Connell says Murray is week to week.
O'Connell also mentioned that the injury won't lead to Murray going on injured reserve, but they'll have to take things a bit slower with his hamstring because of how important Murray's legs are to his game.
The injury obviously isn't ideal, and losing any depth at quarterback hurts, but the Vikings will now get a relatively pressure-free look at their potential new starter.
Wentz has already played in two games this year for Minnesota--a big three-touchdown day in the opener and a quieter day in the Chicago monsoon. The 39-point outburst in Week 1 is still the Vikings' highest-scoring game this season by a mile. The Bills now come to town with an offense rivaling that of the Lions, and there's no question the Vikings will have to put up points.
Up to this point, Murray has done well protecting the football and avoiding the big mistakes that lose games. That's certainly beneficial for a coach who wins over 90% of the time when his team ties or wins the turnover battle. But Murray isn't adding much value beyond that , and has struggled to find receivers and work the middle of the field.
Ideally, Wentz takes care of the ball too, but also finds ways to get the ball to this other guy named Justin Jefferson. It's the worst- kept secret in the NFL right now that Jefferson is unhappy with the offense, and it's hard to blame him. His 6.7 targets per game rank 36th in the NFL, and Murray has struggled to both find Jefferson and then get him the ball accurately.
And while the Bills' offense is ferocious, the defense is allowing 254.7 yards per game through the air (ranked 30th in the league).  So, the opportunity will certainly be there for Wentz to make an impact if he can work the field. Getting the ball to the best player on the planet couldn't hurt either.
If Wentz and the Vikings' offense rolls, does that bring up questions about the quarterback position for the remainder of the season? It should, but for now, O'Connell says he's only focused on Monday night.
Kevin O’Connell says his focus is on this week’s game when asked if Carson Wentz could be the starter going forward if he plays well on Monday Night. pic.twitter.com/ghKhxis1QJ
The Vikings are still 6-1, riding a generational defense. Last week showed a bit of fatigue starting to set in after Brian Flores' unit carried the team for the first two months of the season.
Eventually, the offense will have to do its fair share if the Vikings are to make a deep playoff run. Maybe Wentz is the start of that? If he's not...well, let's try to think about it.

title: Final Vikings Trade Deadline Big Board: Potential Targets for Every Positional Need
full_text:
The Vikings boast a 6-1 record, but their playoff aspirations are all but certain . The NFC North is the best division in football, and it's possible a team could win 10 games but finish dead last. If the Vikings want to avoid that fate, they may need to get aggressive at the fast-approaching trade deadline .
How aggressive general manager Nolan Teasley gets may hinge on their Week 9 result against the Bills, but there's no question the Vikings need to add reinforcements to stay atop the division.
Here's who the Vikings could look to add at some key positions ahead of Tuesday's deadline.
Anything can still happen here, but it's looking less likely by the day that the Vikings will be willing to meet the Colts' asking price for Jonathan Taylor. Head coach Kevin O'Connell talks about team elevators all the time, and Taylor is the trade deadline poster child for one after back-to-back 1,400-yard seasons.
Still, sending first-round value to a running back who will be 28 years old next season on a team that doesn't have its quarterback situation settled is a big gamble. The 2026 defense would be a terrible thing to waste, but the Vikings likely look for a more budget-friendly addition to the backfield.
Pollard has quietly notched four straight 1,000-yard seasons and is enjoying another strong campaign on an otherwise lifeless Titans offense. Tennessee might not want to strip away talent from their young quarterback, Cam Ward, but at 1-7, they may just want to take what they can get for a 29-year-old back.
Pollard is older than Taylor, but would come at a significantly lower price . The Titans' runner could likely be had for third-round value, but his age and fit beyond 2026 could complicate a deal for the Vikings.
Henderson is an intriguing option for Minnesota because of his youth and explosive ability. The Patriots haven't indicated he's on the trade block (out loud, anyway), but Henderson has been demoted on the offense to RB3 just a year after nearly a 1,000-yard season.
The Vikings don't have a home run threat in the backfield, and Henderson would check that box after averaging 5.1 yards per carry in 2025, but Teasley may have to overpay to get the former second-rounder.
After bowing out of the Quenton Nelson sweepstakes, the next best option would be Dickerson , who finds himself on an imploding 2-6 Eagles team. After losing Donovan Jackson to injury, the Vikings' interior has been a weak spot, with Will Fries struggling and UDFA Joe Huber forced into the rotation.
Dickerson offers a short-term improvement and a potential long-term partner for Jackson. At just 28, and with a low base salary in 2026, it's hard to imagine the Vikings not kicking the tires here.
Powers-Johnson was impressive as a rookie, but has seen his play—and snap counts—drop since his breakout debut season with the Raiders. The Vikings could look to rediscover that rookie form and a 93% pass-block win rate, but they'd have to do some digging first.
Ultimately, Powers-Johnson could probably be had for a Day 3 pick and offers some flexibility to play both guard and center.
Cousins makes the most sense if the Vikings feel neither Kyler Murray or Carson Wentz can get the job done come January. He has familiarity with the system and could theoretically jump into the offense with little ramp-up time. The problem is that the Raiders' quarterback is putting up MVP-type numbers and has Las Vegas sitting at 4-4 and right in playoff contention.
If the Raiders win this week, a trade is all but dead. But if Cousins and Las Vegas struggle against the San Francisco, Teasley probably makes the call—at least just to check in.
The Chargers are 0-7 and, at least internally, are likely exploring all options moving forward. There's been no sign that L.A. has any interest in trading their struggling quarterback, but if the Vikings call and offer two first-round picks for Herbert, the Chargers may just have to listen.
Herbert had been a top-10 quarterback in the league until Mike McDaniel got his hands on him in 2026. But for this trade to work, the Chargers need to believe a full reset is the best path forward, and the Vikings need to believe they can fix the worst quarterback in football at the moment.
Another Eagle, Ojomo, is likely available after Philly already handed out big money to Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis. Ojomo had six sacks in 2025 from the interior and could give the Vikings a boost while they wait for Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange to develop.
Still, like Jalen Redmond, Ojomo would be looking to get paid next year too, so would the Vikings have enough to commit to them with plenty of other mouths to feed like Blake Cashman or Andrew Van Ginkel?
Robinson is a seasoned vet who would provide an instant boost to the Vikings' run defense (and apparently pass defense too, as the 6'3", 310-lb lineman has two interceptions this year).

title: Latest Kyler Murray Injury Update Adds to Vikings' Offensive Concerns Ahead of MNF vs. Bills
full_text:
Fresh off their first loss of the 2026 season, the Vikings don't have much time to reflect on defeat as a Monday Night Football showdown against Josh Allen and the Bills looms in Week 9 . With the NFC North race as tight as ever, Kevin O'Connell can't afford consecutive losses; however, the Vikings head coach's job could be a little tougher if he's forced to go into battle without his starting quarterback.
Kyler Murray's Week 9 outlook has been up in the air since he suffered a hamstring injury in the loss to the Lions. Although Murray said he "wasn't really hampered" by the injury on Sunday (h/t ESPN 's Kevin Seifert), it didn't stop fans from worrying about his availability.
Unfortunately, a potential absence seems more likely by the day. On Thursday, NFL insider Adam Schefter appeared on ESPN 's "Get Up" and reported that it's looking like Murray will miss the upcoming clash with the Bills.
"Kyler Murray (the Vikings) said, has a hamstring injury that they're evaluating," Schefter said. "Clearly, his status for Monday is—at best—up in the air. It sounds like it is trending towards Carson Wentz starting."
“It sounds like it is trending towards Carson Wentz starting Monday night.” — @AdamSchefter on how Kyler Murray's injury could affect Bills-Vikings 🤔 pic.twitter.com/Lcu9lZHFZ6
Thursday also marks the Vikings' first practice of the week, so more updates should be on the way in the coming days. Nevertheless, the latest Murray update isn't what Minnesota fans wanted to hear heading into the crucial matchup.
It's no secret that the Vikings' offense has been frustrating to watch more often than not this season. They've been held to fewer than 20 points in more games (four) than they've surpassed that number (three), all while averaging the sixth-fewest points per game (20.0), fourth-fewest yards per game (279.4), and fourth-fewest yards per play (4.7).
For comparison, the Bills rank first or second in all three of those categories. They've also scored 30-plus points in five of their seven games so far, whereas the Vikings haven't hit that mark once.
Murray hasn't been perfect in his first season in Purple and Gold, completing 64.9% of passes for 1,022 passing yards, five touchdowns, three interceptions, and an 86.6 passer rating in six starts. That said, he's been showing signs of improvement lately, with his stats improving over the last three games compared to the first trio:
Kyler Murray's first 3 games
Kyler Murray's last 3 games
With Murray likely missing Monday's action, the Vikings will turn to Wentz under center.
The former Super Bowl Champion has made two appearances so far this season: one in relief for Murray in the season opener against the Packers, and a Week 2 start vs. the Bears. Although the Vikings walked away with wins in both contests, the offense didn't exactly explode under Wentz's watch. He went 23-of-39 (59.0%) for 276 passing yards, three TDs without an INT, and a 106.4 passer rating.
Wentz can clearly lead the Vikings to victory when the defense shuts down the opposition, but that won't be easy against the Bills' high-octane offense. There's a good chance that Minnesota will need to fire on all cylinders if it hopes to have a semblance of a chance to win, and it's hard to see that happening with Wentz, who's thrown for 200 yards just three times in 15 games (10 starts) since Week 6 of the 2022 season.
Hopefully, Murray's injury isn't severe, and if he has to miss time, it's just the one game. Asking Wentz to be the starting QB for an extended period sounds like a disaster waiting to happen, especially when Father Time is undefeated.
If Murray's injury had popped up earlier in the season, the Vikings would have more time to explore potential backup plans . Much to their dismay, the trade deadline is quickly approaching on Tuesday, essentially leaving general manager Nolan Teasley with two options: 1) Maintain the status quo and hope that Wentz is good enough in Murray's absence, or 2) Turn over every possible stone for a last-minute trade .
With the bye already behind them, the Vikings don't have any help to get healthier in the second half of the season. Let's hope that the next updates on Murray's hamstring injury are positive.
Otherwise, the Vikings might be in for a long final stretch.

title: Vikings' Biggest Defensive Concern Can Be Solved by a Trade Call With Eagles
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings may have a lot of bodies available on the defensive line, but many of them are struggling to be effective or are young players who need time to develop before they can become major contributors.
Minnesota should be in the market to trade for players to help stay on top of the NFC North and prepare for a hopeful playoff berth. One player who may be available in trade talks is Philadelphia Eagles defensive lineman Moro Ojomo.
Philadelphia selected Ojomo in the seventh round of the 2023 NFL Draft, and he has played 335 defensive snaps for the Eagles this season. Through eight games, he has 21 tackles, four quarterback hits and three tackles for a loss.
The Vikings' defensive line has some solid play this season. Jalen Redmond is ranked tenth among all defensive linemen with a 78 overall Pro Football Focus grade and should be a priority for Minnesota to re-sign. However, other big men in the trenches haven't fared as well as Redmond.
Here are other Vikings' defensive linemen's PFF grades and rankings through eight weeks:
Ojomo has a 57.6 PFF grade, which would give him the third-highest grade on Minnesota's roster. This season, he has generated 18 quarterback pressures and 14 hurries while earning a 57.1 run defense grade.
Standing 6-foot-3 and weighing 292 pounds, Ojomo is a versatile defender in the trenches who could help give the Vikings more time to develop Banks and Orange slowly, and not rush their development, while still being competitive.
Minnesota has struggled to slow down the run lately and has given up long rushing touchdowns in each of its last two games. According to a clip from The Aftermath shared on X by ESPN senior reporter Jeremy Fowler, Ojomo is a player that Minnesota could show interest in acquiring .
Right now, Vikings fans are waiting for Minnesota to make a move. Trading for a quality player right now would prove that the franchise believes that a deep playoff run is possible. Hopefully, the Purple and Gold can get a deal done before the Nov. 10 trade deadline to make the team as competitive as possible for the remainder of the season.

title: Patriots Players, Coaches Remember Rob Gronkowski Ahead of HOF Induction
full_text:
FOXBORO — Kevin Byard remembers the game well. It was the New England Patriots and Tennessee Titans in the 2017 AFC Divisional game at Gillette Stadium. Byard, then just a second-year player in a upstart Tennessee secondary, can recall lining up against Rob Gronkowski all night long.
"I remember every time Tom Brady saw me lined up against him, he threw the ball at him," he told Patriots On SI this week ahead of Gronkowski's induction into the Patriots Hall of Fame Saturday afternoon. "I want to say he probably completed every single pass, even a touchdown. He's just a big dude, he's hard to cover."
Gronkowski, the Patriots' all-time leading in postseason touchdowns with 12 , finished that game with six receptions for 81 yards and that touchdown in a 35-14 drubbing That game still sticks with Byard, now a Patriots captain.
"He would literally just make a play, try to stiff arm you into the dirt and then he'll get back up and run back to the huddle," Byard said. "He just went about his business."
In general, it's hard not to love Gronk. The best tight end in franchise history, the one that made football fun to play and nearly impossible for any defenders in his area, is getting his red jacket-like flowers. He becomes the 38th member of the Patriots Hall of Fame and the third member of the team's Super Bowl LIII-winning squad to earn his place in New England immortality.
It's clear he made his mark in the region and the region made a mark on him.
"It means everything about my NFL career with the Patriots, just to be able to, you know, be recognized with the greats that were all before me, that’s what it’s all about," Gronkowski said.
It wasn't just the younger generation of Patriots fans that he impacted with his play. Even a young Drake Maye in North Carolina was a fan of the four-time Super Bowl champion — even having him on his fantasy football teams.
"I had a Gronk T-shirt jersey growing up, I remember I was a big T-shirt jersey guy in the NFL, wore it to school," Maye said. "So, I'm a big fan of his game. You see a lot of his film come up in the quarterback room of his ability to break tackles, make catches. ... That's a special player that I've gotten to know with a special personality. Just like I said, another appreciation for, if not the best, one of the best to ever play."
Gronkowski's highlights have been shown in film meetings this year. Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels has made it a point to show off the impressive catches from Gronkowski, like his one-handed one against the Broncos in 2014 and another spear against the Bills three years later.
"He was a great teammate," McDaniels said. "He was unbeliavable to coach, he took coaching very well. He was very smart. He was prepared and Rob always seemed to play his best in the biggest games.
"There's not too many people like him."
McDaniels got to coach him for years. Mike Smith, the Patriots outside linebackers coach, had to gameplan against him. With the Jets from 2010 to 2012 and then again with the Kansas City Chiefs in 2018, Smith knows all too well what Gronkowski brought to the field.
"You can't put a linebacker on him because he's gonna outrun him. A safety, he's gonna big-ball him ... and he'll block your ass off," Smith said.
"Clearly one of the best tight ends that's ever played this game and I love his personality."
In the 2018 AFC title game in Kansas City, Smith groaned remembered that game — where Gronkowski finished with six catches for 79 yards, including several key first down pickups late, as well as plenty of chip blocks at the line of scrimmage. The Patriots would go onto win that game in overtime (and the Super Bowl two weeks later), concluding Gronkowski's career in New England.
"They're not gonna waste Gronk like that," he remembered. "He chipped both edges the entire game and did not even give them an opportunity to direct that game."
Byard said it perfectly in the locker room. Gronkowski's the most dominant tight end to ever play the game, especially after the catch.
"He was incredible," Byard said.
Now, that dominant tight end will forever be enshrined in the Hall .

title: Predicting How Patriots Look vs. Packers: High-Flying QB Battle On Tap
full_text:
Both sitting at 5-3, the New England Patriots and Green Bay Packers have ridden the talents of their young quarterbacks to this point. Drake Maye and Jordan Love have been some of the best passers in the NFL this season and their Sunday matchup should be a good one.
Even though the Packers are sitting in the basement of the NFC North, this game will be a good measuring stick for the Patriots as they look to remain in contention for the top spot in the AFC East.
Ahead of Week 9, Patriots On SI beat reporters Ethan Hurwitz and Zac Ventola break down how the game will unfold, which players will be x-factors and predict a final score. Who do you think is right?
Love has been playing really well this season , especially when it comes to uncorking it and launching it deep. Whether it's Matthew Golden, Christian Watson or Tucker Kraft, the Packers have several guys that can stress the back-end of the Patriots' secondary. They'll need to find a way to limit Green Bay's explosive threats past the sticks. But that's easier said than done.
"A really, really intelligent quarterback, talented, athletic," Mike Vrabel said of Love about what he saw from him coming out of college. "I think all those things have proven to be true. His poise and composure at the line of scrimmage, I think he's worked on cadences, and the operation has really improved from a young quarterback coming out."
X-Factor: WR Mack Hollins (if activated)
Without A.J. Brown for the second-straight week and Romeo Doubs still on IR, the Patriots continue to deal with a depleted wide receiver room (DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, Efton Chism III). If the Patriots choose to activate Hollins off of IR for this game, they'd be able to get some much-needed size back at the position. Hollins hasn't played since Week 4 after dealing with a calf injury suffered in Buffalo, and returned to practice this week.
Final Score Prediction: Patriots 28, Packers 23
The Patriots, despite the slow start in Miami a week ago, feel like they're on a roll. In front of a national audience with Tom Brady calling his first Patriots game, I don't see how this week ends in a loss. What it will take is Maye slinging it just like he's done the last few games and use his legs to extend some plays — as well as not letting Green Bay's rushing attack with Josh Jacobs find its footing.
A week ago, the injury-riddled Patriots played an awful Dolphins squad and narrowly edged out a win. On Sunday, the still-injury-riddled Patriots will have to perform to their highest level for a chance to beat a Packers squad with playoff aspirations.
New England’s best chance at victory? Forcing Green Bay quarterback Jordan Love to make poor decisions. The Packers’ pass-heavy offense averages the second-most yards through the air in the NFL, and the fewest rush yards per game. Green Bay’s 28-year-old signal caller has thrown an interception in each of his past three games, an opportunity New England may need to capitalize on.
This season, Green Bay has relied heavily on second-year wide receiver Matthew Golden. The speedy pass catcher sits top-10 in the NFL in both receptions and receiving yards. I expect Jones to play a major part in attempting to slow down the wideout’s production on Sunday. Not to mention, Jones’ other role for the Patriots — punt returner — is one the Packers have stuffed all season long. Green Bay allows the second-fewest yards per punt return in the NFL.
From locking down a star wideout to boosting the New England offense’s field position, Jones will play a pivotal role in his team’s success on Sunday.
Final Score Prediction: Packers 30, Patriots 24
I would be shocked to see the short-staffed Patriots can pull off a win over this highly touted Packers squad. New England hardly had the talent to take down Miami a week ago. With the Patriots’ receiver room still highlighted by DeMario Douglas , Efton Chism and Kyle Williams, it feels hard to believe they can produce enough offensively to squeak out a win.
But maybe — just maybe — a Super Bowl LI reunion, Tom Brady being back in Gillette Stadium and Rob Gronkowski being inducted into the team’s Hall of Fame might just bring the magic New England needs come Sunday.

title: Tom Brady Returning to Gillette Stadium, Set to Broadcast First Patriots Game
full_text:
This week's New England Patriots game will have all the hoopla surrounding it , and part it won't even be about the football being played on the field. It's the first time that Tom Brady, the seven-time Super Bowl champion quarterback and Patriots Hall of Famer, will be part of the team's broadcast. The now-FOX Sports analyst has made it this far without calling his former team's games and that changes this weekend.
Until this week. As the Patriots prepare for the Green Bay Packers, the legendary Brady is set to return to the stadium where he became an icon and where a statue of him stands right outside one of the entrances.
"It’ll certainly be emotional," Brady said to FOX's Colin Cowherd this week . "To be back there and to really understand what that Patriot organization is all about and to convey that to the fans in a way where I’m not talking about myself, but I’m really talking about this awesome program that’s been built — the Patriots just always seem to do things the right way."
Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel, who played eight years alongside Brady and won three Super Bowl, didn't have the same emotional response when asked about his teammate's return.
"I think I'm required contractually to catch up with him at some point. I'm sure it'll be a Zoom. I'm sure they won't show up here. I'm sure it will be on Zoom," Vrabel said Wednesday, a bit tongue in cheek. "Contractually I'll be talking to him, and I'm sure I'll see him at Gronk's (Rob Gronkowski) induction on Saturday."
Somehow, Brady has evaded calling games since taking over the top analyst role for FOX in 2024. He was reportedly supposed to call a game that season, but because of New England's struggles under new head coach Jerod Mayo, FOX took their No. 1 crew off that game.
He's been back twice since retiring as a player. Once at his Patriots Hall of Fame induction ceremony inside the stadium and then again one year later when the team unveiled his statue . He hasn't been back as much as some fans might have liked (part of that is just because of his minority ownership stake with the Las Vegas Raiders ). It's truly a changing of the guards.
Yes, Brady's statue is outside on the concourse and his plaque hangs in the adjacent Hall of Fame museum. But this isn't Brady's Patriots anymore. His stamp still reverberates around the area, but that's in the past — and his status as a broadcaster doesn't have that large of an impact on the current quarterback.
"Yeah, it's obviously cool. What a legend to come back here, and it's definitely cool for him, I bet, to come back and call a game in the stadium where he won so many games and was a legend in this stadium," Drake Maye said. "Really, him, the fans and their teams built Gillette into what it is now. So, I bet it's cool for him.
"It really doesn't affect me much. You talk to him, and I'm not even sure we're allowed to talk to him in production because he's with the Raiders. But it's always cool to see. You don't hear much back from the TV copies. You don't really watch much of my own TV copies unless it's little things of, if I said anything that I think could hurt us. But really other than that, I know he hangs out around the field sometimes, so you just try to go appreciate him for what he left here, and that's really about it."
Similar to Maye, the Patriots players inside the locker room don't really have much to say about who'll be calling the game. They're more focused on the task at hand, and this week, it's the Packers.
Nobody on the current roster played with Brady when he was with the Patriots. In fact, other than Vrabel, only one active player suited up alongside Brady during his NFL career.
"I did have somewhat of a relationship with him. He was a mentor to a lot of the guys on the team, especially on the recovery aspect," Carlton Davis, who played with Brady and won Super Bowl LV with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2020, told Patriots On SI.
Brady's comments from the broadcast booth won't impact how well the Patriots perform. But considering he'll be back inside Gillette Stadium for a football game for the first time since 2021, this weekend should be a fun one for everyone involved.
Practice squad linebacker Benton Whitley — a Springfield native — can now appreciate just how special Brady and the entire Super Bowl LI team that's being honored pregame was as a fan growing up.
"I remember taking it for granted, honestly," he told Patriots On SI. "It would be a thing where me and my boys would be like 'Oh, are you going to the Super Bowl parade this year?' and then we'd be like 'Nah, we're going to the next one.' But being in the league now, I started to understand how actually hard it is to get to the postseason and then be the winner. ...
"He's arguably the greatest football player of all time."

title: Patriots Get Varying Injury Updates Ahead of Week 9 Matchup
full_text:
FOXBORO - The New England Patriots got a mixed bag of updates on several key players on Friday. Before practice, running back TreVeyon Henderson released a statement addressing his absence from the team. He revealed that he experienced an unexpected and unusual medical emergency that resulted in unexplained neurological symptoms that required several days of hospitalization. "I know that he is well loved and well respected on our football team," Vrabel told the media. "Just trying to make sure that TreVeyon is cared for and the recovery plan is intact and he's comfortable with it." While Vrabel chose not to discuss potentially placing Henderson on the Non-Football Injury list, he did confirm that he will not play Sunday because of this medical emergency. After poor weather forced the team to practice indoors, we got a better look at who else may or may not be available come Sunday.
Vrabel confirmed that Brown will be OUT against the Packers, missing back-to-back games as he continues to manage lingering ankle and knee injuries. He has not practiced since Wednesday, Oct. 28, as concerns surrounding a reported degenerative knee condition continue to swirl. "I know he's working extremely hard to get back," Vrabel said. "He's staying engaged in meetings and everything else and doing everything that we ask him to do." The Patriots traded 2028 first- and fifth-round picks for Brown back in July with an understanding of his medical status. However, so far this season, they haven't gotten the return they hoped for from Brown. With the Patriots set to travel to Munich, Germany, next week, Brown's availability remains an important storyline. "I'm not sure yet," Vrabel said after being asked whether the team would need to make a decision on Brown earlier in the week. "I'll focus on this week and what that looks like."
Vrabel also noted that both tight end Hunter Henry (foot) and cornerback Marcus Jones (foot) will be questionable for Sunday's matchup. Henry returned to practice Friday for the first time after leaving their Week 8 matchup against the Dolphins with a foot injury. As one of Drake Maye's most reliable targets, Henry has been a major contributor to New England's offense. He leads the team in receptions. If he can't go, Eli Raridon, Cameron Latu, and Tanner Arkin will headline the TE room. Tanner Connor remains on the practice squad. Jones was a surprise addition to the injury report this week; after being a full participant on Wednesday, he was nowhere to be seen on Thursday with a foot injury. Like Henry, he returned to the practice field on Friday. Outside of these two, the status for players like Kevin Byard III (chest), Carlton Davis III (neck), Mack Hollins (calf), Gabe Jacas (knee), Dre'Mont Jones (shoulder/knee), Morgan Moses (foot), Brenden Schooler (hamstring) and Greg Van Roten (hamstring) remain uncertain.
When asked about how wide receiver Mack Hollins and guard Greg Van Roten progressed this week, Vrabel left the door open for their return status. "I think we'll see how they come in tomorrow and make some decisions on where they're at," Vrabel told the media. Both players had their 21-day return windows opened this week and are eligible to be activated from injured reserve. With injuries hampering their respective position groups, getting either player back would provide a much-needed boost to New England's depth heading into a tough stretch of the season.

title: Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson Releases Statement Regarding 'Unexpected' Medical Emergency
full_text:
TreVeyon Henderson released a statement addressing his extended absence from the New England Patriots, revealing that he recently experienced an unexpected and unusual medical emergency. Henderson had been away from team activities with what was initially reported as an illness. He was seen leaving the Patriots' facility on Wednesday, Oct. 28, ahead of the team's Week 8 matchup against the Miami Dolphins. He ultimately did not travel with the team. In his statement, Henderson revealed that the medical emergency involved unexplained neurological symptoms that required several days of hospitalization. Although extensive testing has produced reassuring results, the cause of his symptoms remains unknown. Here is Henderson's full statement, released Friday morning.
"I would like to provide an official statement regarding the medical condition I’ve been experiencing. "Recently, I experienced an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms that required hospitalization for several days. During that time, I underwent extensive medical testing and evaluation. While the results of my comprehensive medical testing have come back positive and reassuring, the cause of this remains unknown and unexplainable. "I will continue working closely with specialists and physical therapists to focus on my recovery, as these symptoms have affected my strength, coordination, and some of my physical functions. I am committed to doing everything necessary to return to full health. My health and long-term well-being remain my foremost priorities. "I want to thank my wife for being by my side throughout all of this, and most importantly, I want to thank Jesus for giving me a peace that surpasses all understanding. Despite all of this, my heart rejoices in The Lord and my heart is at peace knowing that He is always faithful and His promise of Romans 8:28 always remain true. “And we know that all things work together for good to those who love God, to those who are the called according to His purpose.” The purpose of trials in life is not to drive us away from God, but to only bring us closer. May God’s Will be done, not mine. "My wife and I are deeply grateful for family and loved ones, the New England Patriots organization, my agent, my medical team, teammates, and everyone who has offered prayers, encouragement, and support. "We respectfully ask for continued prayers and privacy as we focus on my health and recovery. Love, Trey"
🙏🏽 pic.twitter.com/l52XuixPOc
In light of this information, the Patriots will need to prepare for the possibility of being without Henderson for an extended period of time as he focuses on his recovery. New England's running back room currently consists of Rhamondre Stevenson, Corey Kiner and Lan Larison, who was notably signed to the active roster ahead of this news. Terrell Jennings remains on the practice squad.

title: After Ravens' TNF Loss, Should Patriots Trade for Future Hall of Fame RB?
full_text:
The New England Patriots currently have four running backs on their active roster , plus a fifth on the practice squad. But could they — or should they — end up making a deal for another?
Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry, one of the greatest to ever play the game and stuck on a team trending all the way downward, could potentially be on the trade block ahead of the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline .
Do the Patriots swing for the fences?
Last night, the Ravens looked really bad in a Thursday Night Football loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. After injuries decimated the quarterback postion, the Ravens are trying to make it work with rookie Joe Fagnano (and potentially a trade for former Patriots captain Jacoby Brissett). Sitting at 4-5, now is the time for the Ravens to start selling off some of their pieces for something of value.
The Patriots' running game, despite the logjam on the roster, hasn't been all that. Sure, Rhamondre Stevenson has looked great as the starter, but TreVeyon Henderson has been out of sorts for weeks as he works his way through two ankle injuries and now an illness certain to hold him out of Week 9. Corey Kiner, a trade acquisition in August, is a fine runner, but won't light the world on fire. Lan Larison and Terrell Jennings follow up behind.
Operating under the assumption that Henderson will be out for a bit, the Patriots could use another solid runner. Who better than Henry, who spent six seasons with now-Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel in Tennessee. After Vrabel was fired in 2023, Henry departed in free agency to Baltimore.
The Patriots are reportedly interested.
According to AtoZ Sports , both the Patriots and the New York Giants (Henry's former head coach with the Ravens, John Harbaugh, is now the Giants head coach) have reportedly been in conversations for the future Hall of Famer.
It doesn't feel like the Patriots would have to give up the world to acquire Henry. Whether it's a fourth or fifth round pick, that would be a move that a team looking to buy should absolutely pounce on. Henry signed a two-year extension prior to last season, so he's under contract until after 2027. He's only making $1.25 million this year as a base salary ( which the Patriots can afford after restructuring Hunter Henry's contract last week ).
Yes, Henry's 33. But he's shown how good he can be in an offense that's firing. Right now, with Drake Maye playing as well as he is, Henry could thrive.
Vrabel has said all the right things about potentially adding someone or reworking the roster via trade, and you could expect him to be thrilled about the idea of Henry's skill set in this offense.
"I've said this a bunch, and I'm sure that Eliot (Wolf), when he speaks, and Ryan (Cowden) and whoever else speaks on our behalf, we'll always try to look and see ways to make the roster better and make our team better," Vrabel said this week. "There's certainly a lot of things that we have to look at with the roster."
Now, the Patriots should only do this move if they feel like Henderson's illness/absence will bleed deep into the regular season. If it is, pounce. If not, it might not be worth giving up something for another running back and shove your second round pick from a year ago further down on the depth chart.
There are other burning needs that could be addressed further, like another offensive guard or some help along the defensive front, but passing up on a talent like Henry is going to be hard to do.

title: Looking Back at the 5 Best Rob Gronkowski Moments with Patriots
full_text:
Rob Gronkowski was a football unicorn, a man amongst boys, a one-man wrecking crew. Whatever analogy you prefer, they all tell the same story; Gronk was truly one of a kind. His otherworldly athletic ability and Adonis-like stature, paired with his carefree, childlike personality, made him a Hall of Fame talent who captured the hearts of fans across New England. With his Patriots Hall of Fame induction set for Saturday, Nov. 7, l et's take a look back at some of his greatest moments in a Patriots uniform .
Late in the fourth quarter of the Patriots' 42-20 dismantling of the Indianapolis Colts in 2014, Gronkowski delivered one of his most memorable moments in a New England uniform. However, it wasn't a touchdown. He didn't even have the ball. As Patriots running back Jonas Gray scored his fourth touchdown of the day (yes, four), Gronkowski was nearly 10 yards out of bounds, still executing his block on Colts safety Sergio Brown.
When Rob Gronkowski threw Sergio Brown “Out Of The Club.” pic.twitter.com/zp1BRCMGRs
The two former teammates (Brown played for New England from 2010-11) had some history before that moment. Brown was the player who broke Gronkowski's arm during an extra-point attempt in 2012. According to Gronkowski, he had also spent much of their 2014 matchup talking trash. "He was just yappin' at me the whole time," Gronkowski said at the time. "So I took him and threw him out of the club." Gronkowski's postgame comments perfectly captured his hard-nosed play style and instantly became a fan-favorite moment.
In their 2011 bout against Washington, Gronkowski delivered one of the most incredible individual efforts seen on the gridiron. After a diving below-the-knee catch, Gronkowski rolled back to his feet and carried two Washington defenders another five yards toward the sideline. At this point, nearly everyone in the stadium assumed the play was over, including the players on the field. Everyone except Gronkowski. He somehow shook off both defenders, stayed in bounds, broke another tackle, and gained a substantial chunk of yards in the process. "He almost had no room to work with on the sidelines," Bill Belichick said after the game. "He is a tough guy to cover, a tough guy to match up on. We don't tackle him every day in practice, but we have seen plenty of people try to do it." The incredible 49-yard reception set up an even bigger moment. On the very next play, Gronkowski hauled in an 11-yard touchdown, recording his 14th receiving score of the season and breaking the NFL record for most touchdown receptions by a tight end in a single season.
Following New England's 13-3 victory over the Los Angeles Rams in Super Bowl LIII, the Patriots traveled to Fenway Park to participate in the Boston Red Sox's home opener, where several players were set to throw out the ceremonial first pitch. Before the festivities got underway, a handful of Patriots players took some time to practice their throws. That's when Gronkowski had an idea. What if he stepped into the makeshift batter's box against Julian Edelman, using the Lombardi Trophy as his bat? And so it was. Edelman wound up, ready to deliver the pitch, while Gronkowski stood with the Lombardi Trophy in hand. "We're all under the impression, 'No way is he going to swing the Lombardi Trophy,'" safety Devin McCourty said. As Edelman released the pitch, Gronkowski lifted the trophy off his shoulder and positioned it in front of him in a bunt stance. The ball collided with the trophy, leaving a baseball-sized imprint in the team's crowning achievement. "Gronkowski's parting gift," McCourty said. The dented trophy is still on display in the Patriots Hall of Fame.
One of the things that made Gronkowski so feared by opposing defenses was how fluid an athlete he was for his size. Standing 6-foot-6-inches and weighing roughly 265 lbs., you usually aren't supposed to make the acrobatic plays Gronkowski did. Especially the one he made against the Buffalo Bills in Week 16 of  the 2017 season.
Inside the Buffalo 20-yard line, down 10-3 in the second quarter, Tom Brady fired a back-shoulder pass to Gronkowski, who was blanketed by a Bills defender. Despite this, Gronkowski adjusted to the throw, extending his right arm out to haul in the pass before turning his body to get both feet in. Touchdown. Plays like these made Gronkowski a nightmare to cover.
With less than a minute remaining in the first half of Super Bowl XLIX , a game that would ultimately be decided by the thinnest of margins, Gronkowski hauled in a 22-yard touchdown pass from Brady over Seahawks linebacker K.J. Wright . Arguably the most important of Gronkowski's five Super Bowl touchdowns, the score helped give New England a 14-7 lead heading into halftime. Gronkowski finished the night with six catches for 68 yards and a touchdown, earning another championship ring in the process.
At this point in his career, Gronkowski wasn't quite the same player. Injuries had taken their toll, limiting both his availability and effectiveness throughout the season. But when New England needed him most, he came through. With the game tied 3-3 and just under eight minutes remaining, Brady found Gronkowski down the seam for a 29-yard completion, with the tight end making a diving catch to bring New England to the 2-yard line. This catch led to the eventual winning score, as Sony Michel punched it in on the very next play for the game's only touchdown. Gronkowski finished the night with six catches for 87 yards. A fitting stat line for No. 87 in what would be his final game as a Patriot.

title: Rob Gronkowski Tells Hysterical Patriots Practice Story Involving TD Prop
full_text:
FOXBORO — Nobody can spin a tale like Rob Gronkowski .
The legendary New England Patriots tight end , speaking to reporters Thursday, is set to be inducted into the team's Hall of Fame this weekend. His speech is certainly going to be filled with plenty of anecdotes from his nine-year career with the Patriots and his usual jokes.
He gave a little preview on Thursday speaking to a group of reporters virtually, remembering a story from his second season back in 2011. In typical Gronkowski fashion, it was as bizarre as you might expect.
It involved a Staples "That Was Easy" button that was gifted to him through the mail.
"I opened it up Friday before red zone practice and I look at Wes Welker and I go, 'Yo Wes, You that Terrell Owens celebration where he hid the ... marker or the sharpie behind the field goal post and he whipped it out and had the signature?'" said Gronkowski, the 38th inductee into the Patriots Hall of Fame.
That Owens celebration was when the wide receiver hid a Sharpie in his sock, and pulled it out to sign the football in 2002. Gronkowski made it his own, hiding that Staples button behind the goal post during the team's final practice of the week. Welker dared him to do it and hit it after scoring a touchdown.
In Gronkowski fashion, he was up for it.
"All of a sudden, boom! Another red zone play call. I run an in cut back of the end zone, catch it like two feet in front of the goal post," Gronkowski said. "I go, 'Yeah baby, this is it!' ... (I) grab the Staples button and started hitting it. That was easy. That was easy. Coach (Bill) Belichick starts shaking his head getting all pissed off and no one knew what to do because no one's ever seen that (sic) antics before.
"But no one could also say a word because I was absolutely balling that practice and balling in games too. That was one of the best moments, and Wes couldn't believe I pulled it off either. That story lives forever."
Gronkowski was right. He was balling — that year and the ones that would follow. The legendary tight end scored a franchise-record 79 touchdowns and ended his time in New England being on teams that went to the Super Bowl five times, winning three of them.
His induction into the Patriots Hall of Fame was without a doubt happening . He had embedded himself into the fabric of both the team and region, and it was because of stories like that.
"It was the right fit for me, the right people, the right organization, and now I call New England a place for me as home. It really is a home for me. It will always be a home for me for the rest of my life," Gronkowski said. "It’s somewhere where I’ll feel safe. I’ll feel secure, I’ll always feel loved here and that’s what it’s all about and vice versa. I’ll always love New England. I’ll always love the city of Boston, always love the New England Patriots fans, and it’ll be forever with me."
His Patriots career was legendary. So legendary that it oftentimes felt ... easy.
