title: Steelers College Check-In: WRs to Start Watching
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers have several positions of need when the 2027 NFL Draft rolls around. They are still searching for their next starting quarterback once Aaron Rodgers retires. They need a long-term answer in the secondary. Their inside linebacker group could lose an impactful player in the offseason.
But maybe most importantly, the Steelers need a wide receiver. This season has shown that the way they are approaching the position isn't working. Trading for veterans like DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr., while solid ideas on paper, have proved to be unimpactful decisions for the offense.
That means the Steelers have to find another star playmaker in the draft. Similarly to how they identified Germie Bernard in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft, the Steelers must find another wide receiver in the early portion of the 2027 NFL Draft.
Thankfully, there are options currently playing in the NCAA. Even after you remove top option Jeremiah Smith from the equation, there are multiple receivers the Steelers could take in the first few rounds who could finally give them an answer at the position.
Following up on the group of wide receivers who led Indiana to the national championship is no easy task, but Nick Marsh has made that transition smooth for IU. A transfer from Michigan State, Marsh has already exceeded in nine games what he did in a full season with the Spartans the past two years.
Marsh has a bit of everything. He’s big (6’3”), shot out of a cannon at the snap and he’s shown a knack for making contested catches thanks to his big frame.
Marsh would be an ideal part of a wide receiver tandem in Pittsburgh alongside Germie Bernard. The two would complement each other and bring a diversified skill set to the receiver room. Of the players on this list, Marsh is likely to be the highest-drafted player, but that doesn’t mean he’s going to be out of the Steelers’ range next spring.
Selecting a member of the Alabama Crimson Tide worked out splendidly for the Steelers last season, so why not go back to the well in 2027?
Ryan Coleman-Williams is explosive, works out of the slot and can go out wide, and is incredibly young. He made his debut in the NCAA while just 17 years old and he will be 20 during the 2027 NFL Draft.
What I love the most about the youngster is his ability to separate immediately off of the line of scrimmage. He’s not the biggest guy on the field, but he moves like the biggest, fastest, and strongest player out there. He’s so fluid in his lower body, even with some injuries over his time in the NCAA, that he can leave defenders in the dust with a simple move or two.
The fact that he’s only 6’0” will scare off some teams, but I don’t buy it. If he drops to the second or third round, he would be a steal for the Steelers.
The Texas Longhorns have a pair of wide receivers generating early NFL Draft projections, but it's Ryan Wingo who excites me the most. The 6'2", 215-pound junior from St. Louis, Missouri, is such an exciting player to watch.
And what makes him so exciting is his speed after the catch. The criticisms against him are fair, he's dropped some very catchable passes and he's not a technician in his routes, but none of that seems to matter when he has the ball in space.
If you want a player who can go up and get every jump ball with gorilla glue on his gloves, sadly, Wingo is not the player for you.
But if you want a player who is big, strong, explosive in and out of his cuts and can beat man-to-man coverage on the outside, Wingo is a player with huge upside.
And now for something completely different, which is what Nyck Harbor from South Carolina is. He is a player who reminds me a ton of DK Metcalf coming out of the NCAA. He's huge (6'5" and 240 pounds) and is an absolute terror to match up against.
Jump balls are Harbor's best friend. Put the ball in the air, and his huge frame and ability to high-point the ball are unmatched.
And if he has the ball in space, he can kill you with his breakaway speed.
The rest of his game, the route running, the run-blocking, things like that, is a project. Whichever NFL team drafts him will need to round out his game to make him an every-down receiver. But if that happens, he could become truly special at the next level.
A true home-run hitter on the field, Clemson's Bryant Wesco Jr. is currently my favorite wide receiver in the 2027 class.
At 6'2", Wesco possesses NFL speed and supreme agility. His ability to get low and move in and out of breaks is a thing of beauty. Plus, Wesco also has a productive history returning punts in the NCAA. The special teams in Pittsburgh continue to be a struggle, and the Clemson receiver could inject a dose of productivity.
There are two major weaknesses that the Steelers would have to decide on. The first is he underwent spinal surgery in 2025. He clearly is healthy enough to be playing right now, but that type of medical concern might force an NFL franchise to reconsider.
Secondly, he's a rather thin receiver. He's listed at 195 pounds, but that feels generous. There are times when opposing defensive backs can outmuscle him, and that's a concerning trait in his game. Strengthening at the NFL level might alleviate that, but it also might be what keeps franchises away from him at next year's draft until the end of Day 2.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Insider Names One Veteran Steelers Could Trade Away
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers have a big trade deadline ahead of them, and they may need to move on from some important players.
The Steelers have until Nov. 10 at 4:00 p.m. to make moves to bolster their roster for the final nine games of the season, as they stand 6-2 and are on top of the AFC North .
Pittsburgh needs some help offensively, and Albert Breer of Sports Illustrated noted that they are looking at a wide receiver and may part ways with a veteran defensive player.
"Then there’s the Steelers, who, again, are sniffing around at receiver, and could deal veteran LB Cole Holcomb," Breer wrote.
Holcomb is in his fourth season with the Steelers and signed a two-year, $5 million contract extension this offseason.
He has played in all eight games, but with no starts, and just 22 snaps on defense and 134 snaps on special teams.
The Steelers are pretty strong at linebacker, with Patrick Queen and Payton Wilson starting at inside linebacker and playing most snaps.
Payton Wilson leads the Steelers with 69 tackles (36 solo), and has seven tackles for loss, a sack, an interception, a fumble recovery, three passes defended and a fumble recovery.
Queen is second on Pittsburgh with 60 tackles (20 solo), three tackles for loss, 2.5 sacks, an interception and a fumble recovery.
The Steelers also have 2025 seventh-round pick Carson Bruener as another backup option, and Elandon Roberts , who has played extensively with the team, is on the practice squad and will want another opportunity.
Holcomb has been a solid player for the Steelers in the past, but if he isn't going to get much playing time, then moving him, a position of strength, to add to a weaker area of the roster might be just what they do.
Wide receiver is the area the Steelers have looked at and would benefit most from adding at this year's trade deadline.
Both Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. are on Injured Reserve with a finger injury and a foot injury, respectively.
Wilson suffered his injury in the first half of the 34-22 win over the Indianapolis Colts at Acrisure Stadium in Week 5 and Pittman has only played three games and not since the 27-24 defeat to the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field in Week 4.
The Steelers have shown interest in the Colts' Josh Downs and the Jacksonville Jaguars' Brian Thomas Jr. , both of whom could become immediate contributors.
Pittsburgh currently has DK Metcalf , who has struggled in 2026, Germie Bernard, a rookie, and Ben Skowronek, so extra help in the wide receiver room would be welcomed.
Dominic writes for Pittsburgh Pirates On SI, Pittsburgh Panthers Pn SI and also, Pittsburgh Steelers On SI. A Pittsburgh native, Dominic grew up watching Pittsburgh Sports and wrote for The Pitt News as an undergraduate at the University of Pittsburgh, covering Pitt Athletics. He would write for Pittsburgh Sports Now after college and has years of experience covering sports across Pittsburgh.

title: Steelers Legend Sends Warning to Pittsburgh's Opponents
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are not one of the top offenses in the NFL this season.
Despite that, the Steelers are finding success. They are 6-2 despite putting up 22.5 points per game, which ranks 18th in the league.
The Steelers' offensive success is coming almost exclusively through the running game. Led by Jaylen Warren's career-best campaign and a nasty offensive line, the Steelers are producing 117.9 yards on the ground per game.
That ground game, according to former Steelers running back Merril Hoge, has given the offense an identity. Even worse, it's sending a terrifying message to their upcoming opponents.
"I think that they found themselves an identity, and I know that they have been looking for that the entire season," he said on The OG Football Show. "But now, in a couple weeks, you know who you are, and you know what you expect to play like, and that's a scary thing for the opponent, because I didn't think they were gonna find it like that."
Merril Hoge says the Steelers have finally found their identity. Pittsburgh is controlling the line of scrimmage, dictating the tempo, and playing what Hoge calls championship-style football. pic.twitter.com/8x23Cg7aP7
If Hoge is right, this Steelers offense may truly have a championship identity. To his point, the ground game in Pittsburgh is admirable.
Warren is just a nightmare for opposing defenses. Through eight games, he's produced 704 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 119 carries, good for an average of 5.9 yards per carry. In addition, he's hauled in 25 receptions on 35 targets for 294 yards and a touchdown.
Warren's talent is undeniable, and he's having a career-defining season, but he's not the only one helping the ground game succeed.
If this team is going to continue the strong start they've produced and find success in the postseason, it hinges on their offensive line.
And so far, they are one of the easiest position groups to bet on. Center Zach Frazier has finally earned the respect around the league that folks in Pittsburgh have known since his rookie season. He's knocking on the door of a First-Team All-Pro selection, and he might not be alone.
The star of the offensive line this season is guard Mason McCormick. He's the definition of a bruiser and mauler in the trenches. He leads the team with his energy on the field, and he's a brick wall when blocking.
Ever since the team switched out their starting guard and tackle, the right side of the line has been solidified. Along with it, the rest of the offensive line has been complete.
Those are two key building blocks for a championship identity, and as Hoge points out, the Steelers have found it. If they can get the rest of the offense to balance out the run game, there is truly no telling how far they can go in 2026.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Ex-Steelers WR Antonio Brown Coming to Pittsburgh for Fan Event
full_text:
Former Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Antonio Brown will be back in town later this season.
Brown is set to serve as the Terrible Tailgate Guest on November 27 when the Steelers host the Denver Broncos for a Black Friday matinee in Week 12.
The 38-year-old hasn't often made return trips to Pittsburgh since being traded to the Oakland Raiders in March 2019, though he'll be on the North Shore before what's shaping up to be a consequential matchup against the Broncos for the black and gold with both teams currently sitting at 6-2.
A sixth-round pick out of Central Michigan in the 2010 NFL Draft, Brown logged 167 yards as a rookie for a Steelers team that eventually lost to Aaron Rodgers, Mike McCarthy and the Green Bay Packers in Super Bowl XLV.
Brown went on to post 1,108 yards in 2011, resulting in his first Pro Bowl nod. After a relatively quiet 2012 campaign for his standards with 787 yards and five touchdowns, he bounced back with 1,499 yards and eight touchdowns in 2013 en route to another Pro Bowl appearance and second-team All-Pro honors.
From 2014 through 2017, Brown recorded a total of 6,349 yards and 44 touchdowns on 472 receptions, all of which led the NFL over that span. He was a first-team All-Pro and Pro Bowler in all four of those years as well while finishing second in AP Offensive Player of the Year voting on three occasions.
Brown's final season with the Steelers came in 2018, and he posted 1,297 yards with a league-leading 15 touchdowns while making a fifth-straight Pro Bowl.
While his time in Pittsburgh ended on a sour note as his relationship with the organization seemed to deteriorate, Brown is still amongst the best players in franchise history and was arguably the best wide receiver in the NFL for the majority of his time as a Steeler.
With Brown's playing career ending in 2021, he is eligible to be inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame as a member of its Class of 2027.
Whether or not he gets voted in, though, is a different story. While Brown's peak in the mid-2010s is one of the more impressive runs by a wide receiver in recent memory, and he has the accolades to show for it, his long list of off-the-field issues may ultimately prevent him from being enshrined in Canton in a timely fashion.
It's still possible that he will end up as a Hall of Famer, though making it on the first ballot feels rather unlikely for Brown.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Recently-Released Safety Solves Nothing for Steelers
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers could use some reinforcements in the secondary. The team's defense is off to a thunderous start, surrendering the sixth-fewest yards per game.
The Steelers' strength is clearly their front seven, and it's doing a ton of work to cover up for the group's flaws. But the organization is trying to give quarterback Aaron Rodgers that magical fairy-tale ending to his NFL career, and that calls for upgrades before this year's NFL Trade Deadline.
One possible upgrade they could make doesn't require any trade, however. The Buffalo Bills recently released veteran safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson. Naturally, the polarizing defender popped up online as a potential fit. One fan, under the X username @jes6979, asked NFL analyst Jon Ledyard about the possibility of him landing in Pittsburgh.
@LedyardNFLDraft any fit for Gardner-Johnson for the Steelers secondary?
It's a fair question, given Gardner-Johnson has 93 games of NFL experience and a Super Bowl on his resume. The Steelers need help, but not this kind of help on the active roster. Between the inconsistencies over the past few seasons and his propensity for on-field altercations, the Steelers should avoid bringing him into the organization.
Let's put the recent incident that led to his suspension aside and just look at his recent play. My eye test concludes that he's a rotational player at best right now. According to data from Pro Football Reference, that seems to be the case.
He's been targeted 21 times in coverage, with quarterbacks completing 13 of those passing attempts for a total of 179 yards and a touchdown. Receivers are averaging 13.8 yards per reception against him, and he combats that with one interception and two passes defended in six contests.
The number that stands out, in the most negative way, is his missed tackles. According to Pro Football Reference , he is credited with six missed tackles and a missed-tackle rate of 18.8%.
The Steelers have struggled in the secondary this season in all of those areas. They are allowing the 17th-most passing yards per game so far this season and have six defenders with a missed-tackle rate of 10% or greater.
One other number stands out when evaluating Gardner-Johnson's 2026 campaign: zero. That's how many special teams snaps the 29-year-old has played this season. Dating back to the 2022 campaign, he's played a cumulative 13 special teams snaps.
Gardner-Johnson can still contribute to an NFL defense; I'm not arguing against that. The problem is that he doesn't provide anything that will help the Steelers moving forward. He's not a special teams contributor. He doesn't tackle consistently well, and he gives up big plays.
If the Steelers strictly needed a practice squad player, C.J. Gardner-Johnson would make sense as a player to take a flyer on. To address a direct need, however, the veteran is far from the answer the Steelers are searching for.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers' Mike McCarthy Forcing Doubters Into Believers
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers have surprised many in their first eight regular-season contests. The defense is a top-10 unit, led by new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham and multiple veterans playing at an elite level.
The offense is still searching for consistency, but that hasn't stopped the Steelers from jumping out to a 6-2 record.
With the week off, the Steelers get the chance to rest, recuperate and self-scout. It's much needed, but one thing must be said. Head coach Mike McCarthy is doing exactly what he set out to do in his first season with Pittsburgh, and he's forcing all of his critics to confront the possibility that they were wrong.
While the Steelers haven't cracked the code for explosive plays, they are succeeding in two key areas.
One of them is discipline. The offense has been penalized a total of 23 times so far, the ninth-fewest in the NFL. In Week 8 against the Cleveland Browns, the offense was flawless in that regard. The team was flagged five times, but none of them were against the offense.
The other area is mitigating turnovers. Most of that falls on Aaron Rodgers. Aside from multiple instances where the pass hit the receiver's hands and wound up in the defender's, Rodgers has made smart decisions with the football. He has 13 touchdowns compared to five interceptions as he leads this offense.
There have been some problems with keeping possession of the ball from snap to whistle; I grant that, but this team has not turned the ball over as much as they could have. SumerSports data shows that the Steelers' offense turned the ball over eight times in eight games. They've coughed the ball up six times, but they've only surrendered possession twice.
Maybe you believe all of that is outside McCarthy's impact, but the way he has gotten more and more out of the running backs and tight ends is one of his biggest victories as head coach.
The three players who look the most improved in this offense, Jaylen Warren , Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington, have been with the organization for multiple seasons. They've always had recognizable talent and potential to be impact players, but McCarthy and his staff have unlocked something special.
Even as the wide receivers stumble, the other skill positions are flourishing. Running back Jaylen Warren has spent the entirety of his career splitting his time in the backfield, until this season.
Under the watchful eye of McCarthy, the offense has centered on Warren, and the results have been excellent. Through eight games, Warren has 704 rushing yards (sixth in the NFL), and his 5.92 yards per carry tops all running backs with at least 50 touches this season. Add in his 294 receiving yards, and he's pushing 1,000 all-purpose yards as the team recovers during the bye week.
The tight ends are also giving the Steelers valuable production. Both Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington rank among the top 25 tight ends in receiving yards. Washington is averaging 13.37 yards per reception, the 11th-best mark among tight ends.
They've also combined for seven receiving touchdowns, making them one of the most trusted targets on offense.
The Steelers are not a perfect product. They have flaws. Their lack of wide receiver depth is a concerning issue that must be addressed before the Steelers can be considered a frontrunner in the AFC.
But make no mistake, Mike McCarthy is transforming more doubters into believers by the day.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Insider Floats Steelers QB as Potential Trade Target
full_text:
Though the Pittsburgh Steelers are buyers, it's still possible that they could receive some interest in one of their backup quarterbacks ahead of the November 10 trade deadline .
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler noted that while the Steelers are "more likely" to add to their roster over the next few days while sitting at 6-2, Mason Rudolph is a player who could theoretically be moved if the right opportunity presented itself.
“The Steelers are more likely to bring in players at the deadline," Fowler wrote . "In fact, I don’t expect Pittsburgh to move anyone. But it has a surplus at quarterback, and should more quarterback injuries occur around the league, perhaps teams call on Rudolph with an attractive offer.”
In-season quarterback trades are typically a rarity across the NFL.
There have only been five since the start of 2020, but two of them have come during the 2026 campaign, as J.J. McCarthy was sent from the Minnesota Vikings to the New York Giants in late September, while Jacoby Brissett was just dealt to the Baltimore Ravens from the Arizona Cardinals on November 4, following what are likely season-ending injuries to Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley.
Minnesota landed a 2027 fifth-round pick for McCarthy, and Arizona's return for Brissett isn't yet official.
There are a few teams out there, with the Minnesota Vikings being chief among them, who could use another quarterback before the deadline .
Rudolph presents an interesting case as a trade candidate, though, because of both his lack of true upside and recent starting experience.
For example, McCarthy was a first-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft and thus had value due to his untapped potential despite things not working out in Minnesota, while Brissett has started 20 games over the last two seasons for the Cardinals and had spurts where he's looked like a quality option behind center.
As for Rudolph, however, he's made just one start since returning to Pittsburgh in 2025 after a one-year stint with the Tennessee Titans.
The 31-year-old has played a fair amount throughout his NFL career, appearing in 37 games and making 19 starts, but his 53 passing attempts during his second go-around with the Steelers might not be all that alluring on the trade market.
If another team decides they need an upgrade  at backup quarterback or their starter goes down in Week 9, the chances of Rudolph being traded would jump.
Otherwise, it's hard to imagine him not sticking around with the black and gold for the remainder of the year before hitting free agency next offseason.
Equipped with 18 picks over the next two NFL Drafts, the Steelers aren't exactly hurting for extra assets.
At the same time, if they could acquire a mid-to-late Day 3 selection for a veteran on an expiring deal in Rudolph, perhaps it's something they'd consider.
The organization's willingness to move on from Rudolph, though, comes down to their confidence in Will Howard and/or Drew Allar to take another step and fill in as Aaron Rodgers' backup.
Sitting just a game outside of the No. 1 seed in the AFC, and in a tight division race in the AFC North as the first-place team, Pittsburgh can't really afford to slip up over the back-half of its schedule.
If Rodgers were to ever miss a game or two due to injury, Rudolph would likely present the Steelers their best odds of remaining competitive without the future Hall of Famer on the field.
Neither Howard or Allar has taken a regular season snap, though they both played a good amount during the preseason and have continued to grow while serving as the No. 3 and 4 quarterbacks, respectively, behind Rodgers and Rudolph so far this year.
Howard and Allar have higher ceilings than Rudolph and could be in the mix to serve as Pittsburgh's starting quarterback down the line, perhaps as early as 2027, but their collective readiness to play now is a question mark.
If the Steelers believe either could fill in for Rodgers if necessary and keep the offense afloat, than trading Rudolph could be on their radar. If not, holding onto Rudolph would be the right course of action.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: 4 Seahawks Who Must Step Up With So Many Injuries
full_text:
I’m not saying the Seattle Seahawks are the only team in the NFL with a lot of injuries. But they are, as of right now, one of the teams with a lot of injuries . And that means other players will have to step up and produce, perhaps more than typical. Let’s run through some of them here, skipping the obvious candidates like Drew Lock or Josh Jones.
There are a lot of reasons why the Seahawks aren’t running the ball effectively right now , but one thing that’s easy to lose track of is the individual play of the back. It’s understandable given it was his first game back from a significant injury, but part of the problem last Monday was Price not getting it done. We’ve seen better from him this year, and we need better now.
Brian Fleury and the offensive line own a lot of the run game issues. The lack of a real fullback is also an issue. But Price needs to maximize his yardage on the opportunities he gets. With chaos on the offensive line this week, the blocking may not get much better, so it’s going to require great play from Price himself. We need some degree of balance here.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba is doing everything within his power right now, and to ask more of him would be absurd. Cooper Kupp is old. Rashid Shaheed is injured. Montorie Foster Jr isn’t ready to produce against NFL defenses. Tory Horton is the only one who might be able to give us a viable number two receiver right now. And so far, we haven’t seen it.
Some blamed Horton for Sam Darnold’s first interception against the Denver Broncos for running a bad route. I don’t particularly agree with that criticism, but Tory hasn’t exactly wowed so far this season, particularly with his struggles to make contested catches. With the Seahawks living in 11 personnel recently, some production is a must from Horton.
I hate to put more on Reed’s shoulders right now , but there’s no other choice. Leonard Williams and Brandon Pili are out, so the interior defensive line is Byron Murphy II, Jarran Reed, and Rylie Mills. I know Murphy is ready to ball out, as he always does, but Mills has been a massive liability so far this season. That means more snaps for Reed.
Mills is completely unable to hold up against the run, meaning his only chance to contribute positively is as a pass rusher. And the Seahawks aren’t doing a good job at creating those opportunities. Reed needs to clamp down early, until such a time as the Seahawks might be able to open up a big lead. Emphasis on ‘might’, of course.
Lots of Seahawks fans have been going after Hall over the last couple months. I’m not one of them, so don’t construe this as me agreeing with those criticisms. I think Derick has been fine so far this year, and has been worth the contract we gave him in the offseason . But this week would be a great time for him to, for three hours, ascend beyond that.
The Seahawks utterly failed to get pressure on Caleb Williams on Monday. With Uchenna Nwosu still sidelined and Dante Fowler Jr clearly not being trusted by the coaching staff, plus Big Cat not being available for edge snaps, Hall is going to play a lot. And some hits on Minshew tomorrow would go a long way in flipping the current narrative.

title: 5 Burning Questions Ahead of Cardinals vs. Seahawks in Week 9
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are getting ready for their Week 9 matchup against the NFC West rival Arizona Cardinals.
With the game rapidly approaching , we spoke with Arizona Cardinals On SI publisher Donnie Druin to learn more about the Cardinals' current state of affairs.
The Cardinals' offense was simply stagnant under Brissett, who was extremely quick to get the ball out and oftentimes stared down his first read. Arizona was justified in their benching of Brissett, as Gardner Minshew immediately led Arizona to four straight scoring drives.
After making him their QB3, it was an easy decision to trade Brissett for any sort of draft capital, and quite frankly I think they did great in getting a fourth-round pick back.
I'm still 50/50. Many times we see a backup quarterback enter action and have immediate success, and it takes just a few weeks' worth of film for opposing defenses to get film and figure him out. The same goes for Minshew, who has starred in this movie before.
Minshew Magic is fun but will eventually run out. I think the Cardinals will have plenty to offer in terms of different looks with an actual week to gameplan with him at quarterback, though Seattle's defense is incredibly tough and now has a chip on their shoulder entering this week.
For the Cardinals, I think the injuries. They dealt with a slew of banged-up players last season and were hoping to have health on their side for 2026. That hasn't been the case, as plenty of big names have landed on injured reserve already. Arizona's offense has been as expected under a first year head coach while their defense has been on par in terms of being poor.
I'd say familiarity, as they already have updated film on the Seahawks from this season, and often times the loser from the first matchup has a higher chance of performing better in the second go-around. With a new spark at quarterback and a recently better defensive output, Arizona isn't quite the massively overlooked underdogs they typically would be in this spot.
Arizona keeps it close but the Seahawks ultimately get the job done . SEA 28, AZ 21

title: 3 Matchups That Will Decide Seahawks’ Week 9 Clash vs. Cardinals
full_text:
It’s the second encounter of the season between the Seattle Seahawks and Arizona Cardinals. Back in Week 2 in Glendale, Mike Macdonald’s team rolled to a 31-7 victory. It was the ‘Hawks 10th straight win in this NFC West series dating back to the clubs’ second meeting in 2021. That afternoon, Drew Lock got the start behind center in place of banged-up Sam Darnold. He threw for 235 yards, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba was on the receiving end of all three Lock touchdown passes
With Darnold ailing again, Macdonald will once again turn to his backup signal-caller. So what can we expect in a rematch that has the Seahawks coming off a decisive Monday night home loss to the Bears and the Cards (with Gardner Minshew at quarterback) looking to build on a 33-30 overtime win over the Cowboys at Arlington?
His catches and receiving yardage numbers got better each season during his first four seasons in the league, and was a First Team All-Pro selection in 2025. This season, Cardinals’ tight end Trey McBride leads the NFL with 66 receptions, good for 544 yards and five touchdowns. Could he once again top his statistics from the previous season?
McBride will be facing the Seahawks for the 10th time, and he has been on the short end of the scoreboard in each of the previous nine meetings. In those games, he’s been targeted a combined 75 times—the most vs. any team in the league. He’s totaled 49 catches for 486 yards (9.9 average) and three touchdowns.
In this season’s first meeting, McBride saw 10 passes his way. He finished with eight receptions for 41 yards and Arizona’s lone touchdown of the contest. It shapes up as a great battle with veteran Julian Love, who has a pair of picks this season and lead the Seahawks with six passes defensed.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba has a real case for best player in football right now pic.twitter.com/stf9Hj577s
It’s pretty much the polar opposite of McBride facing the Seahawks. In seven contests versus the Arizona Cardinals, Seahawks’ wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba (second in the NFL with 64 receptions) has yet to be on the losing end of a clash with the Cards.
He’s put up pretty impressive numbers in this division rivalry. The four-year pro has been targeted 46 times and snared 36 passes for 536 yards and seven touchdowns. In this season’s first meeting, a 31-7 victory at Arizona, he totaled nine grabs for 155 yards and three scores.
Hence, Cardinals’ defensive coordinator Nick Rallis and his unit will try to do what only one team has done this season: Hold Smith-Njigba to under 100 receiving yards. He was limited to five catches for 76 yards in his team’s 30-23 victory over the Chargers in Week 4.
Tyler Allgeier today vs Dallas 11 rush 147 yds TD 5 rec 44 yds TD Tyler Allgeier just had the best game of his NFL career against the Cowboys. pic.twitter.com/AhiCkhabz7
It’s been an interesting week for the Cardinals’ organization. The team is coming off a thrilling 33-30 overtime victory at Dallas last Sunday. The win came via a big afternoon from 2026 free-agent pickup Tyler Allgeier, who ran for 147 yards and one score, as well as solid relief work from Gardner Minshew. The journeyman signal-caller replaced Jacoby Brissett and threw for 188 yards and three touchdowns in the comeback win.
Now consider that 2026 first-round pick Jeremiyah Love is now on injured reserve, and Brissett is now a member of the Baltimore Ravens’ organization. Interesting may not do the Cardinals justice. In any case, Allgeier is a proven performer who ran for 2,876 yards and 18 scores in four seasons with the Falcons.
Seahawks’ linebacker Drake Thomas has actually graded out higher (74.6) than teammate Ernest Jones IV (57.0) as a run defender by Pro Football Focus this season. That alone makes for a fascinating battle.

title: 3 Seahawks X-Factors Needed To Beat Cardinals
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are coming off another disappointing loss , and they desperately need a Week 9 win against the Arizona Cardinals if they want to stay in the playoff hunt.
Several glaring issues led to the loss to the Bears on Monday night, and the Seahawks have a short week to try to correct those problems. Seattle has already beaten Arizona once this season, and they're looking to sweep the season series on Sunday.
Here are three X-factors that will have a major impact on whether the Seahawks win or lose in Week 9.
The shakeup along the offensive line had brutal consequences for the Seahawks in Week 8. Quenton Nelson plugged in at left guard, moving Grey Zabel to the right side, and starting left tackle Charles Cross was out with an injury. Josh Jones started at left tackle.
That was three big changes to the offensive line in just one week, even if Nelson was supposed to be an upgrade, and it showed. The Seahawks' running back combined for just 61 yards on 17 carries, and quarterback Sam Darnold was sacked three times while being heavily pressured.
That, coupled with poor play calling by offensive coordinator Brian Fleury, doomed the Seahawks' offense. Michael Dickson had a busy night, punting five times. That can't happen again if Seattle wants to win this week. The offensive line has to jell together quickly.
Darnold is out against the Cardinals after suffering quad and rib injuries in the loss to the Bears. That means Lock, who is also working through an injury to his throwing elbow, will start against the Cardinals.
Lock played well in what was essentially two starts earlier this season when Darnold was sidelined. He completed 35 of 48 passes (72.9%) for 422 yards, four touchdowns and zero interceptions. If Lock continues to play well, he could actually be an upgrade over Darnold, who has completed 60.2% of his passes for 1,478 yards, 10 touchdowns and nine interceptions this season.
The Seahawks' offense hinges on the offensive line playing well and Lock stepping up. Those factors are necessary to win the game, as the defense can't continue to will them to victory.
Seattle has one of the best defenses in the NFL, but they're also the worst red zone defense in the league so far this season.
The Seahawks have allowed touchdowns on 83.33% of opponents' red zone trips , which is the worst in the league by more than 3%. For reference, the 6-1 Minnesota Vikings are the best in the league, allowing touchdowns on just 25% of opponents' red zone drives.
Silver lining: The Cardinals have the third-worst red zone offense in the NFL , scoring touchdowns on just 45.45% of their trips. Arizona was 1-for-1 in the red zone in the Seahawks' 31-7 win in Week 2.
Gardner Minshew is now leading Arizona's offense, whereas the Seahawks faced Jacoby Brissett in the first matchup. That could change things, but Seattle's defense has to step up regardless.

title: Seahawks Injury Report Paints a Troubling Picture for Many Players
full_text:
Do the Seattle Seahawks need all hands on deck to beat a heavily-wounded Arizona Cardinals squad this upcoming weekend? We’re about to find out the hard way, because after Friday’s report, it’s clear they will have many hands not on deck. While I don’t believe it’s sufficient to excuse a loss, it’s fair to say this week is about survival more than anything else.
Let’s not bury the lead here. The Seahawks have six starters out for this one. Sam Darnold (ribs, quadricep), Rashid Shaheed (knee), Charles Cross (ankle), Quenton Nelson (knee), Leonard Williams (stinger), and Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) will be sidelined this week, which is a lot to swallow for any team. Brandon Pili (back) will also miss the game.
The Nelson miss in particular stands out, given he was just acquired a week ago and is known for almost never missing games. Per Macdonald, Nelson’s need for a minor procedure that has him week-to-week came up in the last 24 hours. The offensive line will now flip back to the prior arrangement, with Grey Zabel at left guard and Anthony Bradford at right.
Connor O’Toole (foot) is questionable. Everyone else is cleared to go. Anthony Bradford (knee) and Tyrice Knight (thigh) being healthy is not insignificant, and Drew Lock (right elbow) getting firmly backed as the starter is very important. Nick Emmanwori (shoulder), Tory Horton (hand), Derick Hall (back), and Ernest Jones (ankle) are also in the clear. Not all bad news.
Things aren’t quite as much of a punch to the stomach for Cardinals fans, but they are no less beat up than Seattle. Bam Knight (concussion), Jayden Williams (knee), and Jon Gaines II (ankle) have been declared out. Combined with the other, long-term injuries on this squad, this means Arizona has third stringers at left tackle and right guard this week.
Unless the questionable Isaiah Adams (ankle), who has yet to be activated off injured reserve, manages to make it back in time. The odds seem against him, but the Cardinals didn’t rule it out entirely. Max Melton (knee) and Walter Nolen III (knee) are also questionable, putting further potential dents into a defense that has been a liability so far this season.
Beyond that, the Cardinals had several players get rest days earlier this week who were never in danger of not playing, like Budda Baker, Hjalte Froholdt, Isaac Seumalo, and Josh Sweat . Reggie Virgil (back) is also in the clear. Michael Wilson (ribs) is playing, but he’s by no means healthy, so we’ll see if he can get through the whole game.

title: 5 Key Things to Know About Cardinals vs. Seahawks in Week 9
full_text:
It’s quite likely that this is not where the defending Super Bowl champions saw themselves eight weeks into the 2026 season. After a 2-0 start, the Seattle Seahawks have dropped four of their last six games, including two in their own building. They find themselves behind the 6-1 San Francisco 49ers in the NFC West, a team they fell to at Lumen Field, 32-29, back in Week 5.
They enter this Sunday’s rematch with the Arizona Cardinals without starting quarterback Sam Darnold for the second time this season. The good news is that backup Drew Lock was in this identical situation back in Week 2 at Glendale. And Mike McDonald’s team came away with a decisive win.
Still, the Seahawks come off a humbling 34-17 Monday night setback to the Chicago Bears in which they were dominated in the trenches. So can McDonald’s club get back on track this week against an opponent that they have owend in recent seasons?
It’s been pretty dismal as of late for the Cardinals. Back in Week 2 at Glendale, the Seahawks made it 10 straight wins in this series with a 31-7 triumph. Drew Lock got the start in favor of a banged-up Sam Darnold and was sharp., connecting on 19-of-26 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns— all of those scores to Jaxon Smith-Njigba.
Arizona’s last win in this NFC West setting was a 23-13 triumph in Week 11 of 2021 at Seattle. Meanwhile, the Seahawks’ current 10-game winning streak vs. the Cards has come by a combined 273-163 score.
The numbers are very sobering. All told, LaFleur’s team is giving up a league-high 29.8 points per game, and have allowed 30-plus points in six of their eight outings this season. The Cardinals have also surrendered 27 offensive touchdowns (9 rushing, 18 passing)—two or more TDs in each game this season.
A year ago, the Seahawks were tied for 10th in the league in rushing—averaging 123.3 yards per contest. They were even better during their three-game postseason run (130.3 average). After eight weeks, the inconsistent ‘Hawks are running for 109.6 yards per game—less than 100 yards in four of those contests.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba vs. Arizona Cardinals 9 REC 155 YDS 3 TD JSN last 2 games: 17 REC, 277 YDS, 4 TD. Fantasy Football Points Today: 45.5 pic.twitter.com/VGu0eL2yAT
It’s mere speculation as the NFL’s trade deadline grows closer. But for now, Seattle’s offense must deal with eight-time Pro Bowl safety Budda Baker. He ranks third on the Cardinals with 51 tackles, leads the team with 3.5 sacks, one interception, and is tied for second on the clubs with four passes defensed.
In his two appearances this season, one in relief of Sam Darnold in Week 1, Drew Lock has hit on 35-of-48 passes (72.9 percent) for 422 yards, four scores and zero turnovers. And it’s hardly a surprise that all four of those touchdown tosses went to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, covering 42, 82, seven, and 12 yards, respectively.

title: Why the Seahawks Need to Trade for a Tight End at the Deadline
full_text:
Time is running out for all 32 teams to improve their rosters through the NFL Trade Deadline. The Seattle Seahawks (4-4) already dipped into the trade deadline by trading for eight-time Pro-Bowl guard Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts . This was viewed as a huge trade for an offense that desperately needs consistency and impact.
​If there is anything that the dominating 34-17 Week 8 home loss to the Chicago Bears taught the Seahawks, it is that more work may need to be done. The Seahawks might have to turn back to the NFL Trade Deadline if they want to save their season. The best move for Seattle is to trade for a tight end.
​The Seahawks’ offense has been completely dysfunctional and inconsistent this season . Among the biggest reasons is the lack of efficiency and experience from first-year offensive coordinator Brian Fleury and regression from the offensive line and quarterback Sam Darnold. There has also been a lack of impact from the tight end group, which is incredibly disappointing since Fleury was a long-time tight end coach for the San Francisco 49ers.
​Through eight games this season, Seattle has the 18th-ranked passing offense (222.3) and 22nd in quarterback rating (88.5). Darnold hasn’t been able to get the ball to a pass-catcher when escaping pressure. Outside of wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba , the Seahawks don’t have a quick target to turn for a quick gain.
​Third-year AJ Barner has caught 21 receptions for 203 yards and no touchdowns. Fleury has to create play designs just to get the ball out to him. He was called to step up and be a huge part of the Seahawks’ offense as a solid run-blocker and one of Darnold’s most trusted pass-catchers. This season, however, Barner can’t create separation and Darnold is forced to give him the ball in quick throws and screens.
​It may be time for the Seahawks to trade for a number one tight end and move Barner to number two. Seattle can find a solid number one option through the trade deadline on teams potentially looking to sell. The tight end with the highest upside is Detroit Lions’ Sam LaPorta , who is seeking a contract extension.
Through 49 games in his young career, LaPorta has caught 217 receptions for 2,471 yards and 23 touchdowns. LaPorta can easily be a franchise number two and pair well with JSN and head coach Mike Macdonald’s MOB mindset.
​Another addition from a team looking to potentially reload is Philadelphia Eagles’ Dallas Goedert. There are a lot more concerns with Goedert, considering he is about to be 32 years old and is in the final year of his deal . Last season, he caught 60 receptions for 591 yards and 11 touchdowns.
​Other options for the Seahawks include Indianapolis Colts tight ends Tyler Warren or Mo Alie-Cox and Los Angeles Chargers’ David Njoku. Warren might be viewed as a long-term option, while Alie-Cox and Njoku could be traded for short-term options with long-term potential.

title: 3 Bold Predictions for Seahawks vs. Cardinals in Week 9
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks have an opportunity to get back on track this weekend as they host the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9 . Seattle suffered a frustrating loss last Monday night against the Chicago Bears, dropping them to 4-4 on the season.
Arizona, on the other hand, improved to 3-5 on the season after knocking off the Dallas Cowboys. They're going to be full of confidence, but Seattle will as well. Despite Sam Darnold suffering a quad injury, the Seahawks know they can win this one after backup Drew Lock led them to a 31-7 win over the Cardinals in Week 2.
Seattle needs this win to stay in the race for a spot in the NFC playoffs. Securing that win becomes far more likely if the following three bold predictions come true.
Zach Charbonnet made his season debut in Week 8. He made it back quickly from a torn ACL suffered in January, but was still shaking off the rust against Chicago. Charbonnet had 23 yards on just six carries and added six yards on three receptions.
His workload should increase each week as he gets more comfortable on the surgically-repaired knee. In this bold prediction, he turns the extra touches into his first trip into the end zone of the season.
During the first meeting, the Seahawks held Jacoby Brissett to just 95 yards passing and sacked him twice. Brissett was traded to the Baltimore Ravens after losing the starting spot to Gardner Minshew, who will have his hands full with the Dark Side defense. In our second bold prediction, that defense, led by Byron Murphy, sacks Minshew a total of five times.
If the 31-7 win in Week 2 is any indication, the Seahawks should be able to win this one easily. Sure, they will have far more confidence following the performance of Minshew and Tyler Allgeier in Week 8, as they led a 14-point comeback in the fourth quarter.
That said, this defense is far more imposing than what Minshew faced in Week 8 against the Dallas Cowboys. That's why this final bold prediction is that Lock and the Seahawks take a commanding enough lead that Seattle decides to give Jalen Milroe some snaps for the first time this season.

title: Six Players the Seahawks Should Note from College Football Week 9
full_text:
Throughout the College Football Season, we’ll be monitoring top performers who might be available to the Seattle Seahawks in the 2027 draft . We’ll focus on players that play positions that are likely, or at least possibly, going to be one the team considers going after. This should give us a chance to spotlight players that the team targets well ahead of time.
The Miami Hurricanes haven’t played top-end competition yet this season, but there’s no dismissing how good Mensah has been. He’s completing over 80% of his passes and has 25 touchdowns to 1 interception. This last week he provided over 300 total yards of offense and 3 more passing touchdowns. No one is balling as hard as he is right now.
The Louisville backfield features two quality, draftable backs named Brown, and this week it was all about Isaac. On just twelve total touches, he produced 172 yards and 4 touchdowns. You won’t find many better games than that from a back. I wouldn’t build an offense around Isaac Brown, but I think he can slot in very nicely as a meaningful part of one.
With the Elijah Arroyo situation being what it is, I suspect the Seattle Seahawks will need to find another quality tight end this offseason. There are several, and this last week Willie Rodriguez of Kentucky stood out to me. On 7 targets, he had 6 catches for 67 yards, while also maintaining clean numbers in his pass blocking. Time to start paying attention to these guys.
Much has been made of Miami’s mean interior line combo in Justin Scott and Ahmad Moten Sr, but Marquise Lightfoot is part of the conversation as well. Coming off the edge for the Hurricanes, Lightfoot landed hard this weekend with 7 tackles, 2 sacks, a forced fumble, and 7 pressures during the dominant victory. He’s making some waves in the edge class.
We’ve discussed Biles before, but it’s hard to not continue to pound the drum for him this week. The linebacker had 8 tackles with 4 for a loss, which included 3 sacks, 5 total pressures, and a forced fumble, while also handling his coverage duties well enough to allow 21 yards on 2 targets. The Longhorns defense was elite last week, and he was a big reason why.
Another significant reason why the Longhorns allowed only three points this week was the play of McDonald at safety. He kept it simple, with 9 tackles and 3 completions allowed for 14 yards, but sometimes that’s all you need to keep an opposing offense under control. McDonald is a day two safety and continues to move his draft stock up with games like this.

title: Seahawks Mailbag: 4 Questions Leading Into The Cardinals Game
full_text:
It’s a new low point for the 2026 Seattle Seahawks after the punishing loss to the Chicago Bears , and there’s a season to save these next few weeks. I asked my discord server what their biggest questions about the team are right now. Let’s take a look at what’s on the mind of the fans. The wording of the questions has been lightly edited for this article.
“Who should be the playcaller when Fleury gets canned: Peetz or Outten?”
We’re not to the point of Fleury getting canned yet, and I wouldn’t be surprised if Schneider and Macdonald take the perspective of it never being a good idea to make a midseason firing. So I wouldn’t assume anything is imminent, especially if the offense produces against two of the NFL’s worst defenses the next two weeks. But from my perspective, it’s Peetz.
He’s the guy who you liked enough to keep around after 2024 when Ryan Grubb and many other offensive coaches were let go. He also has one year of playcalling experience, although it was in college with the 2021 LSU Tigers. I’d take that over Outten’s two games of calling plays for Denver in 2022, although neither is great. See what Jake has first.
“Why hasn’t Fleury switched to calling plays in the booth?”
It’s yet another reason why Fleury’s incompetence so far is particularly maddening to me. He seems extremely set in his ways and unwilling to try new things. That might make sense for someone who has been doing this for decades and just can’t adjust to the modern direction of the game, but Fleury is a first-time playcaller. He shouldn’t be that married to anything.
Fleury even said before the season that he’d try both sideline and booth playcalling, and given how this has been a disaster on the sideline so far it’s mind-boggling he wouldn’t at least try. Generally speaking, I expect pretty much all coaches in professional sports to be stubborn, but I don’t think it’s a particularly good excuse here. Adapt or find yourself out of a job fast.
“What will it take for the Seahawks to fire Fleury mid-season?”
I have to believe that a bad game against the Arizona Cardinals or Las Vegas Raiders will do it, since the team then has a bye week to consider such a change. Those are two of the worst defenses in the NFL, and the Cardinals in particular should be an easy mark since this offense had their way with them just two months ago. There has to be a limit to the patience.
But again, I think there are a lot of NFL minds who believe that a coaching change is never justified mid-season, and we may have some of those minds in our organization right now. I can understand the reasoning one might have to refuse to partake in such a practice, but if the team is a playoff long-shot (which a loss in the next two games would cause), there’s no risk.
“If Drew Lock plays well in the Cardinals game and beyond, can he be Sam Darnold’s replacement?”
I may be getting ahead of myself a little bit here, but my honest sense is that Darnold’s time in Seattle is up no matter what. He’s had every opportunity to right the ship this year and show some signs that his time under Kyle Shanahan, Kevin O’Connell, and Klint Kubiak in recent seasons had rubbed off on him. Clearly, it hasn’t . There’s no future here.
He’s up for an extension this offseason and his cap hit in 2027 is too big to hold. So unless Lock is truly putrid in the coming weeks or gets hurt, I’m riding with him the rest of the way. As for beyond this season, I can see it as a bridge for 2027. I’m skeptical of him becoming a franchise QB, even a low-tier one, but we’ve been down this road before, so I’ll keep an open mind.

title: 49ers Head Coach Kyle Shanahan Explains Plan for Mike Evans' Return
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans has been one of the best wide receivers in the NFL when he is healthy. However, that  "when healthy" aspect has not been as consistent as the team would like.
Evans left the 49ers' Week 6 win over the Washington Commanders with an Achilles injury. After missing the 49ers' Week 7 loss to the Atlanta Falcons and getting the bye week off, Evans still did not participate in practice when the 49ers returned to the field on Wednesday.
Evans was ruled out for Week 9, but the 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan noted the team has a plan for his potential return.
“Yeah, I think we've made a lot of progress,” Shanahan said of the status of their star free agent addition. “I think he's going the right direction, and I mean it's something we definitely got to be smart with. We're not going to, like, overdo it. We just want to wait till he's healthy and he's still working his way to get there.”
When healthy, Evans is arguably the best receiver in the NFL. He is averaging 3.41 yards per route run. That is second in the NFL behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba. The issue is that he can not always stay on the field at his age.
Evans played 75% of the snaps in Week 1, and left with an injury. He has not played more than 63% in any game since then and has played in less than half of the snaps in two games. Overall, he has only played 46% of the team's snaps, and he is still struggling to stay healthy.
San Francisco is up three games in the loss column against the Los Angeles Rams and Seattle Seahawks. They have also beaten both of those teams already. So, the 49ers are not going to rush him back.
Christian Kirk returned before the bye week, and the team just opened the 21-day practice window for Demarcus Robinson. Jordan Watkins to ok steps before the bye w eek, so the team might have enough depth to get by without Evans for another week or two.
The goal for the 49ers is to maintain their division lead, but also get Evans into the playoffs healthy. If that happens, they have one of the best threats in the NFL. That is more important than a Week 9 matchup.

title: Brandon Aiyuk Says He Wants to Get Reinstated, Doesn't Mention the 49ers
full_text:
SANTA CLARA -- It's still unclear what exactly Brandon Aiyuk wants.
On Friday, he and his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, met with reporters outside the 49ers' business offices around the corner from the team's practice facility. Apparently, Aiyuk still isn't allowed inside the facility.
Perhaps that's because the league hasn't reinstated him despite the fact that he filed for reinstatement on Oct. 27, according to Rosenhaus .
So, Aiyuk and Rosenhaus pulled up to the 49ers' business offices in a luxury van. Rosenhaus stepped out first, and Aiyuk followed him.
"Obviously, Brandon is here to meet with the team," Rosenhaus said with Aiyuk standing next to him. "Fortunately, he's feeling good physically. He's healthy. He's ready to get back to work. Don't really have any comment about where he's going to play. We'll keep that between us and the 49ers. But, obviously, we're here with all the right intentions. I'll let Brandon say a couple things right now."
"Nice to see y'all," Aiyuk said. "I'm feeling great, feeling healthy. It's been a long recovery process, a long rehab process, but I'm back to 100 percent and looking to get reinstated into the National Football League."
At that point, Rosenhaus whisked Aiyuk away before anyone could ask a question. "They're waiting for us right now," Rosenhaus said, and he and Aiyuk disappeared inside the office building.
It sounds like Aiyuk wants to play in the NFL again, but still doesn't want to play for the 49ers. It seems like he thinks Rosenhaus can get him what he has wanted for more than a year -- a release -- so he can sign wherever he wants.
And from the way Rosenhaus spoke, it sounds like he expects Aiyuk to have a new team soon. Rosenhaus doesn't have any comment about where Aiyuk is going to play, but he sure didn't mention the 49ers.
And that's because the 49ers don't seem to want him back. When asked about Aiyuk earlier today, head coach Kyle Shanahan said he "could care less" about what happens to him.
It has been reported that the 49ers believe Aiyuk owes them $13 million in bonus money. Perhaps Rosenhaus and the 49ers' lawyers are negotiating a payout that would satisfy the 49ers and allow Aiyuk to finally leave.
Or, it's possible that the 49ers intend to frustrate Aiyuk and stonewall him as long as the league allows them to do so. And until the league officially reinstates him, the 49ers don't have to do anything.
Stay tuned. This story is far from over.

title: 49ers Rule Out 3 Key Players for Week 9 vs. Raiders
full_text:
Another week without star wide receiver Mike Evans.
The San Francisco 49ers have ruled out three key players, including Evans, for their Week 9 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders .
This will be the second consecutive game that Evans has missed. He was always expected to be out , as he's nursing Achilles tendinitis.
That's not an injury or a condition that will go away in a couple of weeks. Just look at what happened to Christian McCaffrey two years ago.
Granted, his situation was worse. He had bilateral Achilles tendinitis. Still, it's not an issue that will go away quickly. Substantial time and rest are needed.
That means 49ers fans should expect Evans to miss at least a couple more games. They have only themselves to blame for Evans' situation .
Evans suffered his Achilles injury in Week 5 against the Seattle Seahawks. As a result, he didn't participate in a single practice for the following game against the Washington Commanders.
That should've been more than enough to convince the 49ers to keep Evans inactive. If they had wisely held him out against the Commanders, Evans could've kept his Achilles from getting worse.
Instead, they let him dictate the terms and allowed him to play. Teams are supposed to protect players from themselves. They massively failed in this instance.
Now, they most likely have to play several games without him. There's no telling when he will return or if he can remain healthy for the rest of the season.
Another key player that will be out is Deebo Samuel. His absence isn't much of a surprise either. He's been dealing with a hamstring injury since Week 5.
Hamstrings are extremely tricky, especially if Samuel is dealing with a tear. It's best if Samuel slow-plays his return so he doesn't undo his recovery.
As for the last player ruled out, Christian Kirk injured his meniscus in practice this week. It's unclear if he tore it. The 49ers will be without him once again. It's safe to say the 49ers can stop expecting him to help this year.
As for the 49ers who are questionable to play against the Raiders: Nick Bosa (calf), Upton Stout (shoulder), Demarcus Robinson (ankle), and Nate Hobbs (groin).
Kyle Shanahan said Bosa is cleared to go and that Robinson will most likely be activated from Injured Reserve. They are still deciding on Hobbs.

title: Exclusive: George Kittle Reveals What It Means to Lead 49ers TEs in Touchdowns
full_text:
George Kittle's legacy with the San Francisco 49ers is already etched in the franchise's record books, and it wouldn't be surprising to see him immortalized with a sculpture at the team's museum inside Levi's Stadium someday.
The 2026 season marks Kittle's 10th year wearing the famed red and gold, having been selected by Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch in the fifth round of the 2017 NFL Draft. He now joins the elusive 10-year club, further cementing his place among the franchise's longest-serving players.
And perhaps more importantly, Kittle achieved a record that could stand for years to come. Earlier this season, against the Denver Broncos, the 33-year-old overtook Vernon Davis to become the 49ers' all-time leader in touchdown receptions by a tight end.
"Anytime you're on a record list within the 49ers organization, I think that's a pretty special list to be part of," Kittle told 49ers on SI's Henry Cheal .
"It's such a historic franchise, with so many amazing football players who have played here.
"Being in my tenth year of my career here, it's really exciting. It's always fun, and it's something I'm incredibly proud of.
"It's an honour just to be on the same list as Vernon Davis. You're also on lists alongside Jerry Rice and Terrell Owens. It's fascinating because those are guys I grew up watching, and the fact that I'm now mentioned alongside them is really cool.
"It's important to appreciate those achievements and take a moment to enjoy them. At the same time, I know there's still work to be done and more left to achieve. There's more meat on the bone, which I genuinely believe.
"But when you take a moment to sit back and think about it, I feel incredibly lucky and blessed to be in the position I'm in and to be where I am today.
"I'm just very thankful for it."
Kittle's latest milestone signals one thing: there's plenty more history left for him to make in San Francisco. Even more impressively, after spending the offseason rehabilitating an Achilles injury, he has emerged looking sharper than ever.
With five touchdowns and 425 receiving yards already to his name this season, Kittle is proving that the setback has done little to diminish his impact on the field.
Kittle has made it no secret that he wants to stay in San Francisco for his whole career . It's easy to understand why. Now it's about making more history and trying to bring the Super Bowl back home.

title: 49ers Have Only One Major Threat to Overcome Against the Raiders
full_text:
Coming off the Bye, the San Francisco 49ers should be feeling refreshed and locked in heading into Week 9.
Thankfully, they get a soft opening for the second half of their season. They get to play at home against the 4-4 Las Vegas Raiders . Now, the Raiders’ record may be .500, but they can’t hold a candle to the 49ers.
Defensively, the Raiders are a joke. The 49ers will be able to steamroll them, even without Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel. The same can kind of be said about the Raiders’ offense.
They have no threatening running game to worry about. Ashton Jeanty has been playing through pain and is underwhelming. And as sweet as Kirk Cousins has been, he’s nothing to lose sleep over.
However, the Raiders do have one offensive player who will be a problem: tight end Brock Bowers. He is the one and only major threat that the 49ers need to overcome on Sunday. It’s easier said than done, though.
Bowers has been on a tear this season. Nearly every defense that has faced him has been decimated. He’s impossible to silence and extremely difficult to slow down. It’s safe to say he’s playing at an All-Pro level.
“He's a stud,” said defensive coordinator Raheem Morris . “He's one of those guys, he can run through the catch, he plays fast, he can do everything. He's one of those guys, he plays receiver position, he plays tight end position, he creates all types of versatile piece. The ultimate joker as some of the guru offensive coordinators call those guys. Can move him anywhere, be in the backfield, run routes from the backfield. He can do it all, so he presents all kinds of matchup problems.”
The 49ers will need to be on their A-game when defending Bowers. He’s the one player who can prevent the 49ers from winning by more than three scores. It’ll be tough, but also exciting to watch.
Since Bowers is a tight end, he’ll see a handful of matchups with Fred Warner. That’s going to be the premier matchup of the game. These two elite players dueling it out will be one for the books.
The Raiders would do well to move Bowers around so that he doesn’t spend most of his time guarded by Warner. Should that happen, the 49ers will be well prepared to take him on.
“We’ve got a bunch of guys that we’ve got to be able to match up against him. You don't hold guys like that down without having some versatile pieces, some tools for those types of people.
"So, look forward to going against that kind of guy."

title: Raheem Morris Sounds Off On Kirk Cousins Ahead of 49ers-Raiders Matchup
full_text:
It’s been a long time since the San Francisco 49ers have played a .500-record Las Vegas Raiders team.
Usually, the Raiders are bottom-feeders. But this year, they’ve gotten themselves out of the dumps. One reason for that is quarterback Kirk Cousins. He’s been sweet this season.
Entering Week 9, Cousins has thrown for 2,124 yards (third-most), 19 touchdowns (second-most), and only five interceptions. No one could’ve foreseen him performing like this at his age.
But if you were to ask 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris , it wouldn’t surprise him. On Thursday, Morris was asked to share his thoughts on how Cousins has looked this year.
“Kirk's one of the all-time progression quarterbacks that the league has seen,” Morris said. “You go out and you get a guy like Kirk and you get a guy that can operate your offense at a very high level, control things that you want to get controlled. He's a computer during the week. He's taking it all in, going through the process, going through his process.”
“Then once he gets to the game, he's just able to allow himself to go out there and play. He can go through his process and do all the things that's operating. He's operating the right way, particularly at the end of the game and the Jets, big-time game last week for those guys. They started hot and for those guys to pick it up like they did, it's no shock. He's playing with a genuine enthusiasm that I'm used to seeing from him."
Morris spent two seasons with Cousins on the Atlanta Falcons. He’s very familiar with who he is as a person and as a player, having started numerous games for him in Atlanta.
If anyone can speak on Cousins, it’s Morris. He’s going to give it to you straight with his assessment. That should also give him an edge in defending against Cousins.
However, that was the belief entering Week 7 against the Falcons with Michael Penix Jr. Knowing a player well doesn’t mean the edge will be there, but several factors limited the 49ers’ defense in that game.
The pass rush is one of them. That won’t be an issue on Sunday against the Raiders. Morris may have a ton of love for Cousins, but come Sunday, he’ll be scheming to make it miserable for him.

title: Evaluating Chances of 49ers Landing All-Pro Safety in Trade
full_text:
Most people think the San Francisco 49ers will make another trade deadline move in addition to DeForest Buckner. An interesting name to keep an eye on is Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates, according to Bill Barnwell of ESPN .
Barnwell notes that Bates is a big swing who could put the team over the top, and he is familiar with the 49ers coaching staff.
“Finding one player who might be able to swing a playoff game with a big play could be a logical target for Lynch,” wrote Barnwell. “Jessie Bates III is a free agent after the season, and the 29-year-old safety has at least three interceptions in seven of his eight completed campaigns as a pro. He just made one of the plays of the season last week against the Buccaneers, forcing a Bucky Irving fumble on an impromptu speed option for a touchback. Bates is also familiar with Raheem Morris' defense, having played under the 49ers' defensive coordinator in Atlanta during the 2024 and 2025 seasons.”
Bates made the second-team All-Pro last year with the Falcons under the coaching of Morris.
The two issues with the analysis are the 49ers depth at safety and the Falcons staying in the NFC South hunt.
For the 49ers side, while they have Malik Mustapha, Marques Sigle, and Ji’Ayir Brown, none is at the level that Bates is. Brown is likely to leave in free agency after this year, and the team does not have plans to extend the other two, either.
They could even include one of them in a trade with the Falcons. If they traded Mustapha or Sigle, it would give them a safety with more than this year of team control. They would get a younger, cheaper safety who is signed longer than Bates. That would make the trade more worthwhile.
That would also make them more likely to accept a trade. The Falcons are 3-5, but they are also right in the thick of a weak NFC South. The Panthers are 3-4, the Bucs are 3-5, and the Saints are 2-5. So, the Falcons are not quite in a mode of packing it in and tossing away players.
Getting a safety back eases some of that concern, but unless they lose again in Week 9 and things break against them in Week 9, they might not be sellers. This could be a dream addition, but not a realistic one.

title: 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan Reveals the Impact of the DeForest Buckner Trade
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers' decision to bring back DeForest Buckner is a shrewd bit of business .
The best part was that it only cost the front office next year's fourth-round pick.
Though Buckner is 32 and represents another ageing player on an already veteran-heavy roster, his return adds valuable depth in the short term while addressing one of the 49ers' biggest weaknesses.
The move has proven to be very popular among the key names who have played under Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch since the very beginning. The likes of George Kittle, Fred Warner and Nick Bosa are all glad to see his return.
“Yeah, I think just like it does to you guys or just like to fans. Everyone gets excited when you add a player," stated Shanahan to reporters .
"When we’re on break, I get tons of texts from guys on the team just, ‘Man, Buck’s back, that’s awesome.’
"So, everyone talks the same and then you get to work and you get used to it. I think everyone gets that initial burst and then it’s how good the players are, adding someone like Buck, and what it adds to the field and the meetings and everything like that, then that’s where the momentum becomes real.”
Buckner's return could be short-lived, with his contract expiring at the end of the season, although an extension remains a possibility. The 49ers' Super Bowl window is arguably closing, with this season or next potentially representing their final opportunity to compete.
Against that backdrop, the front office's decision to act and bring back a player of Buckner's caliber speaks volumes, especially compared with its inaction 12 months ago, despite the team's encouraging starts on an injury-ravaged roster.
That said, Shanahan believes San Francisco is a stronger team than it was in 2025, making Buckner's return an even more significant addition.
“Yeah, I definitely think we’re a better team than we were last year at the time you asked me that," shared Shanahan.
"I never really think you’re one player away, but I definitely think, I don’t remember our record at the time, but we ended up finishing with a real good record.
"But, I do know our team’s better than it was last year. It was awesome to add Buckner, really awesome, and it’d be great to add someone else if that works out, but we’re not counting on it, but it’d still be great. We’ve still got time.”
Buckner's return to the City by the Bay is incredibly valuable.

title: Reading Between the Lines: What the 49ers are Really Saying about Brandon Aiyuk
full_text:
Brandon Aiyuk is expected at the 49ers’ facility on Friday. He hasn’t played since October 2024, and in that time, he has gone from a contract holdout to a knee injury to a long, public estrangement from the team. Now he has a new agent in Drew Rosenhaus and has filed for reinstatement. John Lynch and Kyle Shanahan haven’t said what the 49ers will do, but what they said and what they avoided saying tells us a lot.
Lynch: “Fluid” and “Management Council”
Lynch started with the 6-1 record, which tells you where the priorities are. Then he said he is working with the NFL Management Council on a “different situation” with “no playbook,” and that he’d been advised to say little.
When a GM brings in the league’s labor arm and a lawyer’s caution, this is about process and protecting the team. It isn’t about a depth chart. Lynch’s phrase about a “pathway for both sides that works” sounds like a negotiated separation, since a player who is coming back doesn’t need a pathway.
He didn’t close the door, either. “Everything’s possible,” he said, and he praised Rosenhaus as reasonable and a man of integrity. That’s how you talk when you want a deal to go smoothly. Lynch also promised more details “in the coming weeks,” and that timeline matters because it runs past next week’s trade deadline.
Shanahan: A door that’s closed but not locked
Shanahan was more direct. He said he has “no expectation,” has “moved on mentally,” and that nothing has changed since he spoke two months ago.
Two other answers stood out. When asked whether the Niners might seek a roster exemption to evaluate Aiyuk, he said he has “zero questions” about him, so there’s no plan to buy time and take a look. And on whether anything gets resolved before Aiyuk shows up, he said Aiyuk “would have to show up for stuff to happen.” That suggests the process only starts once Aiyuk is in the building.
Then came “no absolutes in life.” It’s a coach’s way of not saying never, and I wouldn’t read much more into it than that.
Zero percent chance it happens -- but, how hilarious would it be if Brandon Aiyuk filed for reinstatement and played for the 49ers this season. https://t.co/Wh2llCR23N
Here’s my read, and it’s my opinion.
Release is the most likely outcome. The Management Council involvement, the “pathway for both sides” and the “coming weeks” timeline all fit a negotiated exit. The Niners already voided guarantees on his contract, so the money side of a clean break may be easier than it looks.
A trade is possible but hard. Aiyuk hasn’t played in over a year, and a team would be paying for a player coming off a serious knee injury with a messy history. A deal before the deadline would need a lot to go right quickly.
Staying is the least likely. Aiyuk has publicly criticized management, and Shanahan’s comments don’t sound like someone planning to bring him back into a locker room that’s 6-1. The one thing that could change this is a decision that the on-field help is worth the baggage.
Aiyuk was a second-team All-Pro in 2023 and finished his Niners career with 294 catches, 4,305 yards and 25 touchdowns. As I wrote earlier, this offense needs a receiver who separates on his routes, and Aiyuk fits that description on paper. That’s why this story won’t go away easily. It’s also why the team has to be careful.
When Lynch says “fluid” and Shanahan says “no expectation,” they aren’t describing a reunion. They’re describing a team that has already decided the answer is probably no and is looking for the cleanest way to say it. Friday will tell us more.
